documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Minutes  
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                    January 10, 2023 
                                            
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Mayor Everson at 2:03 PM. 
 
SEA Committee members present: Mayor Bob Everson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin Nelson, Cory 
Aadland, Jon Hart, Doug Greenway, Bryan Dixon, LaRee Rumbolz, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, 
and Jim Johnston 
 
SEA Committee members absent: Jill Larson and Emily Liedtke 
 
Others present: Stephanie Ellwein and Aaron Hieb 
 2. Funding Applications 
 A. No funding applications were submitted at this time. 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Bryan Dixon motioned to approve the previous minutes as presented. 
 
Second: Kevin McCardle seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
4. Financial Report 
City Administrator, Stephanie Ellwein, presented the financial report as of January 5, 2023. 
Collections in December (for November records) were 2.7% above 2021, 30.0% above 2020, 
2.1% above 2019, and 1.5% above 2018. These numbers are current, with only one hotel 
needing to report numbers. 
 
Motion: Jon Hart motioned to approve the financial report as presented. 
 
Second: Bryan Dixon seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 5. Updates/Evaluation Forms/Financials 
 A. No evaluation forms/financials were submitted at this time. 
6. Other Items 
Aaron presented and reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee: 
A. Upcoming Event Updates: 

     i. NAIA Women's Basketball National Championship First & Second Round Host 
       Bid: 

     • Potential games taking place on Tuesday, March 7th & Wednesday, March 8th at 
       the Corn Palace. 
     • Opportunity to pursue the Men's Host Bid as well. 

     i. Dakota Oyate Challenge (DOC): 
     • The DOC Board of Directors officially approved the city of Mitchell and the Corn 
       Palace as the host city and host site for the 35th Annual Boys & 30th Annual Girls 
       Dakota Oyate Challenge on January 25th-27th, 2024. 

 

     i. NAIA Women's Basketball National Championship First & Second Round Host 
       Bid: 

     • Potential games take place Tuesday, March 7th & Wednesday, March 8th at the Corn 
       Palace. Jon Hart will submit a BID packet to the NAIA by February 1st. There is the 
       possibility of being awarded a neutral host site location even if DWU does not make the 
       tournament. The NAIA Basketball National Championships will take place in Sioux City, 
       Iowa. 
     • There is the potential to be some scheduling conflicts with the SoDak 16 Class A and/or 
       Class B being on Tuesday, March 7th. If DWU does get approved as a host site for the 
       NAIA Women's Basketball National Championship First & Second Round games, MHS 
       and the Corn Palace will not put in a request to be a host site for the Class A/Class B 
       SoDak 16 basketball games. 

     i. Dakota Oyate Challenge (DOC): 

     • Doug Greenway and Aaron Hieb received confirmation via email last Wednesday that 
       the DOC Board of Directors officially approved the city of Mitchell and the Corn Palace 
       as the host city and host site for the 35th Annual Boys & 30th Annual Girls Dakota 
       Oyate Challenge on January 25th - 27th, 2024. Aaron will be traveling to Huron on 
       Friday, January 27th, to take in a day and learn about the DOC event.  
     • Some committee members voiced their concern about the event coming to Mitchell 
       because of the scheduling conflicts and challenges it would present for local basketball 
       teams. Also, some committee members disagree with Doug and Aaron about their 
       decision to recruit this event for Mitchell. This is not the right event to bring to Mitchell. 
     • Other committee members expressed the positive financial impact this event would 
       have on the city of Mitchell as well as the potential for many local attractions, 
       businesses, facilities, and restaurants to see a major spike in business during the three 
       days the event is in town. The DOC would be comparable, if not bigger, or as close as 
       Mitchell would get to hosting a "state basketball" type tournament. 
 
B. "Happy Holidays - Thank You" Sponsorship Post Card 

     • The Powder Horn Ranch Regulators - 20th Annual South Dakota State and High 
       Plains Territorial Cowboy Fast Draw Championships (August 8th-13th, 2023) 
 
C. SEA Banners On Display: 

     • Hoop City Classic (December 28th & 30th, 2022) 
              o SEA logo in the Hoop City program. 
              o SEA feather banners (South side of arena floor) 
              o Replaced/Updated SEA banner in the Hospitality Room. 
 
Doug Greenway presented a brief breakdown and update on the ticket numbers for the two 
days the Hoop City Classic was played in Mitchell. 

     • Wednesday, December 28th, tickets sold at the door = 1,731 
     • Friday, December 30th, tickets sold at the door = 1,031 

 
Also, teams confirmed that they stayed in Mitchell hotels during the event. 

     • Thunder Basin WY 
     • Campbell County WY 
     • Providence MN 
     • Waconia MN 

D. Discussion about SEA guidelines/policy regarding distribution of approved grant funds. 
Aaron presented/included this talking point on the agenda to gather thoughts, feedback, and 
direction from the committee about ways/ideas on how to collect the most thorough and most 
accurate information, specifically, the amount of hotel rooms sold, during the respective event. 
This is step one in a multi-step process. Aaron tried to "paint" as clear of a picture as possible 
for the committee about the vision and idea for the end goal, which would be to create a funding 
matrix to help assist the committee when determining the appropriate grant $$ amount based 
on the events potential and/or prior success. 
 
What we are looking for or the purpose of the proposed idea is to create more consistency with 
approval amounts and provide more predictability when it comes to the potential approved 
amount for the event. For example, event X compares to event Y in regards to the city's 
financial impact and the amount of hotel rooms sold. Event Y received this amount for their 
event, so event X should receive a similar amount based on the proposed/past financial 
success and hotel rooms sold during event X. 
 
Since the SEA revenue is generated from a portion of the Hotel Occupancy Tax, it only makes 
sense to have the deciding/starting factor in the funding matrix when determining an amount to 
approve for an event to be based on or heavily weighted on the amount of hotel rooms sold 
during the entirety of the event. So... the obstacle presented is how do we successfully collect 
accurate hotel rooms sold for each event. Also, would there be a way to effectively 
communicate to events that they would receive half the approved grant amount after the initial 
approval, and they would receive the other half after the event successfully submits the 
required post event evaluation form, financials, and hotel rooms sold during the event. This was 
a concern because most, if not all, SEA funded events need or expect the grant amount 
approved in its entirety prior to the event, not a few months down the road after the post event 
forms are submitted. 
 
Discussion was had about there being no easy way to track the people who stay overnight and 
those who stay elsewhere for an event. Most people who stay in a hotel are 
unwilling/uncomfortable to share why they are in town and "check out" without any interaction 
with the front desk. An idea presented was to create some sort of QR Code or Rate Code and 
distribute this "code" each time to the respective SEA approved event main contact. From 
there, the event main contact would share this event specific QR Code with all the participants 
in the event and the code would be used to track if the participant stayed overnight and at which 
hotel/motel. Another concern expressed by the committee was that without some sort of 
tracking system, how do we know that the hotel room numbers submitted on the grant 
application and/or evaluation form are accurate? This concern was in regards to the proposed 
funding matrix idea. 
 
This discussion/talking point will continue to be an agenda item going forward for future 
meetings. The committee was asked to provide Aaron with any ideas and/or feedback about a 
way to accurately and thoroughly track the amount of hotel rooms sold for an SEA event.  
7. Next Meeting Date: February 14th, 2023 @ 2 PM, City Hall - Council Chambers 
Mayor Everson set the next meeting date for Tuesday, February 14th, 2023 @ 2 PM at the City 
Hall - Council Chambers. 
 
Jon Hart commented that he will complete and submit the SEA Grant Applications for the DWU 
Indoor Futsal Winter Classic & DWU/Culvers Boys and Girls Basketball Classic, so these 
funding applications can be included on the February SEA meeting agenda. 
 
Also, Jim "Jocko" Johnston informed the committee that the city of Mitchell and Cadwell Park 
has been approved and will host the South Dakota State Amateur Baseball Tournament 
through 2024. 
8. Adjournment 
There being no further business to discuss. 
 
Meeting adjourned by: Mayor Everson at 2:54 PM.

12/13/2022 - Minutes
Call To Order:
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2 PM.
SEA Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, Kevin Nelson, Jon Hart, Doug Greenway,
LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston.
SEA committee members absent: Mayor Everson, Cory Aadland, and Bryan Dixon.
Others present: Stephanie Ellwein, Tiffany Batdorf, and Aaron Hieb.
Funding Applications:
SEA Grant application presentations conducted by applicants. The SEA Committee reviewed applications
for grant funding. The following applications were presented and considered:
Youth Athletic Foundation: Hoop City Classic - 2022
Date: December 28th - 30th, 2022 Contact: Ernie Kuyper Grant Request: $10,000
Ernie Kuyper was reached via the Council Chambers conference phone and spoke to the SEA
Committee regarding the upcoming Hoop City Classic, which is scheduled for Wednesday, December
28th - 30th, 2022. Games will be played in Mitchell at the Corn Palace on Wednesday, December 28th
and Friday, December 30th. Thursday, December 29th games will be held in Sioux Falls at the Sanford
Pentagon. There will be a total of 18 plus games (roughly 9 each day) while in Mitchell at the Corn
Palace. There are twenty-five in state teams and 10 out of state teams participating in this years Hoop
City Classic. Ernie confirmed that the teams from Wyoming and Arizona will be staying in Mitchell
during the duration of the classic. Also, Ernie will reach out by email to the teams and confirm where
they will be staying for the event. The requested grants funds would be used towards the expenses
associated with the event such as: team travel, meals, lodging, marketing the event, and paying for
staff (referees, security, clock workers, etc.).
Motion: Dave Helleloid motioned to award $5,000.
Second: Emily Liedtke seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and motion passed.
Mitchell Figure Skating Club: 7th Annual Palace Ice Festival
Date: January 13th - 15th, 2023 Contact: Brian Bultje Grant Request: $3,000-$4,000
Brian Bultje, Mitchell Figure Skating Club Secretary, presented the submitted grant application in
person. He briefly described the club/organization and its purpose. They are a non-profit organization
with purpose to provide the youth and young adults of Mitchell & surrounding communities with another
form of skating option. The Palace Ice Festival is a United States Figure Skating (USFS) sanctioned
event, which requires the recruitment of higher, more qualified judges. Currently, there is 1 judge from
1. 2:00 P.M.

Date: January 13th - 15th, 2023 Contact: Brian Bultje Grant Request: $3,000-$4,000
Brian Bultje, Mitchell Figure Skating Club Secretary, presented the submitted grant application in
person. He briefly described the club/organization and its purpose. They are a non-profit organization
with purpose to provide the youth and young adults of Mitchell & surrounding communities with another
form of skating option. The Palace Ice Festival is a United States Figure Skating (USFS) sanctioned
event, which requires the recruitment of higher, more qualified judges. Currently, there is 1 judge from
California, 2 from New Mexico, and 1 from Rapid City. The event takes place on Friday, January 13th -
Sunday, January 15th at the Mitchell Activities Center, with competitions on Friday and Saturday, and a
coaching clinic type event to wrap up the day on Sunday. Brian stated that currently there are thirty-eight
skaters registered for the event and expect more to sign up as event draws closer. Last years event had
thirty-five skaters participate in the event. Registration fees are determined by the number of events
each skater decides to participate in. The requested grant funds would pay for the volunteer judges
hotel rooms and meals. And any proceeds will be used to support the promotion, growth, and higher
level coaching for the club.
Motion: Emily Liedtke motioned to award $3,000.
Second: LaRee Rumbolz seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and motion passed.
Hanson 30-1: Girls & Boys Hanson Classic
Date: Girls - January 14th, 2023 & Boys - January 21st, 2023 Contact: Jim Bridge, Hanson Grant
Request: $2,000
Jim Bridge was reached via the Council Chambers conference phone and spoke to the SEA Committee
regarding the upcoming 40th Annual Girls Hanson Classic on Saturday, January 14th, and the 41st
Annual Boys Hanson Classic on Saturday, January 21st, 2023. There will be 8-9 games for each the
girls and boys classic. The goal of the classics is to provide successful, tournament atmosphere type
games. Jim was uncertain about the amount of hotel rooms sold for the classics, but he has reached
out to teams with an unofficial survey and estimated around 200 rooms are utilized between the teams
that stay and the fans. The requested grants funds would be split between the two classics, with the
girls utilizing approximately $750 and the boys utilizing approximately $1250. The hospitality room food
is prepared by the Hanson FACS/Home Ec classes, they purchase the groceries and prepare the
meals/food. The requested grant funds are used for the hospitality room items for coaches, school
admin., media, and officials. The National Guard, Coca-Cola, and Subway provide a meal for
players/coaches.
Motion: Tim Smith motioned to award $2,000.
Second: Jon Hart seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and motion passed.
Dakota Riptide: TIDE Last Chance Meet
Date: February 4th, 2023 Contact: Jason Wede, Dakota Riptide Grant Request: $2,000
Jason Wede and Rob Schelske presented the submitted grant application in person. Both are hopeful
that the pool will be functional and ready to go for their meet. Currently, swimmers have been traveling to
Huron and Sioux Falls to practice. The hope is to host this meet prior to the end of winter and give
swimmers another option to qualify for the state meet, which is a few weeks later. Huron's pool is only
twenty-five meters, which makes it difficult to host a meet of this caliber. Also, the facility is not set up
for spectators. Most indoor swim meets require a 25 yard pool. The TIDE Last Chance Meet will take
place Saturday, February 4th, 2023 and will last all day. Currently there are confirmed swimmers from
Sioux Falls and Yankton. Also, another way to entice more swimmers is that they are looking to add an
extra event, the mile. No other swim meets are taking place that weekend in Eastern South Dakota. The
only one Jason and Rob were aware of is a meet in Marshall, Minnesota. Dakota Riptide will use this
swim meet as a "re-grand opening" of the facility and a way to promote positive publicity for Mitchell, the
swim team, and the Mitchell Rec Center Indoor Pool facility. The requested grant funds will be used to
cover expenses for the meet, these include: pool rental, lifeguard wages, sound system, printing for
programs, meals for officials and coaches, and some concession expenses. Jason and Rob stated that
if the meet is unable to take place that they will reimburse the SEA for the approved grant amount.
Motion: Dave Helleloid motioned to award $2,000.

Village Bowl: Larry Hauser Memorial Adult/JR Doubles Tournament
Date: March 25th - 26th, 2023 Contact: Nate Sievert, Village Bowl Grant Request: $1,500
Nate Sievert presented the submitted grant application in person. This event will take place on
Saturday, March 25th at Village Bowl starting at Noon. It will partner with a 3rd party event, "The Next
Little Thing" which takes place Sunday, March 26th with registration at 9 AM and bowling begins at 10
AM. This will be the fourth of six events for this tournament/organization. There has already been two
completed events, one in Brookings and one in Chamberlain, where there were thirty-five and thirty-one
bowlers, respectively. Nate has reached out to Logan Luxury Theatre to possibly get some goodie bags
that include discount movie tickets as a way to incentivize the parents/youth bowlers to stay overnight
Saturday in Mitchell. The requested grant funds will be used specifically for the prize fund (scholarships)
for the youth bowlers. Many youth bowlers throughout the state have a "smart account" that specifically
uses the prize money that they collect at bowling tournaments towards scholarships that the bowlers
can access once they graduate high school and are off to college.
Motion: Jon Hart motioned to award $1,500.
Second: Emily Liedtke seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and motion passed.

above 2018.
Motion: Tim Smith motioned to approve the financial report as presented.
Second: Jon Hart seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and motion passed.
Updates/Evaluation Forms/Financials:
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms and Financial Statements submitted from past SEA
funded events with the SEA Committee:
Palace City Pre-Sturgis Party Evaluation Form And Financials
Total spectator attendance of 5,000+, which was derived from lodging occupancy, restaurant feedback,
& event attendance. Four hundred plus hotel/motel rooms sold. Hotels contacted to get numbers were
CoachLight Motel, Comfort Inn & Suites, Days Inn, Hampton Inn, Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites,
Kelly Inn & Suites, Quality Inn, and Super 8 Motel. The awarded funds ($15,000) were used towards
payment for the entertainment. P/L Statement was provided for the event. Net Loss for the event was
$10,551.25, which was paid by Klock Werks. The City of Mitchell, Chamber/CVB, Mitchell Main Street
& Beyond, and Klock Werks representatives have already held two successful planning meetings for
the 2023 event. Palace City Pre-Sturgis Party will not be requesting funding from the SEA going
forward. The City of Mitchell has already budgeted out an amount to be utilized towards this annual
event.

Other Items:
Aaron presented and reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee:
Dakota Territory Gun Collector's Association (DTGCA):
We have proposed a tentative date to the DTGCA Board of Directors for the gun show, November 10th-
12th, 2023 at the Corn Palace. This event would take place over Veteran's Day weekend with set up for
the event taking place all day Friday, and the gun show on Saturday from 9 AM - 5 PM and Sunday from
9 AM - 3 PM. The DTGCA Board of Directors have their annual meeting scheduled for February 4th at
the Aberdeen Gun Show, where they will make a decision about hosting gun show in Mitchell.
USA Powerlifting SD State Championship (USAPL):
Doug Greenway and Aaron Hieb met with Andrew Priebe last Thursday, December 8th about the
possibility of hosting a powerlifting competition in late March, early April at the Corn Palace. Many
positive comments about the high school powerlifting competition held at the lower gym at the Mitchell
High School the previous Saturday, December 3rd. The main concern/obstacle is not the venue and/or
space, but the difficulty obtaining enough and all the required equipment (warm up racks, weights,
platforms) to host this event, since the facility/venue does not have a weight room attached. Also, there
was discussion about it making more sense to host this competition on a Sunday, compared to a
Friday and/or Saturday. Andrew does have good social relationships with other powerlifting school
throughout the state such as: Brandon Valley and Sioux Falls O'Gorman, where if needed, he was
confident, we could utilize their equipment. Also, Midland Lutheran would be another option to possibly
load of their equipment and bring to Mitchell and the Corn Palace. Andrew is currently working on
collecting some feedback on costs and numbers to host an event like this.
SEA Banners On Display
The SEA logo was utilized on the Corn Palace Daktronics signs during the NAIA Women's Volleyball

documents.text:
Grant Guidelines & Information
GRANT PROGRAM
The purpose of the SEA program is to assist organizations in hosting events that will promote a
positive image to potential visitors, generate overnight visits, extend visitor stays, and create a de-
sire to return to the area. First consideration will be given to new festivals, new sports tournaments,
conventions, cultural arts events, and special events benefiting the City of Mitchell.
ELIGIBILITY
• Non-profit organizations, volunteer managed organizations, for-profit LLCs and individuals may
apply.
• Grants must have an impact on overnight stays within Mitchell.
APPLICATION GUIDELINES
• All grants must be matched on a dollar-for-dollar basis, matching funds include: cash
contributions, in-kind contributions or a combination of both.
• In-kind services include complimentary contributions of space, materials, equipment or
professional services (calculated on a local wage scale acceptable to Mitchell).
• Choose the funding category best suited to your event.
• Applications must be legible, accurate, include required event budgets/financials, and signed by
applicant - only complete applications will be considered .
• All events must create a positive image of Mitchell.
• Grants must be used for marketing the project to promote tourism.
Mitchell Sports & Events Authority | 612 N Main St | Mitchell, SD | 57301 | 605.990.7942
| sea@cityofmitchell.org |

--- PAGE 1 OF 2 ---


SEA ADVISORY COMMITTEE REVIEW CRITERIA
• Level of community impact and public benefit.
• Quality of the proposed project/event.
• Evidence of careful financial planning.
• Evidence of need and sustainability/growth potential.
• Projected tourism impact, including visitor spending and hotel/motel room night generation.
APPLICATION PROCEDURES
• Grant applications are reviewed monthly, the second Tuesday at 2 PM.
• Late applications will NOT be accepted. Please complete and submit 45 days before event.
• SEA reviews applications and clarifies areas as needed with applicant.
• The Mitchell SEA Advisory Committee reviews and evaluates applications, completing a stand-
ard rating form, and makes recommendations as a group.
• Approximately 2 weeks after the approval/denial of application, an email will notify applicant of
grant status.
• The Mitchell SEA Advisory Committee reserves the right to accept or reject any or all applications
- all decisions made by the SEA Advisory Committee are final
• 1/2 of grant funds are disbursed prior to the event and the second 1/2 are dispersed, post-
event - AFTER SUBMISSION OF REQUIRED FOLLOW-UP REPORT & FINANCIALS.
INELIGIBLE ORGANIZATIONS & PROGRAMS
• Organizations that discriminate on the basis of race, color, creed, gender, national origin, or sex-
ual orientation.
• Political organizations, candidates for political office, and organizations whose primary purpose is
to influence legislation.
• Building (brick and mortar) or capital campaigns.
• Staffing/administrative costs.
• Individuals and organizations that have not fulfilled all previous grant administrative guidelines.
• Non-profit fundraisers.
Mitchell Sports & Events Authority | 612 N Main St | Mitchell, SD | 57301 | 605.990.7942
| sea@cityofmitchell.org |

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Minutes  
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                   February 14, 2023 
                                            
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM. 
 
SEA Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, Kevin Nelson, Jon Hart, 
Doug Greenway, Bryan Dixon, LaRee Rumbolz, Dave Helleloid, and Tim Smith. 
 
SEA Committee members absent: Mayor Bob Everson, Cory Aadland, Emily Liedtke, and 
Jim Johnston. 
 
Others present: Stephanie Ellwein, Tiffany Batdorf, and Aaron Hieb. 
2. Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Committee reviewed applications 
for grant funding. The following applications were presented and considered: 
A. DWU Athletics: DWU/Culver's Girls & Boys High School Basketball Classic 
Date: February 10th-11th, 2023; Contact: Jon Hart & Brad Bartscher; Grant Request: $2,000 

     • The SEA Grant Application and other event documents were presented to the 
       committee via email, since the event would have been completed by the February 
       14th, Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee meeting. Motion, voting, and 
       approval were done via phone/email. 

Motion: Tim Smith motioned to award $2,000. 
 
Second: Cory Aadland seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
Abstain: Jon Hart abstained from voting. 
B. Buckin' Wild Ranch: Cabin Fever Auction 
Date: February 24th-25th, 2023; Contact: Ashley Coulter; Grant Request: $2,000 

     • Nick Coulter from Buckin' Wild Ranch traveled from Flandreau to present their grant 
       application to the committee. This will be the 5th Annual Buckin' Wild Ranch: Cabin 
       Fever Auction since Nick and his wife, Ashley, took the auction over. It is a 2-day 
       auction that takes place at the Davison County Fairgrounds. The main expenses that 
       Buckin' Wild Ranch accrue for the event are as follows: they pay for the wages of the 
       auctioneers and staff, as well as pay for the hotel rooms for those personnel, which 
       comes to be about 43 rooms for the entirety of the event. 

Motion: Doug Greenway motioned to award $1,200. 
 
Second: Tim Smith seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

     • The SEA Committee requested and approved the following criteria for dispersal of 
       funds: 
            o 1/2 of the grant funds ($600) will be dispersed for the initial approval of the 
              event. 
            o The second 1/2 of grant funds ($600) will be dispersed after the submission of 
              the required post-event Evaluation Form and Financials. 

C. DWU Soccer: DWU 13th Annual Futsal Indoor Classic 
 
Date: February 24th-26th, 2023; Contact: Nicolas Reinhard; Grant Request: $1,500 

     • Coach Nicolas Reinhard and Coach John Hakari, both first year (been with programs 
       for 8 months) Boy's and Girl's soccer coaches for Dakota Wesleyan University, 
       presented the submitted grant application. Currently, there are 60 teams registered at 
       $250 per team, and a team consists of 10 players. Most tournament entry fees are 
       much more than $250 ($25 per player). This year the team/player registration is down 
       almost 50% compared to previous years. This is due to the creator of the event, former 
       DWU Soccer coach, Clayton Glasgow, who is now the current soccer coach at 
       Southwest Minnesota State, hosting two of these indoor futsal events during the winter. 
       Most of the teams, which are from the Dakota Alliance Youth Soccer Club, that have 
       previously competed in this event are now participating in the events at SMSU. Coach 
       Reinhard and Coach Hakari need to re-establish the name and integrity of the event 
       and recruit some of those teams to participate in this event. Currently, teams that are 
       registered are from SD, ND, and MN, with a few Mitchell youth soccer teams 
       participating and a vast number of teams competing from Watertown. Coach Reinhard 
       reviewed the 2023 event budget with the committee. The $1,500 grant request would 
       be used to reward the student-athletes for their participation to certify themselves to be 
       referees for the event. The grant request is also considered, in Coach Reinhard and 
       Coach Hakaris' eyes, as an investment into rebuilding the event to what it once was. 
       The question was presented about possibly using a different date for the event. The 
       coaches stated that this was an inherited event date and that a possibility for future 
       events would be to coordinate/work together with Clayton Glasgow and make sure 
       these events don't overlap each other.  

Motion: Bryan Dixon motioned to award $1,500. 
 
Second: Doug Greenway seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
Abstain: Jon Hart abstained from voting. 
D. Mitchell Music Boosters: Mitchell Show Choir Classic 
Date: March 18th, 2023; Contact: Angella Buenzow; Grant Request: $5,000 

     • Matt Culhane, Mitchell Music Boosters, presented the grant application to the 
       committee. This year will be the 30th Anniversary of the event, taking place on 
       Saturday, March 18th. Currently, there are 20 teams competing in the event from IA, 
       NE, and even Troy, Missouri. Mitchell Show Choir does not compete in this event 
       because they are not eligible to win the competition. Each team brings around 100 
       participants, along with a couple dozen parents. Matt shared some rough numbers with 
       the committee. One team will most likely spend around $7,500 in just hotel revenue. 
       Most teams may not stay both Friday and Saturday night, the majority stay Saturday 
       night. The Mitchell Show Choir was just in Urbandale, Iowa and Matt booked the hotel 
       rooms, which consisted of 15 parent rooms, along with 26 kid rooms. The Mitchell 
       Music Boosters has three major fundraisers throughout a given year, which are: 1st: 
       Up with Show - more of a community show, 2nd: Show Choir Classic, and 3rd: in the 
       spring is another community show. Matt explained the two major expenses for the 
       Show Choir Classic, and they are: getting quality/high caliber judges = five or six 
       judges costing around $5,000 (very influential, can be the determining factor in 
       schools/teams deciding to participate in the event), and concessions (buying the food 
       which they end up selling). Also, merchandise revenue for the event. Matt explained 
       that each year there is a "theme" to the classic and they sell "themed" hoodies, t-shirts, 
       and beanies.  

Motion: Dave Helleloid motioned to award $3,000. 
 
Second: Tim Smith seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Bryan Dixon motioned to approve the previous minutes as presented. 
 
Second: Kevin Nelson seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
4. Financial Report 
City Administrator, Stephanie Ellwein, presented the financial report as of February 10, 2023. 
Collections in January (for December records) were 11.7% down from 2022, 14.5% above 
2021, 25.8% down from 2020, 2.3% down from 2019, and 8.5% down from 2018. These 
numbers are current, with only two hotels needing to report numbers. 
 
Motion: Jon Hart motioned to approve the financial report as presented.   
 
Second: Tim Smith seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
5. Updates/Evaluation Forms/Financials 
No evaluation forms/financials were submitted at this time. 
6. Other Items 
Aaron presented and reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee: 
A. Event Recruitment Updates 
Mitchell Technical College (MTC) Mavericks Rodeo Competition 

     • Aaron met with Head Coach Jimmie Nicolaus on Wednesday, January 18th, 2023 to 
       discuss the possibility and if there is an opportunity to host a college rodeo competition 
       in Mitchell. Aaron shared some of the meeting notes/details with the committee. Coach 
       Nicolaus is quite the guy, very knowledgeable and ambitious. Mitchell Technical 
       College Mavericks Rodeo Team is a part of the National Intercollegiate Rodeo 
       Association (NIRA). Within that association, MTC belongs to the Great Plains Region, 
       which consists of 15 schools from SD, IA, ND, NE, and WI. Out of these 15 schools, 10 
       schools are on the annual rotation for hosting a qualifying rodeo for which you are able 
       to receive points towards the national competition. Coach Nicolaus and Aaron 
       discussed that it would be pointless to create an 11th rodeo, since it wouldn't be 
       eligible to receive national competition qualifying points. For Mitchell/MTC to even 
       consider hosting a college rodeo competition, one of the current ten schools would 
       need to remove themselves from the annual rotation. If an opportunity did arise, MTC 
       would be interested in pursuing a competition for the spring, sometime in April. Aaron 
       gave a brief breakdown of the competition. There are around 270 participants that 
       compete either as a team or individual. Currently, MTC has 21 members on their rodeo 
       team. An estimate, but around 70% of the teams/contestants would stay Thursday 
       through Sunday. The minimum budget ballpark to consider hosting a college rodeo 
       competition is $30,000. 

 
Hoop City Classic 2023 

     • Doug Greenway shared the news about Ernie Kuyper and the Hoop City Classic, 
       bringing all three days (Thursday 28th, Friday 29th, and Saturday 30th) of the event to 
       Mitchell at the end of December 2023. Another aspect of the Hoop City Classic would 
       be the Youth Tournament as well. There would be somewhere around 70-80 youth 
       teams participating as well. 

 
Hanson Girls Basketball Classic 

     • Doug shared the ticketed number of attendees - 1,585 through the door. This does not 
       include athletes/coaches/cheerleaders. 

 
Hanson Boys Basketball Classic 

     • Doug shared the ticketed number of attendees - 1,946 through the door. This does not 
       include athletes/coaches/cheerleaders. 

 
DWU/Culver's High School Basketball Classic vs. SDHSSA State Gymnastics 

     • Discussion was had regarding hosting the DWU/Culver's High School Basketball 
       Classic compared to the SDHSAA State Gymnastics. 
            o DWU/Culver's HS Basketball Classic is a major fundraiser for DWU and, from 
              an event standpoint, the Corn Palace does not want to lose the DWU/Culver's 
              Classic. 
            o The SDHSAA has expressed interest in bringing the State Gymnastics back to 
              Mitchell and the Corn Palace. There has been no signed agreement with the 
              SDHSAA yet. 
            o DWU/Culver's HS Basketball Classic is a much better event to host from a Corn 
              Palace standpoint based on attendance and concession numbers. 
            o From a hotel perspective, (20-24 teams) SDHSAA State Gymnastics does 
              better than the DWU/Culver's Classic. 

 
USA Patriots Amputee Softball Team, formerly known as the Wounded Warrior Amputee 
Softball Team 

     • Tiffany shared with the committee interest from this organization about possibly 
       bringing this one day event and children's camp to Mitchell in the summer of 2024. 
     • The major cost/expense would be covering the travel costs for the teams, which is 
       estimated to be around $7,000. 
     • Jeremy Nielsen would be the first initial contact to reach out to regarding open 
       dates/weekends to possibly host this event at the Cadwell Sports Complex. 

 
Bartholow Brothers Trapshooting Clinic 

     • Bryan Dixon shared this event coming to town. Coachlight already has 7 rooms booked 
       for three nights. 
     • Coming to town last weekend of March/first weekend of April. 
     • Potential to make this an annual event. 
     • Attendees coming from Huron, Watertown, and North Dakota. 
 
B. SEA Banners on Display 
Palace Ice Festival (January 13th-14th, 2023) 

     • SEA square banner hung on the bleachers by the door going into Toshiba Rink. 

 
Hanson Girls & Boys Basketball Classic (January 14th & 21st, 2023) 

     • SEA square banner in the Hospitality Room. 
     • SEA logo on the Corn Palace arena digital boards. 

 
DWU/Culver's Girls & Boys High School Basketball Classic (February 10th-11th, 
2023) 

     • SEA square banner in the Hospitality Room. 
     • SEA feather banners were displayed in the Corn Palace arena. 

C. Discussion about SEA guidelines/policy regarding distribution of approved grant 
funds. 

     • QR Code image(s) 

 


                         
 
                         

     • Hotel Survey 
     • Event QR Code Template 

 

     • Aaron continued discussion with the SEA Committee about the best method to track 
       hotel rooms sold during SEA event. Last meeting, Aaron thought there was a sense of 
       concern or hesitancy about the 'estimate' of hotel rooms on a grant application and/or 
       evaluation form when using that number to determine a funding amount. Aaron 
       presented a QR Code to the committee in three different colors: Gold, White, and 
       Burgundy. The gold and white QR Codes have the most successful, best scan rate 
       compared to the burgundy. Once the QR Code is scanned, it will take the participant to 
       the "landing page", which is a Hotel Survey on the City of Mitchell website. A question 
       was asked if these QR Codes would be distributed to all hotels or if this is just an event 
       specific distribution. For the time being, this QR Code will be included in the approval 
       email along with the Award Letter. There will be instructions about the use and 
       expectations of the QR Code for the Event Organizer/Main Contact. The requirement 
       for an approved event will still be to submit a post-event Evaluation Form with 
       Financials following the completion of the event. The QR Code is meant to have the 
       purpose of being a tool to assist the Event Organizer in determining as accurately the 
       number as possible for the total hotel/motel rooms sold for the entirety of the event. 
       Another question expressed by the committee was who would be filling out or expected 
       to fill out the QR Code... There is concern that there will be duplicate information when 
       multiple family members scan the code and participate, which will cause the 
       hotel/motel room numbers sold to be skewed. For the majority of SEA funded events, 
       the Event Organizer will include or distribute the QR Code to the coach of each team or 
       the individuals competing in the respective SEA funded event. It was expressed that 
       most events nowadays have a designated worker/volunteer that is the "hotel person" 
       and will be in charge of distributing/completing the hotel survey in a successful manner. 
       Going a step further, prior to each SEA funded event, Aaron will take multiple copies of 
       the QR Code Event Flyer to the venue and/or facility and post the QR Codes in 
       accessible locations for fans and spectators to scan as well. This will be in the hopes of 
       gathering information from the fans/spectators attending the event as well as the 
       athletes/participants in the event. Overall, Aaron expressed that the goal was not to 
       create more work for the Event Organizer or not intended to complicate and/or burden 
       an organization or event with completing a SEA Grant Application because of the 
       expected paperwork required after grant approval. 

7. Next Meeting Date: March 14th, 2023 @ 2 PM - City Hall, Council Chambers 
Kevin McCardle set the next meeting date for Tuesday, March 14th, 2023 @ 2 PM at the City 
Hall - Council Chambers. 
8. Adjournment 
There being no further business to discuss. 
 
Meeting adjourned by: Kevin McCardle at 3:09 PM.

DWU ATHLETICS ANNOUNCES DWU/CLUVER’S HIGH SCHOOL CLASSIC
PAIRINGS
Mitchell, S.D. – Dakota Wesleyan University Athletics announced the matchups
for the 8th annual girl’s classic and the 14th annual boy’s classic on Friday,
February 10 and Saturday, February 11. The DWU/Culvers Classic will return to
The Corn Palace for 2023 after being held in Salem, S.D. last year.
"We couldn't be more excited to host an exciting slate of high school basketball
games," DWU Director of Athletics Jon Hart commented. "As always, this event
will feature some of the best teams and players in the state. This event wouldn't
be possible without the cooperation of local teams, sponsors and our headline
partner, Culver's."
Games over both days will feature 10 girls class “B” teams, seven girls class “A”
teams, 10 boys class “B” teams, and eight boys class “A” teams.
Tickets for the two-day event will be sold exclusively at the door each day, $10
for adults, $5 for students, and kids five years of age and under get in free.
All Games will be streamed exclusively online as Pay-Per-View at
https://portal.stretchinternet.com/dwu/. Each day will be separated with a morning
and afternoon session at $8.99 per session.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: Conventions, meetings, retreats etc.
Sporting Events: Tournaments, competitions etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including camping, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Minutes
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
January 10, 2023
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Mayor Everson at 2:03 PM.
SEA Committee members present: Mayor Bob Everson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin Nelson, Cory
Aadland, Jon Hart, Doug Greenway, Bryan Dixon, LaRee Rumbolz, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith,
and Jim Johnston
SEA Committee members absent: Jill Larson and Emily Liedtke
Others present: Stephanie Ellwein and Aaron Hieb
2. Funding Applications
A. No funding applications were submitted at this time.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Bryan Dixon motioned to approve the previous minutes as presented.
Second: Kevin McCardle seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
City Administrator, Stephanie Ellwein, presented the financial report as of January 5, 2023.
Collections in December (for November records) were 2.7% above 2021, 30.0% above 2020,
2.1% above 2019, and 1.5% above 2018. These numbers are current, with only one hotel
needing to report numbers.
Motion: Jon Hart motioned to approve the financial report as presented.
Second: Bryan Dixon seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Updates/Evaluation Forms/Financials
A. No evaluation forms/financials were submitted at this time.
6. Other Items
Aaron presented and reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee:
A. Upcoming Event Updates:
i. NAIA Women's Basketball National Championship First & Second Round Host
Bid:
• Potential games taking place on Tuesday, March 7th & Wednesday, March 8th at
the Corn Palace.
• Opportunity to pursue the Men's Host Bid as well.
i. Dakota Oyate Challenge (DOC):

--- PAGE 1 OF 4 ---


• The DOC Board of Directors officially approved the city of Mitchell and the Corn
Palace as the host city and host site for the 35th Annual Boys & 30th Annual Girls
Dakota Oyate Challenge on January 25th-27th, 2024.
i. NAIA Women's Basketball National Championship First & Second Round Host
Bid:
• Potential games take place Tuesday, March 7th & Wednesday, March 8th at the Corn
Palace. Jon Hart will submit a BID packet to the NAIA by February 1st. There is the
possibility of being awarded a neutral host site location even if DWU does not make the
tournament. The NAIA Basketball National Championships will take place in Sioux City,
Iowa.
• There is the potential to be some scheduling conflicts with the SoDak 16 Class A and/or
Class B being on Tuesday, March 7th. If DWU does get approved as a host site for the
NAIA Women's Basketball National Championship First & Second Round games, MHS
and the Corn Palace will not put in a request to be a host site for the Class A/Class B
SoDak 16 basketball games.
i. Dakota Oyate Challenge (DOC):
• Doug Greenway and Aaron Hieb received confirmation via email last Wednesday that
the DOC Board of Directors officially approved the city of Mitchell and the Corn Palace
as the host city and host site for the 35th Annual Boys & 30th Annual Girls Dakota
Oyate Challenge on January 25th - 27th, 2024. Aaron will be traveling to Huron on
Friday, January 27th, to take in a day and learn about the DOC event.
• Some committee members voiced their concern about the event coming to Mitchell
because of the scheduling conflicts and challenges it would present for local basketball
teams. Also, some committee members disagree with Doug and Aaron about their
decision to recruit this event for Mitchell. This is not the right event to bring to Mitchell.
• Other committee members expressed the positive financial impact this event would
have on the city of Mitchell as well as the potential for many local attractions,
businesses, facilities, and restaurants to see a major spike in business during the three
days the event is in town. The DOC would be comparable, if not bigger, or as close as
Mitchell would get to hosting a "state basketball" type tournament.
B. "Happy Holidays - Thank You" Sponsorship Post Card
• The Powder Horn Ranch Regulators - 20th Annual South Dakota State and High
Plains Territorial Cowboy Fast Draw Championships (August 8th-13th, 2023)
C. SEA Banners On Display:
• Hoop City Classic (December 28th & 30th, 2022)
o SEA logo in the Hoop City program.
o SEA feather banners (South side of arena floor)
o Replaced/Updated SEA banner in the Hospitality Room.

--- PAGE 2 OF 4 ---


Doug Greenway presented a brief breakdown and update on the ticket numbers for the two
days the Hoop City Classic was played in Mitchell.
• Wednesday, December 28th, tickets sold at the door = 1,731
• Friday, December 30th, tickets sold at the door = 1,031
Also, teams confirmed that they stayed in Mitchell hotels during the event.
• Thunder Basin WY
• Campbell County WY
• Providence MN
• Waconia MN
D. Discussion about SEA guidelines/policy regarding distribution of approved grant funds.
Aaron presented/included this talking point on the agenda to gather thoughts, feedback, and
direction from the committee about ways/ideas on how to collect the most thorough and most
accurate information, specifically, the amount of hotel rooms sold, during the respective event.
This is step one in a multi-step process. Aaron tried to "paint" as clear of a picture as possible
for the committee about the vision and idea for the end goal, which would be to create a funding
matrix to help assist the committee when determining the appropriate grant $$ amount based
on the events potential and/or prior success.
What we are looking for or the purpose of the proposed idea is to create more consistency with
approval amounts and provide more predictability when it comes to the potential approved
amount for the event. For example, event X compares to event Y in regards to the city's
financial impact and the amount of hotel rooms sold. Event Y received this amount for their
event, so event X should receive a similar amount based on the proposed/past financial
success and hotel rooms sold during event X.
Since the SEA revenue is generated from a portion of the Hotel Occupancy Tax, it only makes
sense to have the deciding/starting factor in the funding matrix when determining an amount to
approve for an event to be based on or heavily weighted on the amount of hotel rooms sold
during the entirety of the event. So... the obstacle presented is how do we successfully collect
accurate hotel rooms sold for each event. Also, would there be a way to effectively
communicate to events that they would receive half the approved grant amount after the initial
approval, and they would receive the other half after the event successfully submits the
required post event evaluation form, financials, and hotel rooms sold during the event. This was
a concern because most, if not all, SEA funded events need or expect the grant amount
approved in its entirety prior to the event, not a few months down the road after the post event
forms are submitted.
Discussion was had about there being no easy way to track the people who stay overnight and
those who stay elsewhere for an event. Most people who stay in a hotel are
unwilling/uncomfortable to share why they are in town and "check out" without any interaction
with the front desk. An idea presented was to create some sort of QR Code or Rate Code and
distribute this "code" each time to the respective SEA approved event main contact. From
there, the event main contact would share this event specific QR Code with all the participants
in the event and the code would be used to track if the participant stayed overnight and at which

--- PAGE 3 OF 4 ---


hotel/motel. Another concern expressed by the committee was that without some sort of
tracking system, how do we know that the hotel room numbers submitted on the grant
application and/or evaluation form are accurate? This concern was in regards to the proposed
funding matrix idea.
This discussion/talking point will continue to be an agenda item going forward for future
meetings. The committee was asked to provide Aaron with any ideas and/or feedback about a
way to accurately and thoroughly track the amount of hotel rooms sold for an SEA event.
7. Next Meeting Date: February 14th, 2023 @ 2 PM, City Hall - Council Chambers
Mayor Everson set the next meeting date for Tuesday, February 14th, 2023 @ 2 PM at the City
Hall - Council Chambers.
Jon Hart commented that he will complete and submit the SEA Grant Applications for the DWU
Indoor Futsal Winter Classic & DWU/Culvers Boys and Girls Basketball Classic, so these
funding applications can be included on the February SEA meeting agenda.
Also, Jim "Jocko" Johnston informed the committee that the city of Mitchell and Cadwell Park
has been approved and will host the South Dakota State Amateur Baseball Tournament
through 2024.
8. Adjournment
There being no further business to discuss.
Meeting adjourned by: Mayor Everson at 2:54 PM.

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Minutes  
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                    March 14, 2023 
                                            
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Mayor Everson at 2:01 PM. 
 
SEA Committee members present: Mayor Bob Everson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin Nelson, 
Doug Greenway, Bryan Dixon, LaRee Rumbolz, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston. 
 
SEA Committee members absent: Jill Larson, Cory Aadland, Jon Hart, and Emily Liedtke 
 
Others present: Stephanie Ellwein and Aaron Hieb 
2. Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Committee reviewed applications 
for grant funding. The following applications were presented and considered: 
A. Mitchell Area Youth Trapshooters: Bartholow Brothers Youth Trapshooting Clinic 
Date: April 1st-2nd, 2023; Contact: Jerry Opbroek; Grant Request: $1,735 

     • Jerry Opbroek presented the grant application to the committee. Matt and Foster 
       Bartholow are nationally recognized trap shooters and are considered to be the best. 
       The trap shooting clinic is free of charge and will take place at the Davison County 
       Fairgrounds as well as the Mitchell Trap Club during the shooting portion of the clinic. 
       This event/clinic has been in Pierre for the last four years. Jerry expressed that being in 
       Pierre, the participants were mostly west river South Dakota youth. Now that the 
       event/clinic will be hosted in Mitchell, they will be able to reach and provide for a 
       different set of kids, from east river South Dakota. Jerry's hope is that Mitchell will be the 
       host site for this event/clinic on an annual basis or at least share the hosting duties with 
       Pierre. They already have participants registered from Custer, Winner, and Yankton. 
       Jerry praised the Bartholow brothers teaching/coaching skills during the clinic and that 
       they provide detailed expertise to the youth participants. 

 
Motion: Doug Greenway motioned to award $1,735. 
 
Second: Jim Johnston seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
Abstain: Bryan Dixon abstained from voting, since he has rooms for participants currently 
booked at the Coachlight Motel for this event. 
B. Mitchell Skating & Hockey Association: Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament 
Date: April 14th-16th, 2023; Contact: Stacy Murtha; Grant Request: $3,000 

     • Stacy Murtha presented the grant application to the committee. This is the 12th annual 
       Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament and the biggest in the area. The tournament fills 
       up fast. Basically, six days it took Stacy to fill the tournament. Currently, it is full with 
       twenty-one, possibly twenty-two, 14 player teams. Roughly three hundred adult hockey 
       players will take part in this tournament along with their families, which begins Friday, 
       April 14th at Noon and runs through Sunday, April 16th, and will wrap up around 4 or 5 
       pm on Sunday. There will be thirty-nine games during the three days. They have teams 
       from North Dakota, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Iowa, and South Dakota. Sioux Falls is 
       chomping at the bit to be able to host this tournament, but the response that he gets 
       from the five Sioux Falls teams that compete in the Mitchell tournament is that Sioux 
       Falls has no one to organize the event. The two biggest expenses for this tournament 
       are the referee fees($6,000) and the cost of the ice-time for utilizing both sheets of ice, 
       totaling almost $10,000. The proceeds from this event go back into the Mitchell Skating 
       & Hockey Association general fund for youth hockey in Mitchell. Over the last few years, 
       that amount has been anywhere between $6,000-$9,000.  

 
Motion: Tim Smith motioned to award $3,000. 
 
Second: Kevin McCardle seconded the motion. All voted ' Aye' and the motion passed. 
C. Lakeview Golf Course: South Dakota Golf Association Two-Man Championship 
Date: June 9th-11th, 2023; Contact: Eric Hieb; Grant Request: $1,000 

     • Eric Hieb presented the grant application to the committee. The SDGA Two-Man 
       Championship will be the sixth SDGA Championship hosted at Lakeview Golf Course in 
       the past 9 years. Most recently, Lakeview hosted the Women's Senior in 2021, 
       Men's/Women's Amateur in 2022, and this year, 2023, the Two-Man Championship. 
       Over the past few years, there have been many favorable comments from golfers about 
       the hospitality of Lakeview Golf Course and the course conditions. During an event like 
       this, Eric utilizes about 20-30 volunteers to help with the success of hosting the event. 
       Without the volunteers and additional funding, it would be more difficult to put on a class 
       A experience for the golfers and spectators. He provides breakfast (rolls/fruit/beverages) 
       for the players on both days, as well as lunches for the volunteers. He reached out to 
       Aberdeen - Moccasin Creek Country Club, which hosted the event last year, and they 
       estimated about one hundred hotel rooms (50 rooms per night) were sold during the 
       entirety of the event.   

 
Motion: Bryan Dixon motioned to award $1,000. 
 
Second: Dave Helleloid seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Doug Greenway motioned to approve the previous minutes as presented. 
 
Second: Bryan Dixon seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
4. Financial Report 
City Administrator, Stephanie Ellwein, presented the financial report as of March 6, 2023. 
Collections in February (for January records) were 1.4% down from 2022, 16.1% above 
2021, 12.1% down from 2020, 10.6% above 2019, and 4.3% above 2018. 

     • There was a brief discussion/clarification among the committee about how the financials 
       are calculated on a monthly basis. The amounts are determined by when the hotel 
       owners submit/make the payment, which, for 2022, all the numbers are correct and 
       collected for YTD. Currently, there are only two hotels that are outstanding for the 
       previous two months in 2023, but the collection amount for February is for the month of 
       January.   

 
Motion: Tim Smith motioned to approve the financial report as presented. 
 
Second: Jim Johnston seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
5. Updates/Evaluation Forms/Financials 
Aaron Hieb presented and reviewed the following Evaluation Forms with financials and SEA 
Surveys submitted from past SEA funded events with the SEA Committee. 
A. Evaluation Form w/Financials 
Raise Em Rank Bull Riding Finals (September 16th-17th, 2022) 

     • Total spectator attendance of 1,854. This count was derived from Friday and Saturday 
       ticket sales. Not all VIP Sponsor tables were counted, nor were workers/production help. 
       There were 85 bull riders. The estimation of 40? on amount of hotel/motel room nights 
       sold. He reached out to the Corn Palace Inn and Days Inn. The awarded funds ($4,500) 
       from SEA, which were used for the production of the 2022 Raise Em Rank Bull Riding 
       events. There was a net profit for the finals event in Mitchell of $1,951, which will be 
       used to grow the Raise Em Rank series and to bring it back to Mitchell for 2023. 
     • Shared event summary video: https://vimeo.com/779838795 
     • The committee had some discussion about the success of the event and reviewed the 
       Profit/Loss Statement submitted. Also, there was discussion about different ways Diilon 
       and Raise Em Rank could cover more of the expenses for the upcoming 2023 event on 
       September 8th-9th at the Corn Palace. 

 
Hoop City Basketball Classic (December 28th & 30th, 2022) 

     • Total spectator attendance of 2,006. This count was derived from the Rental & Service 
       Rate Report provided by the Corn Palace. There was no estimation of the amount of 
       hotel/motel room nights sold. The only feedback on the Evaluation Form was that Hoop 
       City paid for 50 rooms per night between Sioux Falls and Mitchell, but the majority of the 
       teams and fans reserved and paid for their own rooms. The hotels contacted were: 
       AmericInn Lodge & Suites, Comfort Inn & Suites, and Hampton Inn. The awarded funds 
       ($5,000), which were used for team travel, staff, facilities, promotion, etc. There was a 
       net loss for this event in Mitchell of $4,163.50. 
     • The committee reviewed the Profit/Loss Statement and had some discussion about the 
       travel expenses for the classic. Also, there was discussion about the impact of the event 
       being in Mitchell for all three days, instead of one day in Sioux Falls, this coming 
       December, and the importance of the addition of the youth basketball tournament to the 
       schedule of events. 

B. SEA Survey Responses 
Organization: Raise Em Rank; Main Contact: Dillon Swanson; Date Completed: 3/3/23 
 
Organization: Youth Athletic Foundation - Hoop City Classic; Main Contact: Ernie Kuyper; 
Date Completed: 3/6/23 
6. Other Items 
Aaron presented and reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee: 
A. SEA Banners on Display 
DWU Futsal Indoor Classic (February 25th-26th, 2023) 

     • SEA feather banners were set up in the Christen Center and DWU/Avera Sports 
       Complex. 

 
Buckin' Wild Ranch: Cabin Fever Auction (March 3rd-4th, 2023) 

     • SEA feather banners were set up at the Davison County Fairgrounds. Each banner was 
       set up at the entrance/exit of both complexes that were used. 

B. Discussion about SEA guidelines/policy regarding distribution of approved grant funds. 
SEA QR Code Hotel Survey: 
 
Hotel Survey 

     • Aaron will forward feedback “Why did you choose to stay at the selected hotel/motel?” 
       from the hotel survey to the respective hotel/motel. 
     • When reviewing hotel surveys, we need to be aware and take into consideration the 
       “dates of stay” to correctly account for the total rooms sold per night during the entirety 
       of the event. 
     • During the DWU Futsal Indoor Classic there were fifteen QR Codes scanned and hotel 
       surveys successfully submitted. Based on those surveys, the total hotel/motel rooms 
       sold during the event was twenty. Aaron reiterated, the QR Code/Hotel Survey is not 
       meant to be the final number, but considered as a resource the SEA funded event 
       organizer can use when determining the total hotel/motel rooms sold for the Evaluation 
       Form. Also, the hotel survey can provide beneficial information/feedback to the SEA 
       Committee and hotels throughout Mitchell about why the participant decided to stay at 
       the selected hotel. 
     • During the Buckin Wild Ranch: Cabin Fever Auction, there were zero QR 
       Codes/Surveys scanned and submitted.  

 
Event QR Code Flyer 

     • Ongoing trial and error, so far, coming to find out that a smaller QR Code (Gold or 
       White) compared to the previous one presented has a better scan success rate. 
     • Aaron shared an updated QR Code Flyer for the two upcoming events this Saturday, 
       March 18th, the Mitchell Show Choir Classic and Combat Veteran's Motorcycle 
       Association Comedy Night. 

7. Next Meeting Date: April 11th, 2023 @ 2 PM - City Hall, Council Chambers 
Mayor Everson set the next meeting date for Tuesday, April 11th, 2023 @ 2 PM at the City Hall 
- Council Chambers. 
8. Adjournment 
There being no further business to discuss. 
 
Meeting adjourned by: Mayor Everson at 2:46 PM.

Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Minutes
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
February 14, 2023
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM.
SEA Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, Kevin Nelson, Jon Hart,
Doug Greenway, Bryan Dixon, LaRee Rumbolz, Dave Helleloid, and Tim Smith.
SEA Committee members absent: Mayor Bob Everson, Cory Aadland, Emily Liedtke, and
Jim Johnston.
Others present: Stephanie Ellwein, Tiffany Batdorf, and Aaron Hieb.
2. Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Committee reviewed applications
for grant funding. The following applications were presented and considered:
A. DWU Athletics: DWU/Culver's Girls & Boys High School Basketball Classic
Date: February 10th-11th, 2023; Contact: Jon Hart & Brad Bartscher; Grant Request: $2,000
• The SEA Grant Application and other event documents were presented to the
committee via email, since the event would have been completed by the February
14th, Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee meeting. Motion, voting, and
approval were done via phone/email.
Motion: Tim Smith motioned to award $2,000.
Second: Cory Aadland seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
Abstain: Jon Hart abstained from voting.
B. Buckin' Wild Ranch: Cabin Fever Auction
Date: February 24th-25th, 2023; Contact: Ashley Coulter; Grant Request: $2,000
• Nick Coulter from Buckin' Wild Ranch traveled from Flandreau to present their grant
application to the committee. This will be the 5th Annual Buckin' Wild Ranch: Cabin
Fever Auction since Nick and his wife, Ashley, took the auction over. It is a 2-day
auction that takes place at the Davison County Fairgrounds. The main expenses that
Buckin' Wild Ranch accrue for the event are as follows: they pay for the wages of the
auctioneers and staff, as well as pay for the hotel rooms for those personnel, which
comes to be about 43 rooms for the entirety of the event.
Motion: Doug Greenway motioned to award $1,200.
Second: Tim Smith seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
• The SEA Committee requested and approved the following criteria for dispersal of
funds:
o 1/2 of the grant funds ($600) will be dispersed for the initial approval of the

--- PAGE 1 OF 7 ---


event.
o The second 1/2 of grant funds ($600) will be dispersed after the submission of
the required post-event Evaluation Form and Financials.
C. DWU Soccer: DWU 13th Annual Futsal Indoor Classic
Date: February 24th-26th, 2023; Contact: Nicolas Reinhard; Grant Request: $1,500
• Coach Nicolas Reinhard and Coach John Hakari, both first year (been with programs
for 8 months) Boy's and Girl's soccer coaches for Dakota Wesleyan University,
presented the submitted grant application. Currently, there are 60 teams registered at
$250 per team, and a team consists of 10 players. Most tournament entry fees are
much more than $250 ($25 per player). This year the team/player registration is down
almost 50% compared to previous years. This is due to the creator of the event, former
DWU Soccer coach, Clayton Glasgow, who is now the current soccer coach at
Southwest Minnesota State, hosting two of these indoor futsal events during the winter.
Most of the teams, which are from the Dakota Alliance Youth Soccer Club, that have
previously competed in this event are now participating in the events at SMSU. Coach
Reinhard and Coach Hakari need to re-establish the name and integrity of the event
and recruit some of those teams to participate in this event. Currently, teams that are
registered are from SD, ND, and MN, with a few Mitchell youth soccer teams
participating and a vast number of teams competing from Watertown. Coach Reinhard
reviewed the 2023 event budget with the committee. The $1,500 grant request would
be used to reward the student-athletes for their participation to certify themselves to be
referees for the event. The grant request is also considered, in Coach Reinhard and
Coach Hakaris' eyes, as an investment into rebuilding the event to what it once was.
The question was presented about possibly using a different date for the event. The
coaches stated that this was an inherited event date and that a possibility for future
events would be to coordinate/work together with Clayton Glasgow and make sure
these events don't overlap each other.
Motion: Bryan Dixon motioned to award $1,500.
Second: Doug Greenway seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
Abstain: Jon Hart abstained from voting.
D. Mitchell Music Boosters: Mitchell Show Choir Classic
Date: March 18th, 2023; Contact: Angella Buenzow; Grant Request: $5,000
• Matt Culhane, Mitchell Music Boosters, presented the grant application to the
committee. This year will be the 30th Anniversary of the event, taking place on
Saturday, March 18th. Currently, there are 20 teams competing in the event from IA,
NE, and even Troy, Missouri. Mitchell Show Choir does not compete in this event
because they are not eligible to win the competition. Each team brings around 100
participants, along with a couple dozen parents. Matt shared some rough numbers with
the committee. One team will most likely spend around $7,500 in just hotel revenue.
Most teams may not stay both Friday and Saturday night, the majority stay Saturday
night. The Mitchell Show Choir was just in Urbandale, Iowa and Matt booked the hotel
rooms, which consisted of 15 parent rooms, along with 26 kid rooms. The Mitchell
Music Boosters has three major fundraisers throughout a given year, which are: 1st:

--- PAGE 2 OF 7 ---


Up with Show - more of a community show, 2nd: Show Choir Classic, and 3rd: in the
spring is another community show. Matt explained the two major expenses for the
Show Choir Classic, and they are: getting quality/high caliber judges = five or six
judges costing around $5,000 (very influential, can be the determining factor in
schools/teams deciding to participate in the event), and concessions (buying the food
which they end up selling). Also, merchandise revenue for the event. Matt explained
that each year there is a "theme" to the classic and they sell "themed" hoodies, t-shirts,
and beanies.
Motion: Dave Helleloid motioned to award $3,000.
Second: Tim Smith seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Bryan Dixon motioned to approve the previous minutes as presented.
Second: Kevin Nelson seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
City Administrator, Stephanie Ellwein, presented the financial report as of February 10, 2023.
Collections in January (for December records) were 11.7% down from 2022, 14.5% above
2021, 25.8% down from 2020, 2.3% down from 2019, and 8.5% down from 2018. These
numbers are current, with only two hotels needing to report numbers.
Motion: Jon Hart motioned to approve the financial report as presented.
Second: Tim Smith seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Updates/Evaluation Forms/Financials
No evaluation forms/financials were submitted at this time.
6. Other Items
Aaron presented and reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee:
A. Event Recruitment Updates
Mitchell Technical College (MTC) Mavericks Rodeo Competition
• Aaron met with Head Coach Jimmie Nicolaus on Wednesday, January 18th, 2023 to
discuss the possibility and if there is an opportunity to host a college rodeo competition
in Mitchell. Aaron shared some of the meeting notes/details with the committee. Coach
Nicolaus is quite the guy, very knowledgeable and ambitious. Mitchell Technical
College Mavericks Rodeo Team is a part of the National Intercollegiate Rodeo
Association (NIRA). Within that association, MTC belongs to the Great Plains Region,
which consists of 15 schools from SD, IA, ND, NE, and WI. Out of these 15 schools, 10
schools are on the annual rotation for hosting a qualifying rodeo for which you are able
to receive points towards the national competition. Coach Nicolaus and Aaron
discussed that it would be pointless to create an 11th rodeo, since it wouldn't be
eligible to receive national competition qualifying points. For Mitchell/MTC to even
consider hosting a college rodeo competition, one of the current ten schools would
need to remove themselves from the annual rotation. If an opportunity did arise, MTC
would be interested in pursuing a competition for the spring, sometime in April. Aaron
gave a brief breakdown of the competition. There are around 270 participants that
compete either as a team or individual. Currently, MTC has 21 members on their rodeo

--- PAGE 3 OF 7 ---


team. An estimate, but around 70% of the teams/contestants would stay Thursday
through Sunday. The minimum budget ballpark to consider hosting a college rodeo
competition is $30,000.
Hoop City Classic 2023
• Doug Greenway shared the news about Ernie Kuyper and the Hoop City Classic,
bringing all three days (Thursday 28th, Friday 29th, and Saturday 30th) of the event to
Mitchell at the end of December 2023. Another aspect of the Hoop City Classic would
be the Youth Tournament as well. There would be somewhere around 70-80 youth
teams participating as well.

DWU/Culver's High School Basketball Classic vs. SDHSSA State Gymnastics
• Discussion was had regarding hosting the DWU/Culver's High School Basketball
Classic compared to the SDHSAA State Gymnastics.
o DWU/Culver's HS Basketball Classic is a major fundraiser for DWU and, from
an event standpoint, the Corn Palace does not want to lose the DWU/Culver's
Classic.
o The SDHSAA has expressed interest in bringing the State Gymnastics back to
Mitchell and the Corn Palace. There has been no signed agreement with the
SDHSAA yet.
o DWU/Culver's HS Basketball Classic is a much better event to host from a Corn

o From a hotel perspective, (20-24 teams) SDHSAA State Gymnastics does

C. Discussion about SEA guidelines/policy regarding distribution of approved grant
funds.
• QR Code image(s)

--- PAGE 5 OF 7 ---


• Hotel Survey
• Event QR Code Template
• Aaron continued discussion with the SEA Committee about the best method to track
hotel rooms sold during SEA event. Last meeting, Aaron thought there was a sense of
concern or hesitancy about the 'estimate' of hotel rooms on a grant application and/or
evaluation form when using that number to determine a funding amount. Aaron
presented a QR Code to the committee in three different colors: Gold, White, and
Burgundy. The gold and white QR Codes have the most successful, best scan rate
compared to the burgundy. Once the QR Code is scanned, it will take the participant to
the "landing page", which is a Hotel Survey on the City of Mitchell website. A question
was asked if these QR Codes would be distributed to all hotels or if this is just an event
specific distribution. For the time being, this QR Code will be included in the approval
email along with the Award Letter. There will be instructions about the use and
expectations of the QR Code for the Event Organizer/Main Contact. The requirement
for an approved event will still be to submit a post-event Evaluation Form with
Financials following the completion of the event. The QR Code is meant to have the
purpose of being a tool to assist the Event Organizer in determining as accurately the
number as possible for the total hotel/motel rooms sold for the entirety of the event.
Another question expressed by the committee was who would be filling out or expected
to fill out the QR Code... There is concern that there will be duplicate information when
multiple family members scan the code and participate, which will cause the
hotel/motel room numbers sold to be skewed. For the majority of SEA funded events,
the Event Organizer will include or distribute the QR Code to the coach of each team or
the individuals competing in the respective SEA funded event. It was expressed that
most events nowadays have a designated worker/volunteer that is the "hotel person"
and will be in charge of distributing/completing the hotel survey in a successful manner.
Going a step further, prior to each SEA funded event, Aaron will take multiple copies of
the QR Code Event Flyer to the venue and/or facility and post the QR Codes in
accessible locations for fans and spectators to scan as well. This will be in the hopes of
gathering information from the fans/spectators attending the event as well as the
athletes/participants in the event. Overall, Aaron expressed that the goal was not to
create more work for the Event Organizer or not intended to complicate and/or burden
an organization or event with completing a SEA Grant Application because of the
expected paperwork required after grant approval.
