documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Minutes  
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                     April 11, 2023 
                                            
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM. 
 
SEA Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, Kevin Nelson, Jon Hart, 
Doug Greenway, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, and Jim Johnston. 
 
SEA Committee members absent: Mayor Bob Everson, Cory Aadland, Bryan Dixon, and Tim 
Smith. 
 
Others present: Stephanie Ellwein, City Administrator and Tiffany Batdorf. 
2. Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Committee reviewed applications 
for grant funding. The following applications were presented and considered: 
A. Mitchell School District: SoDak 16 Girls & Boys Basketball 
Date: March 2nd & 7th, 2023; Contact: Cory Aadland; Grant Request: $1,750 

     • Doug Greenway shared the grant application with the SEA Committee. The SEA Grant 
       Application for this event is submitted after the fact because of the quick and short 
       notice process it takes to be awarded host site for the SoDak 16 games. Cory and the 
       Corn Palace were notified 4 days prior to the event, which determines host sites on 
       location and neutral site availability based on the teams that qualify. These were two of 
       the biggest games the Corn Palace hosted during the season: the girls' game brought 
       1,700 in attendance and the boys' game was around 1,550.  

 
Motion: Motion was made by Jim Johnston to award $1,750, and seconded by Jon Hart.  All 
members voted "aye" and the motion passed. 
B. Mitchell Baseball: Mitchell Baseball Tournaments 
Date: May, June, & July, 2023; Contact: Jason Christensen; Grant Request: $6,000 

     • Jason Christensen from Mitchell Baseball presented the application to the committee. 
       They will be hosting four tournaments.  The tournaments will be held May 6 (Early Bird), 
       June 2-3 (Teener Tournament), June 17-18 (Harve/Bryan Memorial), and July 14-16 
       (State 'A' Youth).  The tournament scheduled for July 14-16 is a youth state tournament 
       and Mitchell Baseball anticipated this will be a big tournament.  They anticipate that they 
       will continue to host this tournament every 2-4 years.  Jason also stated that for the one-
       day tournament, they schedule the out-of-town teams to play first to encourage 
       overnight stays. Requested grant funds will be used to pay for umpires, volunteers, and 
       hospitality. The proceeds from the tournaments go back into the program and are put 
       towards projects to enhance the baseball fields and complex. 

 
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to award $6,000, and seconded by Jon Hart.  All 
members voted "aye" and the motion passed. 
C. Corn Palace Cornhole: ACL Regional #15 3rd Annual Corn Palace Cornhole 
Tournament 
Date: May 12th-14th, 2023; Contact: Tyler Earls; Grant Request: $5,000 

     • Tyler Earls presented the application for the 3rd Annual Corn Palace Cornhole 
       tournament to be held May 12-14.  The grant dollars would be used for prize money for 
       the players.  Tyler estimated that 30-100 rooms were used in 2022, and most stayed at 
       the Kelly Inn.   

 
Motion:  Motion was made by Kevin McCardle to award $1,000, seconded by Jill Larson.  Eight 
members voted "aye" and one member voted "nay".  Motion carried. 
D. Kiwanis Club of Mitchell: Kiwanis Youth Baseball Tournament 
Date: May 13th, 2023; Contact: Cory Marek; Grant Request: $1,500, $500 

     • Cory Marek presented the grant application to the committee for the Kiwanis Youth 
       Baseball Tournament.  Cory requested that the request be amended from $1,500 to 
       $500, since the tournament was moved to a one-day event to be held on Saturday, May 
       13.  This is a change in date for the tournament, since the attendance is down from 
       previous years. However, they expect that numbers will increase as the date change is 
       known in future years.  Currently, they have 10 teams.  The grant funds will be used for 
       trophies & umpires. 

 
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to award $500, seconded by Dave Helloloid.  All 
members voted "aye".  Motion carried. 
E. Mitchell Area Community Triathlon: MAC Triathlon 
Date: June 9th-10th, 2023; Contact: Terasa Gillen; Grant Request: $3,000 

     • Emily Hohn presented the grant application to the committee.  The MAC triathlon is 
       going to be held June 10 with registration and packet pick-up, Friday night, June 9.  The 
       grant funds would be used to cover the timing equipment costs of $2,200.  They expect 
       50-70 participants.  Numbers for the event increased when the swimming portion of the 
       event was moved from Lake Mitchell to the Mitchell Aquatic Center outdoor pool. 
        Committee members asked about hotel stays, and the applicant stated that some do 
       stay, but also lots camp or just drive out early.  Committee members encouraged the 
       organizers to suggest the Lake Mitchell Campground since the campground contributes 
       to the BID.  They stated that they do have a good list of volunteers, but they can always 
       use more volunteers to help with turns and intersections, as well as counting laps in the 
       pool.  Madison is not doing their triathlon, so they expect to see some people come to 
       Mitchell that would normally go to Madison. 

 
Motion: Motion was made by Kevin Nelson to award $2,200 to cover the cost of the timing 
equipment, seconded by Jon Hart.  All members voted "aye".  Motion carried. 
F. Department of South Dakota Veterans of Foreign Wars: 93rd Annual VFW State 
Convention 
Date: June 15th-18th, 2023; Contact: Anna Arnold / Dr. Marty Christensen; Grant Request: 
$3,130 
     • Dr. Marty Christensen presented the grant application for the VFW State Convention. 
       Last year, when they hosted the convention, they utilized 78 hotel rooms, and anticipate 
       a similar number in 2023. They will be hosting the convention back again in 3 or 4 years. 
       He is also working on bringing other conventions as well.  They would like assistance 
       from additional volunteers to help with serving the meals, and drivers of vehicles.  They 
       said any volunteer help would be appreciated.  Grant funds would be used to cover the 
       rental cost of the facility for the convention. 

 
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to award $3,130, seconded by Kevin McCardle. 
Eight members voted "aye" and one member voted "Nay".  Motion carried. 
G. Gentle Spirit Horses Rescue: Dakota Showdown Horse Trainer Challenge 
Date: August 12th-13th, 2023; Contact: Tiffany Ring; Grant Request: $3,000 

     • Tiffany Ring presented the grant application to the committee.  This is the second year 
       of the event, but the first year in Mitchell.  Last year they held the event in Scotland, as a 
       "test run".  They are hoping for between 300-500 people to attend the event.  They 
       currently have 22 rescued horses that will be going to trainers that will be showcased 
       during the event (last year they had 1 pony with a trainer at the Scotland event).  They 
       are working with Back 40 for some additional events tied to the Trainer Challenge. 

 
Motion: Motion was made by Kevin Nelson to award $1,000, and seconded by Jill Larson.  All 
members voted "aye".  Motion carried.  Committee members discussed that they appreciated 
that it is a new event being moved to Mitchell, but due to limited funds available, the amount 
awarded was $1,000. 
H. The 301 Rodz: OutKasts Car Show 
Date: September 22nd-24th, 2023; Contact: KayLynn Bren; Grant Request: $2,500 

     • Jerry Wright presented the grant application to the committee.  Registration and cruise 
       night on Friday night, car show Saturday, and donuts/coffee on Sunday morning. Last 
       year's event brought 180 registered cars, along with about 36 hotel rooms, filling the 
       Siesta and Coachlight Motels. Received much praise and appreciation from participants 
       by sending out "Thank-You" cards to everyone. The grant amount requested would be 
       utilized for advertising and reaching other participants in other states by putting ads in 
       different car magazines.  

 
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to award $1,500, and seconded by Jon Hart.  All 
members voted "aye".  Committee members noted that due to limited funds, the grant was 
reduced. 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Jon Hart to approve the previous minutes as presented, 
seconded by LaRee Rumbolz.  All members voted "aye".  Motion carried. 
4. Financial Report 
Committee members reviewed the financial report as of April 6th, 2023. Collections in March 
(for February records) were: 8.9% down from 2022, 15.4% above 2021, 15.5% down from 
2020, 3.5% above 2019, and 1.9% down from 2018. 
 
Motion: Motion was made by Jon Hart to approve the financial report as presented, seconded 
by Jill Larson.  All members voted "aye".  Motion carried. 
5. Updates/Evaluation Forms/Financials 
The following items were not reviewed because of lack of time.  The SEA Committee went into 
Executive Session to discuss and vote on submitted grant applications. 
A. Evaluation Form w/Financials 
Palace Ice Festival (January 13th-14th, 2023) 
 
Larry Hauser Adult/JR Doubles Bowling Tournament (March 25th, 2023) 
6. Other Items 
The following items were not reviewed because of lack of time. Item B. will be added to and 
discussion continued at the May SEA Committee meeting.  The SEA Committee went into 
Executive Session to discuss and vote on submitted grant applications. 
A. SEA Banners on Display 
Show Choir Classic (March 18th, 2023) 

     • SEA feather banner was set up at the Performing Arts Center in the west entrance (2) 
       main hallway/Box Office area. 

 
Combat Veteran's Motorcycle Association Comedy Night (March 18th, 2023) 

     • SEA feather banner was set up at the Highland Conference Center just inside the main 
       entrance/exit doors of the conference center. 

 
Larry Hauser Adult/JR Doubles Bowling Tournament (March 25h, 2023) 

     • SEA feather banners were set up at The Village Bowl next to Lane #1, where the finals 
       took place for the doubles tournament. 

 
Bartholow Brothers Youth Trap Shooting Clinic (April 1st-2nd, 2023) 

     • SEA feather banners were set up at The Davison County 4H Building in the Meeting 
       Room Complex, where they conducted each morning's presentation before they began 
       their outdoor clinic. 

B. Discussion about SEA guidelines/policy regarding distribution of approved grant funds. 
SEA QR Code 

     • A new QR Code was created from a different online QR Code Generator, Beaconstac. 
     • Matt Culhane and Show Choir Classic provided feedback that the current QR Code did 
       not consistently scan successfully with iPhones. 

7. Next Meeting Date 
May 9th, 2023 @ 2 PM - City Hall, Council Chambers 
8. Adjournment 
There being no further business to discuss. 
 
Meeting adjourned by: Kevin McCardle at 4 PM.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.

From: 	noreply@civicplus.com
To: 	Aaron Hieb
Subject: 	Online Form Submittal: Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
Date: 	Tuesday, March 21, 2023 7:52:39 PM
Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

--- PAGE 1 OF 7 ---

Gentle Spirit Horses is a rescue and sanctuary for horses based
out of Scotland, South Dakota. Our mission is to provide
assistance to neglected, abused and unwanted horses, and
through outreach and education, promote responsible horse
ownership.

How will the requested
grant amount be used?
We will use the grant as directed. I noticed the grant information
specified marketing materials so likely for advertising including
creation of a video that can be used on social media and regular
media to promote the event, printing of the event program,
running paid ads both on digital platforms and in
newspapers/magazines throughout the state, and other
marketing costs.
How will
proceeds/profit from
the event be used?
Proceeds from the event will first be split between trainers and
the non-profit as per the agreement - trainers receive 50% of the
adoption fee of the horse. The rescue will use the other 50% to
start planning next year's event, help provide care for the horses
at the rescue's facility, and to expand the rescue's facility to
provide assistance to more horses.

Comments 	Last year was our first year and was very much a "if we're going
to do this, let's just do this." We kept it very small and part of our
annual Open House in Scotland, South Dakota, just basically as
a "dress rehearsal". We always planned on growing and moving
to a larger community but for our first year we had minimal
expenses and a smaller projected audience. We had only 7
horses and trainers and they only worked together for 60 days.
This year we've taken the leap and moved the event to Mitchell
and also implemented a much larger expectation. It is now a
stand alone event and will be held over 2 days. We are sharing
the arena with Carrie Dieters' local barrel series to encourage
increased attendance, are adding a vendor area and tack swap,
and adding a gala type dinner with exclusive access to the
trainer's, which will be held at The Back 40. We intend to open
the dinner to the public with a band that night, and nearly
everyone who comes to that (we are planning on 120 guests,
plus children) will get a hotel room, as will all the trainers. We are
planning for between 18-24 horses and I currently have
applications from 15 trainers ranging from Minnesota to Rapid
City to North Dakota.
Note on attachments: We have not yet finalized the event flyer
for the August event. I have attached last year's program and our
sponsorship flyer and can provide the event flyer when it's
finalized.
(Section Break)
Event Details
Briefly describe the
purpose of your
organization; what your
organization provides
to the community; the
group of people you
are targeting to bring
into the community with
Gentle Spirit Horses Rescue is South Dakota's largest and most
active 501(c)3 non-profit rescue, in a state where there are only a
few horse rescues. Because our ability to assist and improve
horse welfare is limited, we seek to educate the public and
develop partnerships with other professionals through our
various programs. The Dakota Showdown Horse Trainer
Challenge is one of those programs that seeks to provide rescue
horses with training and find them new homes, as well as feature

--- PAGE 4 OF 7 ---


this event? the talented trainers across South Dakota and the neighboring
states. We will be targeting horsemen and women, trainers,
families, potential adopters, and others who just enjoy and
respect good horsemanship.
Describe your event.
Be sure to include who,
what, where, when,
and how activities will
take place.
The Dakota Showdown Horse Trainer Challenge is a competition
in which volunteer foster homes and professional trainers work
with a Gentle Spirit Horses Rescue horse for a minimum of 100
days.
The purpose of the Dakota Showdown Horse Trainer Challenge
is:
To show the public that rescued horses and other equines can
be useful, trainable and enjoyable equine partners.
To provide training and adoption opportunities for rescued
horses.
To provide a fun, competitive venue for Professional and
Amateur trainers to display their horsemanship skills.
While trainers are already applying and will be taking their horses
in starting the end of April, the actual Dakota Showdown event is
August 12-13 and will be held at the Sportsman's Horse Arena in
Mitchell. The event schedule includes:
August 12 - Trainers Arrive, Basic Skills tests; Adoption
appointments; vendor setup, and Carrie Dieters' barrel race
series. Evening includes a gala type dinner at The Back 40 which
will open to the public around 9pm for a live band.
August 13 - the big event! Vendor fair and tack booth all day, and
the horse and trainer pairs will present a freestyle exhibition to
the public. The horses will be available for adoption to approved
adopters through an auction process and a winner will be
crowned!
Explain how your event
benefits the community
and your organization.
Specify whether your
event is a first-time
event, annual event, or
an on-going program.
While this is technically our second year, it's very much a "first-
time event" as we are dramatically increasing the events, budget,
and expected trainers and attendance. A big part of that is
moving it to Mitchell, which we believe to be the perfect location
since the trainers are coming from all over the state. The Mitchell
community provides easy access from the interstate, plenty of
hotel and restaurant choices encouraging people to come for the
whole weekend, and a supportive, horse loving community to
enjoy and be proud of the event.
As for our mission, the event benefits horses and horse lovers in
many ways. Every horse that receives training has a better
chance at a good home, and people are able to benefit from the
training. Trainers will be able to show their talents and market
their services, and the addition of a vendor area will hopefully

--- PAGE 5 OF 7 ---


bring in sales and marketing for businesses. With limited
resources in the rescues participating, every horse that finds a
home will help several others by making space at the rescues'
facilities and allowing them to assist more. Currently, the rescues
involved focus on assisting law enforcement in neglect situations
and South Dakota families in crisis, so people and horses truly in
need will greatly benefit.
What geographic areas
are you bringing event
participants from?
Indicate geographic
areas you are
marketing for visitor
attraction to your event.
Throughout South Dakota, but specifically the geographic
locations of the rescues - Yankton/Wagner and Brookings, as
well as Sioux Falls, Mitchell, Chamberlain, Pierre and Rapid City.
All trainers will be encouraged to provide ongoing social media
updates and work with their own areas to encourage people to
attend and adopt, and also seeking out sponsors.
What are the specific
goals for this event?
To show the public that rescued horses and other equines can
be useful, trainable and enjoyable equine partners.
To provide training and adoption opportunities for rescued
horses.
To provide a fun, competitive venue for Professional and
Amateur trainers to display their horsemanship skills.
Our specific number related goals are:
18-24 horse and trainer pairs
120-150 Trainer's dinner attendees
10 vendor booths
12 adoptions within 30 days of the event
200 attendees outside of trainers and volunteers
Revenue goals are to break even since this is a first year of
several of the event items and increased costs, with the hope
that we would be able to do better than that and be able to build
capacity and get ahead for the following year.
Explain how your grant
request would be used
to promote tourism in
Mitchell? Note the
resulting impact of your
event if the request for
funding were denied.
Mitchell will be heavily featured in all of our marketing including
our reasons for coming, and our goal is to make this an annual
event and for it to continue to grow. It is modeled after the
Appalachian Horse Trainer Challenge, which key members of the
planning committee attended and volunteered at as a final step in
preparing to launch the Dakota Showdown. A quote from their
materials indicates that "in 2021, 2,500 attended, 40 horses were
adopted through the whole event, 75 horses were trained,
$350,000 worth of training was donated and over a MILLION
dollars was put into the local economy!" 2021 was their fourth
year holding their trainer's challenge, and we are hoping for
similar growth in South Dakota - and intend to keep it in Mitchell
if we are supported and wanted!
The impact if denied would likely be less ability to market as we

--- PAGE 6 OF 7 ---


have to focus on sponsorships for actual costs first, and having
to stick to some of the more affordable methods like social media
and press releases. Less marketing would mean less attendance
and slower growth, which would negatively impact both Mitchell
tourism and the Dakota Showdown.
If this is a new event,
what is the estimated
hotel/motel rooms sold
during this event? How
are you able to
estimate this number?
I would say a low estimate would be about 40-50 just by counting
the trainers and the volunteers that would be coming from
various locations. With good marketing, that could be much
higher with out of town visitors.

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Minutes
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
March 14, 2023
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Mayor Everson at 2:01 PM.
SEA Committee members present: Mayor Bob Everson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin Nelson,
Doug Greenway, Bryan Dixon, LaRee Rumbolz, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston.
SEA Committee members absent: Jill Larson, Cory Aadland, Jon Hart, and Emily Liedtke
Others present: Stephanie Ellwein and Aaron Hieb
2. Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Committee reviewed applications
for grant funding. The following applications were presented and considered:
A. Mitchell Area Youth Trapshooters: Bartholow Brothers Youth Trapshooting Clinic
Date: April 1st-2nd, 2023; Contact: Jerry Opbroek; Grant Request: $1,735
• Jerry Opbroek presented the grant application to the committee. Matt and Foster
Bartholow are nationally recognized trap shooters and are considered to be the best.
The trap shooting clinic is free of charge and will take place at the Davison County
Fairgrounds as well as the Mitchell Trap Club during the shooting portion of the clinic.
This event/clinic has been in Pierre for the last four years. Jerry expressed that being in
Pierre, the participants were mostly west river South Dakota youth. Now that the
event/clinic will be hosted in Mitchell, they will be able to reach and provide for a
different set of kids, from east river South Dakota. Jerry's hope is that Mitchell will be the
host site for this event/clinic on an annual basis or at least share the hosting duties with
Pierre. They already have participants registered from Custer, Winner, and Yankton.
Jerry praised the Bartholow brothers teaching/coaching skills during the clinic and that
they provide detailed expertise to the youth participants.
Motion: Doug Greenway motioned to award $1,735.
Second: Jim Johnston seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
Abstain: Bryan Dixon abstained from voting, since he has rooms for participants currently
booked at the Coachlight Motel for this event.
B. Mitchell Skating & Hockey Association: Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament
Date: April 14th-16th, 2023; Contact: Stacy Murtha; Grant Request: $3,000
• Stacy Murtha presented the grant application to the committee. This is the 12th annual
Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament and the biggest in the area. The tournament fills
up fast. Basically, six days it took Stacy to fill the tournament. Currently, it is full with
twenty-one, possibly twenty-two, 14 player teams. Roughly three hundred adult hockey
players will take part in this tournament along with their families, which begins Friday,
April 14th at Noon and runs through Sunday, April 16th, and will wrap up around 4 or 5

--- PAGE 1 OF 5 ---


pm on Sunday. There will be thirty-nine games during the three days. They have teams
from North Dakota, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Iowa, and South Dakota. Sioux Falls is
chomping at the bit to be able to host this tournament, but the response that he gets
from the five Sioux Falls teams that compete in the Mitchell tournament is that Sioux
Falls has no one to organize the event. The two biggest expenses for this tournament
are the referee fees($6,000) and the cost of the ice-time for utilizing both sheets of ice,
totaling almost $10,000. The proceeds from this event go back into the Mitchell Skating
& Hockey Association general fund for youth hockey in Mitchell. Over the last few years,
that amount has been anywhere between $6,000-$9,000.
Motion: Tim Smith motioned to award $3,000.
Second: Kevin McCardle seconded the motion. All voted ' Aye' and the motion passed.
C. Lakeview Golf Course: South Dakota Golf Association Two-Man Championship
Date: June 9th-11th, 2023; Contact: Eric Hieb; Grant Request: $1,000
• Eric Hieb presented the grant application to the committee. The SDGA Two-Man
Championship will be the sixth SDGA Championship hosted at Lakeview Golf Course in
the past 9 years. Most recently, Lakeview hosted the Women's Senior in 2021,
Men's/Women's Amateur in 2022, and this year, 2023, the Two-Man Championship.
Over the past few years, there have been many favorable comments from golfers about
the hospitality of Lakeview Golf Course and the course conditions. During an event like
this, Eric utilizes about 20-30 volunteers to help with the success of hosting the event.
Without the volunteers and additional funding, it would be more difficult to put on a class
A experience for the golfers and spectators. He provides breakfast (rolls/fruit/beverages)
for the players on both days, as well as lunches for the volunteers. He reached out to
Aberdeen - Moccasin Creek Country Club, which hosted the event last year, and they
estimated about one hundred hotel rooms (50 rooms per night) were sold during the
entirety of the event.
Motion: Bryan Dixon motioned to award $1,000.
Second: Dave Helleloid seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Doug Greenway motioned to approve the previous minutes as presented.
Second: Bryan Dixon seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
City Administrator, Stephanie Ellwein, presented the financial report as of March 6, 2023.
Collections in February (for January records) were 1.4% down from 2022, 16.1% above
2021, 12.1% down from 2020, 10.6% above 2019, and 4.3% above 2018.
• There was a brief discussion/clarification among the committee about how the financials
are calculated on a monthly basis. The amounts are determined by when the hotel
owners submit/make the payment, which, for 2022, all the numbers are correct and
collected for YTD. Currently, there are only two hotels that are outstanding for the
previous two months in 2023, but the collection amount for February is for the month of

--- PAGE 2 OF 5 ---


January.
Motion: Tim Smith motioned to approve the financial report as presented.
Second: Jim Johnston seconded the motion. All voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Updates/Evaluation Forms/Financials
Aaron Hieb presented and reviewed the following Evaluation Forms with financials and SEA
Surveys submitted from past SEA funded events with the SEA Committee.
A. Evaluation Form w/Financials
Raise Em Rank Bull Riding Finals (September 16th-17th, 2022)
• Total spectator attendance of 1,854. This count was derived from Friday and Saturday
ticket sales. Not all VIP Sponsor tables were counted, nor were workers/production help.
There were 85 bull riders. The estimation of 40? on amount of hotel/motel room nights
sold. He reached out to the Corn Palace Inn and Days Inn. The awarded funds ($4,500)
from SEA, which were used for the production of the 2022 Raise Em Rank Bull Riding
events. There was a net profit for the finals event in Mitchell of $1,951, which will be
used to grow the Raise Em Rank series and to bring it back to Mitchell for 2023.
• Shared event summary video: https://vimeo.com/779838795
• The committee had some discussion about the success of the event and reviewed the
Profit/Loss Statement submitted. Also, there was discussion about different ways Diilon
and Raise Em Rank could cover more of the expenses for the upcoming 2023 event on
September 8th-9th at the Corn Palace.
Hoop City Basketball Classic (December 28th & 30th, 2022)
• Total spectator attendance of 2,006. This count was derived from the Rental & Service
Rate Report provided by the Corn Palace. There was no estimation of the amount of
hotel/motel room nights sold. The only feedback on the Evaluation Form was that Hoop
City paid for 50 rooms per night between Sioux Falls and Mitchell, but the majority of the
teams and fans reserved and paid for their own rooms. The hotels contacted were:
AmericInn Lodge & Suites, Comfort Inn & Suites, and Hampton Inn. The awarded funds
($5,000), which were used for team travel, staff, facilities, promotion, etc. There was a
net loss for this event in Mitchell of $4,163.50.
• The committee reviewed the Profit/Loss Statement and had some discussion about the
travel expenses for the classic. Also, there was discussion about the impact of the event
being in Mitchell for all three days, instead of one day in Sioux Falls, this coming
December, and the importance of the addition of the youth basketball tournament to the
schedule of events.
B. SEA Survey Responses
Organization: Raise Em Rank; Main Contact: Dillon Swanson; Date Completed: 3/3/23
Organization: Youth Athletic Foundation - Hoop City Classic; Main Contact: Ernie Kuyper;
Date Completed: 3/6/23
6. Other Items

--- PAGE 3 OF 5 ---


Aaron presented and reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee:
A. SEA Banners on Display
DWU Futsal Indoor Classic (February 25th-26th, 2023)
• SEA feather banners were set up in the Christen Center and DWU/Avera Sports
Complex.
Buckin' Wild Ranch: Cabin Fever Auction (March 3rd-4th, 2023)
• SEA feather banners were set up at the Davison County Fairgrounds. Each banner was
set up at the entrance/exit of both complexes that were used.
B. Discussion about SEA guidelines/policy regarding distribution of approved grant funds.
SEA QR Code Hotel Survey:
Hotel Survey
• Aaron will forward feedback “Why did you choose to stay at the selected hotel/motel?”
from the hotel survey to the respective hotel/motel.
• When reviewing hotel surveys, we need to be aware and take into consideration the
“dates of stay” to correctly account for the total rooms sold per night during the entirety
of the event.
• During the DWU Futsal Indoor Classic there were fifteen QR Codes scanned and hotel
surveys successfully submitted. Based on those surveys, the total hotel/motel rooms
sold during the event was twenty. Aaron reiterated, the QR Code/Hotel Survey is not
meant to be the final number, but considered as a resource the SEA funded event
organizer can use when determining the total hotel/motel rooms sold for the Evaluation
Form. Also, the hotel survey can provide beneficial information/feedback to the SEA
Committee and hotels throughout Mitchell about why the participant decided to stay at
the selected hotel.
• During the Buckin Wild Ranch: Cabin Fever Auction, there were zero QR
Codes/Surveys scanned and submitted.
Event QR Code Flyer
• Ongoing trial and error, so far, coming to find out that a smaller QR Code (Gold or
White) compared to the previous one presented has a better scan success rate.
• Aaron shared an updated QR Code Flyer for the two upcoming events this Saturday,
March 18th, the Mitchell Show Choir Classic and Combat Veteran's Motorcycle
Association Comedy Night.
7. Next Meeting Date: April 11th, 2023 @ 2 PM - City Hall, Council Chambers
Mayor Everson set the next meeting date for Tuesday, April 11th, 2023 @ 2 PM at the City Hall
- Council Chambers.
8. Adjournment
There being no further business to discuss.

--- PAGE 4 OF 5 ---


Meeting adjourned by: Mayor Everson at 2:46 PM.

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Minutes  
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                      May 9, 2023 
                                            
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM. 
 
SEA Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, Kevin Nelson, Doug 
Greenway, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston. 
 
SEA Committee members absent: Mayor Everson, Cory Aadland, Jon Hart, Bryan Dixon, and 
LaRee Rumbolz. 
 
Others present: Tiffany Batdorf, Stephanie Ellwein, and Aaron Hieb. 
2. Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Committee reviewed applications 
for grant funding. The following applications were presented and considered: 
A. SD United States Bowling Congress Jamboree 
Date: June 8th-10th, 2023; Contact: Jeff Vander Wilt; Grant Request: $5,000 

     • Jeff Vander Wilt, President of South Dakota USBC, presented the application to the 
       committee. The SD USBC Jamboree will take place from Friday, June 9th through 
       Saturday, June 10th. The host city and host site for the Jamboree is on a rotating 
       schedule; Rapid City hosted in 2021 and Pierre hosted in 2022. Friday's events will take 
       place at the Village Bowl, and include live interaction with Pro Bowler, Carolyn Dorin-
       Ballard and fundraisers throughout the evening. Saturday's events will be hosted at the 
       Highland Conference Center with an awards banquet during the afternoon and Hall of 
       Fame Honoree Banquet in the evening. Jeff estimates between 350-400 people will be 
       in Mitchell over the two days. The requested grant funds would be used to offset the 
       meal costs and hotel room costs for the attendees. This event is a great opportunity to 
       promote the remodeled Village Bowl and its great facilities, along with the Highland 
       Conference Center to all the attendees. Profits/proceeds from the event are used 
       towards the SD USBC youth bowler scholarship fund.  

 
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to award $3,000, and seconded by Doug 
Greenway. All members voted "Aye" and the motion passed. 
B. Ron's Bike Shop: Beers & Gears Mountain Bike Race 
Date: June 23rd-24th, 2023; Contact: Cody Denne; Grant Request: $2,000 

     • Cody Denne from the Palace City Pedalers/Ron's Bike Shop presented the application 
       to the committee. The 2nd annual Beers & Gears Mountain Bike Race will take place on 
       Saturday, June 24th, starting at 9 AM and utilizing the Lake Mitchell North Trail Loop, 
       which includes: Sandy Beach, Harmon Boat Landing, and Camp Arroyo. Friday evening, 
       June 23rd, is packet pick-up at Blarneys, along with a social and gathering. The grant 
       amount requested would be utilized to pay for the timing system that is required to host 
       a successful event. Currently, they have 25 riders registered. Last year, there were 45 
       riders with about 100 participants total between riders, staff, volunteers, etc. They added 
       a new feature this year. For those that don't have a mountain bike, they have bike 
       rentals available for those that would like to participate. Most mountain bikers prefer to 
       stay at campgrounds, but they do have a block of room at the Comfort Inn, and will 
       promote/encourage bikers to stay at the Lake Mitchell Campground, since the BID #2 
       Hotel Tax is collected there. The purpose of the event is to promote the hard work, 
       dedication, and beauty of the Lake Mitchell Trail System. 
     • Discussion about timing system cost and if there is a difference between timing systems 
       that other events have requested SEA grant funding for. 
     • Discussion about the interest and possibility of hosting a Fat Bike Race in the winter on 
       the Lake Mitchell Trails. 

 
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to award $2,000, and seconded by Jim 
Johnston. All voted "Aye" and the motion passed. 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Jim Johnston to approve the previous minutes as presented, 
seconded by Emily Liedtke. All members voted "Aye" and the motion passed. 
4. Financial Report 
Stephanie Ellwein and Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of May 4th, 2023. 
Collections in April (for March records) were: down 3.9% from 2022, up 16.4% from 2021, up 
3.6% from 2020, up 9.1% from 2019, and up 0.5% from 2018. A Fund Balance of $80,270.02, 
with eight committed funding checks that will be cut next Monday, May 15th, after the City 
Council meeting, leaving an Available Fund Balance of $16,690.02.  
 
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the financial report as presented, seconded 
by Doug Greenway. All members voted "Aye" and the motion passed. 
5. Updates/Evaluation Forms/Financials 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms with financials and SEA Survey that were 
submitted from past SEA funded events with the SEA Committee. 
A. Evaluation Form w/Financials 
Girl's & Boy's Hanson Classic (January 14th & January 21st, 2023) 

     • Total spectator attendance for the entire event was 3,532 (Girls = 1,586 & Boys = 
       1,946). This count was derived from the Corn Palace Service and Rental Rate sheet. 
       Information was not available regarding the number of hotel/motel rooms sold for the 
       classics. The awarded funds ($2,000) were used for hospitality and workers. All 
       remaining money, if any, would go towards other expenses... Officials, score table, shot 
       clock, announcers, and back door monitors. Corn Palace Rental and Service reports 
       were submitted, which include revenue made from the ticket sales/admission: Girls = 
       $8,981.60 & Boys = $13,693.50. Aaron shared the Thank You card sent by Jim Bridge 
       to the SEA Committee. 

 
DWU/Culver's Girl's & Boy's HS Basketball Classic (February 10th-11th, 2023) 

     • Total spectator attendance for the entire event was 4,500+. This count was derived from 
       the tickets sold and door counters. Approximately 20 rooms were sold for the event (5-7 
       teams stayed at least one night with a minimum of three rooms per team). The hotels 
       contacted were the Comfort Inn & Suites, Days Inns, and Holiday Inn. The awarded 
       funds ($2,000) were used to offset expenses. Profit of $8,666, this was a fundraiser for 
       our men's and women's basketball programs. The profit will be put into our fundraising 
       accounts to enhance the experience for our student-athletes. 

 
DWU 13th Annual Indoor Futsal Classic (February 24th-26th, 2023) 

     • Total spectator attendance for the entire event was between 300-400. This count was 
       derived from the door counts. The QR Code Hotel Survey indicated 20 hotel/motel 
       rooms were sold, plus the coaches indicated up to 30 rooms, so approximately 50 
       rooms, give or take, were sold for the event. No hotels were contacted, only coaches. 
       The awarded funds (1,500) were used to cover the refereeing expenses that we were 
       able to drastically lower this year due to the help of our student-athletes. In comparison 
       to 2022 ($3,423.91), they saved $1,637.46 in referee expenses for the 2023 ($1,786.45) 
       event. Profit of $12,876.28 was split between the men's and women's soccer teams as a 
       fundraiser. 

 
Bartholow Brothers Trapshooting Clinic (March 31st, April 1st-2nd, 2023) 

     • Total spectator attendance for the entire event was approximately 400 +. This count was 
       derived from visual observation and the seating capacity of the meeting room. 50-60 
       hotel/motel rooms were sold during the event. "I really don't have an accurate number. I 
       contacted several motels and their answer was " I don't know what they came for." A 
       significant number of shooters came from long distances (Illinois, Minnesota, Rapid City, 
       etc.) and they stayed for two days." Coachlight Motel was contacted to determine the 
       number. The awarded funds ($1,735) were used for a variety of expenses (facility rental, 
       food and beverage, and marketing). Net loss of  $189.98 for the event. This event was 
       soon after much of South Dakota was impacted by winter weather/storm, so that did 
       prevent some participants from coming. 

B. SEA Survey 
Organization: Dakota Wesleyan University Soccer; Main Contact: Nicolas Reinhard; Date 
Completed: 5/1/2023 

     • Aaron Hieb highlighted their response to question 6: Are there events that your 
       organization would like to host, but are currently unable to host? They responded "Yes" 
       Outdoor Soccer Tournament at the Pepsi-Cola Soccer Complex, during the summer. 
       Aaron has a meeting set-up with Coach Reinhard and Coach Hakari next Thursday 
       morning to discuss their thoughts and ideas about making this event happen in 2024. 

6. Other Items 
Aaron reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee: 
A. SEA Banners on Display 
Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament (April 14th-16th, 2023) 

     • A SEA square banner and feather banner were set up at the Mitchell Activities Center. A 
       banner was set up at the entrance of the bleachers in each ice rink. 
B. Discussion about SEA guidelines/policy regarding distribution of approved grant funds. 
SEA QR Code 

     • Created a new SEA QR Code from a different online QR Code Generator, Beaconstac. 
     • Received feedback from Matt Culhane and Show Choir Classic that the current QR 
       Code did not consistently scan successfully with iPhones. 

 
SEA Proposed Funding Matrix 

     • Please review the email that will be sent out, most likely, next week. This email will 
       contain the SEA Funding Matrix, along with the idea and vision behind its intention and 
       purpose. 
     • This will give the committee the opportunity to review the email and 
       matrix/spreadsheet(s) on their own. This item will be added to the June SEA meeting 
       agenda, as long as there are not numerous funding applications scheduled for the June 
       meeting. The discussion in the upcoming meeting(s) will determine if the funding matrix 
       is an idea the committee would like to pursue and implement as a tool to help determine 
       funding amounts. 

 
Also, there was discussion about the opportunity for financial assistance from the Mitchell 
Chamber/CVB for events that submit an SEA Grant Application, but the approved funding 
amount is limited or funding is not approved. 
 
Also, there was discussion about limiting or spacing out the total number of SEA Grant 
Applications on each month's meeting agenda. This has been a repeated occurrence in only 
the month of April. The last two April (2022 & 2023) SEA Committee meeting agendas, there 
were over five submitted grant applications to be reviewed during the respective meetings. 
7. Next Meeting Date 
Kevin McCardle set the next meeting date for Tuesday, June 13th, 2023, @ 2 PM, in the City 
Hall - Council Chambers. 
8. Adjournment 
There being no further business to discuss. 
 
Meeting adjourned by: Kevin McCardle at 2:56 PM.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,

The state board of the SD USBC promotes the sport of bowling.
This is done in several different ways. First is by holding state
tournaments for Youth, Mixed, Women, Seniors and an Open
division. Second is we work to promote youth bowling by
providing scholarships for college or tech schools. We also work

The Jamboree is an annual event where bowlers have the
chance to interact with the state board to conduct business for
the up coming year. We also hold an awards ceremony for all of
our scholarship winners and the winners of our state
tournaments. The board works to bring in a professional bowler
to interact with our state bowlers. Time is spent on the lanes with
the professional discussing the sport of bowling and providing
insight on how to improve their game. We also hold an evening
banquet to induct our latest members into our Hall of Fame. This
is an annual event. During the time on the lanes, we also hold a
fund raising event to raise money for veterans and breast cancer
research. This is a fun event where bowlers get to bowl and bid
on auction items that have been donated for the cause. This is all
voluntary and is meant to be a chance to interact with the
professional as well as have some fun while bowling.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

Based on number of individuals who attended our Friday Night

events prefer to utilize the campground- we recommend to all of
them Lake Mitchell and most were very impressed with facilities
last year.
Briefly describe the

this event?
Our purpose of our event is to promote the Lake Mitchell Bike
Trail System. Our trails are something individuals within the
community should be proud of as they are some of the best in
Eastern South Dakota and as far away as Iowa and Minnesota.
Our trail system draws a significant amount of people each year
and by prompting a competition within the trails to all abilities and
levels of riders we are able to showcase these trails even further.
We are targeting both local community members along with
those out of town individuals who prefer to mountain bike.

Loop system mountain bike race on Lake Mitchell's North Trail
System- 3 classes or riders with 3 different length variations.
Women- 8, 16 and 32 mile loops
Men- 8, 16 and 32 mile loops
Youth- 8, 16 and 32 mile loops
Riders will ride the 2023 route in reverse of the 2022 route. Ride
will begin at Sandy Beach and end at Sandy Beach. There will be
a small section of the road that is marked for rides to ride.
The ride features a Friday night Social and Check in at Blarneys
along with snacks and awards after Saturday's event.

are you bringing event
participants from?

bikers from all over South Dakota along with Minnesota and Iowa
and Nebraska. Approximately 30 posters have been sent to bike
shops all over this four state region.

this race.

Our grant requests promotes tourism by brining in bikers from all
parts of South Dakota, Minnesota, Iowa and Nebraska. They are
able to see our Trail System along with spend sales tax dollars
within our local businesses, gas stations and campgrounds. This
race is one of a kind in Eastern, South Dakota and no event in
any other communities on this side of the state that have Single

Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Minutes
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
April 11, 2023
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM.
SEA Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, Kevin Nelson, Jon Hart,
Doug Greenway, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, and Jim Johnston.
SEA Committee members absent: Mayor Bob Everson, Cory Aadland, Bryan Dixon, and Tim
Smith.
Others present: Stephanie Ellwein, City Administrator and Tiffany Batdorf.
2. Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Committee reviewed applications
for grant funding. The following applications were presented and considered:
A. Mitchell School District: SoDak 16 Girls & Boys Basketball
Date: March 2nd & 7th, 2023; Contact: Cory Aadland; Grant Request: $1,750
• Doug Greenway shared the grant application with the SEA Committee. The SEA Grant
Application for this event is submitted after the fact because of the quick and short
notice process it takes to be awarded host site for the SoDak 16 games. Cory and the
Corn Palace were notified 4 days prior to the event, which determines host sites on
location and neutral site availability based on the teams that qualify. These were two of
the biggest games the Corn Palace hosted during the season: the girls' game brought
1,700 in attendance and the boys' game was around 1,550.
Motion: Motion was made by Jim Johnston to award $1,750, and seconded by Jon Hart. All
members voted "aye" and the motion passed.
B. Mitchell Baseball: Mitchell Baseball Tournaments
Date: May, June, & July, 2023; Contact: Jason Christensen; Grant Request: $6,000
• Jason Christensen from Mitchell Baseball presented the application to the committee.
They will be hosting four tournaments. The tournaments will be held May 6 (Early Bird),
June 2-3 (Teener Tournament), June 17-18 (Harve/Bryan Memorial), and July 14-16
(State 'A' Youth). The tournament scheduled for July 14-16 is a youth state tournament
and Mitchell Baseball anticipated this will be a big tournament. They anticipate that they
will continue to host this tournament every 2-4 years. Jason also stated that for the one-
day tournament, they schedule the out-of-town teams to play first to encourage
overnight stays. Requested grant funds will be used to pay for umpires, volunteers, and
hospitality. The proceeds from the tournaments go back into the program and are put
towards projects to enhance the baseball fields and complex.
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to award $6,000, and seconded by Jon Hart. All
members voted "aye" and the motion passed.

--- PAGE 1 OF 5 ---


C. Corn Palace Cornhole: ACL Regional #15 3rd Annual Corn Palace Cornhole
Tournament
Date: May 12th-14th, 2023; Contact: Tyler Earls; Grant Request: $5,000
• Tyler Earls presented the application for the 3rd Annual Corn Palace Cornhole
tournament to be held May 12-14. The grant dollars would be used for prize money for
the players. Tyler estimated that 30-100 rooms were used in 2022, and most stayed at
the Kelly Inn.
Motion: Motion was made by Kevin McCardle to award $1,000, seconded by Jill Larson. Eight
members voted "aye" and one member voted "nay". Motion carried.
D. Kiwanis Club of Mitchell: Kiwanis Youth Baseball Tournament
Date: May 13th, 2023; Contact: Cory Marek; Grant Request: $1,500, $500
• Cory Marek presented the grant application to the committee for the Kiwanis Youth
Baseball Tournament. Cory requested that the request be amended from $1,500 to
$500, since the tournament was moved to a one-day event to be held on Saturday, May
13. This is a change in date for the tournament, since the attendance is down from
previous years. However, they expect that numbers will increase as the date change is
known in future years. Currently, they have 10 teams. The grant funds will be used for
trophies & umpires.
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to award $500, seconded by Dave Helloloid. All
members voted "aye". Motion carried.
E. Mitchell Area Community Triathlon: MAC Triathlon
Date: June 9th-10th, 2023; Contact: Terasa Gillen; Grant Request: $3,000
• Emily Hohn presented the grant application to the committee. The MAC triathlon is
going to be held June 10 with registration and packet pick-up, Friday night, June 9. The
grant funds would be used to cover the timing equipment costs of $2,200. They expect
50-70 participants. Numbers for the event increased when the swimming portion of the
event was moved from Lake Mitchell to the Mitchell Aquatic Center outdoor pool.
Committee members asked about hotel stays, and the applicant stated that some do
stay, but also lots camp or just drive out early. Committee members encouraged the
organizers to suggest the Lake Mitchell Campground since the campground contributes
to the BID. They stated that they do have a good list of volunteers, but they can always
use more volunteers to help with turns and intersections, as well as counting laps in the
pool. Madison is not doing their triathlon, so they expect to see some people come to
Mitchell that would normally go to Madison.
Motion: Motion was made by Kevin Nelson to award $2,200 to cover the cost of the timing
equipment, seconded by Jon Hart. All members voted "aye". Motion carried.
F. Department of South Dakota Veterans of Foreign Wars: 93rd Annual VFW State
Convention
Date: June 15th-18th, 2023; Contact: Anna Arnold / Dr. Marty Christensen; Grant Request:
$3,130

--- PAGE 2 OF 5 ---


• Dr. Marty Christensen presented the grant application for the VFW State Convention.
Last year, when they hosted the convention, they utilized 78 hotel rooms, and anticipate
a similar number in 2023. They will be hosting the convention back again in 3 or 4 years.
He is also working on bringing other conventions as well. They would like assistance
from additional volunteers to help with serving the meals, and drivers of vehicles. They
said any volunteer help would be appreciated. Grant funds would be used to cover the
rental cost of the facility for the convention.
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to award $3,130, seconded by Kevin McCardle.
Eight members voted "aye" and one member voted "Nay". Motion carried.
G. Gentle Spirit Horses Rescue: Dakota Showdown Horse Trainer Challenge
Date: August 12th-13th, 2023; Contact: Tiffany Ring; Grant Request: $3,000
• Tiffany Ring presented the grant application to the committee. This is the second year
of the event, but the first year in Mitchell. Last year they held the event in Scotland, as a
"test run". They are hoping for between 300-500 people to attend the event. They
currently have 22 rescued horses that will be going to trainers that will be showcased
during the event (last year they had 1 pony with a trainer at the Scotland event). They
are working with Back 40 for some additional events tied to the Trainer Challenge.
Motion: Motion was made by Kevin Nelson to award $1,000, and seconded by Jill Larson. All
members voted "aye". Motion carried. Committee members discussed that they appreciated
that it is a new event being moved to Mitchell, but due to limited funds available, the amount
awarded was $1,000.
H. The 301 Rodz: OutKasts Car Show
Date: September 22nd-24th, 2023; Contact: KayLynn Bren; Grant Request: $2,500
• Jerry Wright presented the grant application to the committee. Registration and cruise
night on Friday night, car show Saturday, and donuts/coffee on Sunday morning. Last
year's event brought 180 registered cars, along with about 36 hotel rooms, filling the
Siesta and Coachlight Motels. Received much praise and appreciation from participants
by sending out "Thank-You" cards to everyone. The grant amount requested would be
utilized for advertising and reaching other participants in other states by putting ads in
different car magazines.
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to award $1,500, and seconded by Jon Hart. All
members voted "aye". Committee members noted that due to limited funds, the grant was
reduced.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Jon Hart to approve the previous minutes as presented,
seconded by LaRee Rumbolz. All members voted "aye". Motion carried.
4. Financial Report
Committee members reviewed the financial report as of April 6th, 2023. Collections in March
(for February records) were: 8.9% down from 2022, 15.4% above 2021, 15.5% down from
2020, 3.5% above 2019, and 1.9% down from 2018.

--- PAGE 3 OF 5 ---


Motion: Motion was made by Jon Hart to approve the financial report as presented, seconded
by Jill Larson. All members voted "aye". Motion carried.
5. Updates/Evaluation Forms/Financials
The following items were not reviewed because of lack of time. The SEA Committee went into
Executive Session to discuss and vote on submitted grant applications.
A. Evaluation Form w/Financials
Palace Ice Festival (January 13th-14th, 2023)
Larry Hauser Adult/JR Doubles Bowling Tournament (March 25th, 2023)
6. Other Items
The following items were not reviewed because of lack of time. Item B. will be added to and
discussion continued at the May SEA Committee meeting. The SEA Committee went into
Executive Session to discuss and vote on submitted grant applications.
A. SEA Banners on Display
Show Choir Classic (March 18th, 2023)
• SEA feather banner was set up at the Performing Arts Center in the west entrance (2)
main hallway/Box Office area.
Combat Veteran's Motorcycle Association Comedy Night (March 18th, 2023)
• SEA feather banner was set up at the Highland Conference Center just inside the main
entrance/exit doors of the conference center.
Larry Hauser Adult/JR Doubles Bowling Tournament (March 25h, 2023)
• SEA feather banners were set up at The Village Bowl next to Lane #1, where the finals
took place for the doubles tournament.
Bartholow Brothers Youth Trap Shooting Clinic (April 1st-2nd, 2023)
• SEA feather banners were set up at The Davison County 4H Building in the Meeting
Room Complex, where they conducted each morning's presentation before they began
their outdoor clinic.
B. Discussion about SEA guidelines/policy regarding distribution of approved grant funds.
SEA QR Code
• A new QR Code was created from a different online QR Code Generator, Beaconstac.
• Matt Culhane and Show Choir Classic provided feedback that the current QR Code did
not consistently scan successfully with iPhones.
7. Next Meeting Date
May 9th, 2023 @ 2 PM - City Hall, Council Chambers

--- PAGE 4 OF 5 ---


8. Adjournment
There being no further business to discuss.
Meeting adjourned by: Kevin McCardle at 4 PM.

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Minutes  
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                     June 13, 2023 
                                            
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Mayor Everson at 2:01 PM. 
 
SEA Committee members present: Mayor Everson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin Nelson, Doug 
Greenway, LaRee Rumbolz, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston. 
 
SEA Committee members absent: Jill Larson, Cory Aadland, Jon Hart, Bryan Dixon, and 
Emily Liedtke. 
 
Others present: Tiffany Batdorf, Johanna Allen, Alex Heidinger, and Aaron Hieb. 
2. Funding Applications 
No funding applications were submitted for consideration. 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Doug Greenway made a motion to approve the previous minutes as presented, 
seconded by Tim Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of June 5th, 2023. Total Fund Balance of 
$64,003.02. There are five committed items/events where the checks have not been written. 
Current Available Fund Balance of $17,503.02. Collections in May (for April records) were 
$14,121.00 and there are two hotels that are past due and have not submitted their collections. 
YTD comparison for collections were: down 3.4% from 2022, up 11.9% from 2021, up 21.4% 
from 2020, up 8.5% from 2019, and up 2.8% from 2018. 
 
Motion: Kevin Nelson made a motion to approve the financial report as presented, seconded 
by Dave Helleloid. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
5. Updates/Evaluation Forms/Financials 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms with financials and SEA Survey that were 
submitted from past SEA funded events to the SEA Committee. 
A. Evaluation Form w/Financials 
Cabin Fever Auction (March 3rd-4th, 2023) 

     • This event was rescheduled to the first weekend in March due to winter weather on the 
       original February date. The total spectator attendance for the entire event was 500+. 
       This count was derived from doubling the number of registered buyers. Usually, a buyer 
       brings a significant other with them. The number of hotel/motel rooms sold for the 
       auction was 100+. Hotels/Motels contacted to determine the number were: Coachlight 
       Motel, Comfort Inn & Suites, and Thunderbird Lodge. QR Code feedback was that most 
       of the attendees were older and were not familiar with the QR Code process. The 
       awarded funds ($1,200) were used to offset expenses we incurred, like hotel rooms. 
       Based on the financials submitted, there was a Net Profit of $324.87. 

 
Mitchell Show Choir Classic (March 18th, 2023) 
     • Winter weather affected the attendance at this event, preventing approximately 20 
       teams from being able to make the event to compete. The total spectator attendance for 
       the event was 500. This count was derived from the sales reports generated from our 
       Point of Sale system. The number of hotel/motel rooms sold for the event was 51 in 
       total. The hotels/motels contacted were: Hampton Inn. The awarded funds ($3,000) 
       were used to pay for judges' expenses for the event. Net Profit of $5,001.81, which was 
       down almost 4 times compared to 2022 because of teams unable to travel due to 
       weather. The profit from this event will be used to pay for costs associated with our 
       competition season, such as travel, choreography, costumes, and set. 

 
Combat Veteran's Motorcycle Association Comedy Night (March 18th, 2023) 

     • Winter weather also affected attendance for this event. The total spectator attendance 
       for the event was 132. This count was derived from ticket sales and head count. The 
       number of hotel/motel rooms sold for the event was 7 total. The hotels/motels contacted 
       were Coachlight Motel and Hampton Inn. The QR Code feedback was that the QR Code 
       was hard to scan on the table. The awarded funds ($1,800) were used to pay for the 
       comedian. Profit of $5,772.72. The profit from this event will be used to support 
       community veterans as needed. 

 
Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament (April 14th-16th, 2023) 
 
Stacy Murtha attended the meeting and personally "thanked" the Sports & Event Authority 
Advisory Committee for supporting the Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament. He talked about 
the two biggest expenses for the event, being the cost of ice time and referees. Also, he 
commented that Sioux Falls and Watertown are trying to piggy back off this event and create 
their own in September. Discussion about cash prizes/awards to intrigue teams to keep coming 
to this tournament. This is a premiere event and he greatly appreciates the support from the 
Sports & Events Authority. 

     • The total spectator attendance for the event was 500. This count was derived from what 
       event organizers witnessed during the tournament. The number of hotel/motel rooms 
       sold for the tournament was 82+. The hotels/motels contacted were: AmericInn, Comfort 
       Inn, Days Inn, Hampton Inn, Holiday Inn, Kelly Inn, and Super 8 Motel. QR Code 
       feedback was that it was not a well received option for the event. Even after email 
       communication, there were still teams that did not report where they were staying. The 
       awarded funds ($3,000) were used to help pay for the ice rental time. Profit of 
       $13,002.10 will be used to support youth hockey. 

 
B. SEA Survey 
Organization: Combat Veteran’s Motorcycle Association; Main Contact: Kim/Justin 
Hamer; Date Completed: 5/18/2023 

     • No discussion about submitted SEA Survey. 

6. Other Items 
Aaron reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee: 
A. SEA Banners on Display 
Corn Palace Cornhole Tournament (May 12th-14th, 2023) 
 
A brief discussion was had about the event. A request for Evaluation Form with Financials was 
emailed to the event organizer at the completion of the event. 

     • The SEA feather banners were set up in the Corn Palace arena at each end of the 
       stage. 

 
Mitchell Teener Tournament (June 2nd-3rd, 2023) 

     • A SEA square banner was set up on the fence by the entrance to Drake Field. 

B. Discussion about SEA guidelines regarding distribution of approved grant funds. 
SEA Proposed Funding Matrix 

     • Reviewed the email and Excel spreadsheets that were sent out to the committee. 

 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the Funding Matrix Excel Spreadsheets with the committee. First off, he 
thanked the committee for taking time to read the email and browse through the Excel 
Spreadsheets. He understands that it was probably an overwhelming amount of information, 
but the ideal vision is that the SEA Committee will have very minimal, if any, interaction or need 
to work with these spreadsheets. Basically, this is a compilation of ALL the facts from the SEA 
funded events since 2013, from SEA Grant Applications to post event Evaluation Forms. Aaron 
will use all this information to put together a starting point/amount that the committee can 
reference when determining an appropriate grant amount based on the number of hotel/motel 
rooms sold during the entirety of the event. As discussed in previous meetings, the creation and 
intention of the funding matrix is to provide a more consistent and predictable approach for the 
SEA Committee when reviewing SEA Grant Applications and determining an appropriate 
funding amount. The foundation of the matrix was created with substantial importance in the 
number of hotel/motel rooms sold during the entirety of the event, since ALL of the revenue 
used for the Sports & Events Authority Grant funding comes from the BID #2 Hotel Occupancy 
Tax ($.50 per room per night). Consideration will also be given to the presentation of the event 
(SEA Grant Application and presentation to the committee), will the event promote Mitchell in a 
positive image, and the past/projected overall event success and economic impact for Mitchell. 

     • The SEA Committee received an update from Doug Greenway and had a brief 
       discussion about the Dakota Territory Gun Collector's Association Gun Show. We were 
       unable to lock in a date for 2023 that worked for the Dakota Territory Gun Collector's 
       Association and the Corn Palace. Originally, the dates of November 10th-12th were 
       tentatively scheduled for the gun show, but this date fell through and did not work for the 
       DTGCA. We will remain in contact with the DTGCA and pursue a date(s) for 2024. 

 

     • The SEA Committee had discussion regarding the amount of approved SEA grant 
       funding for the Harve Johnston/Bryan Wilson Memorial Youth Baseball Tournament, 
       since it will only be a one-day tournament compared to the original plan of two days, one 
       day for 10U and one day for 12U. The tournament will take place Saturday, June 17th at 
       the Cadwell Sports Complex. 

 

     • The SEA Committee received an update from Jim Johnston and had a brief discussion 
       about the South Dakota State Amateur Baseball Tournament. The State Amateur 
       Baseball Tournament will be held in Mitchell at Cadwell Park this year (2023) and 2024. 
       Currently, for the 2025 host site, there are bids from Mitchell and Brandon Valley. 

7. Next Meeting Date 
Mayor Everson set the next meeting date for Tuesday, July 11th, 2023, @ 2 PM, in the City Hall 
- Council Chambers. 
8. Adjournment 
There being no further business to discuss. 
 
Meeting adjourned by: Mayor Everson at 2:46 PM.
