Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM.
SEA Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, Kevin Nelson, Doug
Greenway, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston.
SEA Committee members absent: Mayor Everson, Cory Aadland, Jon Hart, Bryan Dixon, and
LaRee Rumbolz.
Others present: Tiffany Batdorf, Stephanie Ellwein, and Aaron Hieb.
2. Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Committee reviewed applications
for grant funding. The following applications were presented and considered:
A. SD United States Bowling Congress Jamboree
Date: June 8th-10th, 2023; Contact: Jeff Vander Wilt; Grant Request: $5,000
• Jeff Vander Wilt, President of South Dakota USBC, presented the application to the
committee. The SD USBC Jamboree will take place from Friday, June 9th through
Saturday, June 10th. The host city and host site for the Jamboree is on a rotating
schedule; Rapid City hosted in 2021 and Pierre hosted in 2022. Friday's events will take
place at the Village Bowl, and include live interaction with Pro Bowler, Carolyn Dorin-
Ballard and fundraisers throughout the evening. Saturday's events will be hosted at the
Highland Conference Center with an awards banquet during the afternoon and Hall of
Fame Honoree Banquet in the evening. Jeff estimates between 350-400 people will be
in Mitchell over the two days. The requested grant funds would be used to offset the
meal costs and hotel room costs for the attendees. This event is a great opportunity to
promote the remodeled Village Bowl and its great facilities, along with the Highland
Conference Center to all the attendees. Profits/proceeds from the event are used
towards the SD USBC youth bowler scholarship fund.
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to award $3,000, and seconded by Doug
Greenway. All members voted "Aye" and the motion passed.
B. Ron's Bike Shop: Beers & Gears Mountain Bike Race
Date: June 23rd-24th, 2023; Contact: Cody Denne; Grant Request: $2,000
• Cody Denne from the Palace City Pedalers/Ron's Bike Shop presented the application
to the committee. The 2nd annual Beers & Gears Mountain Bike Race will take place on
Saturday, June 24th, starting at 9 AM and utilizing the Lake Mitchell North Trail Loop,
which includes: Sandy Beach, Harmon Boat Landing, and Camp Arroyo. Friday evening,
June 23rd, is packet pick-up at Blarneys, along with a social and gathering. The grant
amount requested would be utilized to pay for the timing system that is required to host
a successful event. Currently, they have 25 riders registered. Last year, there were 45
riders with about 100 participants total between riders, staff, volunteers, etc. They added

--- PAGE 1 OF 4 ---


a new feature this year. For those that don't have a mountain bike, they have bike
rentals available for those that would like to participate. Most mountain bikers prefer to
stay at campgrounds, but they do have a block of room at the Comfort Inn, and will
promote/encourage bikers to stay at the Lake Mitchell Campground, since the BID #2
Hotel Tax is collected there. The purpose of the event is to promote the hard work,
dedication, and beauty of the Lake Mitchell Trail System.
• Discussion about timing system cost and if there is a difference between timing systems
that other events have requested SEA grant funding for.
• Discussion about the interest and possibility of hosting a Fat Bike Race in the winter on
the Lake Mitchell Trails.
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to award $2,000, and seconded by Jim
Johnston. All voted "Aye" and the motion passed.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Jim Johnston to approve the previous minutes as presented,
seconded by Emily Liedtke. All members voted "Aye" and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
Stephanie Ellwein and Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of May 4th, 2023.
Collections in April (for March records) were: down 3.9% from 2022, up 16.4% from 2021, up
3.6% from 2020, up 9.1% from 2019, and up 0.5% from 2018. A Fund Balance of $80,270.02,
with eight committed funding checks that will be cut next Monday, May 15th, after the City
Council meeting, leaving an Available Fund Balance of $16,690.02.
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the financial report as presented, seconded
by Doug Greenway. All members voted "Aye" and the motion passed.
5. Updates/Evaluation Forms/Financials
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms with financials and SEA Survey that were
submitted from past SEA funded events with the SEA Committee.
A. Evaluation Form w/Financials
Girl's & Boy's Hanson Classic (January 14th & January 21st, 2023)
• Total spectator attendance for the entire event was 3,532 (Girls = 1,586 & Boys =
1,946). This count was derived from the Corn Palace Service and Rental Rate sheet.
Information was not available regarding the number of hotel/motel rooms sold for the
classics. The awarded funds ($2,000) were used for hospitality and workers. All
remaining money, if any, would go towards other expenses... Officials, score table, shot
clock, announcers, and back door monitors. Corn Palace Rental and Service reports
were submitted, which include revenue made from the ticket sales/admission: Girls =
$8,981.60 & Boys = $13,693.50. Aaron shared the Thank You card sent by Jim Bridge
to the SEA Committee.
DWU/Culver's Girl's & Boy's HS Basketball Classic (February 10th-11th, 2023)
• Total spectator attendance for the entire event was 4,500+. This count was derived from
the tickets sold and door counters. Approximately 20 rooms were sold for the event (5-7
teams stayed at least one night with a minimum of three rooms per team). The hotels

--- PAGE 2 OF 4 ---


contacted were the Comfort Inn & Suites, Days Inns, and Holiday Inn. The awarded
funds ($2,000) were used to offset expenses. Profit of $8,666, this was a fundraiser for
our men's and women's basketball programs. The profit will be put into our fundraising
accounts to enhance the experience for our student-athletes.
DWU 13th Annual Indoor Futsal Classic (February 24th-26th, 2023)
• Total spectator attendance for the entire event was between 300-400. This count was
derived from the door counts. The QR Code Hotel Survey indicated 20 hotel/motel
rooms were sold, plus the coaches indicated up to 30 rooms, so approximately 50
rooms, give or take, were sold for the event. No hotels were contacted, only coaches.
The awarded funds (1,500) were used to cover the refereeing expenses that we were
able to drastically lower this year due to the help of our student-athletes. In comparison
to 2022 ($3,423.91), they saved $1,637.46 in referee expenses for the 2023 ($1,786.45)
event. Profit of $12,876.28 was split between the men's and women's soccer teams as a
fundraiser.
Bartholow Brothers Trapshooting Clinic (March 31st, April 1st-2nd, 2023)
• Total spectator attendance for the entire event was approximately 400 +. This count was
derived from visual observation and the seating capacity of the meeting room. 50-60
hotel/motel rooms were sold during the event. "I really don't have an accurate number. I
contacted several motels and their answer was " I don't know what they came for." A
significant number of shooters came from long distances (Illinois, Minnesota, Rapid City,
etc.) and they stayed for two days." Coachlight Motel was contacted to determine the
number. The awarded funds ($1,735) were used for a variety of expenses (facility rental,
food and beverage, and marketing). Net loss of $189.98 for the event. This event was
soon after much of South Dakota was impacted by winter weather/storm, so that did
prevent some participants from coming.
B. SEA Survey
Organization: Dakota Wesleyan University Soccer; Main Contact: Nicolas Reinhard; Date
Completed: 5/1/2023
• Aaron Hieb highlighted their response to question 6: Are there events that your
organization would like to host, but are currently unable to host? They responded "Yes"
Outdoor Soccer Tournament at the Pepsi-Cola Soccer Complex, during the summer.
Aaron has a meeting set-up with Coach Reinhard and Coach Hakari next Thursday
morning to discuss their thoughts and ideas about making this event happen in 2024.
6. Other Items
Aaron reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee:
A. SEA Banners on Display
Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament (April 14th-16th, 2023)
• A SEA square banner and feather banner were set up at the Mitchell Activities Center. A
banner was set up at the entrance of the bleachers in each ice rink.

--- PAGE 3 OF 4 ---


B. Discussion about SEA guidelines/policy regarding distribution of approved grant funds.
SEA QR Code
• Created a new SEA QR Code from a different online QR Code Generator, Beaconstac.
• Received feedback from Matt Culhane and Show Choir Classic that the current QR
Code did not consistently scan successfully with iPhones.
SEA Proposed Funding Matrix
• Please review the email that will be sent out, most likely, next week. This email will
contain the SEA Funding Matrix, along with the idea and vision behind its intention and
purpose.
• This will give the committee the opportunity to review the email and
matrix/spreadsheet(s) on their own. This item will be added to the June SEA meeting
agenda, as long as there are not numerous funding applications scheduled for the June
meeting. The discussion in the upcoming meeting(s) will determine if the funding matrix
is an idea the committee would like to pursue and implement as a tool to help determine
funding amounts.
Also, there was discussion about the opportunity for financial assistance from the Mitchell
Chamber/CVB for events that submit an SEA Grant Application, but the approved funding
amount is limited or funding is not approved.
Also, there was discussion about limiting or spacing out the total number of SEA Grant
Applications on each month's meeting agenda. This has been a repeated occurrence in only
the month of April. The last two April (2022 & 2023) SEA Committee meeting agendas, there
were over five submitted grant applications to be reviewed during the respective meetings.
7. Next Meeting Date
Kevin McCardle set the next meeting date for Tuesday, June 13th, 2023, @ 2 PM, in the City
Hall - Council Chambers.
8. Adjournment
There being no further business to discuss.
Meeting adjourned by: Kevin McCardle at 2:56 PM.

documents.fileName: July 11th, 2023, SEA Advisory Committee Meeting Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Minutes  
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                     July 11, 2023 
                                            
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Mayor Everson at 2:01 PM. 
 
SEA Committee members present: Mayor Everson, Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, Kevin 
Nelson, Jon Hart, Doug Greenway, Bryan Dixon, and Jim Johnston. 
 
SEA Committee members absent: Cory Aadland, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave 
Helleloid, and Tim Smith. 
 
Others present: Stephanie Ellwein, Johanna Allen, and Aaron Hieb. 
2. Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Committee reviewed applications 
for grant funding. The following applications were presented and considered: 
A. South Dakota Women's State Softball Tournament 
Date: July 29th-30th, 2023; Contact: Kathy Axsom; Grant Request: $5,000 

     • Kathy Axsom, Mitchell Women's Slow Pitch Softball Area Commissioner, presented and 
       shared information about the submitted grant application for the South Dakota Women's 
       State Softball Tournament. The grant request is for $5,000, of which $2,500 would go to 
       the State Association for fees/expenses to host this state tournament. The grant request 
       would also go towards hotel rooms for umpires, meals for umpires, and field/diamond 
       maintenance. The local association does not profit from hosting a state tournament. 
       There is a total of $10,000 in expenses to host a state tournament. The State 
       Association pays $3,500 of these fees, which covers the umpire expenses. The last time 
       Mitchell hosted a Women's State Softball Tournament was eight years ago (2015). This 
       year there are an estimated 50 women's teams that would participate in the state 
       tournament. The biggest expense when hosting a state tournament is hotel rooms for 
       umpires ($3,000). The last few years, the tournament has been held in Sioux Falls. 
       Each year there is an East and West host city/site. This year the East is hosted in 
       Mitchell and the West is hosted in Aberdeen.  

 
Motion: Motion was made by Kevin Nelson to award $3,000 and seconded by Doug Greenway. 
All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
B. South Dakota State Amateur Baseball Tournament 
Date: August 2nd-13th, 2023; Contact: Jim Johnston; Grant Request: $5,000 

     • Jim Johnston, Mitchell Baseball Association, presented and shared information about 
       the submitted grant application for the South Dakota State Amateur Baseball 
       Association. There will be 37 teams over the course of 12 days. An estimated 12,000 
       people come to Mitchell for this tournament. The grant request of $5,000 would be used 
       for the following: meals for the commissioners, old-timers-game social, hotel rooms for 
       the PA announcer, workers, and field maintenance. It has always been hard to 
       determine how many hotel rooms are sold during the tournament. The State Amateur        Baseball Tournament is a win-win for many entities, such as: a fundraiser for the 
       Mitchell Baseball Association, Exchange Club of Mitchell with concessions, and the city 
       of Mitchell. 

 
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to award $5,000 and seconded by Bryan Dixon. 
Jim Johnston abstained from voting. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
C. South Dakota Planners Association Annual Conference 
Date: October 24th-26th, 2023; Contact: Brandi Hanten; Grant Request: $3,000 

     • Karen Wegleitner presented the submitted grant application on behalf of the South 
       Dakota Planners Association. There is an annual conference hosted in a different city 
       each year. This year's conference will be hosted at the Highland Conference Center in 
       Mitchell, SD. The conference will also be hosting and utilizing social events at The Back 
       40 and Blarney's. They are estimating 75 attendees for the conference. Brandi Hanten, 
       Vice President of the South Dakota Planners Association, joined midway through the 
       presentation via conference phone to provide budget/financials to the committee. 
       Membership dues and registration fees provide income for the SDPA to cover expenses 
       for hosting the annual conference. The grant amount request would be used to cover 
       food, speaker(s) costs, and Highland Conference Center rental fees.  

 
Motion: Motion was made by Bryan Dixon to award $1,500 and seconded by Jon Hart. All 
members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Kevin Nelson to approve the previous minutes as presented, 
seconded by Bryan Dixon. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of July 6th, 2023. Total Fund Balance of 
$70,072.52. There are five committed items/events where the checks have not been written. 
Current Available Fund Balance of $23,572.52. Collections in June (for May records) were 
$20,406.00 and there are two hotels that are past due and have not submitted their collections. 
Also, there is still one hotel past due for collection in May (for April records). YTD comparison 
for collections were: down 2.7% from 2022, up 7.8% from 2021, up 37.6% from 2020, up 8.7% 
from 2019, and up 4.4% from 2018. 
 
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to approve the financial report as presented, 
seconded by Jon Hart. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
5. Updates/Evaluation Forms/Financials 
There were no items submitted at this time. 
6. Other Items 
Aaron reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee: 
A. SEA Banners on Display 
South Dakota United States Bowling Congress Jamboree (June 9th-10th, 2023) 

     • Two SEA feather banners were set up at The Village Bowl. 

 South Dakota Golf Association Two-Man Championship (June 10th-11th, 2023) 

     • A SEA square banner was set up on the patio of the south entrance to the clubhouse at 
       Lakeview Golf Course. 

 
South Dakota 93rd Annual VFW State Convention (June 15th-18th, 2023) 

     • SEA feather banners were set up outside, at the entrance of the Davison County Fair 
       Grounds Building. 

 
Harve Johnston/Bryan Wilson Memorial Baseball Tournament (June 17th, 2023) 

     • SEA square banners were set up on the fence by the entrances into the two complexes 
       (D-G & H-K). 

 
Beers & Gears Mountain Bike Race (June 24th, 2023) 

     • A SEA square banner was set up at Sandy Beach (Lake Mitchell), which was 
       headquarters for the race. 

B. Discussion about SEA guidelines/policy regarding distribution of approved grant funds. 
Aaron reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee: 
SEA QR Code Hotel Survey 
The Sports & Events Authority QR Code Hotel Survey was implemented back in February. The 
SEA QR Code flyer is created each time a submitted grant application event is approved. The 
flyer contains the name of the event/organization, the QR Code enlarged in the center, and the 
logo of the respective event/organization at the bottom. The SEA QR Code flyer is included in 
the approval award email to the event main contact. In the email, it is recommended/suggested 
that they provide the QR Code and/or flyer in the registration packet and to the teams, coaches, 
and participants/attendees of the respective event. Also, it states in the email that the QR Code 
results are not the final amount of hotel/motel rooms sold, but that it is still the responsibility of 
event staff to determine the most accurate estimation of hotel/motel rooms sold during the 
entirety of the event and include that number on the post-event Evaluation Form. During SEA 
banner set-up, Aaron will post a handful of flyers throughout the facility or venue. There have 
currently been 15 events that have been provided with the SEA QR Code flyer. Most of the 
results usually have about a handful of participation per event. Two events in particular, DWU 
Futsal Indoor Classic (15) and the South Dakota United State Bowling Congress Jamboree (21) 
were able to gather the most participation on the SEA QR Code Hotel Survey. Those who 
participate in the SEA QR Code Hotel Survey provide feedback about where participants are 
staying/lodging during their time in Mitchell for the SEA funded/assisted event. There are 
instances where we receive positive hotel feedback about why the individual(s) chose to stay at 
the respective hotel. That specific survey is then emailed out to the respective hotel manager, 
so they can provide the positive feedback with their staff. Last of all, the exposure that the 
Mitchell Sports & Events Authority receives from participation in the SEA QR Code Hotel 
Survey is beneficial and will hopefully result in future events choosing Mitchell because of the 
grant opportunity.      • The committee had some discussion about ways to improve the participation rates and 
       effectiveness of the SEA QR Code Hotel Survey and flyer. 

SEA Funding Matrix 
Aaron provided an opportunity for the committee to ask any follow-up questions about the 
funding matrix that was presented at the last meeting. Also, once the committee is in Executive 
Session to discuss and determine appropriate funding for the submitted grant applications, 
Aaron will share the funding matrix amount and how it was determined for each respective 
grant application. 
7. Next Meeting Date 
Mayor Everson set the next meeting date for Tuesday, August 8th, 2023, @ 2 PM, in the City 
Hall - Council Chambers. 
8. Adjournment 
There being no further business to discuss. 
 
Meeting adjourned by: Mayor Everson at 3:02 PM.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.

The purpose of the Mitchell Baseball Association is to fund
Teener, High school and American Legion baseball in Mitchell.
We usually have 70-80 players in our program each year. What
we provide is giving these young men at opportunity to play
baseball every year. People that will be coming to the State
Amateur Baseball Tournament come from all over the state. Over
the two weekends several teams and fans stay overnight. During
the second weekend at least two teams and fans from Rapid City

The State Amateur Baseball Tournament is a 12-day
Tournament that brings 36 teams to Mitchell over the course of
12 days. Teams come from all areas of South Dakota. The 2023
state tournament starts Wednesday, August 2nd and runs
through Sunday August 13th. The tickets sales go to the South
Dakota Amateur Baseball Tournament. The state amateur

--- PAGE 4 OF 6 ---


tournament is played at Cadwell Baseball Stadium and Drake

from all areas of South Dakota. Teams have to qualify to come to
the tournament by playing district tournaments throughout the
state.
What are the specific
goals for this event?
The goal of hosting the South Dakota State Amateur Baseball
Tournament every year is to run a well organized event and
provide funding not only for our association, but by using money
generated at the tournament to go back to improvements at
Cadwell Park to enhance the facility so we remain competitive to
get the tournament back in Mitchell for future years. It's the goal
of the Mitchell Baseball Association to have at least one state
baseball tournament in Mitchell every year. Although we have
had the State Amateur Tournament in Mitchell for several years,
on the years when we don't have the tournament we work on
bringing an American Legion State Tournament to Mitchell.

request would be used
to promote tourism in
Mitchell? Note the
resulting impact of your

The site for the State Amateur Baseball Tournament is decided
every year by the South Dakota State Amateur Baseball
Association. The association consists of 10 commissioners and
three officers who stay in Mitchell throughout the tournament.
Ondays when we have two sessions, we provide meals at
Cadwell Park for the association members in between the two
sessions. We also provide lunch after the old timers game the
first day of the tournament. We also have a social with our
volunteers and the commissioners during the championship
game. These are three things we wouldn't be able to provide
without funding by Sports and Events Authority. We consider
these to be three important things to show our hospitality to the
state commissioners and letting them know how much we
appreciate having the tournament in Mitchell. We also believe it
is important to provide a social at the end of the tournament for
our 60 plus volunteers who give of their time during the 12-day
event because without them we wouldn't be able to host the
tournament. Without the funding we wouldn't be able to provide
these things.

including: Roberts Rules of Order and ex-parte communication,
ag preservation, main street streetscapes, platting, complete

and legal issues of the year. On Tuesday evening we will be

attendees an opportunity to hang out after their arrival to Mitchell.

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Minutes
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
June 13, 2023
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Mayor Everson at 2:01 PM.
SEA Committee members present: Mayor Everson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin Nelson, Doug
Greenway, LaRee Rumbolz, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston.
SEA Committee members absent: Jill Larson, Cory Aadland, Jon Hart, Bryan Dixon, and
Emily Liedtke.
Others present: Tiffany Batdorf, Johanna Allen, Alex Heidinger, and Aaron Hieb.
2. Funding Applications
No funding applications were submitted for consideration.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Doug Greenway made a motion to approve the previous minutes as presented,
seconded by Tim Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of June 5th, 2023. Total Fund Balance of
$64,003.02. There are five committed items/events where the checks have not been written.
Current Available Fund Balance of $17,503.02. Collections in May (for April records) were
$14,121.00 and there are two hotels that are past due and have not submitted their collections.
YTD comparison for collections were: down 3.4% from 2022, up 11.9% from 2021, up 21.4%
from 2020, up 8.5% from 2019, and up 2.8% from 2018.
Motion: Kevin Nelson made a motion to approve the financial report as presented, seconded
by Dave Helleloid. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Updates/Evaluation Forms/Financials
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms with financials and SEA Survey that were
submitted from past SEA funded events to the SEA Committee.
A. Evaluation Form w/Financials
Cabin Fever Auction (March 3rd-4th, 2023)
• This event was rescheduled to the first weekend in March due to winter weather on the
original February date. The total spectator attendance for the entire event was 500+.
This count was derived from doubling the number of registered buyers. Usually, a buyer
brings a significant other with them. The number of hotel/motel rooms sold for the
auction was 100+. Hotels/Motels contacted to determine the number were: Coachlight
Motel, Comfort Inn & Suites, and Thunderbird Lodge. QR Code feedback was that most
of the attendees were older and were not familiar with the QR Code process. The
awarded funds ($1,200) were used to offset expenses we incurred, like hotel rooms.
Based on the financials submitted, there was a Net Profit of $324.87.
Mitchell Show Choir Classic (March 18th, 2023)

--- PAGE 1 OF 4 ---


• Winter weather affected the attendance at this event, preventing approximately 20
teams from being able to make the event to compete. The total spectator attendance for
the event was 500. This count was derived from the sales reports generated from our
Point of Sale system. The number of hotel/motel rooms sold for the event was 51 in
total. The hotels/motels contacted were: Hampton Inn. The awarded funds ($3,000)
were used to pay for judges' expenses for the event. Net Profit of $5,001.81, which was
down almost 4 times compared to 2022 because of teams unable to travel due to
weather. The profit from this event will be used to pay for costs associated with our
competition season, such as travel, choreography, costumes, and set.
Combat Veteran's Motorcycle Association Comedy Night (March 18th, 2023)
• Winter weather also affected attendance for this event. The total spectator attendance
for the event was 132. This count was derived from ticket sales and head count. The
number of hotel/motel rooms sold for the event was 7 total. The hotels/motels contacted
were Coachlight Motel and Hampton Inn. The QR Code feedback was that the QR Code
was hard to scan on the table. The awarded funds ($1,800) were used to pay for the
comedian. Profit of $5,772.72. The profit from this event will be used to support
community veterans as needed.
Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament (April 14th-16th, 2023)
Stacy Murtha attended the meeting and personally "thanked" the Sports & Event Authority
Advisory Committee for supporting the Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament. He talked about
the two biggest expenses for the event, being the cost of ice time and referees. Also, he
commented that Sioux Falls and Watertown are trying to piggy back off this event and create
their own in September. Discussion about cash prizes/awards to intrigue teams to keep coming
to this tournament. This is a premiere event and he greatly appreciates the support from the
Sports & Events Authority.
• The total spectator attendance for the event was 500. This count was derived from what
event organizers witnessed during the tournament. The number of hotel/motel rooms
sold for the tournament was 82+. The hotels/motels contacted were: AmericInn, Comfort
Inn, Days Inn, Hampton Inn, Holiday Inn, Kelly Inn, and Super 8 Motel. QR Code
feedback was that it was not a well received option for the event. Even after email
communication, there were still teams that did not report where they were staying. The
awarded funds ($3,000) were used to help pay for the ice rental time. Profit of
$13,002.10 will be used to support youth hockey.
B. SEA Survey
Organization: Combat Veteran’s Motorcycle Association; Main Contact: Kim/Justin
Hamer; Date Completed: 5/18/2023
• No discussion about submitted SEA Survey.
6. Other Items

--- PAGE 2 OF 4 ---


Aaron reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee:
A. SEA Banners on Display
Corn Palace Cornhole Tournament (May 12th-14th, 2023)
A brief discussion was had about the event. A request for Evaluation Form with Financials was
emailed to the event organizer at the completion of the event.
• The SEA feather banners were set up in the Corn Palace arena at each end of the
stage.
Mitchell Teener Tournament (June 2nd-3rd, 2023)
• A SEA square banner was set up on the fence by the entrance to Drake Field.
B. Discussion about SEA guidelines regarding distribution of approved grant funds.
SEA Proposed Funding Matrix
• Reviewed the email and Excel spreadsheets that were sent out to the committee.
Aaron Hieb reviewed the Funding Matrix Excel Spreadsheets with the committee. First off, he
thanked the committee for taking time to read the email and browse through the Excel
Spreadsheets. He understands that it was probably an overwhelming amount of information,
but the ideal vision is that the SEA Committee will have very minimal, if any, interaction or need
to work with these spreadsheets. Basically, this is a compilation of ALL the facts from the SEA
funded events since 2013, from SEA Grant Applications to post event Evaluation Forms. Aaron
will use all this information to put together a starting point/amount that the committee can
reference when determining an appropriate grant amount based on the number of hotel/motel
rooms sold during the entirety of the event. As discussed in previous meetings, the creation and
intention of the funding matrix is to provide a more consistent and predictable approach for the
SEA Committee when reviewing SEA Grant Applications and determining an appropriate
funding amount. The foundation of the matrix was created with substantial importance in the
number of hotel/motel rooms sold during the entirety of the event, since ALL of the revenue
used for the Sports & Events Authority Grant funding comes from the BID #2 Hotel Occupancy
Tax ($.50 per room per night). Consideration will also be given to the presentation of the event
(SEA Grant Application and presentation to the committee), will the event promote Mitchell in a
positive image, and the past/projected overall event success and economic impact for Mitchell.
• The SEA Committee received an update from Doug Greenway and had a brief
discussion about the Dakota Territory Gun Collector's Association Gun Show. We were
unable to lock in a date for 2023 that worked for the Dakota Territory Gun Collector's
Association and the Corn Palace. Originally, the dates of November 10th-12th were
tentatively scheduled for the gun show, but this date fell through and did not work for the
DTGCA. We will remain in contact with the DTGCA and pursue a date(s) for 2024.
• The SEA Committee had discussion regarding the amount of approved SEA grant
funding for the Harve Johnston/Bryan Wilson Memorial Youth Baseball Tournament,

--- PAGE 3 OF 4 ---


since it will only be a one-day tournament compared to the original plan of two days, one
day for 10U and one day for 12U. The tournament will take place Saturday, June 17th at
the Cadwell Sports Complex.
• The SEA Committee received an update from Jim Johnston and had a brief discussion
about the South Dakota State Amateur Baseball Tournament. The State Amateur
Baseball Tournament will be held in Mitchell at Cadwell Park this year (2023) and 2024.
Currently, for the 2025 host site, there are bids from Mitchell and Brandon Valley.
7. Next Meeting Date
Mayor Everson set the next meeting date for Tuesday, July 11th, 2023, @ 2 PM, in the City Hall
- Council Chambers.
8. Adjournment
There being no further business to discuss.
Meeting adjourned by: Mayor Everson at 2:46 PM.

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Minutes  
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                     August 8, 2023 
                                            
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:02 PM. 
 
SEA Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Kevin Nelson, Doug Greenway, LaRee 
Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston. 
 
SEA Committee members absent: Mayor Everson, Jill Larson, Cory Aadland, Jon Hart, and 
Bryan Dixon. 
 
Others present: Johanna Allen, Stephanie Ellwein, and Aaron Hieb. 
2. Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Committee reviewed applications 
for grant funding. The following applications were presented and considered: 
A. Raise Em Rank Bull Riding Series Finals 

     • Dillon Swanson, Raise Em Rank, presented the submitted SEA grant application for the 
       Raise Em Rank Bull Riding Series Finals to be hosted at the Corn Palace on September 
       8th-9th, 2023. There are 5-6 events throughout the year that qualify for points towards 
       the series finals. They take the top 20 bullriders for the open division and about 30 youth 
       bullriders from ages 6 to 16 that compete from about 6 or 7 different states. Typically, a 
       new event like this takes about 3 years for it to develop to where the members of the 
       community know what the event is about and what to expect. Dillon will work on 
       establishing an awards banquet to be held on Sunday morning, which, in turn, would 
       keep people in Mitchell an extra night longer. Event estimation for hotel/motel rooms 
       sold is a very conservative number of approximately 200 hotel/motel rooms sold for the 
       entirety of the event. A typical show lasts around 2 1/2 hours.   

 
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to award $5,000 and seconded by Kevin Nelson. 
7 members voted 'Aye', 1 member voted 'Nay', and the motion passed. 
B. South Dakota State Disc Golf Championship 

     • Ronnie Hoeltzner with Mitchell Disc Golf presented the submitted SEA Grant Application 
       for the South Dakota State Disc Golf Championship to be held in Mitchell at Dry Run 
       Creek on September 22nd-24th, 2023. Currently there are 124 participants signed up 
       with a cap of 150. The majority of players are from outside of Mitchell, (currently 20 
       registered from Mitchell), including seven different states and Canada. Saturday night 
       they will utilize The Back 40 and provide two comedians for entertainment for the 
       participants. Last year, the state tournament was held in Spearfish. The annual rotation 
       includes Yankton, Spearfish, Aberdeen, and Sioux Falls. Any profit from the event goes 
       towards improvements made to Dry Run Creek Park.    

 
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to award $1,550 and seconded by LaRee Rumbolz. All 
members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
C. Palace City Kiwanis Half Marathon & Relay 

     • Paula, Julie, and Crystal, Kiwanis Club of Mitchell, presented the submitted SEA Grant 
       Application for the Palace City Kiwanis Half Marathon & Relay, 5K & 10K, which will be 
       held on October 1st, 2023, in Mitchell. This will be the 6th annual race. The money that 
       has been raised goes towards the inclusive playground that has been built at the 
       Kiwanis Woodlot Park. Currently there are 113 runners registered. They expect to hit 
       200 runners. The run starts at 7:30 AM on Sunday, October 1st. Runners come from the 
       following: 23 runners come from more than 80 miles away, 9 from out of state 
       (Minnesota, Iowa, and Nebraska) as well as New Mexico, New York, and two from 
       California. The SEA logo is put on the awards and will provide space for a banner to be 
       put on the Corn Palace balcony. Many compliments about the route that is used for the 
       event, which has led to repeat runners. Profit that is raised from the event does not 
       necessarily go back into the event, but back into the community. The next project will be 
       to add some more small libraries throughout town in the local parks.   

 
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to award $2,000 and seconded by Doug 
Greenway. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Jim Johnston to approve the previous minutes as presented, 
seconded by Tim Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of August 3rd, 2023. Total Fund Balance of 
$66,079.02. There are four committed items/events where the checks have not been written. 
Current Available Fund Balance of $22,079.02. Collections in July (for June records) were 
$23,706.00 and there are four hotels that are past due and have not submitted their collections. 
Also, there is still one hotel past due for both May and June collections. YTD comparison for 
collections were: down 5.3% from 2022, up 1.3% from 2021, up 36.4% from 2020, up 2.6% 
from 2019, and down 0.4% from 2018. 
 
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to approve the financial report as presented, 
seconded by Dave Helleloid. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
5. Updates/Evaluation Forms/Financials 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form with financials that was submitted from past 
SEA funded events to the SEA Committee. 
A. Evaluation Form w/Financials 
Beers & Gears Mountain Bike Race (June 24th, 2023) 

     • The total spectator attendance for the event was 65. This count was derived from the 
       number of volunteers and family members watching the event. There were 61 riders, 
       which is an increase from the 42 riders in 2022. The number of hotel/motel rooms sold 
       for the tournament was 1. The hotel/motel contacted was: Hampton Inn. There were 
       quite a few people who used Lake Mitchell Campground and Betts Campground - they 
       liked the locations for their bikes. QR Code feedback was that they offered it to riders, 
       but unsure if any scanned and participated in the hotel survey. The awarded funds 
       ($2,000) were used to pay for the timing system. Profit of $1,697.07 will be used to 
       donate STRIDER BIKES to local preschools - we have so far donated 12 to First 
       Lutheran and will be making a donation back to Palace City Preschool as well. 

6. Other Items 
Aaron reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee: 
A. SEA Banners on Display 
South Dakota State A Youth Baseball Tournament (July 14th-16th, 2023) 

     • Two SEA square banners were set up, one on each fence at the entrances into the two 
       complexes (D-G & H-K). 

 
South Dakota Women's State Softball Tournament (July 29th-30th, 2023) 

     • Two SEA square banners were set up, one on each fence at the entrances into the two 
       complexes (D-G & H-K). 

 
South Dakota State Amateur Baseball Tournament (August 2nd-13th, 2023) 

     • A SEA square banner was put on the fence by the entrance to Drake Field. Also, 
       Mitchell Baseball Association put up two Sports Authority banners at Cadwell Stadium, 
       one on each side of the grandstands towards the top of the fence. 

B. Discussion about Special Olympics lanyards for the upcoming State Fall Classic and 
State Basketball Tournament. 
Darryl Nordquist, Special Olympics - South Dakota, attended the SEA Committee meeting to 
assist with discussion regarding the request of 1,000 lanyards for the Special Olympics to be 
used at the State Fall Classic in September 2023 and State Basketball in March 2024.  
C. Discussion with Special Olympics regarding hotel rooms. 
Darryl Nordquist, Special Olympics - South Dakota, attended the SEA Committee meeting to 
share feedback he has received from delegations regarding the hotel room rates for Special 
Olympics events that are held in Mitchell. 
7. Next Meeting Date 
Kevin McCardle set the next meeting date for Tuesday, September 12th, 2023, @ 2 PM, in the 
City Hall - Council Chambers. 
8. Adjournment 
There being no further business to discuss. 
 
Meeting adjourned by: Kevin McCardle at 3:16 PM.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

Raise Em Rank is about entertainment. We bring an action-
packed show to local communities with the goal of bringing
people together and offering something both unique and exciting
to take part in. Our motto is COURAGE IS CONTAGIOUS as we
highlight the up-and-coming future stars of the sport in our youth

against the best bullriders in the territory. Our events are family

The 2023 Raise Em Rank finals takes place September 8th and

turning the basketball court of the Corn Palace into a rodeo
arena. Bull riding starts Friday night at 7:00 and Saturday at
6:00pm. Gates will open at 4 both nights for fans to come early
and enjoy the vendor booths, check out the merch tent, reserve
seats and meet and greet with competitors who will be present to
sign some autographs. Following the bull riding Saturday night,

sporting events for our region such as Twins and Vikings games.

able to advertise in all of our other markets throughout our 2024

other Raise Em Rank series events.

competitors who look forward to it all year.

Your grant will allow us to get a head start on the advertising and
marketing of this event and help cover some of the larger
overhead costs of production. Without the support of
organizations like this as well as our fans and sponsors we would
simply not be able to produce these events or the series at all. In
the 3 seasons Raise Em Rank has had we have seen the
numbers for kids ages 6-16 competing in rough stock events in
both 4H and high school more than double. And while we are not
the only ones contributing to this surge of new contestants, I do
believe we have played a large part in advancement of the
official sport of South Dakota, Rodeo.

aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Minutes
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
July 11, 2023
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Mayor Everson at 2:01 PM.
SEA Committee members present: Mayor Everson, Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, Kevin
Nelson, Jon Hart, Doug Greenway, Bryan Dixon, and Jim Johnston.
SEA Committee members absent: Cory Aadland, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave
Helleloid, and Tim Smith.
Others present: Stephanie Ellwein, Johanna Allen, and Aaron Hieb.
2. Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Committee reviewed applications
for grant funding. The following applications were presented and considered:
A. South Dakota Women's State Softball Tournament
Date: July 29th-30th, 2023; Contact: Kathy Axsom; Grant Request: $5,000
• Kathy Axsom, Mitchell Women's Slow Pitch Softball Area Commissioner, presented and
shared information about the submitted grant application for the South Dakota Women's
State Softball Tournament. The grant request is for $5,000, of which $2,500 would go to
the State Association for fees/expenses to host this state tournament. The grant request
would also go towards hotel rooms for umpires, meals for umpires, and field/diamond
maintenance. The local association does not profit from hosting a state tournament.
There is a total of $10,000 in expenses to host a state tournament. The State
Association pays $3,500 of these fees, which covers the umpire expenses. The last time
Mitchell hosted a Women's State Softball Tournament was eight years ago (2015). This
year there are an estimated 50 women's teams that would participate in the state
tournament. The biggest expense when hosting a state tournament is hotel rooms for
umpires ($3,000). The last few years, the tournament has been held in Sioux Falls.
Each year there is an East and West host city/site. This year the East is hosted in
Mitchell and the West is hosted in Aberdeen.
Motion: Motion was made by Kevin Nelson to award $3,000 and seconded by Doug Greenway.
All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
B. South Dakota State Amateur Baseball Tournament
Date: August 2nd-13th, 2023; Contact: Jim Johnston; Grant Request: $5,000
• Jim Johnston, Mitchell Baseball Association, presented and shared information about
the submitted grant application for the South Dakota State Amateur Baseball
Association. There will be 37 teams over the course of 12 days. An estimated 12,000
people come to Mitchell for this tournament. The grant request of $5,000 would be used
for the following: meals for the commissioners, old-timers-game social, hotel rooms for
the PA announcer, workers, and field maintenance. It has always been hard to
determine how many hotel rooms are sold during the tournament. The State Amateur

--- PAGE 1 OF 4 ---


Baseball Tournament is a win-win for many entities, such as: a fundraiser for the
Mitchell Baseball Association, Exchange Club of Mitchell with concessions, and the city
of Mitchell.
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to award $5,000 and seconded by Bryan Dixon.
Jim Johnston abstained from voting. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
C. South Dakota Planners Association Annual Conference
Date: October 24th-26th, 2023; Contact: Brandi Hanten; Grant Request: $3,000
• Karen Wegleitner presented the submitted grant application on behalf of the South
Dakota Planners Association. There is an annual conference hosted in a different city
each year. This year's conference will be hosted at the Highland Conference Center in
Mitchell, SD. The conference will also be hosting and utilizing social events at The Back
40 and Blarney's. They are estimating 75 attendees for the conference. Brandi Hanten,
Vice President of the South Dakota Planners Association, joined midway through the
presentation via conference phone to provide budget/financials to the committee.
Membership dues and registration fees provide income for the SDPA to cover expenses
for hosting the annual conference. The grant amount request would be used to cover
food, speaker(s) costs, and Highland Conference Center rental fees.
Motion: Motion was made by Bryan Dixon to award $1,500 and seconded by Jon Hart. All
members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Kevin Nelson to approve the previous minutes as presented,
seconded by Bryan Dixon. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of July 6th, 2023. Total Fund Balance of
$70,072.52. There are five committed items/events where the checks have not been written.
Current Available Fund Balance of $23,572.52. Collections in June (for May records) were
$20,406.00 and there are two hotels that are past due and have not submitted their collections.
Also, there is still one hotel past due for collection in May (for April records). YTD comparison
for collections were: down 2.7% from 2022, up 7.8% from 2021, up 37.6% from 2020, up 8.7%
from 2019, and up 4.4% from 2018.
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to approve the financial report as presented,
seconded by Jon Hart. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Updates/Evaluation Forms/Financials
There were no items submitted at this time.
6. Other Items
Aaron reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee:
A. SEA Banners on Display
South Dakota United States Bowling Congress Jamboree (June 9th-10th, 2023)
• Two SEA feather banners were set up at The Village Bowl.

--- PAGE 2 OF 4 ---


South Dakota Golf Association Two-Man Championship (June 10th-11th, 2023)
• A SEA square banner was set up on the patio of the south entrance to the clubhouse at
Lakeview Golf Course.
South Dakota 93rd Annual VFW State Convention (June 15th-18th, 2023)
• SEA feather banners were set up outside, at the entrance of the Davison County Fair
Grounds Building.
Harve Johnston/Bryan Wilson Memorial Baseball Tournament (June 17th, 2023)
• SEA square banners were set up on the fence by the entrances into the two complexes
(D-G & H-K).
Beers & Gears Mountain Bike Race (June 24th, 2023)
• A SEA square banner was set up at Sandy Beach (Lake Mitchell), which was
headquarters for the race.
B. Discussion about SEA guidelines/policy regarding distribution of approved grant funds.
Aaron reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee:
SEA QR Code Hotel Survey
The Sports & Events Authority QR Code Hotel Survey was implemented back in February. The
SEA QR Code flyer is created each time a submitted grant application event is approved. The
flyer contains the name of the event/organization, the QR Code enlarged in the center, and the
logo of the respective event/organization at the bottom. The SEA QR Code flyer is included in
the approval award email to the event main contact. In the email, it is recommended/suggested
that they provide the QR Code and/or flyer in the registration packet and to the teams, coaches,
and participants/attendees of the respective event. Also, it states in the email that the QR Code
results are not the final amount of hotel/motel rooms sold, but that it is still the responsibility of
event staff to determine the most accurate estimation of hotel/motel rooms sold during the
entirety of the event and include that number on the post-event Evaluation Form. During SEA
banner set-up, Aaron will post a handful of flyers throughout the facility or venue. There have
currently been 15 events that have been provided with the SEA QR Code flyer. Most of the
results usually have about a handful of participation per event. Two events in particular, DWU
Futsal Indoor Classic (15) and the South Dakota United State Bowling Congress Jamboree (21)
were able to gather the most participation on the SEA QR Code Hotel Survey. Those who
participate in the SEA QR Code Hotel Survey provide feedback about where participants are
staying/lodging during their time in Mitchell for the SEA funded/assisted event. There are
instances where we receive positive hotel feedback about why the individual(s) chose to stay at
the respective hotel. That specific survey is then emailed out to the respective hotel manager,
so they can provide the positive feedback with their staff. Last of all, the exposure that the
Mitchell Sports & Events Authority receives from participation in the SEA QR Code Hotel
Survey is beneficial and will hopefully result in future events choosing Mitchell because of the
grant opportunity.

--- PAGE 3 OF 4 ---


• The committee had some discussion about ways to improve the participation rates and
effectiveness of the SEA QR Code Hotel Survey and flyer.
SEA Funding Matrix
Aaron provided an opportunity for the committee to ask any follow-up questions about the
funding matrix that was presented at the last meeting. Also, once the committee is in Executive
Session to discuss and determine appropriate funding for the submitted grant applications,
Aaron will share the funding matrix amount and how it was determined for each respective
grant application.
7. Next Meeting Date
Mayor Everson set the next meeting date for Tuesday, August 8th, 2023, @ 2 PM, in the City
Hall - Council Chambers.
8. Adjournment
There being no further business to discuss.
Meeting adjourned by: Mayor Everson at 3:02 PM.

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Minutes  
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                  September 12, 2023 
                                            
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Mayor Everson @ 2:00 PM. 
 
SEA Committee members present:  Mayor Everson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin Nelson, Jon 
Hart, Doug Greenway, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, and Tim Smith. 
 
SEA Committee members absent: Jill Larson, Cory Aadland, Bryan Dixon, and Jim Johnston. 
 
 Others present: Stephanie Ellwein, Alex Heidinger, and Aaron Hieb. 
2. Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Committee reviewed applications 
 for grant funding. The following applications were presented and considered: 
A. USA State COED Softball Tournament 
Date: September 8th-10th, 2023; Contact: Kathy Axsom; Grant Request: $7,500 

     • The grant application was submitted on August 8th, 2023. 
     • The grant application and additional documents were shared via email with the SEA 
       Advisory Committee. 
     • An email vote was conducted on August 10th, 2023, since the tournament was 
       completed by the September Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee meeting. 
     • A grant amount of $2,500 was approved. 

 
Motion: Motion was made by Kevin Nelson to award $2,500 and seconded by Doug Greenway. 
 All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
B. Palace City 8ball Open 
Date: October 27th-28th, 2023; Contact: Jason Long; Grant Request: $3,000 

     • Jason Long presented the submitted SEA Grant Application for the Mitchell Pool Players 
       and the Palace City 8ball Open. The event will be held on October 27th-28th, downtown, 
       at Dr. Lucky's and Big Dummies. Currently, there are 19 registrations with an initial cap 
       of 32. They are looking to increase the cap to 48. Out of the current registrants, 60%-
       70% are from out of town with participants from Sioux City, Sioux Falls, Western IA, 
       Aberdeen, Yankton, Pierre, and Black Hills. No elimination on the first day of the 
       tournament. They have over 20 sponsors. All sponsorship money goes into the prize 
       fund and that is what the SEA Grant request amount would be used towards increasing 
       the prize fund. They have no expenses, D&E Vending is providing the pool tables at no 
       cost, and Dr. Lucky's and Big Dummies are hosting the event at no cost. Currently, they 
       have $3,000 in prize fund money. 

 
Motion: Motion was made by Kevin Nelson to award $500 and seconded by Jon Hart. 8 
 members voted 'Aye', 1 member voted 'Nay, and the motion passed. 
C. Hoop City Classic 2023 
Date: December 28th-30th, 2023; Contact: Ernie Kuyper; Grant Request: $15,000 

     • Ernie Kuyper presented the submitted SEA Grant Application via phone conference. 
       The entire Hoop City Classic will be held in Mitchell on December 28th-30th, 2023, from 
       high school games to youth tournaments. There will be a total of 27 high school games, 
       9 per day. The Corn Palace/Armory and DWU facilities will be utilized for the basketball 
       games. The requested SEA Grant funds would be utilized for facility rental, official fees, 
       travel, and marketing/advertising. The youth tournament will include teams from Rapid 
       City, Sioux Falls, and Minnesota, with anywhere from 25 to 75 youth teams staying 
       overnight. It all depends on how the transition goes this year.   

 
The Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee agreed to table the Hoop City 
Classic 2023 SEA Grant Application until the October 10th meeting to determine if proper 
SEA Revenue has been generated that matches or exceeds the total amount of funding 
 requests. 
D. Dakota Oyate Challenge 
Date: January 25th-27th, 2024; Contact: James Ferrell; Grant Request: $15,000 

     • James Ferrell, Jesse Bien, George Erdahl, and Tom Cameron, DOC Board members, 
       were in attendance, with Jesse Bien presenting the submitted SEA Grant Application for 
       the Dakota Oyate Challenge. Jesse shared a breakdown of hotel numbers for all 8 
       schools, their meal budget, and the officials hotel rooms with the committee. The Dakota 
       Oyate Challenge is a three-day basketball tournament on January 25th-27th, 2024, 
       which includes cultural games (hand games and archery), a college fair, and vendor 
       booths. The DOC is hoping for an increase in attendance with the venue change from 
       Huron to Mitchell, and Mitchell having an increase in numbers and quality of hotel 
       rooms. This will be the 39th year for the boys and 35th for the girls. Local vendors will 
       be used for printing programs and flyers, and Sun Gold Sports for apparel and awards. 
       The biggest expense will be the officials hotel room costs. The DOC Board voted 
       unanimously to approve moving this event to Mitchell and the Corn Palace.      

 
The Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee agreed to table the Dakota Oyate 
Challenge SEA Grant Application until the October 10th meeting to determine if proper 
SEA Revenue has been generated that matches or exceeds the total amount of funding 
 requests. 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Kevin Nelson to approve the previous minutes as presented, 
 seconded by Doug Greenway. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of September 1st, 2023. Total Fund Balance of 
$64,740.02. There are four committed items/events where the checks have not been written. 
Current Available Fund Balance of $20,740.02. Collections in August (for July records) were 
$26,833.50 and all hotels/motels have submitted their collections. None past due. YTD 
comparison for collections were: down 4.3% from 2022, down 0.5% from 2021, up 34.1% from 
2020, down 0.1% from 2019, and down 0.1% from 2018. 
 
Motion: Motion was made by Jon Hart to approve the financial report as presented, seconded 
 by Kevin McCardle. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
5. Updates/Evaluation Forms/Financials 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms with Financials and SEA Survey that were 
 submitted from past SEA funded events with the SEA Committee. 
A. Evaluation Forms w/Financials 
South Dakota United States Bowling Congress Jamboree (June 9th-10th, 2023) 

     • The total spectator attendance for the event was 258. This count was derived from the 
       number of registrations. The number of hotel/motel room nights sold for the jamboree 
       was 70. The hotels/motels contacted were: Comfort Inn & Suites and Hampton Inn. Next 
       year's jamboree will be held in Rapid City. The awarded funds ($3,000) were used to 
       help offset the cost of food and lodging for the attendees, which reduced registration 
       fees. Net loss for the jamboree of $670.48. 

 
South Dakota Golf Association Two-Man Championship (June 9th-11th, 2023) 

     • The total spectator attendance for the championship was 100. This count was derived 
       from the number of spectators following each group and their caddies. There were 208 
       golfers. The number of hotel/motel room nights sold for the championship was 55. The 
       hotels/motels contacted were: Comfort Inn & Suites, Days Inn, Hampton Inn, and Kelly 
       Inn & Suites. The awarded funds ($1,000) were used to supply complimentary food for 
       the golfers and provide lunches for the volunteers. 

 
MAC Triathlon (June 10th, 2023) 

     • The total spectator attendance for the event was 135. There were 95 total participants, 
       which is an increase from the 53 participants in 2022. The number of hotel/motel room 
       nights sold for the event was 4-5. The hotels/motels contacted were: Comfort Inn & 
       Suites, Quality Inn, and Super 8 Motel. The awarded funds ($2,200) were used to pay 
       for the timing system. Profit of $2,854.77, which some funds were donated to Dakota 
       Riptide. A total of $1,400 was donated.  

 
Department of South Dakota VFW 93rd Annual State Convention (June 15th-18th, 2023) 

     • The total attendee count was 239, which is an increase from the 172 attendees in 2022. 
       The number of hotel/motel room nights sold for the convention was 219. The hotel/motel 
       contacted was: Kelly Inn & Suites. The awarded funds ($3,130) were used to pay for the 
       4-H convention building. Profit of $5,167.12 will be used to help veterans, military 
       members, and their families. 

 
B. SEA Survey(s) 
Organization: Mitchell Area Community Triathlon; Main Contact: Emily Hohn; Date 
Completed: 8/29/2023 
     • Aaron Hieb reviewed the survey with the committee and has reached out to Cody 
       Denne providing the City of Mitchell support for their events and involvement in their 
       planning process for the Fat Tire Bike Race. There is a common theme for bike and 
       running events, and most overnight stays are at campgrounds, but these are great 
       events to host and brings a variety of participants to Mitchell. 

 
6. Other Items 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee: 
A. SEA Banners on Display 
South Dakota State & High Plains Territorial Cowboy Fast Draw Championships (August 8th-
13th, 2023) 

     • Set up one SEA banner at the Mitchell Gun Club. 

 
Raise Em Rank Bull Riding Series Finals (September 8th-9th, 2023) 

     • Set up two SEA feather banners on the Corn Palace arena stage, one on each end. 
     • Brief discussion about the event from the past weekend and Doug Greenway provided 
       ticketing/attendance numbers to the committee. 

 
USA State COED Softball Tournament (September 9th-10th, 2023) 

     • A SEA square banner was hung on the fence by the entrance going into Cadwell Sports 
       Complex Fields D-G. 

 
B. "Thank You" Card 
 Mitchell Area Community Triathlon Committee - MAC Triathlon (June 9th-10th, 2023) 
7. Next Meeting Date 
Mayor Everson set the next meeting date for Tuesday, October 10th, 2023, @ 2 PM, in the City 
 Hall - Council Chambers. 
8. Adjournment 
There being no further business to discuss. 
 
 Meeting adjourned by: Mayor Everson @ 3:16 PM.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events

***Application must be received no less than 45

The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The

will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.

must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.

Briefly describe the

into the community with
this event?
The purpose of this event is to promote the game of pool. Almost
everyone at some point or time has played a game of pool in
their life… some more than others. We have a great pool playing
community across the state and inviting them to our community
to compete against each other not only strengthens the game by
promoting it, but also brings these players and families to Mitchell
for a weekend to see what we have to offer as a community.
Describe your event.
Be sure to include who,
what, where, when,
and how activities will
take place.
Our event is an OPEN pool tournament… meaning that anyone
is able to pay the entry fee, register for the event and play. Our
tournament is split into 2 parts… the first portion of the
tournament will be a true double elimination format where we
play the field down to a “finals” bracket. We then do a redraw of
the players in the finals bracket and they compete against each
other in a single elimination format until we have a winner.
The tournament will be held October 27&28th at both big
dummy’s and dr Lucky’s bars. D&E vending is proving and
setting up the pool tables for the event. We will also be having a
secondary tournament that Saturday afternoon for the players
that have been eliminated from the main tournament to keep
them in town and at the establishments playing. We are
anticipating the event to be completed that Saturday evening by
midnight… however depending on the final number of entries, we
may have to finish on Sunday.
What geographic areas
are you bringing event
participants from?
We will be having pool players coming from all across the state
of South Dakota and the Sioux City area as well.

Our goal is to promote the game of pool and bringing high level
competition of the game back to Mitchell. It has been long
overdue since there was a pool tournament here in town that
drew in the top players from across the state.
Explain how your grant
request would be used
to promote tourism in
Mitchell? Note the

event if the request for
funding were denied.
The grant funding if approved will be given directly back to the
players in the tournament through the prize pool. With the event
being held downtown, it will allow the players and/or their families
to explore Mitchell’s downtown businesses in between matches
and during downtime.
The resulting impact if denied would be less added money to the
prize fund, which could result in some players deciding not to
make the trip to our community.
Note…. We do not have an event budget because there really is
no expenses to take care of. The host sites are not charging us
and we do not have rental fees for the tables. I have enclosed a
list of the sponsors we have for the event so far and the amount
of money they are contributing. ALL of the sponsors money is
going into the players prize fund.
We do not have the flyers completed at this time, but we are in
the process of designing them and getting them ready for print to
distribute across the state to the pool community.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Minutes
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
August 8, 2023
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:02 PM.
SEA Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Kevin Nelson, Doug Greenway, LaRee
Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston.
SEA Committee members absent: Mayor Everson, Jill Larson, Cory Aadland, Jon Hart, and
Bryan Dixon.
Others present: Johanna Allen, Stephanie Ellwein, and Aaron Hieb.
2. Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Committee reviewed applications
for grant funding. The following applications were presented and considered:
A. Raise Em Rank Bull Riding Series Finals
• Dillon Swanson, Raise Em Rank, presented the submitted SEA grant application for the
Raise Em Rank Bull Riding Series Finals to be hosted at the Corn Palace on September
8th-9th, 2023. There are 5-6 events throughout the year that qualify for points towards
the series finals. They take the top 20 bullriders for the open division and about 30 youth
bullriders from ages 6 to 16 that compete from about 6 or 7 different states. Typically, a
new event like this takes about 3 years for it to develop to where the members of the
community know what the event is about and what to expect. Dillon will work on
establishing an awards banquet to be held on Sunday morning, which, in turn, would
keep people in Mitchell an extra night longer. Event estimation for hotel/motel rooms
sold is a very conservative number of approximately 200 hotel/motel rooms sold for the
entirety of the event. A typical show lasts around 2 1/2 hours.
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to award $5,000 and seconded by Kevin Nelson.
7 members voted 'Aye', 1 member voted 'Nay', and the motion passed.
B. South Dakota State Disc Golf Championship
• Ronnie Hoeltzner with Mitchell Disc Golf presented the submitted SEA Grant Application
for the South Dakota State Disc Golf Championship to be held in Mitchell at Dry Run
Creek on September 22nd-24th, 2023. Currently there are 124 participants signed up
with a cap of 150. The majority of players are from outside of Mitchell, (currently 20
registered from Mitchell), including seven different states and Canada. Saturday night
they will utilize The Back 40 and provide two comedians for entertainment for the
participants. Last year, the state tournament was held in Spearfish. The annual rotation
includes Yankton, Spearfish, Aberdeen, and Sioux Falls. Any profit from the event goes
towards improvements made to Dry Run Creek Park.
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to award $1,550 and seconded by LaRee Rumbolz. All

--- PAGE 1 OF 3 ---


members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
C. Palace City Kiwanis Half Marathon & Relay
• Paula, Julie, and Crystal, Kiwanis Club of Mitchell, presented the submitted SEA Grant
Application for the Palace City Kiwanis Half Marathon & Relay, 5K & 10K, which will be
held on October 1st, 2023, in Mitchell. This will be the 6th annual race. The money that
has been raised goes towards the inclusive playground that has been built at the
Kiwanis Woodlot Park. Currently there are 113 runners registered. They expect to hit
200 runners. The run starts at 7:30 AM on Sunday, October 1st. Runners come from the
following: 23 runners come from more than 80 miles away, 9 from out of state
(Minnesota, Iowa, and Nebraska) as well as New Mexico, New York, and two from
California. The SEA logo is put on the awards and will provide space for a banner to be
put on the Corn Palace balcony. Many compliments about the route that is used for the
event, which has led to repeat runners. Profit that is raised from the event does not
necessarily go back into the event, but back into the community. The next project will be
to add some more small libraries throughout town in the local parks.
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to award $2,000 and seconded by Doug
Greenway. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Jim Johnston to approve the previous minutes as presented,
seconded by Tim Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of August 3rd, 2023. Total Fund Balance of
$66,079.02. There are four committed items/events where the checks have not been written.
Current Available Fund Balance of $22,079.02. Collections in July (for June records) were
$23,706.00 and there are four hotels that are past due and have not submitted their collections.
Also, there is still one hotel past due for both May and June collections. YTD comparison for
collections were: down 5.3% from 2022, up 1.3% from 2021, up 36.4% from 2020, up 2.6%
from 2019, and down 0.4% from 2018.
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to approve the financial report as presented,
seconded by Dave Helleloid. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Updates/Evaluation Forms/Financials
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form with financials that was submitted from past
SEA funded events to the SEA Committee.
A. Evaluation Form w/Financials
Beers & Gears Mountain Bike Race (June 24th, 2023)
• The total spectator attendance for the event was 65. This count was derived from the
number of volunteers and family members watching the event. There were 61 riders,
which is an increase from the 42 riders in 2022. The number of hotel/motel rooms sold
for the tournament was 1. The hotel/motel contacted was: Hampton Inn. There were
quite a few people who used Lake Mitchell Campground and Betts Campground - they
liked the locations for their bikes. QR Code feedback was that they offered it to riders,
but unsure if any scanned and participated in the hotel survey. The awarded funds
($2,000) were used to pay for the timing system. Profit of $1,697.07 will be used to

--- PAGE 2 OF 3 ---


donate STRIDER BIKES to local preschools - we have so far donated 12 to First
Lutheran and will be making a donation back to Palace City Preschool as well.
6. Other Items
Aaron reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee:
A. SEA Banners on Display
South Dakota State A Youth Baseball Tournament (July 14th-16th, 2023)
• Two SEA square banners were set up, one on each fence at the entrances into the two
complexes (D-G & H-K).
South Dakota Women's State Softball Tournament (July 29th-30th, 2023)
• Two SEA square banners were set up, one on each fence at the entrances into the two
complexes (D-G & H-K).
South Dakota State Amateur Baseball Tournament (August 2nd-13th, 2023)
• A SEA square banner was put on the fence by the entrance to Drake Field. Also,
Mitchell Baseball Association put up two Sports Authority banners at Cadwell Stadium,
one on each side of the grandstands towards the top of the fence.
B. Discussion about Special Olympics lanyards for the upcoming State Fall Classic and
State Basketball Tournament.
Darryl Nordquist, Special Olympics - South Dakota, attended the SEA Committee meeting to
assist with discussion regarding the request of 1,000 lanyards for the Special Olympics to be
used at the State Fall Classic in September 2023 and State Basketball in March 2024.
C. Discussion with Special Olympics regarding hotel rooms.
Darryl Nordquist, Special Olympics - South Dakota, attended the SEA Committee meeting to
share feedback he has received from delegations regarding the hotel room rates for Special
Olympics events that are held in Mitchell.
7. Next Meeting Date
Kevin McCardle set the next meeting date for Tuesday, September 12th, 2023, @ 2 PM, in the
City Hall - Council Chambers.
8. Adjournment
There being no further business to discuss.
Meeting adjourned by: Kevin McCardle at 3:16 PM.

--- PAGE 3 OF 3 ---
