documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Minutes 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                   October 10, 2023 
                                            
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:00 PM. 
 
SEA Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, Kevin Nelson, Doug 
Greenway, Bryan Dixon, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim 
Johnston. 
 
SEA Committee members absent: Mayor Everson, Cory Aadland, and Jon Hart. 
 
 Others present: Stephanie Ellwein and Aaron Hieb. 
 
2. Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations. The following application, Pheasants Forever Banquet 
Grant Application, was presented to the committee, since the Hoop City Classic and Dakota 
 Oyate Challenge were presented during the September meeting. 
 
A. Pheasants Forever Banquet 
Date: October 20th, 2023; Contact: Kevin Bruscher; Grant Request: $1,500 
 

     • Kevin Bruscher presented the submitted SEA Grant Application for the Pheasants 
       Forever Banquet, which is requesting $1,500. They had just wrapped up their annual 
       youth hunt at the old Rooster Roost Ranch, which had seventeen participants (12-13 
       year old hunters). During this hunt, they shoot trap, feed the hunters lunch, and hunt 
       the released pheasants. Pheasants Forever works to improve the walk-in land habitat 
       around the Mitchell area, within a 35-mile radius. Pheasants Forever Banquet is the 
       Friday night before the pheasant opener at the Corn Palace. The requested $1,500 
       would be earmarked towards the youth hunting experience in the Mitchell area. 
       Pheasants Forever budgets $12,000 to $15,000 specifically for youth hunting and 
       provides equipment (shells and targets). 

 
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to award $1,500 earmarked towards the youth 
hunt and youth hunting experience in the Mitchell area. Seconded by Bryan Dixon. All 
 members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
B. Hoop City Classic 2023 
Date: December 28th-30th, 2023; Contact: Ernie Kuyper; Grant Request: $15,000 
 
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to award $10,000 and seconded by Jim 
 Johnston. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
C. Dakota Oyate Challenge 
Date: January 25th-27th, 2024; Contact: Jesse Bien/James Ferrell; Grant Request: $15,000 
 
Motion: First motion was made by LaRee Rumbolz to award $5,000. Motion failed due to lack 
of a second. The second motion was made by Dave Helleloid to award $2,500. Also, Dave 
included in the motion that he would take the lead and reach out to Mitchell hotels/motels to 
find and comp 11 rooms for DOC officials for four nights during the event. Kevin Nelson 
 seconded the motion. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Bryan Dixon to approve the previous minutes as presented, 
 seconded by LaRee Rumbolz. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of October 3rd, 2023. Total Fund Balance of 
$73,633.02. There are four committed items/events where the checks have not been written. 
Current Available Fund Balance of $29,633.02. Collections in September (for August records) 
were $26,449.50 and there are 3 hotels/motels that have not submitted their collections. YTD 
comparison for collections were: down 4.7% from 2022, down 2.5% from 2021, up 28.7% from 
2020, down 2.8% from 2019, and down 2.4% from 2018. 
 
Also, Aaron shared that the $1.00 collection will end on October 31st and hotels will have the 
voluntary option to collect and submit the $1.00 until the end of 2023. Any revenue submitted 
from the voluntary collection will go to the Sports & Events Authority. All hotels/motels will be 
notified of this via email & letter by the end of next week. 
 
Request to have the City of Mitchell Finance Office provide and send out a letter to 
hotels/motels stating the new, adjusted hotel occupancy tax, so hotels/motels can reach out to 
their Third Party software companies to make the necessary changes before January 1st, 
2024. 
 
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to approve the financial report as presented, 
 seconded by Tim Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form with Financials and SEA Surveys that 
 were submitted from past SEA funded events to the SEA Committee. 
 
A. Evaluation Forms w/Financials 
Mitchell Baseball Youth Tournaments (May 6th, June 2nd-3rd, June 17th, & July 14th-16th, 
2023) 

     • The total spectator count was unsure, but many teams and people attended three of 
       the tournaments. The number of hotel/motel room nights sold was uncertain. The 
       hotels/motels contacted were: Days Inn and Hampton Inn. The awarded funds ($6,000) 
       were used to pay the umpires and for the hospitality area. Net profits for each 
       tournament were as follows: Early Bird = $3,700; Teener Tourney = $50; 
       Harves/Wilson = $1,525; and State Youth = $39,656. 
     • A brief discussion was had about the host site for the upcoming State Youth, State 
       Amateur, and State Legion Baseball Tournaments (2024-2026). 

 
 
B. SEA Survey(s) 
Organization: South Dakota Music Education Association; Main Contact: Mike Bossman; 
Date Completed: 9/19/2023 
 
 Organization: 301 Rodz; Main Contact: Steve Bren; Date Completed: 9/25/2023 
 
6. Other Items 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee: 
 
A. SEA Banners on Display 
South Dakota State Disc Golf Championship (September 22nd-24th, 2023) 

     • Set up two SEA feather banners at Dry Run Creek Disc Golf Course, right behind hole 
       #1 tee pad. 

 
Special Olympics South Dakota State Fall Classic (September 22nd-24th, 2023) 

     • Set up one SEA square banner on the fence by the entrance to the east complex 
       (Fields D-G) at Cadwell for Friday's competitions. 

 
OutKasts Car Show (September 22nd-24th, 2023) 

     • A SEA square banner was displayed next to the registration booth. 

 
Palace City Kiwanis Half Marathon, Relay, 10K, & 5K (October 1st, 2023) 

     • Set up one SEA feather banner in front of the Corn Palace on Main Street, next to the 
       START and FINISH line of the event. 

 
 
B. Upcoming Events 

     • ACT presents 'On Golden Pond' (October 13th-15th, 2023) 
     • VFW Post 2750 Chili Cook-Off (October 14th, 2023) 
     • Pheasants Forever Banquet (October 20th, 2023) 
     • Breed Life Foundation Event (October 21st, 2023) 
     • Heartland Guild Quilt Show (October 21st-22nd, 2023) 
     • South Dakota Planners Association Annual Conference (October 24th-26th, 
       2023) 
     • Palace City 8ball Open (October 27th-28th, 2023) 
     • Palace City Robot Rumble (November 4th, 2023) 
     • DWU Theatre presents 'Hedda Gabler' (November 3rd-5th / 10th-12th, 2023) 
     • Veteran's Day Celebration (November 11th, 2023) 

 
 

     • For a full list of events, visit https://www.mitchellsd.com/events/calendar/2023-10-01 

 
 

     • Aaron Hieb shared information about upcoming DWU Soccer Youth Tournaments. The 
       annual DWU Indoor Futsal Classic is set for February 23rd-25th, 2024. Also, DWU 
       Soccer is going to host a U10-U18 youth soccer tournament at the Pepsi Soccer 
       Complex in May of 2024. 

 
 
7. Next Meeting Date 
Kevin McCardle set the next meeting date for Tuesday, November 14th, 2023, @ 2 PM, in the 
 City Hall - Council Chambers. 
 
8. Adjournment 
There being no further business to discuss. 
 
 Meeting adjourned by: Kevin McCardle @ 3:02 PM.

The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.

will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Minutes
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
September 12, 2023
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Mayor Everson @ 2:00 PM.
SEA Committee members present: Mayor Everson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin Nelson, Jon
Hart, Doug Greenway, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, and Tim Smith.
SEA Committee members absent: Jill Larson, Cory Aadland, Bryan Dixon, and Jim Johnston.
Others present: Stephanie Ellwein, Alex Heidinger, and Aaron Hieb.
2. Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Committee reviewed applications
for grant funding. The following applications were presented and considered:
A. USA State COED Softball Tournament
Date: September 8th-10th, 2023; Contact: Kathy Axsom; Grant Request: $7,500
• The grant application was submitted on August 8th, 2023.
• The grant application and additional documents were shared via email with the SEA
Advisory Committee.
• An email vote was conducted on August 10th, 2023, since the tournament was
completed by the September Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee meeting.
• A grant amount of $2,500 was approved.
Motion: Motion was made by Kevin Nelson to award $2,500 and seconded by Doug Greenway.
All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
B. Palace City 8ball Open
Date: October 27th-28th, 2023; Contact: Jason Long; Grant Request: $3,000
• Jason Long presented the submitted SEA Grant Application for the Mitchell Pool Players
and the Palace City 8ball Open. The event will be held on October 27th-28th, downtown,
at Dr. Lucky's and Big Dummies. Currently, there are 19 registrations with an initial cap
of 32. They are looking to increase the cap to 48. Out of the current registrants, 60%-
70% are from out of town with participants from Sioux City, Sioux Falls, Western IA,
Aberdeen, Yankton, Pierre, and Black Hills. No elimination on the first day of the
tournament. They have over 20 sponsors. All sponsorship money goes into the prize
fund and that is what the SEA Grant request amount would be used towards increasing
the prize fund. They have no expenses, D&E Vending is providing the pool tables at no
cost, and Dr. Lucky's and Big Dummies are hosting the event at no cost. Currently, they
have $3,000 in prize fund money.
Motion: Motion was made by Kevin Nelson to award $500 and seconded by Jon Hart. 8
members voted 'Aye', 1 member voted 'Nay, and the motion passed.

--- PAGE 1 OF 4 ---


C. Hoop City Classic 2023
Date: December 28th-30th, 2023; Contact: Ernie Kuyper; Grant Request: $15,000
• Ernie Kuyper presented the submitted SEA Grant Application via phone conference.
The entire Hoop City Classic will be held in Mitchell on December 28th-30th, 2023, from
high school games to youth tournaments. There will be a total of 27 high school games,
9 per day. The Corn Palace/Armory and DWU facilities will be utilized for the basketball
games. The requested SEA Grant funds would be utilized for facility rental, official fees,
travel, and marketing/advertising. The youth tournament will include teams from Rapid
City, Sioux Falls, and Minnesota, with anywhere from 25 to 75 youth teams staying
overnight. It all depends on how the transition goes this year.
The Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee agreed to table the Hoop City
Classic 2023 SEA Grant Application until the October 10th meeting to determine if proper
SEA Revenue has been generated that matches or exceeds the total amount of funding
requests.
D. Dakota Oyate Challenge
Date: January 25th-27th, 2024; Contact: James Ferrell; Grant Request: $15,000
• James Ferrell, Jesse Bien, George Erdahl, and Tom Cameron, DOC Board members,
were in attendance, with Jesse Bien presenting the submitted SEA Grant Application for
the Dakota Oyate Challenge. Jesse shared a breakdown of hotel numbers for all 8
schools, their meal budget, and the officials hotel rooms with the committee. The Dakota
Oyate Challenge is a three-day basketball tournament on January 25th-27th, 2024,
which includes cultural games (hand games and archery), a college fair, and vendor
booths. The DOC is hoping for an increase in attendance with the venue change from
Huron to Mitchell, and Mitchell having an increase in numbers and quality of hotel
rooms. This will be the 39th year for the boys and 35th for the girls. Local vendors will
be used for printing programs and flyers, and Sun Gold Sports for apparel and awards.
The biggest expense will be the officials hotel room costs. The DOC Board voted
unanimously to approve moving this event to Mitchell and the Corn Palace.
The Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee agreed to table the Dakota Oyate
Challenge SEA Grant Application until the October 10th meeting to determine if proper
SEA Revenue has been generated that matches or exceeds the total amount of funding
requests.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Kevin Nelson to approve the previous minutes as presented,
seconded by Doug Greenway. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of September 1st, 2023. Total Fund Balance of
$64,740.02. There are four committed items/events where the checks have not been written.
Current Available Fund Balance of $20,740.02. Collections in August (for July records) were
$26,833.50 and all hotels/motels have submitted their collections. None past due. YTD
comparison for collections were: down 4.3% from 2022, down 0.5% from 2021, up 34.1% from
2020, down 0.1% from 2019, and down 0.1% from 2018.

--- PAGE 2 OF 4 ---


Motion: Motion was made by Jon Hart to approve the financial report as presented, seconded
by Kevin McCardle. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Updates/Evaluation Forms/Financials
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms with Financials and SEA Survey that were
submitted from past SEA funded events with the SEA Committee.
A. Evaluation Forms w/Financials
South Dakota United States Bowling Congress Jamboree (June 9th-10th, 2023)
• The total spectator attendance for the event was 258. This count was derived from the
number of registrations. The number of hotel/motel room nights sold for the jamboree
was 70. The hotels/motels contacted were: Comfort Inn & Suites and Hampton Inn. Next
year's jamboree will be held in Rapid City. The awarded funds ($3,000) were used to
help offset the cost of food and lodging for the attendees, which reduced registration
fees. Net loss for the jamboree of $670.48.
South Dakota Golf Association Two-Man Championship (June 9th-11th, 2023)
• The total spectator attendance for the championship was 100. This count was derived
from the number of spectators following each group and their caddies. There were 208
golfers. The number of hotel/motel room nights sold for the championship was 55. The
hotels/motels contacted were: Comfort Inn & Suites, Days Inn, Hampton Inn, and Kelly
Inn & Suites. The awarded funds ($1,000) were used to supply complimentary food for
the golfers and provide lunches for the volunteers.
MAC Triathlon (June 10th, 2023)
• The total spectator attendance for the event was 135. There were 95 total participants,
which is an increase from the 53 participants in 2022. The number of hotel/motel room
nights sold for the event was 4-5. The hotels/motels contacted were: Comfort Inn &
Suites, Quality Inn, and Super 8 Motel. The awarded funds ($2,200) were used to pay
for the timing system. Profit of $2,854.77, which some funds were donated to Dakota
Riptide. A total of $1,400 was donated.
Department of South Dakota VFW 93rd Annual State Convention (June 15th-18th, 2023)
• The total attendee count was 239, which is an increase from the 172 attendees in 2022.
The number of hotel/motel room nights sold for the convention was 219. The hotel/motel
contacted was: Kelly Inn & Suites. The awarded funds ($3,130) were used to pay for the
4-H convention building. Profit of $5,167.12 will be used to help veterans, military
members, and their families.
B. SEA Survey(s)
Organization: Mitchell Area Community Triathlon; Main Contact: Emily Hohn; Date
Completed: 8/29/2023

--- PAGE 3 OF 4 ---


• Aaron Hieb reviewed the survey with the committee and has reached out to Cody
Denne providing the City of Mitchell support for their events and involvement in their
planning process for the Fat Tire Bike Race. There is a common theme for bike and
running events, and most overnight stays are at campgrounds, but these are great
events to host and brings a variety of participants to Mitchell.
6. Other Items
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee:
A. SEA Banners on Display
South Dakota State & High Plains Territorial Cowboy Fast Draw Championships (August 8th-
13th, 2023)
• Set up one SEA banner at the Mitchell Gun Club.
Raise Em Rank Bull Riding Series Finals (September 8th-9th, 2023)
• Set up two SEA feather banners on the Corn Palace arena stage, one on each end.
• Brief discussion about the event from the past weekend and Doug Greenway provided
ticketing/attendance numbers to the committee.
USA State COED Softball Tournament (September 9th-10th, 2023)
• A SEA square banner was hung on the fence by the entrance going into Cadwell Sports
Complex Fields D-G.
B. "Thank You" Card
Mitchell Area Community Triathlon Committee - MAC Triathlon (June 9th-10th, 2023)
7. Next Meeting Date
Mayor Everson set the next meeting date for Tuesday, October 10th, 2023, @ 2 PM, in the City
Hall - Council Chambers.
8. Adjournment
There being no further business to discuss.
Meeting adjourned by: Mayor Everson @ 3:16 PM.

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                  November 14, 2023 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:00 PM. 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Kevin Nelson, Cory Aadland, 
LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston. 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Mayor Everson, Jill Larson, Doug Greenway, 
Bryan Dixon, and Dave Helleloid. 
 
 Others present: Johanna Allen, Stephanie Ellwein, and Aaron Hieb. 
 
2. Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed 
 applications for grant funding. The following applications were presented and considered: 
 
A. Dakota Riptide Invite 
Date: December 1st-3rd, 2023; Contact: Jason Wede; Grant Request: $6,000 

     • Jason Wede and Rob Schelske presented the submitted SEA Grant Application for the 
       Dakota Riptide Invite, which is requesting $6,000. The Dakota Riptide swimteam in 
       Mitchell currently has 60+ swimmers. They have a new coach in Christian Fossum. 
       The Dakota Riptide Invite is a 3-day meet that begins at 6 pm Friday night and goes 
       through Sunday. Historically, they have had 250-300 swimmers at past meets. 
       Requested funds would be used to provide a high quality hospitality room for officials, 
       pool/facility rent, and pay for hotels to accommodate officials for the weekend.  

 
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to award $3,750 and seconded by Cory Aadland. All 
 members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
B. Hanson Classic - Girls & Boys 
Date: Girls - January 13th, 2024 & Boys - January 20th, 2024; Contact: Jim Bridge; Grant 
Request: $3,000 ($1,500 ea.) 

     • Jim Bridge presented the submitted SEA Grant Application via conference phone to the 
       SEA Advisory Committee. The Hanson Classics have been going on for 40+ years. 
       The classics (Girls & Boys) bring in 16 different schools/teams, Class A & Class B for 
       each classic, which consists of 8 or 9 games for each classic. The big attraction is 
       being able to play in the Corn Palace. The requested $3,000 would be used for the 
       hospitality room for the officials, workers, and media personnel. Profit from the event is 
       used towards scholarships that they offer to schools that apply for student/athletes. 
       The estimation of hotel room nights sold is about 100 per weekend.   

 
Motion: Motion was made by Jim Johnston to award $3,000 and seconded by LaRee 
 Rumbolz. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the previous minutes as presented, 
 seconded by Kevin Nelson. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of November 7th, 2023. Total Fund Balance of 
$70,416.02. There are four committed items/events where the checks have not been written. 
Current Available Fund Balance of $26,416.02. Collections in October (for September records) 
were $25,450.50 and all hotels/motels have submitted their collections. No outstanding 
collections. YTD comparison for collections were: down 3.5% from 2022, down 1.2% from 
2021, up 27.4% from 2020, down 1.6% from 2019, and down 1.5% from 2018. 
 
Also, Aaron shared that on Monday, November 6th, the City of Mitchell Finance Office mailed 
a letter to hotels/motels stating the new, adjusted hotel occupancy tax effective January 1st, 
2024. Stephanie shared information about the $1.00 collection for the pool of $1,000,000 has 
been met and that the remaining collections for 2023 would go towards Sports & Events 
Authority Revenue.  
 
Motion: Motion was made by Jim Johnston to approve the financial report as presented, 
 seconded by Tim Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
There were no Evaluation Forms with Financials submitted. Aaron Hieb reviewed the following 
SEA Survey that was submitted from a past SEA funded organization/event to the SEA 
 Advisory Committee. 
 
A. SEA Survey(s) 
Organization: South Dakota Planners Association; Main Contact: Amber Vogt; Date 
 Completed: 11/7/2023 
 
6. Other Items 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following items with the SEA Advisory Committee: 
 
A. SEA Banners on Display 
Pheasants Forever Banquet (October 20th, 2023) 
     • Set up one SEA feather banner in the entrance area of the Corn Palace. 

 
South Dakota Planners Association Annual Conference (October 24th-26th, 2023) 

     • Set up two SEA feather banners at the Highland Conference Center in the 
       Benelli/Winchester Room. 

 
Palace City 8ball Open (October 27th-28th, 2023) 

     • Hung one SEA square banner on the southside of the fence by Dr. Lucky's patio area. 

 
 
B. "Thank You" Card 
 Palace City 8ball Open (October 27th-28th, 2023) 
 
C. Upcoming Events 

     • Mitchell Main Street Informational Meeting (November 14th, 2023) 
     • Holiday Arts Christmas Show (November 17th-18th, 2023) 
     • DWU Women's & Men's Basketball 
     • CASA'S Got Talent (November 18th, 2023) 
     • Startz and Endz Presents - Rowan Grace LIVE! (November 18th, 2023) 
     • Mitchell 5k Turkey Trot (November 23rd, 2023) 
     • Christmas at the Palace & Parade of Lights (November 28th, 2023) 
     • Not a Silent Night (December 1st, 2023) 
     • Coney Island Christmas (December 8th-10th, 2023) 

 
 

     • For a full list of events, visit Mitchell Area Chamber of Commerce - Events Calendar 

 
 
7. Next Meeting Date 
Kevin McCardle set the next meeting date for Tuesday, December 12th, 2023, @ 2 PM in the 
 City Hall - Council Chambers. 
 
8. Adjournment 
There being no further business to discuss. 
 
 Meeting adjourned by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:37 PM.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Minutes
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
October 10, 2023
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:00 PM.
SEA Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, Kevin Nelson, Doug
Greenway, Bryan Dixon, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim
Johnston.
SEA Committee members absent: Mayor Everson, Cory Aadland, and Jon Hart.
Others present: Stephanie Ellwein and Aaron Hieb.
2. Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations. The following application, Pheasants Forever Banquet
Grant Application, was presented to the committee, since the Hoop City Classic and Dakota
Oyate Challenge were presented during the September meeting.
A. Pheasants Forever Banquet
Date: October 20th, 2023; Contact: Kevin Bruscher; Grant Request: $1,500
• Kevin Bruscher presented the submitted SEA Grant Application for the Pheasants
Forever Banquet, which is requesting $1,500. They had just wrapped up their annual
youth hunt at the old Rooster Roost Ranch, which had seventeen participants (12-13
year old hunters). During this hunt, they shoot trap, feed the hunters lunch, and hunt
the released pheasants. Pheasants Forever works to improve the walk-in land habitat
around the Mitchell area, within a 35-mile radius. Pheasants Forever Banquet is the
Friday night before the pheasant opener at the Corn Palace. The requested $1,500
would be earmarked towards the youth hunting experience in the Mitchell area.
Pheasants Forever budgets $12,000 to $15,000 specifically for youth hunting and
provides equipment (shells and targets).
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to award $1,500 earmarked towards the youth
hunt and youth hunting experience in the Mitchell area. Seconded by Bryan Dixon. All
members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
B. Hoop City Classic 2023
Date: December 28th-30th, 2023; Contact: Ernie Kuyper; Grant Request: $15,000
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to award $10,000 and seconded by Jim

seconded the motion. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.

Motion: Motion was made by Bryan Dixon to approve the previous minutes as presented,
seconded by LaRee Rumbolz. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of October 3rd, 2023. Total Fund Balance of
$73,633.02. There are four committed items/events where the checks have not been written.
Current Available Fund Balance of $29,633.02. Collections in September (for August records)
were $26,449.50 and there are 3 hotels/motels that have not submitted their collections. YTD
comparison for collections were: down 4.7% from 2022, down 2.5% from 2021, up 28.7% from

Also, Aaron shared that the $1.00 collection will end on October 31st and hotels will have the
voluntary option to collect and submit the $1.00 until the end of 2023. Any revenue submitted

notified of this via email & letter by the end of next week.

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                  December 12, 2023 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:01 PM. 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, Cory Aadland, 
Doug Greenway, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston. 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Mayor Bob Everson, Kevin Nelson, Bryan 
Dixon, and LaRee Rumbolz. 
 
 Others present: Johanna Allen 
 
2. Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentation by applicant. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed an 
 application for grant funding. The following application(s) was presented and considered: 
 
A. SoDak 16 Volleyball 
Date: November 7th, 2023; Contact: Cory Aadland; Grant Request: $650 

     • Cory Aadland shared information about the submitted grant application. Mitchell and 
       the Corn Palace hosted two games of the SoDak 16 Volleyball on November 7th. Also, 
       Doug Greenway shared that the attendance numbers were good, just over 700 in ticket 
       sales and a good night for concessions. The grant request is for $650 to cover the 
       Corn Palace rent. 

 
Motion: Motion was made by Jim Johnston to approve $650 and seconded by Tim Smith. 
Cory Aadland abstained from voting. The remaining seven members voted 'Aye' and the 
 motion passed. 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
 presented, seconded by Cory Aadland. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Doug Greenway reviewed the Financial Report as of December 6th, 2023. Total Fund Balance 
of $71,662.02. There are four committed items/events where the checks have not been 
written. Current Available Fund Balance of $27,662.02. Collections in November (for October 
records) were $20,103.00 with one hotel that has not submitted collections. YTD comparison 
for collections were: down 5.9% from 2022, down 2.9% for 2021, up 21.9% for 2020, 
down 3.6% from 2019, and down 3.4% for 2018. 
 
Motion: Motion was made by Emily Liedtke to approve the financial report as presented and 
 seconded by Jim Johnston. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
Doug Greenway reviewed the following Evaluation Forms with Financials and SEA Surveys 
 that were submitted from past SEA funded events to the SEA Committee: 
 
A. Evaluation Forms w/Financials 
South Dakota State & High Plains Regional Cowboy Fast Draw Shoot (August 8th-13th, 2023) 

     • The total spectator count was 100+. There were 80 participants/shooters. The number 
       of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 148, but they also had campers at the site, 
       Bed & Breakfast lodgings, etc. The hotels/motels contacted were: AmericInn, 
       CoachLight Motel, Comfort Inn & Suites, Holiday Inn Express, Kelly Inn and Quality 
       Inn. This event will be changing the dates for next year's shoot to September 11th-
       15th, 2024, to "piggyback" with Nebraska's state shoot. The awarded funds ($3,000) 
       were used for the Sports & Events Authority special shoot, where all funds were paid 
       directly back to the shooters. Net profit for the event was $1,426.22, which will be used 
       to cover various expenses for their local club, including charities. 

 
OutKasts Car Show powered by The 301 Rodz (September 22nd-24th, 2023) 

     • The total spectator count was 500. There were 50 participants. The number of total 
       hotel/motel room nights sold was 12. The hotels/motels contacted were: CoachLight 
       Motel, Corn Palace Inn, Days Inn, Rodeway Inn, Siesta Motel, and Thunderbird Lodge. 
       The awarded funds ($1,500) were used to purchase awards, fliers, and magnets. Net 
       profit for the event was $896.40, which will be used towards next year's show. 

 
Special Olympics South Dakota Fall Classic (September 22nd-24th, 2023) 

     • The total spectator count was 1,600. There were 800 participants/athletes. The number 
       of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 360. The hotels/motels contacted were: 
       Comfort Inn & Suites, Hampton Inn, and Kelly Inn. This event will take place in Rapid 
       City next year and Mitchell will be host to State Basketball in 2024 & 2025, with the Fall 
       Classic returning in 2026. The awarded funds ($10,000) were used towards expenses 
       related to the event. Net profit for the event was $3,788.22, which will be used to pay 
       for staffing and to cover some of the delegations expenses. 

 
South Dakota Planners Association Annual Conference (October 24th-26th, 2023) 

     • The total spectator/participant count was 85. The number of total hotel/motel room 
       nights sold was 124. The hotels/motels contacted were: Comfort Inn & Suites and 
       Hampton Inn. This event has an annual rotation schedule and will be taking place in 
       Box Elder in September 2024. The awarded funds ($1,500) were used to pay for the 
       event space rental. Net profit for the event was $1,405.49, which will be used to further 
       invest in our membership, which includes outreach and resources to further educate 
       our City and County Planners in South Dakota. 

 
Palace City 8ball Open (October 27th-29th, 2023) 

     • The total spectator count was estimated to be between 50-75. There were 62 players. 
       The number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was between 30-35. The 
       hotels/motels contacted were: Days Inn, Motel 6, Quality Inn, and Super 8 Motel. This 
       event is tentatively planned to be hosted the first weekend in October 2024. The 
       awarded funds ($500) were added to the prize fund that was awarded to players. No 
       profit was made.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

2. Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed
applications for grant funding. The following applications were presented and considered:
A. Dakota Riptide Invite
Date: December 1st-3rd, 2023; Contact: Jason Wede; Grant Request: $6,000
• Jason Wede and Rob Schelske presented the submitted SEA Grant Application for the
Dakota Riptide Invite, which is requesting $6,000. The Dakota Riptide swimteam in
Mitchell currently has 60+ swimmers. They have a new coach in Christian Fossum.
The Dakota Riptide Invite is a 3-day meet that begins at 6 pm Friday night and goes
through Sunday. Historically, they have had 250-300 swimmers at past meets.
Requested funds would be used to provide a high quality hospitality room for officials,
pool/facility rent, and pay for hotels to accommodate officials for the weekend.
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to award $3,750 and seconded by Cory Aadland. All
members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
B. Hanson Classic - Girls & Boys
Date: Girls - January 13th, 2024 & Boys - January 20th, 2024; Contact: Jim Bridge; Grant
Request: $3,000 ($1,500 ea.)
• Jim Bridge presented the submitted SEA Grant Application via conference phone to the
SEA Advisory Committee. The Hanson Classics have been going on for 40+ years.
The classics (Girls & Boys) bring in 16 different schools/teams, Class A & Class B for

--- PAGE 1 OF 3 ---


each classic, which consists of 8 or 9 games for each classic. The big attraction is
being able to play in the Corn Palace. The requested $3,000 would be used for the
hospitality room for the officials, workers, and media personnel. Profit from the event is
used towards scholarships that they offer to schools that apply for student/athletes.
The estimation of hotel room nights sold is about 100 per weekend.

January 9th, 2024, SEA Advisory Committee Meeting Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                    January 9, 2024 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Mayor Everson @ 2:00 PM. 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Everson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin 
Nelson, Doug Greenway, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, and Tim Smith. 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Jill Larson, Cory Aadland, Bryan Dixon, and 
Jim Johnston. 
 
 Others present: Johanna Allen, Stephanie Ellwein, and Aaron Hieb. 
 
2. Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed 
 applications for grant funding. The following application(s) were presented and considered: 
 
A. Palace Ice Festival 
Date: January 12th-14th, 2024; Contact: Brian Bultje; Grant Request: $3,000 

     • Brian Bultje presented the grant application for the 8th Annual Palace Ice Festival. The 
       event currently has 104 entries with skaters from Pierre, Sioux Falls, Rapid City, and 
       Wyoming. The USA certified judges come from California, New Mexico, and two from 
       Minnesota. The team accountant is coming from Rapid City. There is about the same 
       number of skaters as last year, for the fifty-six events that are going on throughout the 
       event. The biggest expense for the event are the judges, providing meals and hotels. 
       Profits go back into the program and providing clinics throughout the season. There is 
       no gate fee, but they did raise the entry fee. The majority of the skaters and spectators 
       stay overnight for one night. 

 
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to approve $750 and seconded by LaRee 
 Rumbolz. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
B. US Paralympic Hockey Camp 
Date: January 17th-21st, 2024; Contact: Dan Brennan; Grant Request: $3,500 

     • Dave Tronnes presented the grant application for the USA Paralympic Sled Hockey 
       Team Camp. Prior to the presentation, we shared a couple of short video clips to 
       familiarize everyone with sled hockey. Dan Brennan is the Director of USA Hockey, 
       which is a non-profit 501c3. The USA Olympic National Sled Hockey Team, winning 4 
       gold medals and 5 world championships. They will be in Mitchell for 4 days with two a 
       day practices. On Saturday, the Olympic team will scrimmage the Siouxland Sled 
       Team based out of Sioux Falls. They will contribute over 100 hotel room nights and van 
       rental from Iversons. The team will arrive on the 17th and leave on the 21st. Typically, 
       this event is hosted in a big city down south.  

 
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve $3,500 and seconded by Kevin McCardle. 
 All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
C. DWU/Culvers Girls & Boys High School Basketball Classic 
Date: February 9th-10th, 2024; Contact: Brad Bartscher; Grant Request: $5,000 

     • Brad Bartscher and Jason Christensen attended the SEA meeting with Jason 
       Christensen presenting the DWU/Culvers Girls & Boys High School Basketball Classic 
       Grant Application. This will be the 15th year for the boys and 9th year for the girls. 
       There are basically 10 teams/schools out of the 32 that are predicted to provide 
       overnight stays. Scheduling is done so that the further away teams will play either an 
       earlier game or later game. The first game will start at 10 AM on Friday. The grant 
       request would be used for refs and table workers. The profits made from this event are 
       put in a fundraising account, with a majority of the profits going towards athletic 
       scholarships. 

 
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to approve $3,000 and seconded by Kevin 
 Nelson. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
D. DWU Annual Indoor Futsal Winter Classic 
Date: February 23rd-25th, 2024; Contact: Nicolas Reinhard; Grant Request: $2,500 

     • Coach Reinhard & Coach Hakari attended the committee meeting, with Coach 
       Reinhard presenting the DWU Annual Indoor Futsal Winter Classic Grant Application. 
       This is the second year for both Coach Reinhard & Coach Hakari. The objective in the 
       first couple years regarding this event was to build the numbers/teams back to where it 
       was about 5 years ago with former coach Clayton Glasgow. There will be teams from 
       SD, ND, MN, and NE. One of the unexpected costs of last year's event was the 
       championship medals. The biggest expense last year was the referee costs, which this 
       year they are certifying their student-athletes to reduce these costs by almost half. The 
       grant request would be used for the outsourced costs such as: custodians, referee 
       fees, certification costs, and food.  
     • Coach Reinhard shared information about the work in progress on hosting a summer 
       youth soccer tournament at the Pepsi-Cola Soccer Complex. Tentative date of May 
       24th-25th. 

 
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to approve $2,500 and seconded by Kevin 
 McCardle. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
E. Combat Veterans Motorcycle Association Comedy Night 
Date: March 16th, 2024; Contact: Kim Hamer; Grant Request: $2,000 

     • Grant application contact did not answer. Aaron received an email from Kim Hamer, 
       that Aaron did not see until after the meeting that her allotted time she blocked off from 
       work was up. 
     • Grant application tabled and added to the February 13th, 2024 SEA Committee 
       meeting agenda. 

 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
 presented, seconded by Kevin McCardle. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the Financial Report as of January 5th, 2024. Total Fund Balance of 
$87,292.02. There are five committed items/events where the checks have not been 
written. Current Available Fund Balance of $42,642.02. Collections in December (for 
November records) were $17,824.00 with three hotels/motels that have not submitted 
collections. YTD comparison for collections were: down 4.5% from 2022, down 1.8% for 2021, 
up 24.3% for 2020, down 2.3% from 2019, and down 2.9% for 2018. 
 
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to approve the financial report as presented 
 and seconded by LaRee Rumbolz. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms with Financials that were submitted from 
 past SEA funded events to the SEA Committee: 
 
A. Evaluation Forms w/Financials 
South Dakota Disc Golf Championship (September 22nd-24th, 2023) 

     • The event exceeded expectations. Total spectator count was 20-30. There were 100 
       participants. The number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 50ish. The 
       hotels/motels contacted were: Corn Palace Inn, Holiday Inn Express, and Thunderbird 
       Lodge. The awarded funds ($1,500) were used for porta potties, trophies, signage, 
       park closure and insurance certificate fees. No net profit. 

 
Palace City Kiwanis Half Marathon & Relay, 5K & 10K (October 1st, 2023) 

     • The event was hosted above expectations, runner registrations were up about 20% this 
       year, and they appreciate the Sports & Events Authority's continued support of the 
       event. Total spectator count was 400+. There were 225 participants. The number of 
       total hotel/motel room nights sold was 40. The hotels/motels contacted were: 
       AmericInn, Days Inn, and Kelly Inn. The awarded funds ($2,000) were used for the 
       race medals. Net profit for the event was $6,928.44, which will be used for Kiwanis 
       Woodlot Park improvements, scholarships, Girls on the Run, Abbott House, First 
       Responder Blanket Project, and other children's initiatives. 

 
Dakota Riptide Invite (December 1st-3rd, 2023) 

     • The event met expectations. Total spectator count was 550. There were 282 
       swimmers. The number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 65. The hotels/motels 
       contacted were: Comfort Inn & Suites, Hampton Inn, and Holiday Inn Express. The 
       awarded funds ($3,750) were used to pay for the pool and sound system rent, lifeguard 
       wages, and other facility expenses. Net profit for the event was $16,349.97, which will 
       be used to help fund the swim team and keep our monthly dues affordable. 

 
 
6. Other Items 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee: 
 
A. SEA Banners on Display 
Hoop City Classic (December 28th-30th, 2023) 

     • Mitchell Sports & Events Authority banner is permanently hung in the Hospitality Room. 
       Also, the Mitchell Sports & Events Authority logo is published on page 2 of the digital 
       program, as well as displayed on the digital billboards throughout the Corn Palace. 

 
 
B. Upcoming Events 

     • MHS Girls & Boys Basketball 
     • DWU Women's & Men's Basketball 
     • Hanson Girls Classic (Saturday, January 13th) 
     • USA National Paralympic Sled Hockey Team Camp (Wednesday, January 17th-
       Saturday, January 20th) 
     • Comedy Night at the Highland (Friday, January 19th) 
     • Hanson Boys Classic (Saturday, January 20th) 
     • MHS Friend de Coup Show Choir Community Show (Tuesday, January 23rd) 
     • Dakota Oyate Challenge (Thursday, January 25th-Saturday, January 27th) 
     • Winter Crazy Days! (Friday, January 26th-Sunday, January 28th) 
     • Mitchell Virtual Job Fair (Wednesday, January 31st) 
     • South Dakota No-Till Association - Mitchell Soil Health Event (Thursday, February 8th) 

 
Full list of events - Mitchell Chamber Events Calendar 
 
 *BOLD - Awarded Sports & Events Authority Grant funding. 
 
7. Next Meeting Date 
Aaron Hieb shared the next meeting date for Tuesday, February 13th, 2024, @ 2 PM - City 
 Hall, Council Chambers. 
 
8. Adjournment 
There being no further business to discuss. 
 
 Meeting adjourned by: Mayor Everson @ 3:02 PM.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

This event is a standard U.S. Figure Skating Nonqualifying Competition
I. COMPETITION OVERVIEW
The 8 th Annual Palace Ice Festival will be conducted in accordance with the rules and
regulations of U.S. Figure Skating, as set forth in the current rulebook, and/or current Compete
USA handbook as well as any pertinent updates that have been posted on the U.S. Figure Skating
website.
This competition is open to all eligible, restricted, reinstated or readmitted persons as defined
by the Eligibility Rules. Skaters must be a currently registered member of a U.S. Figure Skating
member club, Learn to Skate USA® member, a collegiate club or who is an individual member
in accordance with the current rulebook. For non-U.S. citizens, please refer to the rulebook for
more information.
II. ELIGIBILITY
Singles Excel and Well Balanced Events:
- 	Skaters must meet at least the minimum singles test requirements for the event’s level.
A skater’s singles test level may be higher than the minimum requirement.
o 	Skate Up: skaters may skate up one level higher than their highest singles test
level allows.
- 	Skaters may not register for an event level lower than allowed by their competitive
floor. An athlete’s competitive floor is set by one of the following scenarios:
o 	If an athlete has participated in the NQS series, the event level registered for in
the most recent NQS series will become the lowest level they may compete at in
any U.S. Figure Skating sanctioned event.
o 	If an athlete has participated in the Excel Series, the event level registered for in
the most recent Excel series will become the lowest level they may compete in
any Excel event. For Well Balanced and Specialty events the skater will be
permitted to register at one level lower than the “floor” set by their excel series
entry.
- 	Skaters are not permitted to enter an Excel and a Well Balanced event of the same type
and same level (example: Juvenile Girls Free Skate and Juvenile Girls Excel Free Skate) at
the same competition. However, they are permitted to enter an Excel and a Well
Balanced event of different types (example: Intermediate Women Short Program and
Intermediate Women Excel Free Skate).
- 	If an athlete, coach, parent and/or guardian needs assistance with confirming their
eligibility, email events@usfigureskating.org or refer to information sheet HERE.
Age restrictions/requirements:

--- PAGE 2 OF 11 ---


3
Updated 8/2/2023
Singles free skate events (well-balanced program) have the following requirements:
Juvenile: Girls – 12 years or younger; Boys – 13 years or younger
Open Juvenile: Girls – 13 years or older; Boys – 14 years or older
Intermediate must be under the age of 18
Adults must be 21 years or older
Skaters entering pre-juvenile and lower events will be divided as closely as possible by age
should the number of entries warrant more than one group.
Please note: Boys Pre-Juvenile and below: If not enough boys are registered to hold an event,
boys will skate with girls in Compulsory, Moves in the Field, and Showcase. They have the
option to compete with the girls for the non-IJS Free Skate events or skate an exhibition.
ADULT EVENTS:

● 	Class I: 21 years through 35 years

● 	Class IV: 56 years through 65 years
● 	Class V: 66 years and older
Age classes for all solo free dance and solo pattern dance events:
● 	Young Adult/Class I/II: 18 years through 45 years
● 	Class III/IV/V: 46 years and older
All age classes may be divided or combined depending on the number of entries and at the
discretion of the chief referee and/or the competition committee.
Adult 1-6, adult beginner, adult high beginner, adult pre-bronze and adult bronze
program/free skate events that meet Adult Competition Series guidelines are offered at this
competition. Adult Competition Series participants must submit a photo, scanned copy, email
attachment or screenshot of the results sheet to adultcompetitionseries@gmail.com by the
deadline published in the most recent Adult Competition Series Handbook to receive credit
and series points.
All other singles and partner events (such as Adults, Pairs, Ice Dance):
- 	Skaters must meet the minimum test requirements for the events level, but not exceed
the maximum permissible test requirement.

OUR COMMUNITY:
U.S. Figure Skating is dedicated to fostering a culture of belonging and community that is
welcoming for all individuals. We are committed to championing diversity, equity and inclusion
and understand its value in combating discrimination and challenging inequalities necessary to
develop champions both on and off the ice. We are actively working toward developing
equitable practices and policies that foster safety and empower all individuals to authentically
pursue their unique path in all areas of our sport. We stand firmly on the belief that our
members are the most important asset to our organization and that our differences are
meaningful and strengthen our sport. We believe that skating is for everyone.
NON-DISCRIMINATION:
U.S. Figure Skating commits in policy, principle and practice to sustain a non-discriminatory
approach on and off the ice for all members. We strive to provide equal opportunity for all
despite their varied backgrounds, experiences and identities, and want all members to feel values
and respected at every level of organization. U.S. Figure Skating’s SkateSafe® Program received,
investigates and addresses allegations of discrimination or harassment throughout its
membership and the organization. Please refer to the SkateSafe® Program Handbook for further
definition of harassment, discrimination and abuse.
By attending this event, all participants are willingly committing to upholding U.S. Figure Skating’s
Code of Ethics (
GR 1.01) and Code of Conduct (
GR 1.02), as detailed within the U.S. Figure Skating
Rulebook.
To report a concern of discrimination or harassment to U.S. Figure Skating, please
visit www.USFigureSkating.org/SkateSafe or email SkateSafe@USFigureSkating.org.
COMPLIANCE:
For full details about participant compliance requirements, refer to the U.S. Figure Skating
SkateSafe® webpage: https://www.usfigureskating.org/skatesafe#compliance.
COACHES
To be an eligible coach at a nonqualifying competition, coaches must meet the applicable
compliance requirements and verified by U.S. Figure Skating. Coach compliance falls into two
categories, Coach Compliance (includes choreographers) and Learn to Skate USA® Instructor
Compliance. Details regarding compliance requirements can be found HERE. All compliance
requirements must be met at the time of check-in to access the competition, no exceptions.

--- PAGE 6 OF 11 ---


7
Updated 8/2/2023
Athletes age 18+ as of the competition start date who will be competing on a team (i.e., synchro,
ice dance, pairs, shadow dance, theatre, etc.) with at least one Minor Athlete must complete
SafeSport™ Training. *
Minor athletes who turn 18 mid-season are encouraged to seek parental consent to take the online
SafeSport™ Training early to avoid any disruptions in their ability to participate as the training is
required upon turning 18. The athlete will not be compliant until they have completed the training
and their Members Only portal reflects completion. Please email skatesafe@usfigureskating.org for
instructions or questions regarding parental consent.
III. REGISTRATION INFORMATION
Entry for all events will be thru EntryEeze. Fees and discounts for all events will be in EntryEeze.
Deadline for registration is December 16, 2023 at 23:59 CST. Deadlines are subject to change at
the discretion of the local organizing committee and any adjusted deadlines will be posted in
EntryEeze. Late entries will be accepted only at the discretion of the Competition Chief Referee
and will be assessed at $25.00 late entry fee. A fee of $25.00 will also be charged for any changes
to entries, competition level, age or events entered if requested after the December 16, 2023
deadline.
Compete USA events is $65 for the 1 st event per competitor and $35 for each additional event.
USFSA Non-Qualifying events is $105 for the 1 st event per competitor and $35 for each
additional event.
Payment via secure credit card payment will be made on EntryEeze at the time of registration. A
3.8% processing fee will be applied to all entries. Electronic entries paid with a successful credit
card transaction will be considered a valid entry. There will be an additional $50 fee for any credit
card entry that is disputed.
JUDGING SYSTEM
The 6.0 Majority Judging System will be used for all events except USFS Showcase which will be
Component Judging System (CJS) as noted in the table of events. There will be no IJS events.
MUSIC SUBMISSION/UPLOAD:
All individual skaters and skating teams must submit music electronically via EntryEeze by the music
deadline of December 31, 2023. Any music file submitted after the deadline will incur a $25 late fee.
Music submitted to EntryEeze by contestants will be deleted after the competition is complete.
Competitors must also have available a backup copy of their competition music on a cell phone
and it must be immediately available rink side whenever the skater competes. If the phone does
not have the standard round headset connector, an appropriate adapter, such as an Apple Lightning
connector or Samsung USB-C adapter is required to be attached. The phone should be presented
to the music person with the file ready to play, phone in airplane mode and volume turned to
maximum.

--- PAGE 7 OF 11 ---


8
Updated 8/2/2023
REFUND POLICY
Entry fees will not be refunded after entry deadline unless no competition exists or the event is
canceled. There will be no refunds for medical withdrawals. The online processing fees are not
refundable. Checks returned for non-sufficient funds and contested credit charges will be incur
a $50 fee. Payment of the fee will be required before the skater is allowed to participate in
practice ice or events.
LIABILITY:
U.S. Figure Skating, Learn to Skate USA®, Mitchell Figure Skating Club and the Mitchell Activity
Center accept no responsibility for injury or damage sustained by any participant in this
competition. This is in accordance with Rule 1600 of the official U.S. Figure Skating Rulebook.
IV. COMPETITION DETAILS
FACILITIES:
Mitchell Activities Center 	Rink Size: 85’ x 200’ with rounded ends.
1001 Minnesota St
Mitchell, SD 57301
LOCKER ROOMS & CHANGING AREAS
Locker rooms and changing areas at U.S. Figure Skating competitive events are for athletes
only and will be labeled with regard to specific use, and where identified, will be gender
specific. An exception can be made for athletes under 11 years old that will allow for one
parent of the same sex to assist their child immediately prior to and after their skating event(s).
Please review the Locker Room and Changing Area Policy in the SkateSafe® Handbook. Locker
room assignments will be available at check-in.
OFFICIAL WEBSITE & UPDATES:
Competition information and schedule will be posted on EntryEeze. An official bulletin board
will be maintained at the registration/check in desk. It is the responsibility of each competitor,
parent and coach to check the bulletin board frequently for any schedule changes and/or
additional information pertaining to the competition. Skaters should arrive 45 minutes prior to
the scheduled time of their events. A tentative schedule of events will be posted prior to the
competition.
The competition will utilize online results. Links to the results will be posted on the competition
bulletin board at the registration desk.
SCHEDULE
Competitors may be scheduled on any day or time during the announced dates of the
competition. The competition and practice ice schedule will be available after the close of
entries. All participants will be notified via email once available.

--- PAGE 8 OF 11 ---


9
Updated 8/2/2023
PRACTICE ICE:
Practice ice will be available for purchase on the EntryEeze competition website. It is suggested
that you reserve your practice ice when you register so that you will have first choice of times
once the schedule is posted online. You will choose the number of practice ice sessions you want
to reserve and pay for them at that time. Each skater will be allowed to reserve one session per
event registered. You will receive an email from EntryEeze with a PIN number in order to access
your practice ice records and select your sessions on a first come first served basis. Practice ice
cost will be $20/session. Any remaining open spots for practice ice will be available for purchase
at the registration desk during the competition for $25/session. All sessions are 20 minutes. No
music will be played during individual skater practice ice.
After the schedule has been posted and those that reserved practice ice have had the opportunity
to select their sessions, additional practice ice will be available for purchase at $25/session.
Practice ice for Mini Production Ensembles and Production Ensembles will be available for
purchase at $40/20 minutes per group. Music will be allowed. Time will be determined after
the close of registration of the competition.
Notification of competition and practice ice times will not be available by phone, mail, or
email. Skaters’ and Coaches’ schedules will be available via the web at the EntryEeze
competition website. Please check back often.
ONSITE CHECK-IN:
The Registration/Check-In Desk will be open one-half hour prior to start of scheduled events
which is dependent on entries. The registration desk will remain open during all individual
practice ice sessions and events. The Registration Desk is located inside the Toshiba Ice Rink
(north rink), located within the Mitchell Activity Center. Please register promptly upon arrival.
Registration will be your final confirmation of event(s) and competition time(s).
If you are participating in a role requiring compliance, please be sure to download or
print your compliance card to verify your compliance status on-site, if requested. If you
believe your compliance card does not accurately reflect your compliance status, please
contact skatesafe@usfigureskating.org at least 2 business days prior to the competition
for assistance.
AWARDS:
Awards will be provided for each event 1st -6 th place. Award ceremony will be held in the lobby
throughout the competition when results are finalized.
PHOTO/VIDEO:

TEST SESSION:

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
December 12, 2023
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:01 PM.
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, Cory Aadland,
Doug Greenway, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston.
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Mayor Bob Everson, Kevin Nelson, Bryan
Dixon, and LaRee Rumbolz.
Others present: Johanna Allen
2. Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentation by applicant. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed an
application for grant funding. The following application(s) was presented and considered:
A. SoDak 16 Volleyball
Date: November 7th, 2023; Contact: Cory Aadland; Grant Request: $650
• Cory Aadland shared information about the submitted grant application. Mitchell and
the Corn Palace hosted two games of the SoDak 16 Volleyball on November 7th. Also,
Doug Greenway shared that the attendance numbers were good, just over 700 in ticket
sales and a good night for concessions. The grant request is for $650 to cover the
Corn Palace rent.
Motion: Motion was made by Jim Johnston to approve $650 and seconded by Tim Smith.
Cory Aadland abstained from voting. The remaining seven members voted 'Aye' and the
motion passed.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented, seconded by Cory Aadland. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
Doug Greenway reviewed the Financial Report as of December 6th, 2023. Total Fund Balance
of $71,662.02. There are four committed items/events where the checks have not been

--- PAGE 1 OF 4 ---


written. Current Available Fund Balance of $27,662.02. Collections in November (for October
records) were $20,103.00 with one hotel that has not submitted collections. YTD comparison
for collections were: down 5.9% from 2022, down 2.9% for 2021, up 21.9% for 2020,
down 3.6% from 2019, and down 3.4% for 2018.
Motion: Motion was made by Emily Liedtke to approve the financial report as presented and
seconded by Jim Johnston. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys
Doug Greenway reviewed the following Evaluation Forms with Financials and SEA Surveys
that were submitted from past SEA funded events to the SEA Committee:
A. Evaluation Forms w/Financials
South Dakota State & High Plains Regional Cowboy Fast Draw Shoot (August 8th-13th, 2023)
• The total spectator count was 100+. There were 80 participants/shooters. The number
of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 148, but they also had campers at the site,
Bed & Breakfast lodgings, etc. The hotels/motels contacted were: AmericInn,
CoachLight Motel, Comfort Inn & Suites, Holiday Inn Express, Kelly Inn and Quality
Inn. This event will be changing the dates for next year's shoot to September 11th-
15th, 2024, to "piggyback" with Nebraska's state shoot. The awarded funds ($3,000)
were used for the Sports & Events Authority special shoot, where all funds were paid
directly back to the shooters. Net profit for the event was $1,426.22, which will be used
to cover various expenses for their local club, including charities.
OutKasts Car Show powered by The 301 Rodz (September 22nd-24th, 2023)
• The total spectator count was 500. There were 50 participants. The number of total
hotel/motel room nights sold was 12. The hotels/motels contacted were: CoachLight
Motel, Corn Palace Inn, Days Inn, Rodeway Inn, Siesta Motel, and Thunderbird Lodge.
The awarded funds ($1,500) were used to purchase awards, fliers, and magnets. Net
profit for the event was $896.40, which will be used towards next year's show.
Special Olympics South Dakota Fall Classic (September 22nd-24th, 2023)
• The total spectator count was 1,600. There were 800 participants/athletes. The number
of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 360. The hotels/motels contacted were:
Comfort Inn & Suites, Hampton Inn, and Kelly Inn. This event will take place in Rapid
City next year and Mitchell will be host to State Basketball in 2024 & 2025, with the Fall
Classic returning in 2026. The awarded funds ($10,000) were used towards expenses
related to the event. Net profit for the event was $3,788.22, which will be used to pay
for staffing and to cover some of the delegations expenses.
South Dakota Planners Association Annual Conference (October 24th-26th, 2023)
• The total spectator/participant count was 85. The number of total hotel/motel room
nights sold was 124. The hotels/motels contacted were: Comfort Inn & Suites and

--- PAGE 2 OF 4 ---


Hampton Inn. This event has an annual rotation schedule and will be taking place in
Box Elder in September 2024. The awarded funds ($1,500) were used to pay for the
event space rental. Net profit for the event was $1,405.49, which will be used to further
invest in our membership, which includes outreach and resources to further educate
our City and County Planners in South Dakota.
Palace City 8ball Open (October 27th-29th, 2023)
• The total spectator count was estimated to be between 50-75. There were 62 players.
The number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was between 30-35. The
hotels/motels contacted were: Days Inn, Motel 6, Quality Inn, and Super 8 Motel. This
event is tentatively planned to be hosted the first weekend in October 2024. The
awarded funds ($500) were added to the prize fund that was awarded to players. No
profit was made.
