documents.fileName: February 13th, 2024, Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Meeting Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                   February 13, 2024 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:00 PM. 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, Kevin Nelson, 
Cory Aadland, Doug Greenway, Bryan Dixon, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston. 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Mayor Everson, Jason Christensen, LaRee 
Rumbolz, and Emily Liedtke. 
 
 Others present: Stephanie Ellwein, Johanna Allen, and Aaron Hieb. 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed 
 applications for grant funding. The following application(s) were presented and considered: 
 
A. Cabin Fever Auction 
Date: February 23rd-24th, 2024; Contact: Ashley Coulter; Grant Request: $2,000 

     • Nick Coulter presented the grant application for the Buckin' Wild Ranch Cabin Fever 
       Auction, which will be held on February 23 & 24, 2024, at the Davison County 
       Fairgrounds. This event draws between 400–500 people to Mitchell for two or three 
       days. The grant request would go towards workers' wages, newspaper advertisements, 
       posters, and facility costs. They hire around 25 employees to help with the event, 
       including auctioneers, whom they pay $250 per day and provide hotel rooms for them.  

 
 
B. South Dakota Middle School All-State Band 
Date: March 1st-2nd, 2024; Contact: Holly Gage; Grant Request: $300 

     • Holly Gage, co-chair of SDMEA Middle School All State Band, presented the grant 
       application via conference phone for the South Dakota Middle School All-State Band. 
       This event includes 200 middle school students from all over the state. She anticipates 
       overnight stays for one or two nights. The students usually come with their 
       parents/families, so they make their own hotel/motel reservations. The grant request 
       would be spent locally, throughout Mitchell, to provide a Hospitality Room and snacks 
       for the band directors and students throughout the event. This event rotates to Mitchell 
       every other year with the exception of Middle School All State Band being in Mitchell 
       the next two years because of the great location. Middle School All State Jazz Band is 
       in Mitchell on a yearly basis.   

 
 
C. Show Choir Classic 
Date: March 16th, 2024; Contact: Angella Buenzow; Grant Request: $5,000 

     • Jayson Plamp presented the grant application for the Show Choir Classic. The Mitchell 
       Show Choir has about 75 participants. Show expenses are usually around $120,000 
       each year. One of the largest fundraisers is the Show Choir Classic. Currently, there 
       are 20 teams, which generates around 1,500 spectators as well. Teams competing 
       come from Omaha, Missouri, and Chicago. Currently, they have teams from Omaha, 
       Vermillion, Groton, Aberdeen, Sioux City, Hot Springs, Chicago, and Missouri. Their 
       budget for this particular event is $30,000. Their biggest line item expense is the 
       judges, which brings them to Mitchell and provides hotels as well. Last year attendance 
       was down because of winter weather and road closures.    

 
 
D. Combat Veterans Motorcycle Association Comedy Night 
Date: March 16th, 2024; Contact: Kim Hamer; Grant Request: $2,000 

     • Kim Hamer, public relations officer of CVMA for Eastern South Dakota, presented the 
       grant application via conference phone for the Combat Veterans Motorcycle 
       Association Comedy Night. The 3rd Annual CVMA Comedy Night will take place on 
       March 16th at the Highland Conference Center. Last year's event attendance was 
       greatly impacted by the winter weather. Attendees have come from Rapid City and 
       Luverne, MN. This year's event will team up with Helping with Horsepower, which 
       includes a group of veterans building a motorcycle together. CVMA is hosting their 
       monthly meeting in Mitchell as well.   

 
 
E. Knights of Columbus Special Olympics Banquet 
Date: March 23rd, 2024; Contact: Gene Kessler; Grant Request: $1,700 

     • Vince Boddicker presented the grant application for the Knights of Columbus Special 
       Olympics Banquet. The event will take place on March 23rd in St. John Paul II 
       Auditorium. This is the fourth time that the Knights of Columbus has hosted this 
       banquet since 2017. Currently, there are 785 athletes signed up for the banquet. They 
       will serve spaghetti and meatballs, garlic bread, water, and dilly bars from Dairy 
       Queen. The attendees will be served in about an hour and a half (5:30 PM to 7:00 PM). 
       Starting at 6 PM until 9 PM, there will be a DJ in the multipurpose room for a dance. 
       Their budget is a little over $4,500 which is all designated for food, and the school 
       donates the use of the facility and there is no profit being made from this banquet. 
       They utilize around 40 volunteers to host the banquet. 
 
 
F. Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament 
Date: April 12th-14th, 2024; Contact: Stacy Murtha; Grant Request: $4,000 

     • Stacy Murtha presented the grant application for the Lucky Devils Adult Hockey 
       Tournament. This will be the 13th year. Last year the event hosted 21 teams. 
       Currently, there are 19, possibly 20 teams. Teams come from 5 states (WI, MN, ND, 
       SD, IA, NE). This event brings over 300–400 players and families to Mitchell. Each 
       team gets one game a day. The biggest expenses are referees and ice time. The profit 
       made goes back into youth hockey for the Mitchell community. Sioux Falls has already 
       started an event like this and Watertown, with the new facility, is looking to start an 
       event like this in March. The grant request would help keep their expenses in check, so 
       they can continue to host this event in Mitchell. Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Non-Profit 
       was created as well. 

 
 
G. Shootout at the Lake 
Date: June 21st-22nd, 2024; Contact: Wade Musick; Grant Request: $20,000 

     • Tabled and added to the March 12th agenda. 

 
 
H. USA Sled Hockey Camp 
Date: January 17th-20th, 2024; Contact: Dave Tronnes; Grant Request: any additional 
support up to $1,250 

     • Dave Tronnes reached out to Aaron Hieb and the SEA Advisory Committee with a 
       request for any additional support to go along with the previously awarded $3,500. This 
       additional funding would go to the USA Paralympic Sled Hockey Team to help cover 
       some of the unplanned travel expenses due to the weather. 

 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Jim Johnston to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
 presented, seconded by Tim Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb and Stephanie Ellwein reviewed the Financial Report as of February 5th, 2024. 
This was the final financial report for the BID #2 - $1.50 Total Collections. Going forward, the 
financial report will show BID #4 - $2.00 Total Collections based on the $100,000 that has 
been budgeted by the BID #4 Board for Sports & Events Authority revenue/funding.  
 
The total revenue for 2023 was $106,518.50. This number is misleading because the last two 
months (November and December) of collections for the year included the entire $1.50 of the 
hotel occupancy tax, not just the $.50. Total Fund Balance of $78,250. There are now only 
three committed items/events, all Special Olympics, where the checks have not been written. 
These will carry over into the BID #4 Financials and be designated to come out of each 
respective years SEA Revenue budget. Current Available Fund Balance of $78,250. 
Collections in January (for December records) were $14,488.50 with ALL hotels/motels 
reporting. This was the second-highest collection for the month of December in the past eight 
years. YTD comparison for collections were: up 15.4% from 2023, up 6.4% for 2022, up 29.4% 
for 2021, down 11.4% from 2020, up 15.4% for 2019, and up 9.7% for 2018. 
 
The BID #4 Board met towards the end of January. They discussed and approved an SEA 
Revenue budget of $100,000 for 2024. Looking ahead to the March SEA Financials, 
collections will be submitted and collected in February for January records. This will be the 
$2.00 collection and 12 out of the 15 hotels/motels will submit collections. The Budget Inn, 
CoachLight Motel, and Siesta Motel have less than 28 rooms, so they were excluded from the 
BID #4 composition. If any of those 3 motels would like to continue to submit the collections, it 
would be considered a donation, similar to the Lake Mitchell Campground. 
 
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the financial report as presented and 
 seconded by Bryan Dixon. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms with Financials to the SEA Committee.  
 
Due to time constraints, Aaron suggested the committee review the SEA Survey that was 
submitted by D&E Music and Vending on behalf of Carol Steilen (Pink Ladies Darts) at their 
 convenience. 
 
A. Evaluation Form w/Financials 
South Dakota State Amateur Baseball Tournament (August 2nd-13th, 2023) 

     • The event was above expectations. There were 32 Class B teams and 5 Class A 
       teams. The number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 300 +. The hotels/motels 
       contacted were: Comfort Inn & Suites, Hampton Inn, and Holiday Inn Express Hotel & 
       Suites. Mitchell will be the host this year, 2024. It will be in Brandon in 2025 and back 
       in Mitchell in 2026. The awarded funds ($5,000) were used for hospitality purposes for 
       the commissioners, umpires, and tournament personnel. Profit from the tournament is 
       used to fund the Mitchell Baseball Association baseball operations and improvements 
       for Cadwell Park. 

 
Dakota Showdown Horse Trainer Challenge (August 11th-12th, 2023) 

     • The event itself went above expectations. There were quite a few challenges with the 
       vendors that made them feel unwelcome and unwanted. They booked the Horsemen's 
       Sports Arena and a month before were told they could no longer use their arena. The 
       new location they provided by Trail King did not go as planned, and it was a difficult 
       experience. The total spectator count was 200-250. There were 20 participants. The 
       number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 20-24. The hotels/motels contacted 
       were: CoachLight Motel, Kelly Inn & Suites, and Thunderbird Lodge. The awarded 
       funds ($1,000) were used to cover the lease of the location. Total profit of $334.73, 
       which went back to the support of the Gentle Spirit Horses Rescue. 

 
USA Paralympic Sled Hockey Team Camp (January 15th-21st, 2024) 

     • https://www.mitchellrepublic.com/opinion/letters/letter-the-economy-is-not-1  
     • The event exceeded expectations. The volunteers and Hotel/arena staff were all great. 
       Total spectator count was 85. There were 26 participants on the hockey team. The 
       number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 90. The hotel that the team utilized 
       was the Comfort Inn & Suites. The awarded funds ($3,500) were used to offset costs 
       for the arena rental and meals. 

 
 
B. SEA Survey(s) 

     • Organization: D&E Music and Vending; Main Contact: Carol Steilen; Date 
       Completed: 1/19/2024 

 
 
6. Other Items 
Due to time constraints, Aaron Hieb suggested the committee review the SEA Banners on 
Display at their convenience.  
 
Aaron shared briefly that Diane Royalty, on behalf of the Powderhorn Ranch Regulators, sent 
a 'Thank You' sponsor letter to the SEA Committee.  
 
Again, due to time constraints, Aaron suggested that the committee review the list of upcoming 
events at their convenience. They can always find a full list of events on the Mitchell Chamber 
Events Calendar and that any BOLD events on this list have been awarded SEA funding

DWU/Culver's Girls & Boys High School Basketball Classic (February 9th-10th, 2024)

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
January 9, 2024
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Mayor Everson @ 2:00 PM.
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Everson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin
Nelson, Doug Greenway, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, and Tim Smith.
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Jill Larson, Cory Aadland, Bryan Dixon, and
Jim Johnston.
Others present: Johanna Allen, Stephanie Ellwein, and Aaron Hieb.
2. Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed
applications for grant funding. The following application(s) were presented and considered:
A. Palace Ice Festival
Date: January 12th-14th, 2024; Contact: Brian Bultje; Grant Request: $3,000
• Brian Bultje presented the grant application for the 8th Annual Palace Ice Festival. The
event currently has 104 entries with skaters from Pierre, Sioux Falls, Rapid City, and
Wyoming. The USA certified judges come from California, New Mexico, and two from
Minnesota. The team accountant is coming from Rapid City. There is about the same
number of skaters as last year, for the fifty-six events that are going on throughout the
event. The biggest expense for the event are the judges, providing meals and hotels.
Profits go back into the program and providing clinics throughout the season. There is
no gate fee, but they did raise the entry fee. The majority of the skaters and spectators
stay overnight for one night.
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to approve $750 and seconded by LaRee
Rumbolz. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
B. US Paralympic Hockey Camp
Date: January 17th-21st, 2024; Contact: Dan Brennan; Grant Request: $3,500
• Dave Tronnes presented the grant application for the USA Paralympic Sled Hockey
Team Camp. Prior to the presentation, we shared a couple of short video clips to

--- PAGE 1 OF 5 ---


familiarize everyone with sled hockey. Dan Brennan is the Director of USA Hockey,
which is a non-profit 501c3. The USA Olympic National Sled Hockey Team, winning 4
gold medals and 5 world championships. They will be in Mitchell for 4 days with two a
day practices. On Saturday, the Olympic team will scrimmage the Siouxland Sled
Team based out of Sioux Falls. They will contribute over 100 hotel room nights and van
rental from Iversons. The team will arrive on the 17th and leave on the 21st. Typically,
this event is hosted in a big city down south.
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve $3,500 and seconded by Kevin McCardle.
All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
C. DWU/Culvers Girls & Boys High School Basketball Classic
Date: February 9th-10th, 2024; Contact: Brad Bartscher; Grant Request: $5,000
• Brad Bartscher and Jason Christensen attended the SEA meeting with Jason
Christensen presenting the DWU/Culvers Girls & Boys High School Basketball Classic
Grant Application. This will be the 15th year for the boys and 9th year for the girls.
There are basically 10 teams/schools out of the 32 that are predicted to provide
overnight stays. Scheduling is done so that the further away teams will play either an
earlier game or later game. The first game will start at 10 AM on Friday. The grant
request would be used for refs and table workers. The profits made from this event are
put in a fundraising account, with a majority of the profits going towards athletic
scholarships.
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to approve $3,000 and seconded by Kevin
Nelson. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
D. DWU Annual Indoor Futsal Winter Classic
Date: February 23rd-25th, 2024; Contact: Nicolas Reinhard; Grant Request: $2,500
• Coach Reinhard & Coach Hakari attended the committee meeting, with Coach
Reinhard presenting the DWU Annual Indoor Futsal Winter Classic Grant Application.
This is the second year for both Coach Reinhard & Coach Hakari. The objective in the
first couple years regarding this event was to build the numbers/teams back to where it
was about 5 years ago with former coach Clayton Glasgow. There will be teams from
SD, ND, MN, and NE. One of the unexpected costs of last year's event was the
championship medals. The biggest expense last year was the referee costs, which this
year they are certifying their student-athletes to reduce these costs by almost half. The
grant request would be used for the outsourced costs such as: custodians, referee
fees, certification costs, and food.
• Coach Reinhard shared information about the work in progress on hosting a summer
youth soccer tournament at the Pepsi-Cola Soccer Complex. Tentative date of May
24th-25th.
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to approve $2,500 and seconded by Kevin
McCardle. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.

--- PAGE 2 OF 5 ---


E. Combat Veterans Motorcycle Association Comedy Night
Date: March 16th, 2024; Contact: Kim Hamer; Grant Request: $2,000
• Grant application contact did not answer. Aaron received an email from Kim Hamer,
that Aaron did not see until after the meeting that her allotted time she blocked off from
work was up.
• Grant application tabled and added to the February 13th, 2024 SEA Committee
meeting agenda.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented, seconded by Kevin McCardle. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the Financial Report as of January 5th, 2024. Total Fund Balance of
$87,292.02. There are five committed items/events where the checks have not been
written. Current Available Fund Balance of $42,642.02. Collections in December (for
November records) were $17,824.00 with three hotels/motels that have not submitted
collections. YTD comparison for collections were: down 4.5% from 2022, down 1.8% for 2021,
up 24.3% for 2020, down 2.3% from 2019, and down 2.9% for 2018.
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to approve the financial report as presented
and seconded by LaRee Rumbolz. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms with Financials that were submitted from
past SEA funded events to the SEA Committee:
A. Evaluation Forms w/Financials
South Dakota Disc Golf Championship (September 22nd-24th, 2023)
• The event exceeded expectations. Total spectator count was 20-30. There were 100
participants. The number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 50ish. The
hotels/motels contacted were: Corn Palace Inn, Holiday Inn Express, and Thunderbird
Lodge. The awarded funds ($1,500) were used for porta potties, trophies, signage,
park closure and insurance certificate fees. No net profit.
Palace City Kiwanis Half Marathon & Relay, 5K & 10K (October 1st, 2023)
• The event was hosted above expectations, runner registrations were up about 20% this
year, and they appreciate the Sports & Events Authority's continued support of the
event. Total spectator count was 400+. There were 225 participants. The number of
total hotel/motel room nights sold was 40. The hotels/motels contacted were:
AmericInn, Days Inn, and Kelly Inn. The awarded funds ($2,000) were used for the

--- PAGE 3 OF 5 ---


race medals. Net profit for the event was $6,928.44, which will be used for Kiwanis
Woodlot Park improvements, scholarships, Girls on the Run, Abbott House, First
Responder Blanket Project, and other children's initiatives.
Dakota Riptide Invite (December 1st-3rd, 2023)
• The event met expectations. Total spectator count was 550. There were 282
swimmers. The number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 65. The hotels/motels
contacted were: Comfort Inn & Suites, Hampton Inn, and Holiday Inn Express. The
awarded funds ($3,750) were used to pay for the pool and sound system rent, lifeguard
wages, and other facility expenses. Net profit for the event was $16,349.97, which will
be used to help fund the swim team and keep our monthly dues affordable.
6. Other Items
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee:
A. SEA Banners on Display
Hoop City Classic (December 28th-30th, 2023)
• Mitchell Sports & Events Authority banner is permanently hung in the Hospitality Room.
Also, the Mitchell Sports & Events Authority logo is published on page 2 of the digital
program, as well as displayed on the digital billboards throughout the Corn Palace.
B. Upcoming Events
• MHS Girls & Boys Basketball
• DWU Women's & Men's Basketball
• Hanson Girls Classic (Saturday, January 13th)
• USA National Paralympic Sled Hockey Team Camp (Wednesday, January 17th-
Saturday, January 20th)
• Comedy Night at the Highland (Friday, January 19th)
• Hanson Boys Classic (Saturday, January 20th)
• MHS Friend de Coup Show Choir Community Show (Tuesday, January 23rd)
• Dakota Oyate Challenge (Thursday, January 25th-Saturday, January 27th)
• Winter Crazy Days! (Friday, January 26th-Sunday, January 28th)
• Mitchell Virtual Job Fair (Wednesday, January 31st)
• South Dakota No-Till Association - Mitchell Soil Health Event (Thursday, February 8th)
Full list of events - Mitchell Chamber Events Calendar
*BOLD - Awarded Sports & Events Authority Grant funding.

--- PAGE 4 OF 5 ---


7. Next Meeting Date
Aaron Hieb shared the next meeting date for Tuesday, February 13th, 2024, @ 2 PM - City
Hall, Council Chambers.
8. Adjournment
There being no further business to discuss.
Meeting adjourned by: Mayor Everson @ 3:02 PM.

documents.text:
From: 	noreply@civicplus.com
To: 	Aaron Hieb
Subject: 	Online Form Submittal: Sports & Events Authority Evaluation Form
Date: 	Wednesday, January 17, 2024 11:39:20 PM
Sports & Events Authority Evaluation Form
Sports & Events Authority Evaluation
Form
Event Information
Name of Event: 	Dakota Showdown Horse Trainer Challenge Finale
Date(s) of Event: 	August 11-12, 2023
Evaluation Information
How well did this event
meet your
expectations:
4 - Above Expectations
Additional Feedback -
Please share the
positive takeaways, as
well as, ways the SEA
can assist in the growth
of the event:
Hi! We were very happy with how the event itself went, however
ran into quite a few challenges with our vendors and such in
Mitchell that made it challenging to hold and really ended up
making us feel unwelcome and unwanted. The event itself was a
success, with 20 horses receiving professional training and
having a good weekend, several of them getting adopted with
fees ranging from $1000-3100 through an auction process, and a
decent turnout. The newspaper gave us a great article and that
was exciting!
However, we did run into some issues with vendors. We booked
the Horseman's Sports Arena and about a month before the
event they called us and informed us they decided to hold their
own event and we could no longer use the arena. They were
very helpful in finding a new location and even arranged for
bleachers and parking, however when the weekend arrived they
could not get bleachers delivered and the person who had given
permission for parking decided to not let us use it. Trail-Eze was
gracious, however, in letting us use their lot for parking, but all in
all it was a difficult experience that definitely affected how the
event went.
Total spectator 	approx 200-250 based on bracelets given away at entry

March 12th, 2024, Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Meeting Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                    March 12, 2024 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Mayor Everson at 2 PM. 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Everson, Kevin McCardle, Jason 
Christensen, Doug Greenway, Bryan Dixon, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, 
and Jim Johnston. 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Jill Larson, Kevin Nelson, Cory Aadland, and 
Tim Smith. 
 
 Others present: Johanna Allen, Stephanie Ellwein, Sage Bohn, and Aaron Hieb. 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed 
 applications for grant funding. The following application(s) were presented and considered: 
 
A. DWU Spring Golf Invite 
Date: April 8th-9th, 2024; Contact: Jeff Meyerink; Grant Request: $2,000 

     • Jeff Meyerink, DWU Men's & Women's Head Golf Coach, presented the DWU Spring 
       Golf Invite Sports & Events Authority Grant Application. He is requesting $2,000. It has 
       been over ten years since DWU has hosted a home golf tournament. The requested 
       funds would be used to pay for players' meals and drinks on both days, coach's cart 
       rental(s), and range balls. Currently, there are 88 players that are registered to 
       compete. Jeff estimates that hotel room nights sold would be between 60 and 80. 

 
 
B. Harve's Sport Shop Soccer Tournament 
Date: April 19th-21st, 2024; Contact: Robert Hoffman; Grant Request: $5,000 

     • Jodie Cain-Lambert presented the Harve's Sport Shop Soccer Tournament Sports & 
       Events Authority Grant Application for the Tempo Soccer Club. Hosting the soccer 
       tournament in association with Tempo Soccer out of Tea, SD to utilize the Pepsi 
       Soccer Complex in Mitchell, SD. The grant request will be earmarked and go towards 
       referees' expense, which is their biggest expense.  
 
C. South Dakota State United States Bowling Congress Open Tournament 
Date: April 5th-7th; 12th-14th; 19th-21st; 26th-28th; May 3rd-5th; & 10th-12th, 2024; Contact: 
Nate Sievert & Jeff Vander Wilt; Grant Request: $4,500 

     • Nate Sievert, Village Bowl, presented the SD USBC Open Tournament Sports & 
       Events Authority Grant Application. This event was to be hosted in Mitchell next year 
       (2025), but due to health issues in Yankton, the event has been relocated to Mitchell 
       for 2024. The event will run every Friday, Saturday, and Sunday of April and the first 
       two weekends in May. The grant request of $4,500 will be designated as follows: 
       $3,000 will go towards the prize fund and $1,500 will be to help offset costs for the 
       tournament manager coming from Rapid City. Mitchell hosted the Open Tournament in 
       2019 and there were 326 - 4-person teams. 

 
 
D. Shootout at the Lake 
Date: June 21st-22nd, 2024; Contact: Wade Musick; Grant Request: $20,000 

     • Sheldon Tobin presented the Shootout at the Lake Sports & Events Authority Grant 
       Application on behalf of the Horsemen's Sports Inc. Each night the event will consist of 
       a rodeo and a concert. This will be the second year this event has taken place. The 
       first night will be Ned Ledoux and the second night will be Dustin Evans and the Good 
       Times Band. Sheldon is estimating that the event will bring in 3,000 to 4,000 people 
       each night.  

 
 
E. Palace City Kiwanis Half Marathon 
Date: October 6th, 2024; Contact: Paula Deckert; Grant Request: $5,000 

     • Crystal Freund presented the Palace City Kiwanis Half Marathon Sports & Events 
       Authority Grant Application on behalf of the Kiwanis Club of Mitchell. This will be the 
       seventh year of the event. The grant request of $5,000 is for the SEA to consider being 
       the Event Sponsor. Their biggest expense is the timing system.  

 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Kevin McCardle to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
 presented and seconded by Doug Greenway. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb and Stephanie Ellwein reviewed the financial report as of March 7th, 2024.  
 
This is the first financial report for the BID #4 - $2.00 monthly collections. As reviewed in the last meeting, the BID #4 Board recommended and the City Council approved the annual SEA 
budget of $100,000 for 2024. Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 
2024 are $31,750. Total Fund Balance of $68,250. There are three committed award checks 
for the Special Olympics, 2025, 2026, and 2027 where the checks are designated to come out 
of each respective years SEA Revenue budget. Currently, there are two award checks for 
approved events where the checks have yet to be written for 2024. The Combat Veterans 
Motorcycle Association Comedy Night ($1,000) and Knights of Columbus Special Olympics 
Banquet ($1,700) award checks. Current Available Fund Balance of $65,550.  
 
Collections in February (for January records) were $13,500.50 with four establishments not 
past due, but reported partial collections. These four establishments have been contacted and 
will submit the remaining collections. Going forward, the YTD comparisons for each month will 
list and compare the total room nights sold, not the total $ amount of collections, since it only 
makes sense to compare the number that remains consistent when collecting either the $1.50 
or $2.00 tax. 
 
YTD comparison for room nights sold were: up .6% (94 room nights sold) from 2023, up 1.0% 
(164 room nights sold) for 2022, up 18.1% (2,970 room nights sold) for 2021, down 11.0% 
(1,800 room nights sold) from 2020, up 11.8% (1,929 room nights sold) for 2019, and up 6.4% 
(1,054 room nights sold) for 2018. 
 
Motion: Motion was made by Bryan Dixon to approve the financial report as presented and 
 seconded by Jim Johnston. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form w/Financials to the SEA Committee: 
 
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials 
Palace Ice Festival (January 12th-13th, 2024) 

     • The event met expectations. This weekend's weather conditions were very poor, but 
       they had approximately 317 spectators, along with 32 skaters, 10 coaches, and 5 US 
       Figure Skating Judges & Representatives. The number of total hotel/motel room nights 
       sold was 29. The hotels/motels contacted were: Comfort Inn & Suites, Days Inn, 
       Hampton Inn, and Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites. The awarded funds ($750) were 
       used to offset expenses for the Palace Ice Festival Skating Competition. Profits will be 
       used to bring in skating clinicians to hold skating clinics here in Mitchell to help our 
       figure skaters learn and grow, and to have other out-of-town clubs come to Mitchell and 
       learn as well. 

 
 
6. Other Items 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee: 
 
A. SEA Banners on Display 
Cabin Fever Auction (February 23rd-24th, 2024)      • Set up two, SEA feather banners outside, at the entrance doors of the Davison County 
       Fairgrounds building. Posted five, SEA QR Code Hotel Survey fliers throughout the 
       lobby of the Davison County Fairgrounds. 

 
DWU Annual Indoor Futsal Winter Classic (February 23rd-25th, 2024) 

     • Hung up two SEA square banners, one at the DWU/Avera Sports & Wellness Complex 
       and the other, in the Christen Athletic Center gymnasium. Also, DWU Soccer athletes 
       assisted with the SEA QR Code Hotel Survey flier and gathering participant feedback. 

 
South Dakota Middle School All-State Band (March 1st-2nd, 2024) 

     • Hung a SEA square banner in the Band Director's Room at the Mitchell Performing 
       Arts Center, next to the hospitality table and food/beverages provided by the SEA 
       funds. 

 
 
B. Upcoming Events 

     • Head Over Heels: The Musical (March 15th-17th & March 22nd-24th) 
            o DWU Black Box Theatre at the Dakota Discovery Museum 
     • Show Choir Classic (Saturday, March 16th @ Performing Arts Center) 
     • Combat Veterans Motorcycle Association Comedy Night (Saturday, March 16th 
       @ Highland Conference Center) 
     • Lake Mitchell Informational Meeting (Tuesday, March 19th 6-8 PM @ Corn Palace) 
     • CHS Pancakes at the Palace (Wednesday, March 20th 5-7 PM @ Corn Palace) 
     • Lifequest Dancing for Dreams 2024 (Friday, March 22nd 6 PM @ Highland Conference 
       Center) 
     • Knights of Columbus Special Olympics State Basketball Banquet (Saturday, 
       March 23rd 5:30 – 9 PM @ John Paul II Auditorium & Multi-Purpose Room) 
     • Special Olympics SD State Basketball Tournament (March 23rd-24th) 
     • Disabled American Veterans Chapter 27 Pancake Feed (Saturday, March 23rd 8 AM-
       Noon @ Davison County 4-H Grounds) 
     • 40&08 Handgun Tournament (Saturday, March 23rd 10 AM -2 PM @ Davison 
       Shooting Club Indoor Range) 
     • Spring Moose Lodge Vendor Fair (Saturday, March 23rd 10 AM-2 PM @ Moose 
       Lodge) 
     • Kiwanis Spaghetti Dinner (Saturday, March 23rd 11 AM-2 PM @ Mitchell Technical 
       College Campus Center Building) 
     • Wingapalooza (Saturday, March 23rd 1-4 PM @ Corn Palace) 
     • Mitchell Food Pantry Easter Ham Dinner Giveaway (Tuesday, March 26th 5-6 PM @ 
       parking lot between TMA & Graham Tire) 
     • A Night at the Races (Friday, April 5th @ 6:30 PM Highland Conference Center) 

 
Complete list of events - Mitchell Chamber Events Calendar  
 *BOLD - Awarded Sports & Events Authority Grant funding 
 
7. Executive Session in accordance with SDCL 9-34-19: Discussion of confidential trade 
secrets, commercial, or financial information. 
 
 
8. Approval of Funding Applications 
DWU Spring Golf Invite 
Date: April 8th-9th, 2024; Contact: Jeff Meyerink; Grant Request: $2,000 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to award $1,500 and seconded by Dave 
       Helleloid. Remaining members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
     • Abstain: Jason Christensen abstained from voting. 

 
Harve's Sport Shop Soccer Tournament 
Date: April 19th-21st, 2024; Contact: Robert Hoffman; Grant Request: $5,000 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Kevin McCardle to table the voting decision until the April 
       9th meeting and seconded by Bryan Dixon. Remaining members voted 'Aye' and the 
       motion passed. 
     • Abstain: Jim Johnston abstained from voting. 

 
South Dakota State United States Bowling Congress Open Tournament 
Date: April 5th-7th; 12th-14th; 19th-21st; 26th-28th; May 3rd-5th; & 10th-12th, 2024; Contact: 
Nate Sievert & Jeff Vander Wilt; Grant Request: $4,500 

     • Motion: Motion was made by LaRee Rumbolz to award $3,000 and seconded by 
       Jason Christensen. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
Shootout at the Lake 
Date: June 21st-22nd, 2024; Contact: Wade Musick; Grant Request: $20,000 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to award $5,000 and seconded by Jim 
       Johnston. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
Palace City Kiwanis Half Marathon 
Date: October 6th, 2024; Contact: Paula Deckert; Grant Request: $5,000 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Kevin McCardle to award $1,500 ($1,000 donation in 
       support of event & $500 BAG Sponsor) and seconded by Dave Helleloid. All members 
       voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
 9. Next Meeting Date 
Mayor Everson shared the next meeting date of Tuesday, April 9th, 2024, @ 2 PM - City Hall, 
 Council Chambers. 
 
10. Adjournment 
There being no further business to discuss. 
 
 Meeting adjourned by: Mayor Everson @ 3:22 PM.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

From: 	noreply@civicplus.com
To: 	Aaron Hieb
Subject: 	Online Form Submittal: Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
Date: 	Thursday, March 7, 2024 11:02:42 AM
Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

Tempo Soccer Club (TSC) is a 501c3 non-profit youth soccer
organization founded in 2011. We are a member of both US Club
Soccer & US Youth Soccer. We offer year-round competitive
soccer programs.
Tempo is one of the fastest growing competitive soccer clubs in
the State of South Dakota. Tempo’s unique model of utilizing
licensed parent coaches, who volunteer to lead each of our
teams, is resulting in significant success for the club. Our teams
consistently compete at the highest levels in the region and
successfully challenge for championships in most of the
tournaments they attend.

SD STATE USBC OPEN TOURNAMENT RULES
1. 	Eligibility for this USBC certified tournament #06957 is limited to bowlers who are current members in good standing of USBC, SD
State USBC, and a local South Dakota Bowling Association. Bowler must have a minimum of 21 games in South Dakota State
sanctioned leagues in the current or previous season, prior to the date of participation in this tournament.
2. 	You may bowl the Team event TWICE with change of two members of the team. You may bowl Doubles and Singles only ONCE.
However, if you enter the Doubles event, you must also enter the Singles event and vice-versa. Bowlers will be scheduled two (2)
per lane for the Doubles and Singles event.
3. 	Team, Doubles and Singles events will be bowled in two (2) handicap divisions and an optional scratch division. The handicap
division split will be at the averages of 181 and above and 180 and below. Your FIRST Team score will be used for calculating
All Events. The optional All Events will consist of one (1) Handicap Division and one (1) Scratch Division. The optional “Special
Scratch” event consists of the two (2) highest games from your Doubles event and the two (2) highest games from your Singles
event. All prize money will be returned 100% in cash and awards in each event and division collected. The added prize money
of $3,000.00 by the host association will be distributed to the two handicap divisions of the Team, Doubles and Singles events.
4. 	Prizes will be awarded to the handicap and scratch division champions in Team, Doubles, Singles and All Events. In case of a
tie for the championship of any event, co-champions will be declared, and duplicate prizes will be awarded. The representative
to the National Masters Tournament will be the bowler with the highest Scratch All Events score of the tournament provided
he/she is entered in the scratch All Events; highest single game will determine the participant in case of a tie (continuing down
until tie is broken. The SD STATE USBC will reimburse the entry fee for the South Dakota representative and will pay the
representative $350.00 in travel expense upon proof of participation.
5. 	Entry fees for Team, Doubles and Singles events are $33.00 per bowler, per event, divided as follows:
Prize Fund - $14.05, bowling and scoring - $11.50, tournament expense - $7.50.
The entry fee for the Optional Handicap All Events is $6.00. ($5.00 prize fund / $1.00 expense)
The entry fee for the Optional Scratch All Events is $10.00. ($8.00 prize fund / $2.00 expense)
The entry fee for the Optional Special Scratch event is $10.00. ($8.00 prize fund / $2.00 expense)
6. 	AVERAGES: The average to be used by the entrant must be their HIGHEST USBC single league average based on a
minimum of 21 games, regardless of whether bowled as a regular or substitute. Averages will be accepted in the following
order:
(A) Entrant must use their highest USBC certified league average as of the end of the previous season. A minimum of 21
games is required.
(B) If “A” does not apply, an entrant shall use their highest USBC certified average as of January 1, 2024. A minimum of 21
games is required.
(C) If neither “A” or “B” applies, use the highest current USBC certified average as of the date of participation in the State
Tournament. A minimum of 21 games is required.
(D) If neither “A”, “B” or "C" applies, use the highest current USBC certified composite average of all leagues, including
leagues with less than 21 games bowled, as of the date of participation in the State Tournament. A minimum of 21 total
games with written verification of each league average making up the composite average is required.
(E) Any bowler who has only a USBC Sport league average must utilize the chart, which will determine the adjusted average.
Chart can be found on bowl.com or in the USBC Playing Rules book.
(WRITTEN VERIFICATION OF AVERAGE MUST BE PROVIDED IF AVERAGE IS NOT AVAILABLE
ON WWW.BOWL.COM, OR AT REQUEST OF THE TOURNAMENT MANAGER)
Team Captain must verify the average of each individual entrant. If the entrant is also a member in another association, the Team
Captain must also verify membership and average.
SUBSTITUTES: Team Captains must report to tournament headquarters at least 30 minutes prior to their first shift time to report
any substitutes. Substitutes will bowl in the lineup position of the bowler they are replacing.
7. 	All entries will be processed on a first-paid, first-served basis. Entries close Friday, March 29, 2024 or when last shift is full. At
the Tournament Manager’s discretion, an additional weekend may be added, if necessary. All entries must be submitted on an
official entry form, or a copy thereof, and must be accompanied by full entry fees. Insufficient Funds Checks: Subject to
$30.00 charge and entry rejection. Telephone or e-mail reservations will be held for seven (7) days to ensure shift choice.
8. 	Any errors in scoring must be reported and corrected immediately. All scores as recorded on the scoring computer after the completion
of each game will be declared final and official.
9. 	Any protest must be submitted in writing to the tournament manager within 72 hours of close of tournament. No unsigned protest will
be considered.
10. DRESS CODE: You must wear appropriate attire; shirts with offensive language/artwork and CAPS will not be allowed.
Team Captains are responsible for ensuring team members adhere to dress code. 	Tournament Manager has final
discretion as to appropriate attire.
11. CODE OF CONDUCT: Any obnoxious behavior and/or over consumption of alcohol that affects tournament play will
NOT be tolerated. The result will be immediate disqualification and removal from the tournament.
12. All USBC rules will apply, unless otherwise stated.
ATTENTION BOWLERS: Entry fees are NON-REFUNDABLE, as per USBC Rule 314.
USBC Rule 319A 1-3-4 and 319C & E concerning submission of averages is in effect.
The 10-pin re-rate rule is not in effect.

***Application must be received no less than 45

The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.

Comments 	Last year’s event was a pilot event that was held due to the
desire of the community of Mitchell to have a rodeo event in the
summer of 2023. The previously scheduled rodeo event was
suddenly canceled which gave the Horsemen's Sports Inc.

rodeo event. Because of the short notice, only one band was
contracted for one night of the event. This year, the Horsemen's
Sports Inc. committee has contracted two Nashville recording
artists; Ned LeDoux and the Western Underground, for Friday
night and, Dustin Evans and the Good Times Band, for Saturday
night. This along with many top rodeo contenders will, we
believe, bring in many more spectators from, not only Mitchell,
but across South Dakota and beyond. Community and regional
support has been extremely supportive and suggestions to
proceed with a yearly event has been highly encouraged. This

The Horsemen's Sports Inc. is an organization based on equine
enthusiasts that enjoy rodeo events for all ages. We provide

rodeo genre. From competitive competitions to casual

Shootout At The Lake is a rodeo event that includes 2 nights of
Saddle Bronc riding and Bull riding competitions. It also includes
youth Mutton Busting and concerts following each night. The
rodeo takes place on June 21 & 22, 2024 at the Horsemen's
Sport Arena located at 4013 N. Main St. in Mitchell, SD and will
began at 7:00 pm both nights. The concerts will follow
immediately after and will run until approximately 11:30 pm. Ned
LeDoux and the Western Underground will perform on Friday,
June 21, 2024, with Dustin Evans and the Good Times Band
preforming Saturday, June 22, 2024. The contestants will consist
of top PRCA and PBR athletes on a personal invite only basis
with an average of 16 participants per night. Mutton Busting co-
ed participants will be ages 4 through 8 years old on a first
come/first serve sign-up draw basis, with an average of 15
participants per night. 12-time PBR Stock Contractor of the Year,
Chag Berger and PRCA Contractor Dakota Rodeo will provide
stock for both nights. Concession stands, beverages and alcohol
will be provided at a cost to consumers.

We will have participants from South Dakota and various states
all across the country. Last year we had participants from as far
away as Mexico and several from Brazil. We expect many
visitors from throughout South Dakota and the surrounding
states.
What are the specific
goals for this event?
The goal of Horsemen's Sport Inc. is to provide a professional
and elite rodeo and concert venue for the city of Mitchell, South
Dakota.

request would be used
to promote tourism in

funding were denied.
Having a quality rodeo event with top notch performers and
professional live music from renowned artists would bring many
overnight visitors to Mitchell that would stay the weekend for the
entire event, which in turn, would result in the purchase of rooms,
dinning, gas, shopping, etc. If funding were denied, the
Horsemen's Sports Inc. committee would not be able to provide
the type of entertainment to draw the larger crowds.

The Palace City Kiwanis Half Marathon is an A-MAIZE-ING race
that starts and ends at the World's Only Corn Palace on the first
Sunday of October (October 6, 2024). The PCKH started in 2018
as a collaboration between the Kiwanis Club of Mitchell and the
Palace City Women Run Club. Our event includes a Half
Marathon, Half Marathon Relay, 10K and a 5K as well as a Kids
Fun Run. The Half Marathon and Relay takes participants
through town and then around Lake Mitchell. The 10K and 5K
routes go around Cadwell Park. The Kids Fun Run will go from
the Corn Palace to 1st Avenue and back on Saturday, October
5th to encourage additional overnight stays.

Participants come from all over South Dakota, the Midwest and
beyond. Last year, we had runners from both coasts. In fact, 13%
travel over 100 miles to attend our event and 8% come from out
of state. We market to runners in the 50 state half marathon
clubs which also gives us national exposure.

The Palace City Kiwanis Half brings in people from all over the
country for this bucket-list race experience. Our participants
come to our event and they bring their friends and families to
cheer them on. We are anticipating further growth this year and
hopefully will reach our goal of having each state represented.
We are grateful for your support in the past and would love for
SEA to be our event sponsor. Please note, we recently updated
our sponsorship levels to reflect increasing costs (event growth,
inflation, etc.). If we do not receive funding, it will significantly
impact our ability to produce the quality of event our participants
and community are accustomed to and represent our community
well. It would also have a serious impact on our ability to grow
this event.

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
February 13, 2024
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:00 PM.
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, Kevin Nelson,
Cory Aadland, Doug Greenway, Bryan Dixon, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston.
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Mayor Everson, Jason Christensen, LaRee
Rumbolz, and Emily Liedtke.
Others present: Stephanie Ellwein, Johanna Allen, and Aaron Hieb.
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed
applications for grant funding. The following application(s) were presented and considered:
A. Cabin Fever Auction
Date: February 23rd-24th, 2024; Contact: Ashley Coulter; Grant Request: $2,000
• Nick Coulter presented the grant application for the Buckin' Wild Ranch Cabin Fever
Auction, which will be held on February 23 & 24, 2024, at the Davison County
Fairgrounds. This event draws between 400–500 people to Mitchell for two or three
days. The grant request would go towards workers' wages, newspaper advertisements,
posters, and facility costs. They hire around 25 employees to help with the event,
including auctioneers, whom they pay $250 per day and provide hotel rooms for them.
B. South Dakota Middle School All-State Band
Date: March 1st-2nd, 2024; Contact: Holly Gage; Grant Request: $300
• Holly Gage, co-chair of SDMEA Middle School All State Band, presented the grant
application via conference phone for the South Dakota Middle School All-State Band.
This event includes 200 middle school students from all over the state. She anticipates
overnight stays for one or two nights. The students usually come with their
parents/families, so they make their own hotel/motel reservations. The grant request
would be spent locally, throughout Mitchell, to provide a Hospitality Room and snacks
for the band directors and students throughout the event. This event rotates to Mitchell

--- PAGE 1 OF 8 ---


every other year with the exception of Middle School All State Band being in Mitchell
the next two years because of the great location. Middle School All State Jazz Band is
in Mitchell on a yearly basis.
C. Show Choir Classic
Date: March 16th, 2024; Contact: Angella Buenzow; Grant Request: $5,000
• Jayson Plamp presented the grant application for the Show Choir Classic. The Mitchell
Show Choir has about 75 participants. Show expenses are usually around $120,000
each year. One of the largest fundraisers is the Show Choir Classic. Currently, there
are 20 teams, which generates around 1,500 spectators as well. Teams competing
come from Omaha, Missouri, and Chicago. Currently, they have teams from Omaha,
Vermillion, Groton, Aberdeen, Sioux City, Hot Springs, Chicago, and Missouri. Their
budget for this particular event is $30,000. Their biggest line item expense is the
judges, which brings them to Mitchell and provides hotels as well. Last year attendance
was down because of winter weather and road closures.
D. Combat Veterans Motorcycle Association Comedy Night
Date: March 16th, 2024; Contact: Kim Hamer; Grant Request: $2,000
• Kim Hamer, public relations officer of CVMA for Eastern South Dakota, presented the
grant application via conference phone for the Combat Veterans Motorcycle
Association Comedy Night. The 3rd Annual CVMA Comedy Night will take place on
March 16th at the Highland Conference Center. Last year's event attendance was
greatly impacted by the winter weather. Attendees have come from Rapid City and
Luverne, MN. This year's event will team up with Helping with Horsepower, which
includes a group of veterans building a motorcycle together. CVMA is hosting their
monthly meeting in Mitchell as well.
E. Knights of Columbus Special Olympics Banquet
Date: March 23rd, 2024; Contact: Gene Kessler; Grant Request: $1,700
• Vince Boddicker presented the grant application for the Knights of Columbus Special
Olympics Banquet. The event will take place on March 23rd in St. John Paul II
Auditorium. This is the fourth time that the Knights of Columbus has hosted this
banquet since 2017. Currently, there are 785 athletes signed up for the banquet. They
will serve spaghetti and meatballs, garlic bread, water, and dilly bars from Dairy
Queen. The attendees will be served in about an hour and a half (5:30 PM to 7:00 PM).
Starting at 6 PM until 9 PM, there will be a DJ in the multipurpose room for a dance.
Their budget is a little over $4,500 which is all designated for food, and the school
donates the use of the facility and there is no profit being made from this banquet.
They utilize around 40 volunteers to host the banquet.

--- PAGE 2 OF 8 ---


F. Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament
Date: April 12th-14th, 2024; Contact: Stacy Murtha; Grant Request: $4,000
• Stacy Murtha presented the grant application for the Lucky Devils Adult Hockey
Tournament. This will be the 13th year. Last year the event hosted 21 teams.
Currently, there are 19, possibly 20 teams. Teams come from 5 states (WI, MN, ND,
SD, IA, NE). This event brings over 300–400 players and families to Mitchell. Each
team gets one game a day. The biggest expenses are referees and ice time. The profit
made goes back into youth hockey for the Mitchell community. Sioux Falls has already
started an event like this and Watertown, with the new facility, is looking to start an
event like this in March. The grant request would help keep their expenses in check, so
they can continue to host this event in Mitchell. Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Non-Profit
was created as well.
G. Shootout at the Lake
Date: June 21st-22nd, 2024; Contact: Wade Musick; Grant Request: $20,000
• Tabled and added to the March 12th agenda.
H. USA Sled Hockey Camp
Date: January 17th-20th, 2024; Contact: Dave Tronnes; Grant Request: any additional
support up to $1,250
• Dave Tronnes reached out to Aaron Hieb and the SEA Advisory Committee with a
request for any additional support to go along with the previously awarded $3,500. This
additional funding would go to the USA Paralympic Sled Hockey Team to help cover
some of the unplanned travel expenses due to the weather.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Jim Johnston to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented, seconded by Tim Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb and Stephanie Ellwein reviewed the Financial Report as of February 5th, 2024.
This was the final financial report for the BID #2 - $1.50 Total Collections. Going forward, the
financial report will show BID #4 - $2.00 Total Collections based on the $100,000 that has
been budgeted by the BID #4 Board for Sports & Events Authority revenue/funding.
The total revenue for 2023 was $106,518.50. This number is misleading because the last two

--- PAGE 3 OF 8 ---


months (November and December) of collections for the year included the entire $1.50 of the
hotel occupancy tax, not just the $.50. Total Fund Balance of $78,250. There are now only
three committed items/events, all Special Olympics, where the checks have not been written.
These will carry over into the BID #4 Financials and be designated to come out of each
respective years SEA Revenue budget. Current Available Fund Balance of $78,250.
Collections in January (for December records) were $14,488.50 with ALL hotels/motels
reporting. This was the second-highest collection for the month of December in the past eight
years. YTD comparison for collections were: up 15.4% from 2023, up 6.4% for 2022, up 29.4%
for 2021, down 11.4% from 2020, up 15.4% for 2019, and up 9.7% for 2018.
The BID #4 Board met towards the end of January. They discussed and approved an SEA
Revenue budget of $100,000 for 2024. Looking ahead to the March SEA Financials,
collections will be submitted and collected in February for January records. This will be the
$2.00 collection and 12 out of the 15 hotels/motels will submit collections. The Budget Inn,
CoachLight Motel, and Siesta Motel have less than 28 rooms, so they were excluded from the
BID #4 composition. If any of those 3 motels would like to continue to submit the collections, it
would be considered a donation, similar to the Lake Mitchell Campground.
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the financial report as presented and
seconded by Bryan Dixon. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms with Financials to the SEA Committee.
Due to time constraints, Aaron suggested the committee review the SEA Survey that was
submitted by D&E Music and Vending on behalf of Carol Steilen (Pink Ladies Darts) at their
convenience.
A. Evaluation Form w/Financials
South Dakota State Amateur Baseball Tournament (August 2nd-13th, 2023)
• The event was above expectations. There were 32 Class B teams and 5 Class A
teams. The number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 300 +. The hotels/motels
contacted were: Comfort Inn & Suites, Hampton Inn, and Holiday Inn Express Hotel &
Suites. Mitchell will be the host this year, 2024. It will be in Brandon in 2025 and back
in Mitchell in 2026. The awarded funds ($5,000) were used for hospitality purposes for
the commissioners, umpires, and tournament personnel. Profit from the tournament is
used to fund the Mitchell Baseball Association baseball operations and improvements
for Cadwell Park.
Dakota Showdown Horse Trainer Challenge (August 11th-12th, 2023)
• The event itself went above expectations. There were quite a few challenges with the
vendors that made them feel unwelcome and unwanted. They booked the Horsemen's
Sports Arena and a month before were told they could no longer use their arena. The
new location they provided by Trail King did not go as planned, and it was a difficult
experience. The total spectator count was 200-250. There were 20 participants. The
number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 20-24. The hotels/motels contacted

--- PAGE 4 OF 8 ---


were: CoachLight Motel, Kelly Inn & Suites, and Thunderbird Lodge. The awarded
funds ($1,000) were used to cover the lease of the location. Total profit of $334.73,
which went back to the support of the Gentle Spirit Horses Rescue.
USA Paralympic Sled Hockey Team Camp (January 15th-21st, 2024)
• https://www.mitchellrepublic.com/opinion/letters/letter-the-economy-is-not-1
• The event exceeded expectations. The volunteers and Hotel/arena staff were all great.
Total spectator count was 85. There were 26 participants on the hockey team. The
number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 90. The hotel that the team utilized
was the Comfort Inn & Suites. The awarded funds ($3,500) were used to offset costs
for the arena rental and meals.

April 9th, 2024, Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Meeting Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                     April 9, 2024 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Mayor Everson @ 2:00 PM. 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Everson, Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson 
(phone), Kevin Nelson, Doug Greenway, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, and 
Jim Johnston. 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Cory Aadland, Jason Christensen, Bryan 
Dixon, and Tim Smith. 
 
 Others present: Johanna Allen and Aaron Hieb. 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed 
 applications for grant funding. The following application(s) were presented and considered: 
 
A. Special Olympics State Basketball Tournament 
*Special Olympics South Dakota is proposing to donate $6,000 of the previously awarded 
$12,000 for the Special Olympics State Basketball Tournament to the Mitchell Special 
 Olympics Delegation, since the event was shortened to one day because of weather. 
 
B. Harve's Sport Shop Soccer Tournament 

     • Jodie Cain-Lambert provided an update regarding the progress of the Harve's Sport 
       Shop Soccer Tournament. Currently, there are 31 teams signed up to participate in the 
       current, two-day tournament, starting at 8 AM on Saturday, April 20th. This will now be 
       a U12 and U10 youth tournament because there are no high school teams due to prom 
       and school-affiliated activities. Because of the low turnout, Tempo Soccer Club: 
       Harve's Sport Shop Soccer Tournament is withdrawing their funding request of $5,000 
       and asking the committee to consider awarding whatever amount the committee 
       considers appropriate at their discretion based on the information and team(s) count 
       provided. The biggest expense for the event is the referee costs. 

 
 
C. DBS Entertainment: Dr. Lucky's Street Dance 
     • James "Bubba" Startz, DBS Entertainment, presented the Dr. Lucky's Street Dance 
       Grant Application to the committee. The event correlates with MMS&B Memorial 
       Weekend in Mitchell on Saturday, May 25th. The event will take place on W. 2nd Ave. 
       adjacent to Dr. Lucky's Bar & Grill. The grant request of $2,500 would go primarily 
       towards the promotional expenses.  

 
 
D. MAC Triathlon 

     • Terasa Gillen and Emily Hohn presented the MAC Triathlon Grant Application. The 
       event takes place on Saturday, June 8th, starting at Hitchcock Park. The biggest 
       expense for this event is the timing system, which usually costs around $2,500. 
       Participant expectations are for around 85–90 athletes competing in the tri-series 
       events. There are not many hotel/motel room nights sold for this event, some stay at 
       campgrounds and others come the morning of the event traveling with very expensive 
       gear. They shared information about the sponsorship levels and what the exposure is 
       for being a sponsor.  

 
 
E. South Dakota State & High Plains Territorial Cowboy Fast Draw Championships 

     • Diane Royalty and Troy Bollock presented the South Dakota State & High Plains 
       Territorial Cowboy Fast Draw Championships. This year's event dates have changed 
       from previous years. This year the event is hosted on Wednesday, September 11th 
       through Sunday, September 15th, which will piggyback with the Kansas and Nebraska 
       state shoots. The grant request of $4,500 will go towards 100% payout for a 
       designated bracket shoot sponsored by the SEA. The expectations with the 5 shoots 
       during the event that participation will be over 100 shooters.  

 
 
F. 20th Annual OutKasts Car Show 

     • Jerry Wright, The 301 Rodz, presented the 20th Annual OutKasts Car Show Grant 
       Application. The 3-day event will take place from Friday, September 20th through 
       Sunday, September 22nd. This year's car show is correlating with MMS&B 
       Oktoberfest, and they are allowing all makes/models/years of cars to enter the car 
       show. The grant request of $2,000 will go towards awards and marketing materials 
       (radio ads, invitations, and fliers). The 301 Rodz is non-profit, so any profit from the 
       event will go back to the community. 

 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Jim Johnston to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
 presented and seconded by Kevin McCardle. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of April 5th, 2024.  
 
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2024 are $43,750.  
 
Current Available Fund Balance of $56,250.  
 
Collections in February (for January records) have increased to $14,493.50 with only one 
establishment that has not reported the full collection amount. Collections in March (for 
February records) is $14,210.50 with one establishment that is past due. The YTD collections 
for 2024 is $43,192.50, which equates to 24,011 total room nights sold.  
 
YTD comparison for room nights sold were: up 2.0% (487 room nights sold) from 2023, down 
2.7% (648 room nights sold) from 2022, up 20.8% (5,006 room nights sold) from 2021, down 
10.7% (2,559 room nights sold) from 2020, up 9.6% (2,310 room nights sold) from 2019, and

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.

Christensen, Doug Greenway, Bryan Dixon, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid,

2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed
applications for grant funding. The following application(s) were presented and considered:
A. DWU Spring Golf Invite
Date: April 8th-9th, 2024; Contact: Jeff Meyerink; Grant Request: $2,000
• Jeff Meyerink, DWU Men's & Women's Head Golf Coach, presented the DWU Spring
Golf Invite Sports & Events Authority Grant Application. He is requesting $2,000. It has
been over ten years since DWU has hosted a home golf tournament. The requested
funds would be used to pay for players' meals and drinks on both days, coach's cart
rental(s), and range balls. Currently, there are 88 players that are registered to
compete. Jeff estimates that hotel room nights sold would be between 60 and 80.
B. Harve's Sport Shop Soccer Tournament
Date: April 19th-21st, 2024; Contact: Robert Hoffman; Grant Request: $5,000
• Jodie Cain-Lambert presented the Harve's Sport Shop Soccer Tournament Sports &
Events Authority Grant Application for the Tempo Soccer Club. Hosting the soccer
tournament in association with Tempo Soccer out of Tea, SD to utilize the Pepsi
Soccer Complex in Mitchell, SD. The grant request will be earmarked and go towards
referees' expense, which is their biggest expense.

--- PAGE 1 OF 6 ---

Date: April 5th-7th; 12th-14th; 19th-21st; 26th-28th; May 3rd-5th; & 10th-12th, 2024; Contact:
