Events Authority Grant Application. This event was to be hosted in Mitchell next year
(2025), but due to health issues in Yankton, the event has been relocated to Mitchell
for 2024. The event will run every Friday, Saturday, and Sunday of April and the first
two weekends in May. The grant request of $4,500 will be designated as follows:
$3,000 will go towards the prize fund and $1,500 will be to help offset costs for the
tournament manager coming from Rapid City. Mitchell hosted the Open Tournament in
2019 and there were 326 - 4-person teams.
D. Shootout at the Lake
Date: June 21st-22nd, 2024; Contact: Wade Musick; Grant Request: $20,000
• Sheldon Tobin presented the Shootout at the Lake Sports & Events Authority Grant
Application on behalf of the Horsemen's Sports Inc. Each night the event will consist of
a rodeo and a concert. This will be the second year this event has taken place. The
first night will be Ned Ledoux and the second night will be Dustin Evans and the Good
Times Band. Sheldon is estimating that the event will bring in 3,000 to 4,000 people
each night.
E. Palace City Kiwanis Half Marathon
Date: October 6th, 2024; Contact: Paula Deckert; Grant Request: $5,000
• Crystal Freund presented the Palace City Kiwanis Half Marathon Sports & Events
Authority Grant Application on behalf of the Kiwanis Club of Mitchell. This will be the
seventh year of the event. The grant request of $5,000 is for the SEA to consider being
the Event Sponsor. Their biggest expense is the timing system.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Kevin McCardle to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented and seconded by Doug Greenway. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb and Stephanie Ellwein reviewed the financial report as of March 7th, 2024.
This is the first financial report for the BID #4 - $2.00 monthly collections. As reviewed in the

--- PAGE 2 OF 6 ---


last meeting, the BID #4 Board recommended and the City Council approved the annual SEA
budget of $100,000 for 2024. Current expenses and award checks that have been written for
2024 are $31,750. Total Fund Balance of $68,250. There are three committed award checks
for the Special Olympics, 2025, 2026, and 2027 where the checks are designated to come out
of each respective years SEA Revenue budget. Currently, there are two award checks for
approved events where the checks have yet to be written for 2024. The Combat Veterans
Motorcycle Association Comedy Night ($1,000) and Knights of Columbus Special Olympics
Banquet ($1,700) award checks. Current Available Fund Balance of $65,550.
Collections in February (for January records) were $13,500.50 with four establishments not
past due, but reported partial collections. These four establishments have been contacted and
will submit the remaining collections. Going forward, the YTD comparisons for each month will
list and compare the total room nights sold, not the total $ amount of collections, since it only
makes sense to compare the number that remains consistent when collecting either the $1.50
or $2.00 tax.
YTD comparison for room nights sold were: up .6% (94 room nights sold) from 2023, up 1.0%
(164 room nights sold) for 2022, up 18.1% (2,970 room nights sold) for 2021, down 11.0%
(1,800 room nights sold) from 2020, up 11.8% (1,929 room nights sold) for 2019, and up 6.4%
(1,054 room nights sold) for 2018.
Motion: Motion was made by Bryan Dixon to approve the financial report as presented and
seconded by Jim Johnston. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form w/Financials to the SEA Committee:
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials
Palace Ice Festival (January 12th-13th, 2024)
• The event met expectations. This weekend's weather conditions were very poor, but
they had approximately 317 spectators, along with 32 skaters, 10 coaches, and 5 US
Figure Skating Judges & Representatives. The number of total hotel/motel room nights
sold was 29. The hotels/motels contacted were: Comfort Inn & Suites, Days Inn,
Hampton Inn, and Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites. The awarded funds ($750) were
used to offset expenses for the Palace Ice Festival Skating Competition. Profits will be
used to bring in skating clinicians to hold skating clinics here in Mitchell to help our
figure skaters learn and grow, and to have other out-of-town clubs come to Mitchell and
learn as well.

May 14th, 2024, SEA Advisory Committee Meeting Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                     May 14, 2024 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:00 PM 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, Kevin Nelson, 
Cory Aadland, Jason Christensen, Doug Greenway, LaRee Rumbolz, Tim Smith, and Jim 
Johnston 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Mayor Everson, Bryan Dixon, Emily Liedtke, 
and Dave Helleloid 
 
 Others present: Johanna Allen, Stephanie Ellwein, and Aaron Hieb 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed 
 applications for grant funding. The following application(s) were presented and considered: 
 
A. SoDak 16 Boys Basketball 

     • Cory Aadland presented the SoDak 16 Boys Basketball Grant Application. The two 
       games took place on Tuesday, March 5th. The grant request of $700 would cover the 
       Corn Palace rental fee.   

 
 
B. Lowell Rang Memorial Girls Fastpitch Softball Tournament 

     • Pat Larson and Jim Misiaszek presented the Lowell Rang Memorial Girls Fastpitch 
       Softball Tournament Grant Application. Currently, there are 72 teams registered to play 
       over 3 days, June 7th-9th. The grant request of $3,500 would go towards lodging for 
       the umpires. Since there is no longer a league in Mitchell, umpires have to be recruited 
       from other cities in the state. This tournament provides the umpires with pay per game, 
       meals, and lodging. Profits from the event have been used to pay for the portable 
       fences. 

 
 
C. Palace City Mountain Bike Classic 

     • Kourtney Denne and Emily Hohn presented the Palace City Mountain Bike Classic 
       Grant Application. This event was previously known as the Beers & Gears Mountain 
       Bike Race. A new non-profit was created known as the MAC Area Events Inc. Last 
       year's event hosted 65 riders. Currently, there are 45 registered riders, and on track to 
       host 90 riders. The majority of the riders that stay overnight will utilize campgrounds 
       over hotels. Friday night on June 21st is the rider social with the event taking place at 
       7:30 AM on Saturday, June 22nd. Profits from the event go back into the community 
       and the bike trails around Mitchell. This year's profits will go towards outdoor workout 
       equipment around the bike trails. The grant request of $2,000 would go towards the 
       timing equipment fees, which is their biggest expense. 

 
 
D. Arts in the Park 

     • Nancy Conzemius presented the Arts in the Park Grant Application. The Arts in the 
       Park hasn't taken place in Mitchell for 17 years. Currently, they have received around 
       100 vendor applications, which mostly come from out of state. The event dates are July 
       26th-28th. The grant request of $1,000 would go towards paying the city fees for 
       facility/equipment rental, security, advertising, and insurance. 

 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
presented and seconded by Jason Christensen. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion 
 passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of April 30th, 2024.  
 
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2024 are $46,250.  
 
Current Available Fund Balance of $53,750. 
 
These balances do reflect the $6,000 returned from the Special Olympics South Dakota State 
Basketball Tournament.  
 
Collections in February (for January records) still has one establishment that has not reported 
the full collection amount. Collections in March (for February records) increased to $14,276.50 
with zero establishments past due. Collections in April (for March records) is $17,769.00 with 
zero establishments past due. The YTD collections for 2024 is $61,027.50, which equates to 
32,929 total room nights sold.  
 
YTD comparison for room nights sold were: down 3.0% (981 room nights sold) from 2023, 
down 6.9% (2,284 room nights sold) from 2022, up 14.1% (4,647 room nights sold) from 2021, 
up 0.8% (248 room nights sold) from 2020, up 5.8% (1,904 room nights sold) from 2019, and 
down 2.3% (741 room nights sold) from 2018.  
 
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to approve the financial report as presented 
 and seconded by Kevin Nelson. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms w/Financials and SEA Survey to the SEA 
 Committee: 
 
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials 
Hanson Girl's & Boy's Classic (January 13th & 20th, 2024) 

     • The event met expectations. The Girl's Classic was canceled due to weather. An 
       estimated total spectator attendance of 3,000-3,300. The number of total hotel/motel 
       room nights sold was not able to accurately be tracked. The awarded funds ($1,500) 
       were used to pay for hospitality food for workers and teams. 

 
Dakota Oyate Challenge (January 25th-27th, 2024) 

     • The event met expectations. Schools and fans appreciated the availability of hotel 
       rooms and eating establishments. A total of 935 tickets were sold with 16 girls and 
       boys teams, along with five archery and 14 hand games teams. The number of total 
       hotel/motel room nights sold was around 200 plus for each night. The hotels/motels 
       contacted were: Comfort Inn & Suites, Hampton Inn, Holiday Inn, and Kelly Inn. The 
       awarded funds ($2,500) were used to help pay for the awards. Any profit will be used 
       to start up for next year's Dakota Oyate Challenge. 

 
DWU Indoor Futsal Classic (February 23rd-25th, 2024) 

     • The event exceeded expectations. The event grew this year and went smoothly. An 
       estimated total spectator attendance of 2,000-3,000, with 87 teams/870 athletes. The 
       number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was between 150-200. The hotels/motels 
       contacted were: Comfort Inn & Suites, Days Inn, Hampton Inn, Holiday Inn, Kelly Inn, 
       and Quality Inn. The awarded funds ($2,500) were used to pay for referee costs. Profit 
       of $18,581.61, which is split up between the men's and women's soccer as an annual 
       fundraiser. 
     • Aaron shared updates and information regarding DWU Soccer, Coach Reinhard & 
       Coach Hakari hosting a couple of youth events at the Pepsi Soccer Complex in July.  

 
Combat Veteran's Motorcycle Association Comedy Night (March 16th, 2024) 

     • The event exceeded expectations. We had an excellent turnout and fun was had by all. 
       A total of 160 attendees with 14 total hotel/motel room nights sold. The hotels/motels 
       contacted were: Comfort Inn & Suites, Hampton Inn, Kelly Inn, and Thunderbird Lodge. 
       The event will be hosted, most likely, in mid-March 2025 at the Highland. The awarded 
       funds ($1,000) were used to pay for venue and advertising. Profit of $5,885.93, with 
       $3,000 being donated to Helping with Horsepower and any additional funds go to area 
       veterans on an 'as needed' basis. 

 
Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament (April 12th-14th, 2024) 

     • The event met expectations. The event ran on schedule and participants had a great 
       time in Mitchell partaking in a variety of other activities along with hockey. An estimated 
       total spectator attendance of 200-300, with 20 teams = 280 players. The number of 
       total hotel/motel room nights sold was 88. The hotels/motels contacted were: Comfort 
       Inn & Suites, Days Inn, Holiday Inn, Kelly Inn, and Thunderbird Lodge. The event will 
       be hosted in the Mitchell Activies Center on April 11th-13th, 2025. The awarded funds 
       ($3,000) were used to pay for the City ice time bill. Profit of $10,045.58 will be used to 
       start a sponsorship for 8U hockey, "Little Devils". 

 
 
B. SEA Survey(s) 

     • Organization: South Dakota SkillsUSA; Main Contact: Nikki Mark; Date Completed: 
       4/12/2024 

 
 
6. Other Items 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee: 
 
A. SEA Banners on Display 
Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament (April 12th-14th, 2024) 

     • Hung SEA square banner on the entrance of the bleachers in the Toshiba (North) Rink 
       at the Mitchell Activities Center. 

 
Harve's Sport Shop Soccer Classic (April 20th-21st, 2024) 

     • Hung SEA square banner on the fence next to the south walk-through gate entrance at 
       the Pepsi Cola Soccer Complex. 

 
 
B. Thank You card 

     • Show Choir Classic (March 16th, 2024) 

 
 
C. Upcoming Events 
     • Candidate & Issue Forum (Tuesday, May 14th) 

          o  DWU Sherman Center 

     • Gilligan’s Island The Musical (Friday, May 17th – Sunday, May 19th) 

          o  Mitchell Area Community Theatre 

     • Mitchell High School Graduation (Sunday, May 19th) 

          o  The World’s Only Corn Palace 

     • Memorial Weekend in Mitchell (Saturday, May 25th) 

          o  South end of Mitchell Main Street 

     • Dr. Lucky’s Block Party/Street Dance (Saturday, May 25th) 

          o  Dr. Lucky’s Bar & Grill 

     • Memorial Day Services 2024 (Monday, May 27th) 

          o  VFW Post 2750 

     • Family Fun Day (Saturday, June 1st) 

          o  Davison County Fairgrounds 

     • Mitchell Main Street & Beyond: 1st Fridays on Main – Garden Party (Friday, June 7th) 

          o  Mitchell Main Street  

     • Lowell Rang Memorial Softball Tournament (Friday, June 7th – Sunday, June 9th) 

          o  Cadwell Sports Complex 

     • Archeology Awareness Weekend (Saturday, June 8th – Sunday, June 9th) 

          o  Mitchell Prehistoric Indian Village 

     • MAC Triathlon (Saturday, June 8th) 

          o  Hitchcock Park – Mitchell Aquatic Center 

         
   Complete list of events – MITCHELL CHAMBER EVENTS CALENDAR 
 
      *BOLD – Awarded Sports & Events Authority Grant funding. 
 
7. Executive Session in accordance with SDCL 9-34-19: Discussion of confidential trade 
secrets, commercial, or financial information. 
 
 
8. Approval of Funding Applications 
SoDak 16 Boys Basketball 
Date: March 5th, 2024; Contact: Cory Aadland; Grant Request: $700 

        • Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to award $700 and seconded by Jim 
          Johnston. Eight members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
        • Abstain: Cory Aadland abstained from voting. 

 
Lowell Rang Memorial Girls Fastpitch Softball Tournament 
Date: June 7th-9th, 2024; Contact: Pat Larson; Grant Request: $3,500 

        • Motion: Motion was made by Jim Johnston to award $2,000 and seconded by 
          LaRee Rumbolz. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
Palace City Mountain Bike Classic 
Date: June 21st-22nd, 2024; Contact: Kourtney Denne; Grant Request: $2,000 

        • Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to award $1,500 towards the timing 
          system fees and seconded by Jason Christensen. All members voted 'Aye' and the 
          motion passed. 

 
Arts in the Park 
 
Date: July 26th-28th, 2024; Contact: Nancy Conzemius/Jordan Hanson; Grant 
Request: $1,000 

        • Motion: Motion was made by LaRee Rumbolz to award $1,000 and seconded by 
          Doug Greenway. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
 
9. Next Meeting Date 
Kevin McCardle shared the next meeting date of Tuesday, June 11th, 2024, @ 2 PM - City 
 Hall, Council Chambers. 
 
10. Adjournment 
There being no further business to discuss.  
 
 Meeting adjourned by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:55 PM.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
April 9, 2024
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Mayor Everson @ 2:00 PM.
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Everson, Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson
(phone), Kevin Nelson, Doug Greenway, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, and
Jim Johnston.
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Cory Aadland, Jason Christensen, Bryan
Dixon, and Tim Smith.
Others present: Johanna Allen and Aaron Hieb.
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed
applications for grant funding. The following application(s) were presented and considered:
A. Special Olympics State Basketball Tournament
*Special Olympics South Dakota is proposing to donate $6,000 of the previously awarded
$12,000 for the Special Olympics State Basketball Tournament to the Mitchell Special
Olympics Delegation, since the event was shortened to one day because of weather.
B. Harve's Sport Shop Soccer Tournament
• Jodie Cain-Lambert provided an update regarding the progress of the Harve's Sport
Shop Soccer Tournament. Currently, there are 31 teams signed up to participate in the
current, two-day tournament, starting at 8 AM on Saturday, April 20th. This will now be
a U12 and U10 youth tournament because there are no high school teams due to prom
and school-affiliated activities. Because of the low turnout, Tempo Soccer Club:
Harve's Sport Shop Soccer Tournament is withdrawing their funding request of $5,000
and asking the committee to consider awarding whatever amount the committee
considers appropriate at their discretion based on the information and team(s) count
provided. The biggest expense for the event is the referee costs.
C. DBS Entertainment: Dr. Lucky's Street Dance

--- PAGE 1 OF 7 ---


• James "Bubba" Startz, DBS Entertainment, presented the Dr. Lucky's Street Dance
Grant Application to the committee. The event correlates with MMS&B Memorial
Weekend in Mitchell on Saturday, May 25th. The event will take place on W. 2nd Ave.
adjacent to Dr. Lucky's Bar & Grill. The grant request of $2,500 would go primarily
towards the promotional expenses.
D. MAC Triathlon
• Terasa Gillen and Emily Hohn presented the MAC Triathlon Grant Application. The
event takes place on Saturday, June 8th, starting at Hitchcock Park. The biggest
expense for this event is the timing system, which usually costs around $2,500.
Participant expectations are for around 85–90 athletes competing in the tri-series
events. There are not many hotel/motel room nights sold for this event, some stay at
campgrounds and others come the morning of the event traveling with very expensive
gear. They shared information about the sponsorship levels and what the exposure is
for being a sponsor.
E. South Dakota State & High Plains Territorial Cowboy Fast Draw Championships
• Diane Royalty and Troy Bollock presented the South Dakota State & High Plains
Territorial Cowboy Fast Draw Championships. This year's event dates have changed
from previous years. This year the event is hosted on Wednesday, September 11th
through Sunday, September 15th, which will piggyback with the Kansas and Nebraska
state shoots. The grant request of $4,500 will go towards 100% payout for a
designated bracket shoot sponsored by the SEA. The expectations with the 5 shoots
during the event that participation will be over 100 shooters.
F. 20th Annual OutKasts Car Show
• Jerry Wright, The 301 Rodz, presented the 20th Annual OutKasts Car Show Grant
Application. The 3-day event will take place from Friday, September 20th through
Sunday, September 22nd. This year's car show is correlating with MMS&B
Oktoberfest, and they are allowing all makes/models/years of cars to enter the car
show. The grant request of $2,000 will go towards awards and marketing materials
(radio ads, invitations, and fliers). The 301 Rodz is non-profit, so any profit from the
event will go back to the community.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Jim Johnston to approve the previous meeting minutes as

--- PAGE 2 OF 7 ---


presented and seconded by Kevin McCardle. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of April 5th, 2024.
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2024 are $43,750.
Current Available Fund Balance of $56,250.
Collections in February (for January records) have increased to $14,493.50 with only one
establishment that has not reported the full collection amount. Collections in March (for
February records) is $14,210.50 with one establishment that is past due. The YTD collections
for 2024 is $43,192.50, which equates to 24,011 total room nights sold.
YTD comparison for room nights sold were: up 2.0% (487 room nights sold) from 2023, down
2.7% (648 room nights sold) from 2022, up 20.8% (5,006 room nights sold) from 2021, down
10.7% (2,559 room nights sold) from 2020, up 9.6% (2,310 room nights sold) from 2019, and
up 4.6% (1,115 room nights sold) from 2018.
Motion: Motion was made by Kevin Nelson to approve the financial report as presented and
seconded by Doug Greenway. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms w/Financials to the SEA Committee:
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials
Hoop City Classic (December 28th-30th, 2023)
• The event was above expectations. The staff was exceptionally helpful. A total of 4,970
tickets were sold, and 756 comp tickets, along with 38 varsity teams, 17 JV teams, and
40 youth teams. The number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 340. The
hotels/motels contacted were: AmericInn Lodge & Suites, Comfort Inn & Suites, and
Hampton Inn. The event will be hosted in Mitchell at the Corn Palace, December 27th-
30th, 2024. The awarded funds ($10,000) were used to pay for expenses related to the
event as detailed on the attached P/L statement. Profit of $76.59 will assist with the
Youth Athletic Foundation mission.
SDMEA South Dakota Middle School All-State Band (March 1st-2nd, 2024)
• The event exceeded expectations. Thank you for your donation. Mitchell is a great
community to work with. Total spectator attendance of 700, along with 200 participants.
The number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 200. The hotels/motels contacted
were: AmericInn Lodge & Suites, Comfort Inn & Suites, Holiday Inn, and Kelly Inn &
Suites. Next year's event will be hosted on March 7th-8th, 2025. The awarded funds
($500) were used to purchase snacks for the students and teachers.

Aaron Hieb reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee:
A. SEA Banners on Display

documents.fileName: Hanson Classics 2024 supporters
documents.text:
Hanson Classic supporters:
The 2024 Hanson Classics were memorable and yet a little unforgettable.
The unpredictability of South Dakota weather can always make things interesting and especially a
challenge with this year no exception.
The Girls Classic was unable to be played on the date we planned.
However with an incredible amount of scheduling and cooperation we will have made up 7 of the 8
games.
On Jan. 19 th at the Corn Palace.
 	Mt. Vernon–Plankinton vs. Vermillion
 	Centerville vs. Wagner two classic teams included their regular season game with the other
games.
 	Ethan vs. Arlington
On Jan. 23 rd at Sioux Valley in Volga
 	Sisseton vs. Lennox took place at Sioux Valley
On Jan. 27 th at Leola
 	Timber Lake vs. Leola Frederick
On Feb. 3 rd at the Corn Palace
 	Hanson vs. Florence Henry
 	Centerville vs. Flandreau
On Feb. 13 th at Wall
 	Lyman vs. St. Thomas More
Note:
• 	All of the programs were able to be used at the various events.
• 	All students that earned a scholarship will still receive it.
• 	All participants will still receive their souvenir t-shirts.
A sincere appreciation to Doug Greenway at the Corn Palace, all of the great sponsors, the schools
participating and for everyone’s patience and cooperation in rescheduling of the games.
We appreciate the support in helping us with this very popular South Dakota event as well making the
very best that we could under the circumstances of the weather.
The Hanson Boys Classic did go on as planned with all teams making it to the Corn Palace for regular
scheduled date.
The day was filled with excellent match-ups and extremely competitive games.
Thank you.
Jim Bridge
Superintendent/Athletic Director

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                     June 11, 2024 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Mayor Everson @ 2:00 PM. 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Everson, Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, 
Kevin Nelson, Jason Christensen, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, 
and Jim Johnston. 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Cory Aadland, Doug Greenway, and Bryan 
Dixon. 
 
 Others present: Aaron Hieb, Stephanie Ellwein, and Johanna Allen. 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed 
 applications for grant funding. The following application(s) were presented and considered 
 
A. SEA Promotional Water Bottle Cost Quote 

     • Aaron Hieb presented and shared the two, SEA Promotional Water Bottle Cost 
       Quote(s), one from McCleod's and the other from Make-It-Mine Design. 

 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Kevin Nelson to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
 presented and seconded by Tim Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of June 5th, 2024.  
 
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2024 are $50,750. 
 
There is one event that has been awarded funding, but the award check has not been written 
yet. The SoDak 16 Boys Basketball award check of $700 will be approved at the June 17th 
City Council meeting and written June 18th, and put in the mail. 
 
Current Available Fund Balance of $48,550.  
 
Collections in February (for January records) still has one establishment that has not reported 
the full collection amount. Collections in May (for April records) are $24,132.00 with zero 
establishments past due. The YTD collections for 2024 is $85,159.50, which equates to 
44,995 total room nights sold.  
 
YTD comparison for room nights sold were: up 2.8% (1,273 room nights sold) from 2023, 
down 0.4% (186 room nights sold) from 2022, up 14.6% (6,556 room nights sold) from 2021, 
up 20.1% (9,028 room nights sold) from 2020, up 10.6% (4,783 room nights sold) from 2019, 
and up 5.6% (2,529 room nights sold) from 2018.  
 
Motion: Motion was made by Jim Johnston to approve the financial report as presented and 
 seconded by Jason Christensen. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form w/Financials to the SEA Committee: 
 
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials 
DWU/Culver's High School Basketball Classic (February 9th-10th, 2024) 

     • The event exceeded expectations. A total of 34 boys and girls teams competed in the 
       classic. St. Thomas More, Potter County, and Wall stayed at hotels/motels. The 
       hotels/motels contacted were: Comfort Inn & Suites and Hampton Inn. The awarded 
       funds ($3,000) were used to help pay for officials and table workers. A net income of 
       $16,104.33 was used towards scholarships for the two basketball programs. 

 
 
6. Other Items 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee: 
 
A. SEA Banners on Display 
Lowell Rang Memorial Girls Fastpitch Softball Tournament (June 7th-9th, 2024) 

     • Hung SEA square banner on the fence at the entrance of the east complex at Cadwell 
       Park. 

 
MAC Triathlon (June 8th, 2024) 

     • A SEA square banner was set up at the finish line at Hitchcock Park. 

 
 
B. USA Paralympic Sled Hockey Team Camp 
January 17th-21st, 2024 
     • https://youtu.be/VFurFhzsDuw?si=i5zdSWOKJ3KWaEQu 

 
 
C. Upcoming Events 

     • Farmers Market (June 12th, 19th, 26th, July 3rd, 10th, 17th, 24th, 31st, August 7th, & 
       14th) 
            o Hitchcock Park 
     • Mitchell Municipal Band Concert (June 12th, 19th, 26th, July 3rd, 10th, 17th, 24th, & 
       31st) 
            o Hitchcock Park Band Shell

            o Iverson Auto

            o Hitchcock Park

            o Palace Park Mall 
     • Shootout at the Lake (Friday, June 21st & Saturday, June 22nd) 
            o Horseman’s Sports Arena

            o Lake Mitchell North Trail Loop

7. Executive Session in accordance with SDCL 9-34-19: Discussion of confidential trade 
secrets, commercial, or financial information. 
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid and second by LaRee Rumbolz to go into 
 Executive Session. All members voted 'Aye.'

Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
May 14, 2024
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:00 PM
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, Kevin Nelson,
Cory Aadland, Jason Christensen, Doug Greenway, LaRee Rumbolz, Tim Smith, and Jim
Johnston
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Mayor Everson, Bryan Dixon, Emily Liedtke,
and Dave Helleloid
Others present: Johanna Allen, Stephanie Ellwein, and Aaron Hieb
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed
applications for grant funding. The following application(s) were presented and considered:
A. SoDak 16 Boys Basketball
• Cory Aadland presented the SoDak 16 Boys Basketball Grant Application. The two
games took place on Tuesday, March 5th. The grant request of $700 would cover the
Corn Palace rental fee.
B. Lowell Rang Memorial Girls Fastpitch Softball Tournament
• Pat Larson and Jim Misiaszek presented the Lowell Rang Memorial Girls Fastpitch
Softball Tournament Grant Application. Currently, there are 72 teams registered to play
over 3 days, June 7th-9th. The grant request of $3,500 would go towards lodging for
the umpires. Since there is no longer a league in Mitchell, umpires have to be recruited
from other cities in the state. This tournament provides the umpires with pay per game,
meals, and lodging. Profits from the event have been used to pay for the portable
fences.

--- PAGE 1 OF 6 ---


C. Palace City Mountain Bike Classic
• Kourtney Denne and Emily Hohn presented the Palace City Mountain Bike Classic
Grant Application. This event was previously known as the Beers & Gears Mountain
Bike Race. A new non-profit was created known as the MAC Area Events Inc. Last
year's event hosted 65 riders. Currently, there are 45 registered riders, and on track to
host 90 riders. The majority of the riders that stay overnight will utilize campgrounds
over hotels. Friday night on June 21st is the rider social with the event taking place at
7:30 AM on Saturday, June 22nd. Profits from the event go back into the community
and the bike trails around Mitchell. This year's profits will go towards outdoor workout
equipment around the bike trails. The grant request of $2,000 would go towards the
timing equipment fees, which is their biggest expense.
D. Arts in the Park
• Nancy Conzemius presented the Arts in the Park Grant Application. The Arts in the
Park hasn't taken place in Mitchell for 17 years. Currently, they have received around
100 vendor applications, which mostly come from out of state. The event dates are July
26th-28th. The grant request of $1,000 would go towards paying the city fees for
facility/equipment rental, security, advertising, and insurance.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented and seconded by Jason Christensen. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion
passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of April 30th, 2024.
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2024 are $46,250.
Current Available Fund Balance of $53,750.
These balances do reflect the $6,000 returned from the Special Olympics South Dakota State
Basketball Tournament.
Collections in February (for January records) still has one establishment that has not reported
the full collection amount. Collections in March (for February records) increased to $14,276.50
with zero establishments past due. Collections in April (for March records) is $17,769.00 with
zero establishments past due. The YTD collections for 2024 is $61,027.50, which equates to
32,929 total room nights sold.
YTD comparison for room nights sold were: down 3.0% (981 room nights sold) from 2023,
down 6.9% (2,284 room nights sold) from 2022, up 14.1% (4,647 room nights sold) from 2021,

--- PAGE 2 OF 6 ---


up 0.8% (248 room nights sold) from 2020, up 5.8% (1,904 room nights sold) from 2019, and
down 2.3% (741 room nights sold) from 2018.
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to approve the financial report as presented
and seconded by Kevin Nelson. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms w/Financials and SEA Survey to the SEA
Committee:
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials
Hanson Girl's & Boy's Classic (January 13th & 20th, 2024)
• The event met expectations. The Girl's Classic was canceled due to weather. An
estimated total spectator attendance of 3,000-3,300. The number of total hotel/motel
room nights sold was not able to accurately be tracked. The awarded funds ($1,500)
were used to pay for hospitality food for workers and teams.
Dakota Oyate Challenge (January 25th-27th, 2024)
• The event met expectations. Schools and fans appreciated the availability of hotel
rooms and eating establishments. A total of 935 tickets were sold with 16 girls and
boys teams, along with five archery and 14 hand games teams. The number of total
hotel/motel room nights sold was around 200 plus for each night. The hotels/motels
contacted were: Comfort Inn & Suites, Hampton Inn, Holiday Inn, and Kelly Inn. The
awarded funds ($2,500) were used to help pay for the awards. Any profit will be used
to start up for next year's Dakota Oyate Challenge.
DWU Indoor Futsal Classic (February 23rd-25th, 2024)
• The event exceeded expectations. The event grew this year and went smoothly. An
estimated total spectator attendance of 2,000-3,000, with 87 teams/870 athletes. The
number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was between 150-200. The hotels/motels
contacted were: Comfort Inn & Suites, Days Inn, Hampton Inn, Holiday Inn, Kelly Inn,
and Quality Inn. The awarded funds ($2,500) were used to pay for referee costs. Profit
of $18,581.61, which is split up between the men's and women's soccer as an annual
fundraiser.
• Aaron shared updates and information regarding DWU Soccer, Coach Reinhard &
Coach Hakari hosting a couple of youth events at the Pepsi Soccer Complex in July.
Combat Veteran's Motorcycle Association Comedy Night (March 16th, 2024)
• The event exceeded expectations. We had an excellent turnout and fun was had by all.
A total of 160 attendees with 14 total hotel/motel room nights sold. The hotels/motels
contacted were: Comfort Inn & Suites, Hampton Inn, Kelly Inn, and Thunderbird Lodge.
The event will be hosted, most likely, in mid-March 2025 at the Highland. The awarded
funds ($1,000) were used to pay for venue and advertising. Profit of $5,885.93, with

$3,000 being donated to Helping with Horsepower and any additional funds go to area
veterans on an 'as needed' basis.
Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament (April 12th-14th, 2024)
• The event met expectations. The event ran on schedule and participants had a great
time in Mitchell partaking in a variety of other activities along with hockey. An estimated
total spectator attendance of 200-300, with 20 teams = 280 players. The number of
total hotel/motel room nights sold was 88. The hotels/motels contacted were: Comfort
Inn & Suites, Days Inn, Holiday Inn, Kelly Inn, and Thunderbird Lodge. The event will
be hosted in the Mitchell Activies Center on April 11th-13th, 2025. The awarded funds
($3,000) were used to pay for the City ice time bill. Profit of $10,045.58 will be used to
start a sponsorship for 8U hockey, "Little Devils".

July 9th, 2024, SEA Advisory Committee Meeting Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                      July 9, 2024 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:00 PM. 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin 
Nelson, Cory Aadland, Doug Greenway, Bryan Dixon, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave 
Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston. 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Jill Larson and Jason Christensen. 
 
 Others present: Aaron Hieb, Stephanie Ellwein, and Johanna Allen. 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed 
 applications for grant funding. The following application(s) were presented and considered: 
 
A. Mitchell Disc Golf Open 2024 

     • Cary Muilenburg presented the Mitchell Disc Golf Open 2024 Grant Application. The 
       Mitchell Disc Golf Open is on Saturday, July 20th at Dry Run Creek Disc Golf Course. 
       The grant application requests $500 to help cover the $300 Special Event Permit Dry 
       Run Creek Disc Golf Course Closure Fee. Currently, there are five participants signed 
       up for the tournament. 

 
 
B. South Dakota State Amateur Baseball Tournament 

     • Jim Johnston presented the SD State Amateur Baseball Tournament Grant 
       Application. The tournament will run from August 7th-18th at Cadwell Stadium and 
       Drake Field. The event estimates that 10,000 to 13,000 will come to Mitchell during this 
       tournament. Brandon Valley will host the tournament in 2025, but the tournament will 
       be back in Mitchell for 2026 and 2027. The grant request of $5,000 will go towards 
       catered meals for the commissioners, field costs, and operating costs. Hotel room 
       nights sold are estimated to be around 350. 

 
 
C. Cornicupia 2024 

     • Alyson Palmer and Arien Tingle presented the Cornicupia 2024 Grant Application. 
       Cornicupia will be on Friday, September 6th through Sunday, September 8th at the 
       Pepsi Soccer Complex. The last tournament was hosted by Mitchell Soccer 
       Association at the Pepsi Soccer Complex in 2019. The grant request of $7,500 will go 
       towards field costs and referees, which are their biggest expenses. They are hoping for 
       20–22 teams to register for this tournament. Hotel room nights sold are estimated to be 
       around 390. 

 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by LaRee Rumbolz to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
 presented and seconded by Bryan Dixon. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of July 2nd, 2024.  
 
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2024 are $51,450.  
 
Current Available Fund Balance of $48,550. 
 
Collections in February (for January records) have all been collected; $14,549.00.  
 
Collections in June (for May records) are $29,828.00 with one establishment past due.  
 
The YTD collections for 2024 is $115,043.00, which equates to 59,936 total room nights sold.  
 
YTD comparison for room nights sold were: up 4.0% (2,384 room nights sold) from 2023, up 
0.9% (522 room nights sold) from 2022, up 11.0% (6,616 room nights sold) from 2021, up 
29.9% (17,917 room nights sold) from 2020, up 11.3% (6,777 room nights sold) from 2019, 
and up 7.6% (4,547 room nights sold) from 2018.  
 
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the financial report as presented and 
 seconded by Doug Greenway. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms w/Financials with the SEA Committee: 
 
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials 
Show Choir Classic (March 16th, 2024) 

     • The event met expectations. An estimated total spectator attendance of 1,200. Total 
       participants of 1,000. The number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 75 
       (Comfort Inn and Hampton Inn). The awarded funds ($5,000) were used primarily to 
       pay for judges' expenses. The profit of $16,763.05 will be used for travel and show 
       expenses in the upcoming competition season. 

 
Special Olympics State Basketball Tournament (March 23rd, 2024) 

     • The event was above expectations, even though the event was shortened to a one-day 
       event due to incoming weather. An estimated total spectator attendance of 1,000. Total 
       participants of 900+. The number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 150 
       (AmericInn and Comfort Inn). The awarded funds ($6,000) were used to offset 
       expenses at the event. The profit of $2,886.32 was used towards staffing expenses. 
       $12,000 was donated to Phil Collins and the Mitchell Special Olympics Delegation. 

 
 
6. Other Items 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee: 
 
A. Upcoming Events 

     • Farmers Market (July 10th, 17th, 24th, 31st, August 7th, & 14th) 
            o Hitchcock Park 
     • Mitchell Municipal Band Concert (July 10th, 17th, 24th, & 31st) 
            o Hitchcock Park Band Shell 
     • Summer Courtyard Concert Series (July 12th) 
            o Palace Park Mall 
     • Corn Palace Stampede Community Kick-Off (Tuesday, July 16th) 
            o The Arena at Stampede Park 
     • Corn Palace Stampede Rodeo (Thursday, July 18th – Sunday, July 21st) 
            o The Arena at Stampede Park 
     • Corn Palace Stampede Rodeo Parade (Saturday, July 20th) 
            o Mitchell Main Street 
     • Crazy Days (Friday, July 19th – Saturday, July 20th) 
            o Mitchell Main Street 
     • Children’s Day at the Village (Saturday, July 20th) 
            o Mitchell Prehistoric Indian Village 
     • Mitchell Open Disc Golf Tournament (Saturday, July 20th) 
            o Dry Run Creek Disc Golf Course 
     • Corn Palace Stampede Rodeo Chili Cook-Off & Family Fun Day (Sunday, July 21st) 
            o The Arena at Stampede Park 
     • Arts in the PARK (Friday, July 26th – Sunday, July 28th) 
            o Hitchcock Park 
     • Palace City Pre-Sturgis Party (Thursday, August 1st) 
            o Mitchell Main Street 
     • Mitchell A.C.T. Presents “The Church Basement Ladies in a Mighty Fortress is Our 
       Basement” (Friday, August 2nd – Sunday, August 4th & Friday, August 9th – Sunday, 
       August 11th) 
            o Mitchell Area Community Theatre 

 
Complete list of events – MITCHELL CHAMBER EVENTS CALENDAR 
 
 *BOLD – Awarded Sports & Events Authority Grant funding. 
 
7. Executive Session in accordance with SDCL 9-34-19: Discussion of confidential trade 
secrets, commercial, or financial information. 
 
 
8. Approval of Funding Applications 
Mitchell Disc Golf Open 2024 
Date: July 20th, 2024; Contact: Cary Muilenburg; Grant Request: $500 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to deny funding based on the small 
       number of players (5) currently registered and if the field of participants remains small, 
       it should not be necessary to close the Dry Run Creek Disc Golf Course, and seconded 
       by Dave Helleloid. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
South Dakota State Amateur Baseball Tournament 
Date: August 7th-18th, 2024; Contact: Jim Johnston; Grant Request: $5,000 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to award $5,000 and seconded by Bryan 
       Dixon. Nine members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
     • Abstain: Tim Smith and Jim Johnston abstained from voting. 

 
Cornicupia 2024 
Date: September 6th-8th, 2024; Contact: Scott Mullenmeister; Grant Request: $7,500 

     • Motion: Motion was made by LaRee Rumbolz to table the funding decision until the 
       August 13th meeting when the Mitchell Soccer Association will share an updated 
       presentation providing an accurate list of teams registered, and seconded by Bryan 
       Dixon. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
 
9. Next Meeting Date 
Kevin McCardle shared the next meeting date of Tuesday, August 13th, 2024, @ 2 PM - City 
 Hall, Council Chambers. 
 
10. Adjournment 
There being no further business to discuss.  
 
 Meeting adjourned by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:56 PM.

***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

every year by the South Dakota State Amateur Baseball
Association. The association consists of 10 commissioners and
three officers who stay in Mitchell throughout the tournament. On
days when we have two sessions, we provide meals at Cadwell
Park for the association members in between the two sessions.
We also provide lunch after the old timers game the first day of
the tournament. We also have a social with our volunteers and
the commissioners during the championship game. These are
three things we wouldn't be able to provide without funding by
Sports and Events Authority. We consider these to be three
important things to show our hospitality to the state
commissioners and letting them know how much we
appreciate having the tournament in Mitchell. We also believe it
is important to provide a social at the end of the tournament for
our 60 plus volunteers who give of their time during the 12-day
event because without them we wouldn't be able to host the
tournament. Without the funding we wouldn't be able to provide
these things.

August 13th, 2024, SEA Advisory Committee Meeting Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                    August 13, 2024 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:00 PM. 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin 
Nelson, Jason Christensen, Doug Greenway, Dave Helleloid, and Tim Smith. 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Jill Larson, Cory Aadland, Bryan Dixon, LaRee 
Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, and Jim Johnston. 
 
 Others present: Aaron Hieb, Stephanie Ellwein, and Johanna Allen. 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed 
 applications for grant funding. The following application(s) were presented and considered: 
 
A. Tour de Corn 

     • Kourtney Denne presented the Tour de Corn Grant Application, which is requesting 
       $3,000.  

 
This year will be the 30th Annual. They are expecting around 350 riders this year, which 
begins Friday, August 16th evening and goes until Sunday, August 18th. They estimate about 
50% of the riders are outside the 50+ mile radius. Much of the profits raised from this event go 
 back to the Mitchell community and Lake Mitchell Trails. 
 
B. Cornicupia 2024 

     • Scott Mullenmeister presented the follow-up information for Cornicupia 2024, which is 
       requesting $7,500. 

 
Mitchell Soccer Association is a non-profit. Currently, there are 13 out of town (Rapid City-
Ignite, Brookings, Watertown, Brandon Valley, Larchwood, IA, and Aberdeen) teams 
registered, along with 7 teams from Mitchell. This tournament will host the U10, U12, U13, & 
U14 divisions. The largest expense is referees. The Mitchell Soccer Association is 
coordinating with some main street businesses (Subway, Big Dummy's, Scoreboard, and Main 
Street Mercantile) about running meal specials during their tournament to get teams/fans 
 downtown in between games.  
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
 presented, and seconded by Tim Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb and Stephanie Ellwein reviewed the financial report as of July 29th, 2024.  
 
SEA Revenue received an additional $50,000 for FY 2024 based on the BID #4 Board 
recommendation. 
 
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2024 are $56,450.  
 
Current Available Fund Balance of $93,550.  
 
Collections in June (for May records) are $29,828.00 with one establishment past due. 
Collections in July (for June records) are $31,240.00 with two establishments past due.  
 
The YTD collections for 2024 is $146,283.00, which equates to 75,556 total room nights sold.  
 
YTD comparison for room nights sold were: up 0.6% (419 room nights sold) from 2023, 
down 3.1% (2,361 room nights sold) from 2022, up 3.6% (2,709 room nights sold) from 2021, 
up 28.4% (21,449 room nights sold) from 2020, up 4.8% (3,630 room nights sold) from 2019, 
and up 1.9% (1,466 room nights sold) from 2018.  
 
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to approve the financial report as presented, 
 and seconded by Tim Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms w/Financials with the SEA Committee: 
 
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials 
Cabin Fever Auction (February 23rd-24th, 2024) 

     • The event was above expectations. An estimated total spectator attendance of 600. 
       Total participants of 296. The estimated number of total hotel/motel room nights sold 
       was 300 (AmericInn, Comfort Inn, and Thunderbird Lodge). The awarded funds 
       ($1,500) were used towards advertising and hotel rooms. The profit of $12,847.21 will 
       go towards making next year better. This year, items were of higher quality and sold at 
       higher than normal prices. 

 
SD United States Bowling Congress Open Tournament (April 5th-7th, 12th-14th, 19th-21st, 
26th-28th, May 3rd-5th, & 10th-12th, 2024) 

     • The event met expectations. Total participants of 1,164 bowlers, which is 291 4-person 
       teams. The number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was estimated based on the 
       QR Code results, which was an estimated 129+ (Comfort Inn, Days Inn, Hampton Inn, 
       and Holiday Inn Express). The awarded funds ($3,000) were added to the tournament 
       prize fund. The PL statement showed no profit. 

 
DWU Spring Golf Invite (April 8th-9th, 2024) 

     • The event was above expectations. An estimated total spectator attendance of 30-50. 
       Total participants of 83 golfers, 10 coaches. The number of total hotel/motel room 
       nights sold was estimated at 50-65 (Comfort Inn, Hampton Inn, and Holiday Inn 
       Express). The awarded funds ($1,500) were used for player/coaches meals and range 
       ball expenses. Total expenses for the event were $7,520. 

 
Harve's Sport Shop Soccer Classic (April 20th-21st, 2024) 

     • The event was above expectations. The staff were very accommodating and helpful. 
       An estimated total spectator attendance of 1,500. Total participants of 372. The 
       estimated number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 10 (Comfort Inn and Days 
       Inn). The awarded funds ($2,500) were used to offset tournament expenses. The profit 
       of $7,609.42 will be used towards future tournaments. 

 
 
6. Other Items 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee: 
 
A. Thank You Card 
 Palace City Mountain Bike Classic (June 29th, 2024) 
 
B. Upcoming Events 

     • South Dakota State Amateur Baseball Tournament (August 7th-18th) 
            o Cadwell Park  
     • Farmers Market (August 14th) 
            o Hitchcock Park 
     • Summer Courtyard Concert Series – Brian Hoffman (August 16th) 
            o Palace Park Mall 
     • Tour de Corn (August 16th-18th) 
            o Kiwanis Park, Corn Palace, Lake Mitchell 
     • MHS Marching Band 2024 Boat Parade (August 16th) 
            o Lake Mitchell 
     • Dakotafest (August 20th-22nd) 
            o 2300 E. Spruce St. 
     • Corn Palace Festival (August 21st-25th) 
            o Mitchell Main Street 
     • Mitchell Blood Donor Day (August 23rd) 
            o 819 E. Spruce St. Ste. 150 
     • Vern Eide Wheels Wednesday (August 28th) 
            o Vern Eide Ford south parking lot 
     • South Dakota State Pedal Pull (September 2nd) 
            o Corn Palace 
     • 1st Fridays on Main (September 6th) 
            o Mitchell Main Street 

 
Complete list of events – MITCHELL CHAMBER EVENTS CALENDAR 
 
 *BOLD – Awarded Sports & Events Authority Grant funding. 
 
7. Executive Session in accordance with SDCL 9-34-19: Discussion of confidential trade 
secrets, commercial, or financial information. 
 
 
8. Approval of Funding Applications 
Tour de Corn 
Date: August 16th-18th, 2024; Contact: Kourtney Denne; Grant Request: $3,000 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to award $2,000, and seconded by Doug 
       Greenway. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
Cornicupia 2024 
Date: September 6th-8th, 2024; Contact: Scott Mullenmeister; Grant Request: $7,500 

     • Tabled from the July meeting. 
     • Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to award $5,000, plus the Sports & Events 
       Authority Advisory Committee will have future discussion and consideration to the 
       Mitchell Soccer Association about awarding future, financial, tournament incentives for 
       team(s) outside a 60+ mile radius, and seconded by Doug Greenway. All members 
       voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
 
9. Next Meeting Date 
Kevin McCardle shared the next meeting date of Tuesday, September 10th, 2024, @ 2 PM - 
 City Hall, Council Chambers. 
 
10. Adjournment 
There being no further business to discuss.  
 
 Meeting adjourned by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:51 PM.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
July 9, 2024
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:00 PM.
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin
Nelson, Cory Aadland, Doug Greenway, Bryan Dixon, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave
Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston.
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Jill Larson and Jason Christensen.
Others present: Aaron Hieb, Stephanie Ellwein, and Johanna Allen.
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed
applications for grant funding. The following application(s) were presented and considered:
A. Mitchell Disc Golf Open 2024
• Cary Muilenburg presented the Mitchell Disc Golf Open 2024 Grant Application. The
Mitchell Disc Golf Open is on Saturday, July 20th at Dry Run Creek Disc Golf Course.
The grant application requests $500 to help cover the $300 Special Event Permit Dry
Run Creek Disc Golf Course Closure Fee. Currently, there are five participants signed
up for the tournament.
B. South Dakota State Amateur Baseball Tournament
• Jim Johnston presented the SD State Amateur Baseball Tournament Grant
Application. The tournament will run from August 7th-18th at Cadwell Stadium and
Drake Field. The event estimates that 10,000 to 13,000 will come to Mitchell during this
tournament. Brandon Valley will host the tournament in 2025, but the tournament will
be back in Mitchell for 2026 and 2027. The grant request of $5,000 will go towards
catered meals for the commissioners, field costs, and operating costs. Hotel room
nights sold are estimated to be around 350.

--- PAGE 1 OF 4 ---


C. Cornicupia 2024
• Alyson Palmer and Arien Tingle presented the Cornicupia 2024 Grant Application.
Cornicupia will be on Friday, September 6th through Sunday, September 8th at the
Pepsi Soccer Complex. The last tournament was hosted by Mitchell Soccer
Association at the Pepsi Soccer Complex in 2019. The grant request of $7,500 will go
towards field costs and referees, which are their biggest expenses. They are hoping for
20–22 teams to register for this tournament. Hotel room nights sold are estimated to be
around 390.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by LaRee Rumbolz to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented and seconded by Bryan Dixon. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of July 2nd, 2024.
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2024 are $51,450.
Current Available Fund Balance of $48,550.
Collections in February (for January records) have all been collected; $14,549.00.
Collections in June (for May records) are $29,828.00 with one establishment past due.
The YTD collections for 2024 is $115,043.00, which equates to 59,936 total room nights sold.
YTD comparison for room nights sold were: up 4.0% (2,384 room nights sold) from 2023, up
0.9% (522 room nights sold) from 2022, up 11.0% (6,616 room nights sold) from 2021, up
29.9% (17,917 room nights sold) from 2020, up 11.3% (6,777 room nights sold) from 2019,
and up 7.6% (4,547 room nights sold) from 2018.
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the financial report as presented and
seconded by Doug Greenway. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms w/Financials with the SEA Committee:
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials
Show Choir Classic (March 16th, 2024)
• The event met expectations. An estimated total spectator attendance of 1,200. Total
participants of 1,000. The number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 75
(Comfort Inn and Hampton Inn). The awarded funds ($5,000) were used primarily to
pay for judges' expenses. The profit of $16,763.05 will be used for travel and show

--- PAGE 2 OF 4 ---


expenses in the upcoming competition season.
Special Olympics State Basketball Tournament (March 23rd, 2024)
• The event was above expectations, even though the event was shortened to a one-day
event due to incoming weather. An estimated total spectator attendance of 1,000. Total
participants of 900+. The number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 150
(AmericInn and Comfort Inn). The awarded funds ($6,000) were used to offset
expenses at the event. The profit of $2,886.32 was used towards staffing expenses.
$12,000 was donated to Phil Collins and the Mitchell Special Olympics Delegation.
6. Other Items
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee:
A. Upcoming Events
• Farmers Market (July 10th, 17th, 24th, 31st, August 7th, & 14th)
o Hitchcock Park
• Mitchell Municipal Band Concert (July 10th, 17th, 24th, & 31st)
o Hitchcock Park Band Shell
• Summer Courtyard Concert Series (July 12th)
o Palace Park Mall
• Corn Palace Stampede Community Kick-Off (Tuesday, July 16th)
o The Arena at Stampede Park
• Corn Palace Stampede Rodeo (Thursday, July 18th – Sunday, July 21st)
o The Arena at Stampede Park
• Corn Palace Stampede Rodeo Parade (Saturday, July 20th)
o Mitchell Main Street
• Crazy Days (Friday, July 19th – Saturday, July 20th)
o Mitchell Main Street
• Children’s Day at the Village (Saturday, July 20th)
o Mitchell Prehistoric Indian Village
• Mitchell Open Disc Golf Tournament (Saturday, July 20th)
o Dry Run Creek Disc Golf Course
• Corn Palace Stampede Rodeo Chili Cook-Off & Family Fun Day (Sunday, July 21st)
o The Arena at Stampede Park
• Arts in the PARK (Friday, July 26th – Sunday, July 28th)
o Hitchcock Park
• Palace City Pre-Sturgis Party (Thursday, August 1st)
o Mitchell Main Street
• Mitchell A.C.T. Presents “The Church Basement Ladies in a Mighty Fortress is Our
Basement” (Friday, August 2nd – Sunday, August 4th & Friday, August 9th – Sunday,
August 11th)
o Mitchell Area Community Theatre

--- PAGE 3 OF 4 ---


Complete list of events – MITCHELL CHAMBER EVENTS CALENDAR
*BOLD – Awarded Sports & Events Authority Grant funding.
7. Executive Session in accordance with SDCL 9-34-19: Discussion of confidential trade
secrets, commercial, or financial information.
8. Approval of Funding Applications
Mitchell Disc Golf Open 2024
Date: July 20th, 2024; Contact: Cary Muilenburg; Grant Request: $500
• Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to deny funding based on the small
number of players (5) currently registered and if the field of participants remains small,
it should not be necessary to close the Dry Run Creek Disc Golf Course, and seconded
by Dave Helleloid. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
South Dakota State Amateur Baseball Tournament
Date: August 7th-18th, 2024; Contact: Jim Johnston; Grant Request: $5,000
• Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to award $5,000 and seconded by Bryan
Dixon. Nine members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
• Abstain: Tim Smith and Jim Johnston abstained from voting.
Cornicupia 2024
Date: September 6th-8th, 2024; Contact: Scott Mullenmeister; Grant Request: $7,500
• Motion: Motion was made by LaRee Rumbolz to table the funding decision until the
August 13th meeting when the Mitchell Soccer Association will share an updated
presentation providing an accurate list of teams registered, and seconded by Bryan
Dixon. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
9. Next Meeting Date
Kevin McCardle shared the next meeting date of Tuesday, August 13th, 2024, @ 2 PM - City
Hall, Council Chambers.
10. Adjournment
There being no further business to discuss.
Meeting adjourned by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:56 PM.

documents.fileName: September 10th, 2024, SEA Advisory Committee Meeting Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                  September 10, 2024 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:00 PM. 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, 
Jason Christensen, Doug Greenway, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, and Tim 
Smith. 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Kevin Nelson, Cory Aadland, Bryan Dixon, and 
Jim Johnston. 
 
 Others present: Stephanie Ellwein and Aaron Hieb. 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed 
 applications for grant funding. The following application(s) were presented and considered: 
 
A. Raise Em Rank Bull Riding Series Finals 

     • Dillon Swanson presented the Raise Em Rank Bull Riding Series Finals Grant 
       Application via conference phone, which is requesting $5,000. 

 
This year will be the 3rd year for the series finals in Mitchell at The World's Only Corn Palace. 
The event will take place on Friday, October 4th - Saturday, October 5th. There will likely be 
between 50-60 head of bulls being bucked each night. The youth participation will be limited to 
35–40 minutes. Participants will come from Texas, Australia, South Dakota, North Dakota, and 
Nebraska. The series finals (Corn Palace-Mitchell, SD) have been promoted throughout the 
entire summer at all the Raise Em Rank events. The grant request goes towards facility rental 
 and marketing/advertising for the series finals. 
 
B. Dakota Oyate Challenge Volleyball 

     • George Erdahl, Dakota Oyate Challenge Board of Director, presented the Dakota 
       Oyate Challenge Volleyball Grant Application, which is requesting $6,500 plus 11 
       COMP hotel rooms for 2 nights. 

 This is a 1st annual event, which they are expanding off of the Dakota Oyate Challenge 
Basketball, and cross-country may be added next year. There will be 16 teams participating in 
this event on Friday, October 11th - Saturday, October 12th, 2024. The grant request will be 
 used to offset some of the expenses for a new event. 
 
C. Hoop City Classic 

     • Brad Bartscher, Hoop City Classic Representative, presented the Hoop City Classic 
       Grant Application, which is requesting $15,000. 

 
This is the 13th annual Hoop City Classic which takes place from Friday, December 27th 
through Monday, December 30th. As of last year, the entire event moved back to Mitchell, 
which is the plan going forward for years to follow. This year there are 30-32 varsity teams, 18 
 junior varsity teams, and 60-80 youth teams. Last year the event hosted 46 youth teams. 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by LaRee Rumbolz to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
 presented, and seconded by Tim Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of September 6th, 2024.  
 
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2024 are $63,450.  
 
Current Available Fund Balance of $86,550.  
 
Collections in June (for May records) are $29,834.00 with all collected. Collections in July (for 
June records) are $33,762.00 with all collected. Collections in August (for July records) are 
$36,839.00 with all collected.  
 
The YTD collections for 2024 is $185,650.00, which equates to 95,240 total room nights sold.  
 
YTD comparison for room nights sold were: up 2.3% (2,214 room nights sold) from 2023, 
down 2.1% (1,964 room nights sold) from 2022, up 1.9% (1,766 room nights sold) from 2021, 
up 27.2% (25,887 room nights sold) from 2020, up 2.2% (2,094 room nights sold) from 2019, 
and up 2.2% (2,104 room nights sold) from 2018.  
 
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the financial report as presented, and 
 seconded by Doug Greenway. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
 None were submitted at this time. 
 
6. Other Items 
 Aaron Hieb and Doug Greenway reviewed the following item(s) with the SEA Committee: 
 A. Upcoming Events 

     • South Dakota State & High Plains Territorial Cowboy Fast Draw 
       Championships (September 11th-15th) 
            o Mitchell Trap Club  
     • Collegepalooza (September 12th) 
            o The World’s Only Corn Palace Plaza 
     • Holiday Arts Fall Craft Show (September 13th-14th) 
            o Davison County Fairgrounds 
     • Kernel Bowl (September 14th) 
            o MHS/Joe Quintal 
     • DWU Basketball Tiger Academy (September 15th) 
            o DWU Avera Sports & Wellness Complex

The following information is in regards to the 1st Annual DOC
Volleyball Tournament in Mitchell, SD, at the Corn Palace. We
will use two gyms the main corn palace floor and the auxiliary
gym on the second floor. The dates for this years’ tournament
are Friday and Saturday October 11th & October 12th, 2024.
Pool play will begin on Friday, October 11th at 9:00am.
Locker Rooms: Locker rooms are available at the facility and will
be marked by school name. Please take your belongings with
you after your team is dressed, as we have a rolling schedule
and other teams will need to get dressed.
Teams: The teams for the pools are as follows:
Pool A Pool B
1. Pine Ridge High School 1. Omaha Nation High School
2. Lakota Tech High School 2. Wakpala High School
3. Lower Brule High School 3. Little Wound High School
4. Tiospaye Topa High School 4. Mahpiya Luta High School
5. Tiospa Zina High School 5. Cheyenne-Eagle Butte High
School
6. St. Francis High School 6. Marty Indian High School
7. Santee High School 7. Crazy Horse High School
8. Flandreau Indian High School 8. Takini High School
Play: Our format for the tournament is Round Robin style of play
with two pools. We will be playing best of 3 and rally scoring to
25 for the first 2 games and if it goes into the 3rd game, we will
play to 25. The tournament will be a single-elimination
tournament, at the end of pool play we will be cross-bracketing
the top team in each pool. We will be using 2 courts throughout
the tournament so please keep your team in the arena as the first
game is the only set game time. Games from that point on will be
on the first available court.
Warm-up time: During the first round only, each team will have a
warm-up of 4-8-8 after the first round we will start as soon as the
books are ready, no serving. Please stay in the area with your
team so that we can stay on schedule.
Grand Entry: Grand Entry information and line up will be in the
coaches’ packet, Grand Entry is on Saturday after pool play.
Awards: We will be giving team awards for 1st to 4th place.
There will be championship ¼ zip jackets for a 15-team roster 2
coaches and 1 manager. There will also be awards for Most
Valuable Player, Outstanding Setter, Best Defensive Player and
team sportsmanship and ¼ zip jackets for a 16 team all-
tournament team (1 from each team). Each coach will pick one
(1) player for the all-tournament team from their own team.
Program: We will need a 15-player roster and photo sent to
McLeod’s Printing by September 4, 2024 no exceptions!! Email

comp@mcleodprint.com , send your roster and picture for the
program. If your roster and picture are not submitted by this date
you will not be included in the program as it will go to print ASAP.

Only! Friday October 11, 2024 at 8:30am.
The Dakota Oyate Challenge Board and Coordinator look
forward to seeing you and your teams in October. This is a great
way to showcase our Native American lady athletes, their style of
play and their athleticism. Good Luck to you all! Let’s have a
great tournament.

athletes the best possible sports experience possible. DOC

traditions. The board knows that attendance at Volleyball games

events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.
