documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
August 13, 2024
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:00 PM.
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin
Nelson, Jason Christensen, Doug Greenway, Dave Helleloid, and Tim Smith.
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Jill Larson, Cory Aadland, Bryan Dixon, LaRee
Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, and Jim Johnston.
Others present: Aaron Hieb, Stephanie Ellwein, and Johanna Allen.
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed
applications for grant funding. The following application(s) were presented and considered:
A. Tour de Corn
• Kourtney Denne presented the Tour de Corn Grant Application, which is requesting
$3,000.
This year will be the 30th Annual. They are expecting around 350 riders this year, which
begins Friday, August 16th evening and goes until Sunday, August 18th. They estimate about
50% of the riders are outside the 50+ mile radius. Much of the profits raised from this event go
back to the Mitchell community and Lake Mitchell Trails.
B. Cornicupia 2024
• Scott Mullenmeister presented the follow-up information for Cornicupia 2024, which is
requesting $7,500.
Mitchell Soccer Association is a non-profit. Currently, there are 13 out of town (Rapid City-
Ignite, Brookings, Watertown, Brandon Valley, Larchwood, IA, and Aberdeen) teams
registered, along with 7 teams from Mitchell. This tournament will host the U10, U12, U13, &
U14 divisions. The largest expense is referees. The Mitchell Soccer Association is
coordinating with some main street businesses (Subway, Big Dummy's, Scoreboard, and Main

--- PAGE 1 OF 4 ---


Street Mercantile) about running meal specials during their tournament to get teams/fans
downtown in between games.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented, and seconded by Tim Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb and Stephanie Ellwein reviewed the financial report as of July 29th, 2024.
SEA Revenue received an additional $50,000 for FY 2024 based on the BID #4 Board
recommendation.
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2024 are $56,450.
Current Available Fund Balance of $93,550.
Collections in June (for May records) are $29,828.00 with one establishment past due.
Collections in July (for June records) are $31,240.00 with two establishments past due.
The YTD collections for 2024 is $146,283.00, which equates to 75,556 total room nights sold.
YTD comparison for room nights sold were: up 0.6% (419 room nights sold) from 2023,
down 3.1% (2,361 room nights sold) from 2022, up 3.6% (2,709 room nights sold) from 2021,
up 28.4% (21,449 room nights sold) from 2020, up 4.8% (3,630 room nights sold) from 2019,
and up 1.9% (1,466 room nights sold) from 2018.
Motion: Motion was made by Doug Greenway to approve the financial report as presented,
and seconded by Tim Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms w/Financials with the SEA Committee:
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials
Cabin Fever Auction (February 23rd-24th, 2024)
• The event was above expectations. An estimated total spectator attendance of 600.
Total participants of 296. The estimated number of total hotel/motel room nights sold
was 300 (AmericInn, Comfort Inn, and Thunderbird Lodge). The awarded funds
($1,500) were used towards advertising and hotel rooms. The profit of $12,847.21 will
go towards making next year better. This year, items were of higher quality and sold at
higher than normal prices.
SD United States Bowling Congress Open Tournament (April 5th-7th, 12th-14th, 19th-21st,
26th-28th, May 3rd-5th, & 10th-12th, 2024)
• The event met expectations. Total participants of 1,164 bowlers, which is 291 4-person

--- PAGE 2 OF 4 ---


teams. The number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was estimated based on the
QR Code results, which was an estimated 129+ (Comfort Inn, Days Inn, Hampton Inn,
and Holiday Inn Express). The awarded funds ($3,000) were added to the tournament
prize fund. The PL statement showed no profit.
DWU Spring Golf Invite (April 8th-9th, 2024)
• The event was above expectations. An estimated total spectator attendance of 30-50.
Total participants of 83 golfers, 10 coaches. The number of total hotel/motel room
nights sold was estimated at 50-65 (Comfort Inn, Hampton Inn, and Holiday Inn
Express). The awarded funds ($1,500) were used for player/coaches meals and range
ball expenses. Total expenses for the event were $7,520.
Harve's Sport Shop Soccer Classic (April 20th-21st, 2024)
• The event was above expectations. The staff were very accommodating and helpful.
An estimated total spectator attendance of 1,500. Total participants of 372. The
estimated number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 10 (Comfort Inn and Days
Inn). The awarded funds ($2,500) were used to offset tournament expenses. The profit
of $7,609.42 will be used towards future tournaments.
6. Other Items

Mitchell Soccer Association about awarding future, financial, tournament incentives for

documents.fileName: October 8th, 2024, SEA Advisory Committee Meeting Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                    October 8, 2024 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:00 PM 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, 
Kevin Nelson, Jason Christensen, Doug Greenway, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave 
Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Cory Aadland and Bryan Dixon 
 
 Others present: Aaron Hieb and Stephanie Ellwein 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed 
 applications for grant funding. The following application(s) were presented and considered: 
 
A. Pheasants Forever Banquet 

     • Tim Smith shared some information about the Pheasants Forever Banquet Grant 
       Application, which is requesting $3,000. 

 
Kevin Bruscher was unable to attend the Sports & Events Authority meeting, so prior to the 
meeting, Kevin reached out to and shared some information with Tim Smith. 
 
Tim Smith shared some information regarding Pheasant Country, Chapter 872 and their 
involvement with the youth pheasant hunt and the youth hunting experience(s) around the 
Mitchell community. Also, he shared their hard work and contributions towards additional 
habitat area(s) around the Mitchell area as well. The upcoming Pheasants Forever Banquet at 
the Corn Palace is the largest banquet in the nation, which gets attendance upwards of 750 
 attendees. 
 
B. Cursed Chains Challenge Disc Golf Tournament 

     • Dan Woodraska presented the Cursed Chains Challenge Disc Golf Tournament Grant 
       Application, which is requesting $500. 

 
The Cursed Chains Challenge Disc Golf Tournament will be Saturday, October 26th at Dry 
Run Creek. The grant request of $500 would help cover the Special Event Permit Park 
Closure fee and porta potties. Dan also shared information from the UDISC App that has a 
monthly subscription fee of $30, but this app summarizes the majority of participation stats for 
Dry Run Creek Disc Golf Course on a monthly basis. Tournament participation is capped at 
 100, with a majority of players being from out of town. Currently, there are 15 registered. 
 
C. Palace City Cup - Squirt B & C Hockey Tournament 

     • Eric Sabers presented the Palace City Cup - Squirt B & C Hockey Tournament Grant 
       Application, which is requesting $1,000. 

 
The Palace City Cup - Squirt B & C Hockey Tournament (10U) will be November 15th-17th at 
the Mitchell Activities Center. The grant request of $1,000 would help cover the ice rental costs 
and referee's expenses. A minimum of 5–6 teams per division (2) is necessary to make this 
event worthwhile. Two teams will participate from Mitchell along with, hopefully, teams from 
 West River SD, IA, MN, and NE. A goal of 8 teams per division, so 16 total teams. 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
presented, and seconded by Jason Christensen. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion 
 passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of October 4th, 2024.  
 
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2024 are $85,150.  
 
Current Available Fund Balance of $64,850.  
 
Collections in September (for August records) are $38,636.00 with all collected.  
 
The YTD collections for 2024 is $224,286.00, which equates to 114,558 total room nights sold. 
YTD comparison for room nights sold were: up 2.8% (3,174 room nights sold) from 2023, 
down 1.3% (1,536 room nights sold) from 2022, up 1.0% (1,135 room nights sold) from 2021, 
up 24.9% (28,552 room nights sold) from 2020, up 0.6% (677 room nights sold) from 2019, 
and up 1.0% (1,192 room nights sold) from 2018.  
 
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the financial report as presented, and 
 seconded by Kevin Nelson. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms w/Financials with the SEA Committee: 
 
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials 
MAC Triathlon (June 8th, 2024) 
     • The event was above expectations. An estimated total spectator attendance of 60. 
       Total participants of 66. The estimated number of total hotel/motel room nights sold 
       was 4 (Comfort Inn, Super 8, and Thunderbird Lodge). The awarded funds ($1,500) 
       were used towards the cost of the timing system. The profit of $2,522.97 will go 
       towards outdoor fitness equipment in Cadwell Park. 

 
Shoot out at the Lake (June 21st-22nd, 2024) 

     • The event was below expectations - mother nature did not cooperate and Mitchell 
       experienced excessive rainfall amounts. An estimated total spectator attendance of 
       1,250. Total participants of 90 (45 each night). The estimated number of total 
       hotel/motel room nights sold was 75 (Super 8 Motel). The awarded funds ($5,000) 
       were used towards the cost of the bleachers. No profit ($5,652.98) 

 
Palace City Mountain Bike Classic (June 29th, 2024) 

     • The event exceeded expectations. An estimated total spectator attendance of 45. Total 
       participants of 61. The estimated number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 5 
       (CoachLight Motel, Comfort Inn, Hampton Inn, and Holiday Inn). Cyclists prefer to stay 
       at campgrounds rather than hotels. Individuals love the Lake Mitchell Campground! 
       The awarded funds ($1,500) were used towards the cost of the timing system. The 
       profit of $6,250.09 will go towards continuing to host more events geared towards 
       health, wellness, and fitness. Also, towards workout equipment at Cadwell Park. 

 
Tour de Corn (August 16th-18th, 2024) 

     • The event exceeded expectations. An estimated total spectator attendance of 375. 
       Total participants of 307. The estimated number of total hotel/motel room nights sold is 
       uncertain. The awarded funds ($2,000) were used towards the cost of the meal for the 
       riders. No profit ($5,198.06) 

 
CorniCUPia 2024 (September 7th-8th, 2024) 

     • The event was above expectations. An estimated total spectator attendance of 1,400. 
       Total participants of 492, 41 teams. The estimated number of total hotel/motel room 
       nights sold was 300. The awarded funds ($5,000) were used towards offsetting 
       tournament expenses. The profit of $14,808.55 will go back into the soccer programs 
       and purchasing infrastructure for future tournaments. 
            o Scott Mullenmeister and Alyson Palmer, Mitchell Soccer Association, were 
              present to give an in-person event recap for their CorniCUPia 2024 soccer 
              tournament. 

 
 
B. SEA Survey(s) 
     • Organization: Mitchell Soccer Association; Main Contact: Scott Mullenmeister; Date 
       Completed: 9/26/2024 

 
 
6. Other Items 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following item(s) with the SEA Committee: 
 
A. Upcoming Events 

     • Dakota Oyate Challenge Volleyball (October 11th-12th) 
            o The World’s Only Corn Palace 
     • Mitchell A.C.T Presents: “The Miraculous Journey of Edward Tulane” (October 11th-
       13th) 
            o Mitchell Area Community Theatre 
     • DWU Homecoming Week (October 7th-13th) 
            o Tiger Trail Trek 5K – October 12th 
            o DWU Blue & White Days Parade – October 12th 
            o DWU Homecoming Tailgate – October 12th 
     • VFW Chili Cook-Off (October 12th) 
            o 2nd & Rowley Parking Lot – Behind the VFW 
     • Davison County 4-H Carnival (October 12th) 
            o Davison County 4-H Grounds 
     • Pheasants Forever Banquet (October 18th) 
            o The World’s Only Corn Palace 
     • Mitchell Hall & The Tennessee Trio Johnny Cash Tribute Band (October 19th) 
            o Mitchell Area Community Theatre 
     • LyricWood Orchestra Concert (October 20th) 
            o DWU Sherman Center 
     • Forest of Fears Haunted Trail (October 25th-27th) 
            o Reclamation Ranch 
     • Mitchell ACT Haunted Theatre Fundraiser (October 25th-26th) 
            o Mitchell Area Community Theatre 
     • Cursed Chains Challenge Disc Golf Tournament (October 26th) 
            o Dry Run Creek 
     • Mitchell Downtown Trick-Or-Treat (October 26th) 
            o Mitchell’s Main Street 
     • Monster Mash (October 27th) 
            o The Moose Lodge 
     • James Valley Community Center 

 
Complete list of events – MITCHELL CHAMBER EVENTS CALENDAR 
 
 *BOLD – Awarded Sports & Events Authority Grant funding. 
 
7. Executive Session in accordance with SDCL 9-34-19: Discussion of confidential trade 
secrets, commercial, or financial information. 
 
 
8. Approval of Funding Applications 
Pheasants Forever Banquet  
Date: October 18th, 2024; Contact: Kevin Bruscher; Grant Request: $3,000 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to award $2,000 earmarked towards youth 
       hunting activities, and seconded by Doug Greenway. All members voted 'Aye' and the 
       motion passed. 

 
Cursed Chains Challenge Disc Golf Tournament 
Date: October 26th, 2024; Contact: Dan Woodraska; Grant Request: $500 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Jason Christensen to award $500, and seconded by 
       LaRee Rumbolz. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
Palace City Cup - Squirt B & C Hockey Tournament 
Date: November 15th-17th, 2024; Contact: Darcy Sabers; Grant Request: $1,000 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to award $1,000, and seconded by Tim 
       Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
 
9. Next Meeting Date 
Tim Smith, Aaron Hieb, and Stephanie Ellwein shared information from last week's Business 
Improvement District #4 Board meeting. 

     • Jerry Thomsen will put together and distribute a survey to all Mitchell hotels/motels. 
       The purpose of this survey is to give all hotels/motels an opportunity to provide 
       feedback and express their opinion(s) on what/where the BID 4 Hotel Tax Collections 
       should go towards (Marketing, event recruitment, facility enhancement, etc.). 
     • The following will be shared and discussed during the next BID #4 Board meeting in 
       December: 
            o Johanna Allen, CVB Representative, will attend and share a marketing 
              overview with the BID #4 Board. 
            o Aaron Hieb will share information and comparisons regarding other Business 
              Improvement Districts - Hotel Occupancy Tax that are established in 
              municipalities throughout South Dakota. 
            o Aaron Hieb will also share a comparison regarding Sports Tourism Index - 
              Scout and another platform that works as a recruiting tool and provides a list of 
              potential events that can be bid on and possibly hosted in your city. 
              Subscription fees will also be provided. 
     • BID #4 Board has designated $150,000 towards the Sports & Events Authority for FY 
       2025. 
     • $30,000 for the next three years (2024, 2025, and 2026) totaling $90,000 has been 
       approved for the Dakota Riptide for their debt service towards the Indoor Aquatics 
       Center. 
     • Mitchell has been awarded the Class A (12U) Swim Meet in February 2025.  

 
Kevin McCardle shared the next meeting date of Tuesday, November 12th, 2024, @ 2 PM - 
 City Hall, Council Chambers. 
 
10. Adjournment 
There being no further business to discuss.  
 
 Meeting adjourned by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:57 PM.

The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
September 10, 2024
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:00 PM.
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson,
Jason Christensen, Doug Greenway, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, and Tim
Smith.
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Kevin Nelson, Cory Aadland, Bryan Dixon, and
Jim Johnston.
Others present: Stephanie Ellwein and Aaron Hieb.
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed
applications for grant funding. The following application(s) were presented and considered:
A. Raise Em Rank Bull Riding Series Finals
• Dillon Swanson presented the Raise Em Rank Bull Riding Series Finals Grant
Application via conference phone, which is requesting $5,000.
This year will be the 3rd year for the series finals in Mitchell at The World's Only Corn Palace.
The event will take place on Friday, October 4th - Saturday, October 5th. There will likely be
between 50-60 head of bulls being bucked each night. The youth participation will be limited to
35–40 minutes. Participants will come from Texas, Australia, South Dakota, North Dakota, and
Nebraska. The series finals (Corn Palace-Mitchell, SD) have been promoted throughout the
entire summer at all the Raise Em Rank events. The grant request goes towards facility rental
and marketing/advertising for the series finals.
B. Dakota Oyate Challenge Volleyball
• George Erdahl, Dakota Oyate Challenge Board of Director, presented the Dakota
Oyate Challenge Volleyball Grant Application, which is requesting $6,500 plus 11
COMP hotel rooms for 2 nights.

--- PAGE 1 OF 4 ---


This is a 1st annual event, which they are expanding off of the Dakota Oyate Challenge
Basketball, and cross-country may be added next year. There will be 16 teams participating in
this event on Friday, October 11th - Saturday, October 12th, 2024. The grant request will be
used to offset some of the expenses for a new event.
C. Hoop City Classic
• Brad Bartscher, Hoop City Classic Representative, presented the Hoop City Classic
Grant Application, which is requesting $15,000.
This is the 13th annual Hoop City Classic which takes place from Friday, December 27th
through Monday, December 30th. As of last year, the entire event moved back to Mitchell,
which is the plan going forward for years to follow. This year there are 30-32 varsity teams, 18
junior varsity teams, and 60-80 youth teams. Last year the event hosted 46 youth teams.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by LaRee Rumbolz to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented, and seconded by Tim Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of September 6th, 2024.
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2024 are $63,450.
Current Available Fund Balance of $86,550.
Collections in June (for May records) are $29,834.00 with all collected. Collections in July (for
June records) are $33,762.00 with all collected. Collections in August (for July records) are
$36,839.00 with all collected.
The YTD collections for 2024 is $185,650.00, which equates to 95,240 total room nights sold.
YTD comparison for room nights sold were: up 2.3% (2,214 room nights sold) from 2023,
down 2.1% (1,964 room nights sold) from 2022, up 1.9% (1,766 room nights sold) from 2021,
up 27.2% (25,887 room nights sold) from 2020, up 2.2% (2,094 room nights sold) from 2019,
and up 2.2% (2,104 room nights sold) from 2018.
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the financial report as presented, and
seconded by Doug Greenway. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys
None were submitted at this time.

documents.fileName: November 12th, 2024, SEA Advisory Committee Meeting Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                  November 12, 2024 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2 PM. 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, 
Kevin Nelson, Jason Christensen, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, 
and Jim Johnston. 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Cory Aadland and Bryan Dixon. 
 
 Others present: Aaron Hieb, Stephanie Ellwein, and Johanna Allen. 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed 
 applications for grant funding. The following application(s) were presented and considered: 
 
A. Dakota Riptide Swim Meet 

     • Jason Wede and Rob Schelske presented the Dakota Riptide Swim Meet Grant 
       Application, which is requesting $5,000. 

 
The Dakota Riptide Swim Meet will be (Friday evening-Sunday) December 6th-8th, 2024. Last 
year's attendance had 282 swimmers. This will be the first of three swim meets. There will be 
one in January 2025, along with the 12 & Under State Meet in February 2025. The deadline to 
 register for the December swim meet is November 29th. 
 
B. Palace City Robot Rumble 

     • Ryan Tupper presented the Palace City Robot Rumble Grant Application, which is 
       requesting $1,500. 

 
The Palace City Robot Rumble has been hosted for many years and is in its second year 
hosting in the Corn Palace. The rumble takes place on Saturday, December 7th with doors 
opening at 7 AM and lasting until approximately 4 PM. Last year there were 28 teams, with 
teams coming from: Omaha, NE; Spearfish and Douglas, SD. The event usually hosts 20–30 
teams with 2–4 kids per team plus parents. The requested grant amount would go towards  offsetting the cost of the Corn Palace rental. 
 
C. South Dakota Fire Instructors Conference 

     • Justin Adams presented the South Dakota Fire Instructors Conference Grant 
       Application, which is requesting $4,206.44. 

 
The South Dakota Fire Instructors Conference will be January 4th-5th, 2025. The conference 
holds a meeting on Friday evening, with a full day of events on Saturday, and concludes with a 
half day on Sunday. In years past, the conference has been held in Pierre, SD, but the 
conference is relocating and looking for a new annual home. Average attendance is 
approximately 125. The requested grant amount will cover the cost of an instructor from out of 
state. Registration fee is $35 per person, but $25 of that fee goes towards the cost of the 
 annual insurance to cover the instructors as they teach classes throughout the year. 
 
D. Dakota Oyate Challenge Basketball Tournament 

     • George Erdahl presented the Dakota Oyate Challenge Basketball Tournament Grant 
       Application, which is requesting $10,500, plus kindly requesting the same amount (11 
       rooms x 4 nights) of Comp rooms for basketball officials. 

 
The Dakota Oyate Challenge is in its 36th year for the boys and 31st year for the girls. The 
requested grant amount will help offset numerous costs as well as help to lower the entry fees 
for each school. Schools pay a $2,000 entry fee and the hope is to lower the entry fee to 
$1,400. The total event budget is usually around $30,000. The event hosts 8 schools, which 
 brings a total of 16 basketball teams (8 boys & 8 girls). 
 
E. South Dakota Middle School All State Band 

     • Holly Gage via conference phone presented the South Dakota Middle School All State 
       Band Grant Application, which is requesting $1,000. 

 
The South Dakota Middle School All State Band will be March 7th-8th, 2025 at the Mitchell 
Performing Arts Center. The event brings in 200 participants plus parents. All participants will 
stay overnight on Friday and some, depending on travel distance, will stay overnight on 
Saturday. All the meals take place at local restaurants throughout the Mitchell community. The 
requested grant amount will be used to provide a hospitality room and purchase snacks and 
beverages locally for the students and band directors. The event wants to provide a "swag" 
item for all the participants and directors this year as well. Mitchell will be the host site for 
 2026. 
 
F. North Dakota Country Fest 

     • Dan Beukelman presented the North Dakota Country Fest Grant Application, which is 
       requesting $7,500.  
The North Dakota Country Fest is a 4-day camping festival in Bismarck, North Dakota. 
Attendance is estimated at around 50,000. This request is for the Your Town Tour, which is an 
extension of the ND Country Fest, which provides music event(s) in smaller cities throughout 
North Dakota and South Dakota. Aberdeen and Sioux Falls were some of the cities included in 
this tour during 2024. The event is scheduled for Friday, April 25th, 2025, from 6:30 PM until 
11 PM at The World's Only Corn Palace. The grant request would not nearly cover all the 
 expenses, but it would help assist with marketing and promotions. 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
 presented, and seconded by Tim Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of November 1st, 2024.  
 
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2024 are $88,650. 
 
Current Available Fund Balance of $61,350.  
 
Collections in October (for September records) are $34,734.00 with all collected.  
 
The YTD collections for 2024 is $259,020.00, which equates to 131,925 total room nights 
sold.  
 
YTD comparison for room nights sold were: up 2.7% (3,574 room nights sold) from 2023, 
down 0.8% (1,049 room nights sold) from 2022, up 1.6% (2,096 room nights sold) from 2021, 
up 23.7% (31,214 room nights sold) from 2020, up 1.1% (1,457 room nights sold) from 2019, 
and up 1.2% (1,605 room nights sold) from 2018.  
 
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to approve the financial report as presented, and 
 seconded by Jim Johnston. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
 No Evaluation Forms, Financials, or Surveys were submitted at this time. 
 
6. Other Items 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following item(s) with the SEA Committee: 
 
A. Upcoming Events

            o Mitchell Main Street and The World’s Only Corn Palace

            o Mitchell Indoor Aquatic Center

            o Mitchell Area Community Theatre

 *BOLD – Awarded Sports & Events Authority Grant funding. 
 
7. Executive Session in accordance with SDCL 9-34-19: Discussion of confidential trade 
secrets, commercial, or financial information. 
 
 
8. Approval of Funding Applications 
Dakota Riptide Swim Meet 
Date: December 6th-8th, 2024; Contact: Jason Wede; Grant Request: $5,000 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to award $5,000 towards the December        2024 and January 2025 swim meet(s), seconded by LaRee Rumbolz. All members 
       voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
Palace City Robot Rumble  
Date: December 7th, 2024; Contact: Mark Wilson; Grant Request: $1,500 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to award $1,500 and seconded by Jim 
       Johnston. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
South Dakota Fire Instructors Conference 
Date: January 4th-5th, 2025; Contact: Justin Adams; Grant Request: $4,206.44 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Jason Christensen to award $4,210 and seconded by 
       Emily Liedtke. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
Dakota Oyate Challenge Basketball Tournament  
Date: January 30th-February 1st, 2025; Contact: Silas Blaine; Grant Request: $10,500, plus, 
kindly requesting the same amount (11 rooms x 4 nights) of Comp rooms for basketball 
officials. 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Jim Johnston to award $5,000, but no COMP hotel 
       rooms were able to be secured, seconded by Tim Smith.  

 
Members voted 'Aye': Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, Kevin Nelson, LaRee 
Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston.  
 
Members voted 'Nay': Jason Christensen and Dave Helleloid.  
 
The majority vote 'Aye' motion passed. 
 
South Dakota Middle School All State Band 
Date: March 7th-8th, 2025; Contact: Holly Gage; Grant Request: $1,000 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to award $1,000 and seconded by Jason 
       Christensen. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
North Dakota Country Fest 
Date: April 25th, 2025; Contact: Luke Shafer; Grant Request: $7,500 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Jason Christensen to table any action until the 
       December 10th meeting and seconded by LaRee Rumbolz. All members voted 'Aye' 
       and the motion passed. 

 
 
9. Next Meeting Date Kevin McCardle shared the next meeting date of Tuesday, December 10th, 2024, @ 2 PM - 
 City Hall, Council Chambers. 
 
10. Adjourn 
There being no further business to discuss.  
 
 Meeting adjourned by: Kevin McCardle @ 3:09 PM.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

10-8-24 SEA Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
October 8, 2024
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:00 PM
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson,
Kevin Nelson, Jason Christensen, Doug Greenway, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave
Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Cory Aadland and Bryan Dixon
Others present: Aaron Hieb and Stephanie Ellwein
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed
applications for grant funding. The following application(s) were presented and considered:
A. Pheasants Forever Banquet
• Tim Smith shared some information about the Pheasants Forever Banquet Grant
Application, which is requesting $3,000.
Kevin Bruscher was unable to attend the Sports & Events Authority meeting, so prior to the
meeting, Kevin reached out to and shared some information with Tim Smith.
Tim Smith shared some information regarding Pheasant Country, Chapter 872 and their
involvement with the youth pheasant hunt and the youth hunting experience(s) around the
Mitchell community. Also, he shared their hard work and contributions towards additional
habitat area(s) around the Mitchell area as well. The upcoming Pheasants Forever Banquet at
the Corn Palace is the largest banquet in the nation, which gets attendance upwards of 750
attendees.
B. Cursed Chains Challenge Disc Golf Tournament
• Dan Woodraska presented the Cursed Chains Challenge Disc Golf Tournament Grant
Application, which is requesting $500.

--- PAGE 1 OF 6 ---


The Cursed Chains Challenge Disc Golf Tournament will be Saturday, October 26th at Dry
Run Creek. The grant request of $500 would help cover the Special Event Permit Park
Closure fee and porta potties. Dan also shared information from the UDISC App that has a
monthly subscription fee of $30, but this app summarizes the majority of participation stats for
Dry Run Creek Disc Golf Course on a monthly basis. Tournament participation is capped at
100, with a majority of players being from out of town. Currently, there are 15 registered.
C. Palace City Cup - Squirt B & C Hockey Tournament
• Eric Sabers presented the Palace City Cup - Squirt B & C Hockey Tournament Grant
Application, which is requesting $1,000.
The Palace City Cup - Squirt B & C Hockey Tournament (10U) will be November 15th-17th at
the Mitchell Activities Center. The grant request of $1,000 would help cover the ice rental costs
and referee's expenses. A minimum of 5–6 teams per division (2) is necessary to make this
event worthwhile. Two teams will participate from Mitchell along with, hopefully, teams from
West River SD, IA, MN, and NE. A goal of 8 teams per division, so 16 total teams.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented, and seconded by Jason Christensen. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion
passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of October 4th, 2024.
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2024 are $85,150.
Current Available Fund Balance of $64,850.
Collections in September (for August records) are $38,636.00 with all collected.
The YTD collections for 2024 is $224,286.00, which equates to 114,558 total room nights sold.
YTD comparison for room nights sold were: up 2.8% (3,174 room nights sold) from 2023,
down 1.3% (1,536 room nights sold) from 2022, up 1.0% (1,135 room nights sold) from 2021,
up 24.9% (28,552 room nights sold) from 2020, up 0.6% (677 room nights sold) from 2019,
and up 1.0% (1,192 room nights sold) from 2018.
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the financial report as presented, and
seconded by Kevin Nelson. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms w/Financials with the SEA Committee:
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials
MAC Triathlon (June 8th, 2024)

--- PAGE 2 OF 6 ---


• The event was above expectations. An estimated total spectator attendance of 60.
Total participants of 66. The estimated number of total hotel/motel room nights sold
was 4 (Comfort Inn, Super 8, and Thunderbird Lodge). The awarded funds ($1,500)
were used towards the cost of the timing system. The profit of $2,522.97 will go
towards outdoor fitness equipment in Cadwell Park.
Shoot out at the Lake (June 21st-22nd, 2024)
• The event was below expectations - mother nature did not cooperate and Mitchell
experienced excessive rainfall amounts. An estimated total spectator attendance of
1,250. Total participants of 90 (45 each night). The estimated number of total
hotel/motel room nights sold was 75 (Super 8 Motel). The awarded funds ($5,000)
were used towards the cost of the bleachers. No profit ($5,652.98)
Palace City Mountain Bike Classic (June 29th, 2024)
• The event exceeded expectations. An estimated total spectator attendance of 45. Total
participants of 61. The estimated number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 5
(CoachLight Motel, Comfort Inn, Hampton Inn, and Holiday Inn). Cyclists prefer to stay
at campgrounds rather than hotels. Individuals love the Lake Mitchell Campground!
The awarded funds ($1,500) were used towards the cost of the timing system. The
profit of $6,250.09 will go towards continuing to host more events geared towards
health, wellness, and fitness. Also, towards workout equipment at Cadwell Park.
Tour de Corn (August 16th-18th, 2024)
• The event exceeded expectations. An estimated total spectator attendance of 375.
Total participants of 307. The estimated number of total hotel/motel room nights sold is
uncertain. The awarded funds ($2,000) were used towards the cost of the meal for the
riders. No profit ($5,198.06)
CorniCUPia 2024 (September 7th-8th, 2024)
• The event was above expectations. An estimated total spectator attendance of 1,400.
Total participants of 492, 41 teams. The estimated number of total hotel/motel room
nights sold was 300. The awarded funds ($5,000) were used towards offsetting
tournament expenses. The profit of $14,808.55 will go back into the soccer programs
and purchasing infrastructure for future tournaments.
o Scott Mullenmeister and Alyson Palmer, Mitchell Soccer Association, were
present to give an in-person event recap for their CorniCUPia 2024 soccer
tournament.

9. Next Meeting Date
Tim Smith, Aaron Hieb, and Stephanie Ellwein shared information from last week's Business
Improvement District #4 Board meeting.
• Jerry Thomsen will put together and distribute a survey to all Mitchell hotels/motels.
The purpose of this survey is to give all hotels/motels an opportunity to provide
feedback and express their opinion(s) on what/where the BID 4 Hotel Tax Collections
should go towards (Marketing, event recruitment, facility enhancement, etc.).
• The following will be shared and discussed during the next BID #4 Board meeting in
December:
o Johanna Allen, CVB Representative, will attend and share a marketing
overview with the BID #4 Board.

Improvement Districts - Hotel Occupancy Tax that are established in
municipalities throughout South Dakota.

Scout and another platform that works as a recruiting tool and provides a list of
potential events that can be bid on and possibly hosted in your city.
Subscription fees will also be provided.

2025.
• $30,000 for the next three years (2024, 2025, and 2026) totaling $90,000 has been

Center.

City Hall, Council Chambers.

documents.fileName: December 10th, 2024, SEA Advisory Committee Meeting Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                  December 10, 2024 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2 PM 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin 
Nelson, Jason Christensen, Bryan Dixon, Emily Liedtke, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Jill Larson, Cory Aadland, LaRee Rumbolz, 
and Dave Helleloid 
 
 Others present: Stephanie Ellwein and Aaron Hieb 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed 
 applications for grant funding. The following application(s) were presented and considered: 
 
A. 1st Annual Mitchell Pickleball Indoor Tournament 
     • Tim Smith presented the 1st Annual Mitchell Pickleball Indoor Tournament Grant 
       Application, which is requesting $2,500. 

 
The tournament will be hosted at the DWU/Avera Sports & Wellness Complex on January 4th-
5th, 2025. Currently, there are 72 registered individual players with a goal of 80 players. 
Round Robin tournament for each division, which ultimately will lead to a champion for each 
division. The tournament, in its first year, is requesting $2,500 to help get the event going and 
on its feet. An estimation of hotel/motel room nights is around or above 50 rooms sold for the 
 tournament. 
 
B. Hanson Girl's & Boy's Classic 
     • Tyler Payer and Josh Oltmanns presented the Hanson Girl's & Boy's Classic Grant 
       Application, which is requesting $3,000 ($1,500 for each classic). 

 
The grant request would go towards hospitality for the Hanson Classic(s). The Hospitality 
Room would provide something to eat for the coaches, officials, and volunteers. There are 
seven teams that are traveling from 100 to 150 miles, which could result in overnight stays 
(hotel/motel room nights). If awarded funding, the sponsorship puts the Mitchell Sports & 
 Events Authority logo on programs and the t-shirts. 
 
C. North Dakota Country Fest 
Dan Beukelman shared an update on the North Dakota Country Fest Grant Application, which 
is requesting $7,500. 
 
The Your Town Tour takes place at The World's Only Corn Palace on Friday, April 25th, 2025. 
The organization reached out to Aberdeen, SD, Sturgis, SD, Minot, ND, and Jamestown, ND 
regarding hotel/motel room nights, and the feedback estimates that an additional 125 room 
nights. The grant request would go towards additional marketing for the event to help keep the 
tickets affordable, between $35 and $20. The sponsorship would put the Sports & Events 
 Authority logo on all marketing and the Your Town Tour website. 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Bryan Dixon to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
presented, and seconded by Jason Christensen. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion 
 passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of December 4th, 2024.  
 
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2024 are $100,360. 
 
There is one committed item that the award check has not been written yet. 
 

     • Dakota Oyate Challenge $5,000 

 
Current Available Fund Balance of $44,640.  
 
Collections in November (for October records) are $31,326.00 with one establishment 
outstanding.  
 
The YTD collections for 2024 is $290,632.00, which equates to 147,731 total room nights 
sold.  
 
YTD comparison for room nights sold were: up 2.6% (3,865 room nights sold) from 2023, 
down 2.0% (2,971 room nights sold) from 2022, up 1.3% (1,884 room nights sold) from 2021, 
up 21.3% from 2020, up 0.5% from 2019, and up 0.6% from 2018.  
 
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the financial report as presented, and 
 seconded by Kevin Nelson. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms w/Financials with the SEA Committee: 
 
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials 
South Dakota State Amateur Baseball Tournament (August 7th-18th, 2024) 
     • The event exceeded expectations. This year's tournament set a record gate, 
       financially. Total participants of 32 - Class 'B' teams and 5 - Class 'A' teams. The 
       estimated number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 300+ (AmericInn & Super 8 
       Motel). The tournament will be in Brandon this year and Mitchell in 2026 & 2027. The 
       awarded funds ($5,000) were used towards hospitality for commissioners and the costs 
       of the PA announcer. 
     • Jim Johnston also provided and shared feedback and results from the tournament. He 
       will put together and provide financials that will be sent out to the committee. 

 
OutKasts Car Show (September 20th-22nd, 2024) 

     • The event exceeded expectations. An estimated total spectator attendance of 3,000. 
       Total participants of 200 registered and club cars. The estimated number of total 
       hotel/motel room nights sold was 75 (Budget Inn, CoachLight Motel, Corn Palace Inn, 
       Days Inn, Quality Inn, Rodeway Inn, Siesta Motel, and Thunderbird Lodge). The 
       awarded funds ($1,500) were used towards the cost of awards given to the winners. 
       Profit ($1,920.70) will go towards next year's show. 

 
 
6. Other Items 
Tim Smith and Aaron Hieb reviewed and provided an update to the committee from the 
previous week's Business Improvement District #4 Board meeting. 

     • Mitchell Chamber and CVB Marketing/Promotions Presentation by Johanna Allen. 
     • Shared information and discussion about the South Dakota Business Improvement 
       District(s) Hotel Occupancy Tax Comparisons. 
     • Sports Tourism Index vs. Playeasy 
            o BID #4 Board approved the use and purchase ($4,995/annually) of the 
              Playeasy platform for 2025. 

 
 
A. Upcoming Events 
     • Dance Expressions Christmas Recital (December 11th) 
            o The World’s Only Corn Palace 
     • Mitchell’s Comedy Night at the Area Community Theatre (December 12th) 
            o Mitchell Area Community Theatre 
     • MHS Girls’ & Boys’ Basketball 
            o The World’s Only Corn Palace 
     • Klock Werks Christmas Extravaganza! (December 13th) 
            o Klock Werks 
     • The Mitchell A.C.T. Presents “A Christmas Chaos” (December 13th-15th) 
            o Mitchell Area Community Theatre 
     • DWU Women & Men's Basketball 
            o The World’s Only Corn Palace 
     • Figure Skating Holiday Show (December 15th) 
            o Mitchell Activities Center 
     • Holiday Jam with the Hegg Brothers (December 16th) 
            o Mitchell Performing Arts Center 
     • Shaun Johnson’s Big Band Experience – Holiday Tour (December 17th) 
            o Mitchell Area Community Theatre 
     • MHS Gymnastics (December 21st) 
            o The World’s Only Corn Palace 
     • Hoop City Classic (December 27th-30th) 
            o The World’s Only Corn Palace 
     • Sacred Hoops Basketball Classic (January 4th, 2025) 
            o The World’s Only Corn Palace 
     • Mitchell Hockey Pink the Rink (January 4th, 2025) 
            o Mitchell Activities Center 
     • South Dakota Fire Instructors Conference (January 4th-5th, 2025) 
            o Highland Conference Center 
     • Mitchell Fire Department’s Chase the Ace 
            o The Back 40 
     • James Valley Community Center 
     • Highland Conference Center 

 
Complete list of events – MITCHELL CHAMBER EVENTS CALENDAR 
 
 *BOLD – Awarded Sports & Events Authority Grant funding 
 
7. Executive Session in accordance with SDCL 9-34-19: Discussion of confidential trade 
secrets, commercial, or financial information. 
 
 
8. Approval of Funding Applications 
1st Annual Mitchell Pickleball Indoor Tournament 
Date: January 4th-5th, 2025; Contact: Tim Smith; Grant Request: $2,500 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Jim Johnston to award $2,500, and seconded by Bryan 
       Dixon. Seven members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
     • Abstain: Tim Smith abstained from voting. 

 
Hanson Girl's & Boy's Classic 
Date: January 18th & 25th, 2025; Contact: Tyler Payer; Grant Request: $3,000 ($1,500 for 
each classic) 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Bryan Dixon to award $3,000 ($1,500 for each classic), 
       and seconded by Tim Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
North Dakota Country Fest 
Date: April 25th, 2025; Contact: Luke Shafer; Grant Request: $7,500 
     • Tabled from the November meeting. 
     • Motion: Motion was made by Bryan Dixon to award $7,500, and seconded by Tim 
       Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
 
9. Next Meeting Date 
Kevin McCardle shared the next meeting date of Tuesday, January 14th, 2025, @ 2 PM - City 
 Hall, Council Chambers. 
 
10. Adjourn 
There being no further business to discuss.  
 
 Meeting adjourned by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:46 PM.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

11-12-24 SEA Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
November 12, 2024
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2 PM.
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson,
Kevin Nelson, Jason Christensen, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith,
and Jim Johnston.
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Cory Aadland and Bryan Dixon.
Others present: Aaron Hieb, Stephanie Ellwein, and Johanna Allen.
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed
applications for grant funding. The following application(s) were presented and considered:
A. Dakota Riptide Swim Meet
• Jason Wede and Rob Schelske presented the Dakota Riptide Swim Meet Grant
Application, which is requesting $5,000.
The Dakota Riptide Swim Meet will be (Friday evening-Sunday) December 6th-8th, 2024. Last
year's attendance had 282 swimmers. This will be the first of three swim meets. There will be
one in January 2025, along with the 12 & Under State Meet in February 2025. The deadline to
register for the December swim meet is November 29th.
B. Palace City Robot Rumble
• Ryan Tupper presented the Palace City Robot Rumble Grant Application, which is
requesting $1,500.
The Palace City Robot Rumble has been hosted for many years and is in its second year
hosting in the Corn Palace. The rumble takes place on Saturday, December 7th with doors
opening at 7 AM and lasting until approximately 4 PM. Last year there were 28 teams, with
teams coming from: Omaha, NE; Spearfish and Douglas, SD. The event usually hosts 20–30
teams with 2–4 kids per team plus parents. The requested grant amount would go towards

--- PAGE 1 OF 6 ---


offsetting the cost of the Corn Palace rental.
C. South Dakota Fire Instructors Conference
• Justin Adams presented the South Dakota Fire Instructors Conference Grant
Application, which is requesting $4,206.44.
The South Dakota Fire Instructors Conference will be January 4th-5th, 2025. The conference
holds a meeting on Friday evening, with a full day of events on Saturday, and concludes with a
half day on Sunday. In years past, the conference has been held in Pierre, SD, but the
conference is relocating and looking for a new annual home. Average attendance is
approximately 125. The requested grant amount will cover the cost of an instructor from out of
state. Registration fee is $35 per person, but $25 of that fee goes towards the cost of the
annual insurance to cover the instructors as they teach classes throughout the year.
D. Dakota Oyate Challenge Basketball Tournament
• George Erdahl presented the Dakota Oyate Challenge Basketball Tournament Grant
Application, which is requesting $10,500, plus kindly requesting the same amount (11
rooms x 4 nights) of Comp rooms for basketball officials.
The Dakota Oyate Challenge is in its 36th year for the boys and 31st year for the girls. The
requested grant amount will help offset numerous costs as well as help to lower the entry fees
for each school. Schools pay a $2,000 entry fee and the hope is to lower the entry fee to
$1,400. The total event budget is usually around $30,000. The event hosts 8 schools, which
brings a total of 16 basketball teams (8 boys & 8 girls).
E. South Dakota Middle School All State Band
• Holly Gage via conference phone presented the South Dakota Middle School All State
Band Grant Application, which is requesting $1,000.
The South Dakota Middle School All State Band will be March 7th-8th, 2025 at the Mitchell
Performing Arts Center. The event brings in 200 participants plus parents. All participants will
stay overnight on Friday and some, depending on travel distance, will stay overnight on
Saturday. All the meals take place at local restaurants throughout the Mitchell community. The
requested grant amount will be used to provide a hospitality room and purchase snacks and
beverages locally for the students and band directors. The event wants to provide a "swag"
item for all the participants and directors this year as well. Mitchell will be the host site for
2026.
F. North Dakota Country Fest
• Dan Beukelman presented the North Dakota Country Fest Grant Application, which is
requesting $7,500.

--- PAGE 2 OF 6 ---


The North Dakota Country Fest is a 4-day camping festival in Bismarck, North Dakota.
Attendance is estimated at around 50,000. This request is for the Your Town Tour, which is an
extension of the ND Country Fest, which provides music event(s) in smaller cities throughout
North Dakota and South Dakota. Aberdeen and Sioux Falls were some of the cities included in
this tour during 2024. The event is scheduled for Friday, April 25th, 2025, from 6:30 PM until
11 PM at The World's Only Corn Palace. The grant request would not nearly cover all the
expenses, but it would help assist with marketing and promotions.

January 14th, 2025, SEA Advisory Committee Meeting Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                   January 14, 2025 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2 PM  
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, 
Kevin Nelson, Dave Sietsema, LaRee Rumbolz, and Tim Smith 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Cory Aadland, Jason Christensen, Bryan 
Dixon, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, and Jim Johnston 
 
 Others present: Stephanie Ellwein and Aaron Hieb 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.  
 
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding. The following 
 application(s) were presented and considered: 
 
A. Palace Ice Festival 
     • Brian Bultje, Mitchell Figure Skating Club, presented the Palace Ice Festival Grant 
       Application, which is requesting $750. 

 
The Palace Ice Festival is January 17th-19th. There are 35 skaters registered and 17 coaches 
coming. Skaters are coming from Sioux Falls and Watertown, and locally from Mitchell and 
Mitchell area. The grant request of $750 will go towards judges fees and ice fees (offset 
 expenses). 
 
B. DWU/Culver's Girls & Boys High School Basketball Classic 
     • Brad Bartscher presented the DWU/Culver's Girls & Boys High School Basketball 
       Classic Grant Application, which is requesting $3,000. 

 
The girls (12th annual) classic will take place on Friday, February 14th and the boys (16th 
annual) will be on Saturday, February 15th at The World's Only Corn Palace. There are 36 
total teams, 18 girls and 18 boys, which results in 9 games each day. The grant request of 
$3,000 will go towards the cost of table workers, referees, and rent of the Corn Palace. 
 
* Brad announced that next year, January 3rd, 2026, Mitchell and The World's Only Corn 
 Palace will host the Midwest Miracle Classic. 
 
C. Dakota Riptide 12U State 'A' Swim Championships 
     • Jason Wede and Rob Schelske, Dakota Riptide, presented the Dakota Riptide 12U 
       State 'A' Swim Championships Grant Application, which is requesting $5,000. 

 
The state swim meet will take place February 21st-23rd at the Mitchell Indoor Aquatics Center, 
which will bring in between 320-350 swimmers. The grant request would go towards pool 
rental, lifeguard wages, sound system rental, programs, meals for coaches and officials, bag 
 tags for swimmers, and concession costs. 
 
D. DWU 15th Annual Indoor Futsal Winter Classic 
     • Nico Reinhard, DWU Soccer, presented the DWU 15th Annual Indoor Futsal Winter 
       Classic Grant Application, which is requesting $3,500. 

 
The Indoor Futsal Winter Classic will take place February 21st-23rd at the DWU/Avera Sports 
Complex and DWU Christen Family Center. There will be teams represented from 5 
surrounding states (SD, ND, MN, NE, IA). They are estimating over 100 teams participating 
this year. The requested grant amount would be used to cover the senior referee assignment 
fee(s), as well as the student referee certification/background checks. These costs have 
lessened drastically over the last couple of years because they are certifying more student-
athletes rather than paying senior referees. No entry or gate fee is charged. The teams pay a 
 registration fee. Concessions are provided. 
 
E. Mitchell Music Boosters New Black Concert Chairs Purchase for PAC 
     • Joel Van Peursem, Mitchell Music Boosters, presented the Mitchell Music Boosters 
       New Black Concert Chairs Purchase for PAC Grant Application, which is requesting 
       $4,000. 

 
The (140) chairs would be used only for SDHSAA and SDMEA concerts and events. The 
chairs would be stored at the PAC. The Mitchell Area Charitable Foundation awarded $10,000 
as well.  

     • Joel Van Peursem, South Dakota Music Education Association, presented the South 
       Dakota Middle School All-State Jazz Band Grant Application, which is requesting 
       $1,500.  
            o This application was submitted over the weekend, Saturday, January 11th. 

 
The Middle School All-State Jazz Band is taking place January 31st-February 1st at the 
Performing Arts Center. This year, 42 students will attend from around the state and rehearse, 
and eventually put on a show on Saturday, February 1st. The final show charges adult tickets 
($5), which goes back to SDMEA. The grant request of $1,500 will go towards the cost of 
 bringing in two, nationally known clinicians to assist with the final show. 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
 presented, and seconded by Kevin Nelson. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb and Stephanie Ellwein reviewed the financial report as of January 7th, 2025. 
 
Final Expenses for FY 2024 is $118,360.  
 
Final SEA Fund Balance for FY 2024 is $31,640, which will be earmarked to SEA and 
reflected in the BID #4 Fund.  
 
BID #4 designated $150,000 towards SEA for FY 2025.  
 
There is a committed item, Special Olympics State Basketball for $12,000, which the funding 
check will be authorized and cut in the upcoming weeks. This will leave a Current Available 
Fund Balance for the SEA of $138,000 for FY 2025. 
 
Updated Collections in November (for October records) are $31,396.00 with all collected. 
 
Collections in December (for November records) are $24,482.00 with one establishment 
outstanding.  
 
The YTD collections for 2024 is $315,184.00, which equates to 160,007 total room nights 
sold.  
 
YTD comparison for room nights sold were: up 1.9% (2,969 room nights sold) from 2023, 
down 1.9% (3,104 room nights sold) from 2022, up 0.9% (1,411 room nights sold) from 2021, 
up 21.7% from 2020, up 0.3% from 2019, and down 0.3% from 2018.  
 
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the financial report as presented, and 
 seconded by Dave Sietsema. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms w/Financials with the SEA Committee: 
 
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials 
Arts in the Park (July 26th-27th, 2024) 

     • The event was above (4) expectations. SEA was a huge help! Total spectator 
       attendance of 8,000-10,000. Total participants of 120 vendors. The estimated number 
       of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 101 (Comfort Inn, Hampton Inn, Holiday Inn). 
       The awarded funds ($1,000) were used towards overnight security. There was a net 
       loss of $795. 
     • Mayor Hanson shared a review of the 2024 event and provided an update for 2025. 

 
South Dakota State & High Plains Regional Cowboy Fast Draw Shoot (September 11th-15th, 
2024) 

     • The event met (3) expectations. An estimated total spectator attendance of 40-50 per 
       day. Total participants of 80. The estimated number of total hotel/motel room nights 
       sold was 148 (AmericInn, Budget Inn, Coachlight Motel, Comfort Inn, Days Inn, 
       Hampton Inn, Kelly Inn). The awarded funds ($3,000) were used to pay the 
       shooters/winners on the SEA sponsored shoot on Friday. Profit ($1,024.00) were 
       awarded as cash donations or awards to veterans, Shoot for the Stars Scholarship 
       Program, and Davison County Youth Trap Club. 

 
 
6. Other Items 
Aaron Hieb and Tim Smith reviewed and provided an update to the committee from the 
 previous week's Business Improvement District #4 Board meeting. 
 
A. Update and Review of Playeasy 
Aaron Hieb and Tim Smith reviewed the current progress of the Playeasy platform and 
highlighted some of the features regarding specific microsites for the Mitchell Sports & Events 
Authority. 

     • Facilities 
     • Hotels 
     • Attractions (Food & Drink, Entertainment, Shopping, Transport, and Services) 
     • Events 
     • Reports 

 
Aaron also shared the current leads that are being reviewed: 

     • 2026 and 2027 Move United Education Conference 
     • American Broomball Alliance National Championship 2026 and 2027 
     • Under Armour Next HS Football Camp Series 2025+ 

 
The first on-boarding training session with a Playeasy representative was on Thursday, 
 January 9th. 
 
B. Upcoming Events 
     • Mitchell Fire Department’s Chase the ACE 
            o The Back 40 
     • Burger Showdown (January 1st-31st) 
            o Mitchell, SD 
     • MHS Girls and Boys Basketball 
            o The World’s Only Corn Palace 
     • Young Professionals Trivia Night! (January 14th) 
            o Palace City Brewing Co. 
     • Mitchell Chamber & Development Annual Recognition Event (January 15th) 
            o The Masonic Hall 
     • Dakota Riptide Swim Meet (January 17th-18th) 
            o Mitchell Indoor Aquatic Center 
     • 42nd Annual Hanson Girls Classic (January 18th) 
            o The World’s Only Corn Palace 
     • DWU Women and Men Basketball 
            o The World’s Only Corn Palace 
     • Avera Queen of Peace Winter Wonderland Gala (January 24th) 
            o Highland Conference Center 
     • Mitchell Marlins Candy Cup Mite Hockey Tournament (January 25th-26th) 
            o Mitchell Activities Center 
     • The Village Bowl Doubles Tournament (January 25th-26th) 
            o The Village Bowl 
     • 43rd Annual Hanson Boys Classic (January 25th) 
            o The World’s Only Corn Palace 
     • Dakota Oyate Challenge (January 30th-February 1st) 
            o The World’s Only Corn Palace 
     • Big Friend Little Friend’s Annual Winter Escape (February 1st) 
            o The Village Bowl 
     • James Valley Community Center 
     • Highland Conference Center 
     • MHS Performing Arts Center 

 
Complete list of events – MITCHELL CHAMBER EVENTS CALENDAR 
 
 *BOLD – Awarded Sports & Events Authority Grant funding. 
 
7. Executive Session in accordance with SDCL 9-34-19: Discussion of confidential trade 
secrets, commercial, or financial information. 
 
 
8. Approval of Funding Applications 
Palace Ice Festival 
Date: January 17th-19th, 2025; Contact: Brian Bultje; Grant Request: $750 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Kevin Nelson to award $750, and seconded by Tim 
       Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
South Dakota Middle School All-State Jazz Band 
Date: January 31st-February 1st, 2025; Contact: Ellie Kenkel; Grant Request: $1,500 
 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to award $1,000, and seconded by Mayor 
       Hanson. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
DWU/Culver's Girls & Boys High School Basketball Classic 
Date: February 14th-15th, 2025; Contact: Jason Christensen; Grant Request: $3,000 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Kevin McCardle to award $3,000, and seconded by 
       LaRee Rumbolz. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
Dakota Riptide 12U State 'A' Swim Championships 
Date: February 21st-23rd, 2025; Contact: Jason Wede; Grant Request: $5,000 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Kevin McCardle to award $4,000, and seconded by Tim 
       Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
DWU 15th Annual Indoor Futsal Winter Classic 
Date: February 21st-23rd, 2025; Contact: Nicolas Reinhard; Grant Request: $3,500 

     • Motion: Motion was made by LaRee Rumbolz to award $3,500, and seconded by 
       Dave Sietsema. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
Mitchell Music Boosters New Black Concert Chairs Purchase for PAC 
Date: March 7th-8th, 2025; Contact: Joel Van Peursem; Grant Request: $4,000 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to award $4,000, and seconded by Kevin 
       Nelson. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
 
9. Next Meeting Date 
Kevin McCardle shared the next meeting date of Tuesday, February 11th, 2025, @ 2 PM - City 
 Hall, Council Chambers. 
 
10. Adjournment 
There being no further business to discuss.  
 
 Meeting adjourned by: Kevin McCardle @ 3:03 PM

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed
applications for grant funding. The following application(s) were presented and considered:
A. 1st Annual Mitchell Pickleball Indoor Tournament
• Tim Smith presented the 1st Annual Mitchell Pickleball Indoor Tournament Grant
Application, which is requesting $2,500.
The tournament will be hosted at the DWU/Avera Sports & Wellness Complex on January 4th-
5th, 2025. Currently, there are 72 registered individual players with a goal of 80 players.
Round Robin tournament for each division, which ultimately will lead to a champion for each
division. The tournament, in its first year, is requesting $2,500 to help get the event going and
on its feet. An estimation of hotel/motel room nights is around or above 50 rooms sold for the
tournament.
B. Hanson Girl's & Boy's Classic
• Tyler Payer and Josh Oltmanns presented the Hanson Girl's & Boy's Classic Grant
Application, which is requesting $3,000 ($1,500 for each classic).
The grant request would go towards hospitality for the Hanson Classic(s). The Hospitality
Room would provide something to eat for the coaches, officials, and volunteers. There are
seven teams that are traveling from 100 to 150 miles, which could result in overnight stays
(hotel/motel room nights). If awarded funding, the sponsorship puts the Mitchell Sports &
Events Authority logo on programs and the t-shirts.

The Your Town Tour takes place at The World's Only Corn Palace on Friday, April 25th, 2025.

tickets affordable, between $35 and $20. The sponsorship would put the Sports & Events
Authority logo on all marketing and the Your Town Tour website.
