documents.fileName: February 11th, 2025, SEA Advisory Committee Meeting Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                   February 11, 2025 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2 PM 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, 
Kevin Nelson, Jason Christensen, Dave Sietsema, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave 
Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Cory Aadland and Bryan Dixon 
 
 Others present: Johanna Allen, Stephanie Ellwein, and Aaron Hieb 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.  
 
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.  
 
 The following application(s) were presented and considered: 
 
A. Buckin' Wild Ranch Cabin Fever Auction 
Nick Coulter, Buckin' Wild Ranch, presented the Cabin Fever Auction Grant Application, which 
is requesting $2,000. 

     • The Cabin Fever Auction is going on its 7th annual, which takes place at the Davison 
       County Fairgrounds on February 21st-22nd. The grant request would help cover the 
       costs of hotel rooms for workers, food, and costs of the venue. Last year the event had 
       over 500 bidder numbers. Attendees come from WY, MT, SD, ND, and IA. 

 
 
B. Rob Marchand/Harve Johnston Basketball Tourney 
Jason Christensen presented the Rob Marchand/Harve Johnston Basketball Tourney Grant 
Application, which is requesting $750. 

     • The Rob Marchand/Harve Johnston Basketball Tourney is Saturday, March 8th, 
       utilizing multiple facilities throughout Mitchell. The grant request provides food for the 
       volunteers and workers. Currently, there are 32 teams signed up so far. Entry fee for 
       teams is $125 per team with 3 games minimum. Some teams are coming from 
       Watertown, Aberdeen, Pierre, and Mobridge. 
 
 
C. 4th Annual Combat Veterans Motorcycle Association Comedy Night 
Justin Hamer, Kyle, and Rick, Combat Veterans Motorcycle Association, presented the CVMA 
Comedy Night Grant Application, which is requesting $1,500. 

     • The 4th Annual CVMA Comedy Night is being held on Saturday, March 22nd at the 
       Highland Conference Center. This is the biggest fundraising event of the year for 
       CVMA. Last year they teamed up locally, with Helping with Horsepower. Last year the 
       profit was $5,900, which was split between CVMA and Helping with Horsepower. There 
       were 138 tickets sold for last year's event. This year will consist of Dueling with Pianos 
       and a live auction. 

 
 
D. DWU Spring Golf Invite 
Jeff Meyerink, DWU Golf, presented the DWU Spring Golf Invite Grant Application, which is 
requesting $5,000. 

     • The DWU Spring Golf Invite is April 7th-8th at Lakeview Golf Course. Last year there 
       were 82 players, mainly from North Dakota. As of December 2nd, 2024, there are 110 
       players registered for the event. This year the event format is practice round on 
       Sunday, April 6th, 36-hole competition on Monday, April 7th, and final 18 holes on 
       Tuesday, April 8th. The grant request would help cover costs such as cart rentals for 
       the 36 hole competition day, range balls, and complimentary meals for 
       players/coaches. 

 
 
E. Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament 
Stacy Murtha presented the Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament Grant Application, which 
is requesting $4,000. 

     • The Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament is April 11th-13th at the Mitchell Activities 
       Center, utilizing both ice rinks. This is the 14th year for the event. SD, ND, MN, and WI 
       teams with over 300 hockey players plus families. Two years ago Sioux Falls created a 
       similar tournament, as well as, one year ago, Watertown did so as well. There is 
       competition to keep teams coming to the Mitchell tournament over going to the other 
       two cities. There is a max capacity of 22 teams for this tournament. This event does 
       support and sponsor 8U hockey here in Mitchell as well. The two biggest expenses for 
       this tournament are ice time and referee costs. 

 
 
F. Powderhorn Ranch Regulators Outlaw Gauntlet Shoot (Jackpot Shoots, Blast for 
Cash, & Veteran's Shoot) 
Troy Bollock, Powderhorn Ranch Regulators, presented the Outlaw Gauntlet Shoot Grant 
Application, which is requesting $4,500. 
     • The Powderhorn Ranch Regulators Outlaw Gauntlet Shoot is June 12th-15th out at the 
       Mitchell Gun Club. This is the 22nd year for the cowboy fast draw. Due to changes in 
       the association, the date has changed to June and the title of the event is no longer SD 
       State & Territorial High Plains, but Outlaw Gauntlet Shoot. The grant request of $4,500 
       goes back into the shoot as payout prizes, none of it is kept by the PHRR.  

 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by LaRee Rumbolz to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
 presented, and seconded by Jim Johnston. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of February 4th, 2025.  
 
Designated revenue for FY 2025 is $150,000.  
 
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2025 are $28,250. This 
amount does include the $12,000 Special Olympics State Basketball award check.  
 
Current Available Fund Balance of $121,750.  
 
Collections in December (for November records) are 24,482.00 with one establishment still 
past due.  
 
Collections in January (for December records) are $14,704.00 with one establishment past 
due.  
 
The YTD collections for 2025 is $14,704.00, which equates to 7,352 total room nights sold.  
 
YTD comparison for room nights sold were: down 31.4% (2,307 room nights sold) from 2024, 
down 11.1% (817 room nights sold) from 2023, down 22.9% (1,687 room nights sold) from 
2022, up 7.2% from 2021, down 46.3% from 2020, and down 11.1% from 2019. 
 
The one establishment past due for January collections has provided an average over the past 
three years of 1,918 room nights sold. This would bring our YTD room nights sold to above 
9,200 room nights sold, which is a more respectable number.  
 
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to approve the financial report as presented, and 
 seconded by Jason Christensen. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms w/Financials with the SEA Committee: 
 
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials 
Palace City Kiwanis Half Marathon/10K/5K (October 6th, 2024) 
     • The event met (3) expectations. A little disappointed in this year's turnout, but they 
       have hired a media professional for 2025. An estimated total spectator attendance of 
       200. Total participants of 166. The estimated number of total hotel/motel room nights 
       sold was 33 (Hampton Inn, Kelly Inn, My Place). The awarded funds ($1,500) were 
       used to offset the costs of the run - medals, shirts, swag bags, porta potties, and timing 
       and registration company. $1,000 was a donation in support of the event and $500 was 
       towards a 'BAG' sponsorship. Profits ($13,803.87) will be used for children's programs 
       throughout the community and support for Salvation Army, CASA, Abbott House, and 
       other agencies. 

 
Cursed Chains Challenge Disc Golf Tournament (October 22nd, 2024) 

     • The event met (3) expectations. Total participants of 63. The estimated number of total 
       hotel/motel room nights sold was 0 (My Place). The awarded funds ($500) were used 
       to pay for the Special Event Permit and portable bathrooms. No Profit Gained. 

 
SD Fire Instructors Conference (January 4th-5th, 2025) 

     • The event was above (4) expectations. With the help of the grant they were able to 
       spend more money than normal on an instructor and provide better educational 
       learning for the group. Total participants of 78. The estimated number of total 
       hotel/motel room nights sold was 80 (Comfort Inn, Hampton Inn). The awarded funds 
       ($4,210) were used to help cover the cost of the instructor along with cost of the venue. 
       Profits ($2,173.04) will go towards next year's conference in Mitchell on January 10th-
       11th, 2026. 

 
Girls & Boys Hanson Classic (January 18th & 25th, 2025)  

     • Aaron Hieb shared and read a “Thank You” card to the committee from the Hanson 
       Classic Committee. 

 
 
6. Other Items 
Aaron Hieb reviewed and provided an update to the committee on the processes and action 
 items of Playeasy. 
 
A. Update and Review of Playeasy 
Aaron Hieb completed a second on-boarding training from Playeasy last Wednesday. 
 
Aaron Hieb continued to review the current progress of the Playeasy platform and highlighted 
some of the features regarding specific microsites for the Mitchell Sports & Events Authority. 

     • Home 'Start A Post' 
     • Facilities 
     • Hotels 
     • Attractions (Food & Drink, Entertainment, Shopping, Transport, and Services) 
     • Events - Search Engine Organization (SEO), which filters search results in search 
       engines specific to Playeasy, higher up in the results list. 
     • Reports 

 
Aaron also shared the total leads within the platform (279) and current leads specific to the 
Mitchell Sports & Events Authority (156) that are being reviewed: 

     • The 2026 and 2027 Move United Education Conference - BID was submitted on 
       Wednesday, January 29th. 
     • American Broomball Alliance National Championship 2026 and 2027 
            o Additional criteria within the RFP did not make sense or suit Mitchell, South 
              Dakota to continue to pursue the bid. 
     • 5v5 Soccer - Aaron and Scott Mullenmeister met with Andrew Vorce (President of 5v5 
       Soccer) to learn more about the event and hosting criteria. 
            o Scott will share information with the Mitchell Soccer Association during their 
              March 10th Board meeting. 

 
 
B. Upcoming Events 
     • MHS Girls and Boys Basketball

            o The Depot Pub & Grill

     • Women in Blue Jeans Conference (February 21st-22nd) 
            o Highland Conference Center

            o The World’s Only Corn Palace 
     • Norm Foster’s The Foursome (February 28th-March 2nd; March 7th-9th)

7. Executive Session in accordance with SDCL 9-34-19: Discussion of confidential trade 
secrets, commercial, or financial information. 
 
 
8. Approval of Funding Applications

Date: February 21st-22nd, 2025; Contact: Ashley Coulter; Grant Request: $2,000

***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.

Comments 	We use the best equipment available of the 1800’s: single action
revolvers and center fire cartridges. We’re out to capture the feel
of the Peacemaker in your hand, the smell of holster leather, and
the exhilaration of reacting as fast as you dare while remaining
cool-headed enough to hit your mark as you compete head to
head in classic old west fashion. In Cowboy Fast Draw we can
find out how we would have shot in the 1800’s with gunfighter
period guns and rigs.
Guns: STOCK .45 caliber single actions with minimum barrel
length of 4.5″, with no external alterations other than smoothing
the hammer knurling. No aluminum barrels or cylinders. Front
sights are optional. Actions jobs that do not alter the factory-
designed external operation of the six-gun are fine.
Holsters: Pre 1900 style Mexican Loop or Slim Jim. No steel
liners. Holsters will be worn on the side of the leg. No cross
draws.
The Target: The original CFDA target was a 24″ (60.96cm) round
disc, start light in the center, with a Lexan lens. Targets are black
with white lithium grease applied to the target to verify all hits.
There is a sensor attached to the back of the target which
detects hits which are then displayed on digital timers. In 2015
the 17 – 3/16″ target was developed and is shot at a distance of
15′, creating the same proportions and level of difficulty as the
original 24″ target. Target distances are 15’(4.57m), and
21’(6.40m). With the 17″ Plate at 15’ now being the mainly used
CFDA Titled Championship Distance.
Time Clocks: Must time multiple lanes to the thousandth of a
second. CFDA’s Official Timer is the Gunslinger Fast Draw
Timer. Only timers approved by CFDA may be used in CFDA
Titled Championships.
Contests: Contests are conducted elimination style, normally
best 3 out of 5 between two contestants. The loser of a round
receives an “X”. In major competitions when a competitor
receives 4-X’s they are eliminated from the contest. However,
CFDA has several elimination formats that are very popular in
club and regional formats.
Shooting Style: Thumbing and fanning, trigger finger must be
outside of the trigger guard. If fanning the fanning hand may not
be placed in front of the shooter’s body before the start light
comes on.

--- PAGE 4 OF 7 ---


Clothing: Western-Style Clothing is an essential part of the
atmosphere we create. Late 1800’s period clothing is the theme.
No Tennis Shoes, ball caps, short sleeve shirts, or sponsor logos
are permitted.
Alias: Selecting an Alias is a big part of what makes Cowboy
Fast Draw so fun! Your alias may not be duplicated once it is
registered with CFDA.

Cowboy Fast Draw is the newest and oldest shooting sport
today. It is a timed sport using single action .45 caliber western
style six shooters.
The Cowboy Fast Draw Association (CFDA) is the largest
organization devoted to the Sport of Fast Draw to ever exist.
Since 2002 we have signed up over 7,500 members. Our Motto
is: Safety First, Fun Second and Competition Third. Not that our
competitions aren’t important, we shoot hundreds of events a
year for prize money, prizes and titles. It’s just that we place

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
January 14, 2025
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2 PM
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson,
Kevin Nelson, Dave Sietsema, LaRee Rumbolz, and Tim Smith
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Cory Aadland, Jason Christensen, Bryan
Dixon, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, and Jim Johnston
Others present: Stephanie Ellwein and Aaron Hieb
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding. The following
application(s) were presented and considered:
A. Palace Ice Festival
• Brian Bultje, Mitchell Figure Skating Club, presented the Palace Ice Festival Grant
Application, which is requesting $750.
The Palace Ice Festival is January 17th-19th. There are 35 skaters registered and 17 coaches
coming. Skaters are coming from Sioux Falls and Watertown, and locally from Mitchell and
Mitchell area. The grant request of $750 will go towards judges fees and ice fees (offset
expenses).
B. DWU/Culver's Girls & Boys High School Basketball Classic
• Brad Bartscher presented the DWU/Culver's Girls & Boys High School Basketball
Classic Grant Application, which is requesting $3,000.
The girls (12th annual) classic will take place on Friday, February 14th and the boys (16th
annual) will be on Saturday, February 15th at The World's Only Corn Palace. There are 36
total teams, 18 girls and 18 boys, which results in 9 games each day. The grant request of
$3,000 will go towards the cost of table workers, referees, and rent of the Corn Palace.
* Brad announced that next year, January 3rd, 2026, Mitchell and The World's Only Corn
Palace will host the Midwest Miracle Classic.

--- PAGE 1 OF 6 ---


C. Dakota Riptide 12U State 'A' Swim Championships
• Jason Wede and Rob Schelske, Dakota Riptide, presented the Dakota Riptide 12U
State 'A' Swim Championships Grant Application, which is requesting $5,000.
The state swim meet will take place February 21st-23rd at the Mitchell Indoor Aquatics Center,
which will bring in between 320-350 swimmers. The grant request would go towards pool
rental, lifeguard wages, sound system rental, programs, meals for coaches and officials, bag
tags for swimmers, and concession costs.
D. DWU 15th Annual Indoor Futsal Winter Classic
• Nico Reinhard, DWU Soccer, presented the DWU 15th Annual Indoor Futsal Winter
Classic Grant Application, which is requesting $3,500.
The Indoor Futsal Winter Classic will take place February 21st-23rd at the DWU/Avera Sports
Complex and DWU Christen Family Center. There will be teams represented from 5
surrounding states (SD, ND, MN, NE, IA). They are estimating over 100 teams participating
this year. The requested grant amount would be used to cover the senior referee assignment
fee(s), as well as the student referee certification/background checks. These costs have
lessened drastically over the last couple of years because they are certifying more student-
athletes rather than paying senior referees. No entry or gate fee is charged. The teams pay a
registration fee. Concessions are provided.
E. Mitchell Music Boosters New Black Concert Chairs Purchase for PAC
• Joel Van Peursem, Mitchell Music Boosters, presented the Mitchell Music Boosters
New Black Concert Chairs Purchase for PAC Grant Application, which is requesting
$4,000.
The (140) chairs would be used only for SDHSAA and SDMEA concerts and events. The
chairs would be stored at the PAC. The Mitchell Area Charitable Foundation awarded $10,000
as well.
• Joel Van Peursem, South Dakota Music Education Association, presented the South
Dakota Middle School All-State Jazz Band Grant Application, which is requesting
$1,500.
o This application was submitted over the weekend, Saturday, January 11th.
The Middle School All-State Jazz Band is taking place January 31st-February 1st at the
Performing Arts Center. This year, 42 students will attend from around the state and rehearse,
and eventually put on a show on Saturday, February 1st. The final show charges adult tickets
($5), which goes back to SDMEA. The grant request of $1,500 will go towards the cost of
bringing in two, nationally known clinicians to assist with the final show.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the previous meeting minutes as

--- PAGE 2 OF 6 ---


presented, and seconded by Kevin Nelson. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb and Stephanie Ellwein reviewed the financial report as of January 7th, 2025.
Final Expenses for FY 2024 is $118,360.
Final SEA Fund Balance for FY 2024 is $31,640, which will be earmarked to SEA and
reflected in the BID #4 Fund.
BID #4 designated $150,000 towards SEA for FY 2025.
There is a committed item, Special Olympics State Basketball for $12,000, which the funding
check will be authorized and cut in the upcoming weeks. This will leave a Current Available
Fund Balance for the SEA of $138,000 for FY 2025.
Updated Collections in November (for October records) are $31,396.00 with all collected.
Collections in December (for November records) are $24,482.00 with one establishment
outstanding.
The YTD collections for 2024 is $315,184.00, which equates to 160,007 total room nights
sold.
YTD comparison for room nights sold were: up 1.9% (2,969 room nights sold) from 2023,
down 1.9% (3,104 room nights sold) from 2022, up 0.9% (1,411 room nights sold) from 2021,
up 21.7% from 2020, up 0.3% from 2019, and down 0.3% from 2018.
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the financial report as presented, and
seconded by Dave Sietsema. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms w/Financials with the SEA Committee:
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials
Arts in the Park (July 26th-27th, 2024)
• The event was above (4) expectations. SEA was a huge help! Total spectator
attendance of 8,000-10,000. Total participants of 120 vendors. The estimated number
of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 101 (Comfort Inn, Hampton Inn, Holiday Inn).
The awarded funds ($1,000) were used towards overnight security. There was a net
loss of $795.
• Mayor Hanson shared a review of the 2024 event and provided an update for 2025.
South Dakota State & High Plains Regional Cowboy Fast Draw Shoot (September 11th-15th,
2024)
• The event met (3) expectations. An estimated total spectator attendance of 40-50 per

--- PAGE 3 OF 6 ---


day. Total participants of 80. The estimated number of total hotel/motel room nights
sold was 148 (AmericInn, Budget Inn, Coachlight Motel, Comfort Inn, Days Inn,
Hampton Inn, Kelly Inn). The awarded funds ($3,000) were used to pay the
shooters/winners on the SEA sponsored shoot on Friday. Profit ($1,024.00) were
awarded as cash donations or awards to veterans, Shoot for the Stars Scholarship
Program, and Davison County Youth Trap Club.
6. Other Items
Aaron Hieb and Tim Smith reviewed and provided an update to the committee from the
previous week's Business Improvement District #4 Board meeting.
A. Update and Review of Playeasy
Aaron Hieb and Tim Smith reviewed the current progress of the Playeasy platform and
highlighted some of the features regarding specific microsites for the Mitchell Sports & Events
Authority.
• Facilities
• Hotels
• Attractions (Food & Drink, Entertainment, Shopping, Transport, and Services)
• Events
• Reports
Aaron also shared the current leads that are being reviewed:
• 2026 and 2027 Move United Education Conference
• American Broomball Alliance National Championship 2026 and 2027
• Under Armour Next HS Football Camp Series 2025+
The first on-boarding training session with a Playeasy representative was on Thursday,
January 9th.
B. Upcoming Events
• Mitchell Fire Department’s Chase the ACE
o The Back 40
• Burger Showdown (January 1st-31st)
o Mitchell, SD
• MHS Girls and Boys Basketball
o The World’s Only Corn Palace
• Young Professionals Trivia Night! (January 14th)

o The Masonic Hall
• Dakota Riptide Swim Meet (January 17th-18th)
o Mitchell Indoor Aquatic Center

--- PAGE 4 OF 6 ---


• 42nd Annual Hanson Girls Classic (January 18th)
o The World’s Only Corn Palace
• DWU Women and Men Basketball
o The World’s Only Corn Palace
• Avera Queen of Peace Winter Wonderland Gala (January 24th)
o Highland Conference Center
• Mitchell Marlins Candy Cup Mite Hockey Tournament (January 25th-26th)
o Mitchell Activities Center
• The Village Bowl Doubles Tournament (January 25th-26th)
o The Village Bowl

*BOLD – Awarded Sports & Events Authority Grant funding.
7. Executive Session in accordance with SDCL 9-34-19: Discussion of confidential trade
secrets, commercial, or financial information.
8. Approval of Funding Applications
Palace Ice Festival

• Motion: Motion was made by Kevin Nelson to award $750, and seconded by Tim
Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
South Dakota Middle School All-State Jazz Band

Kevin McCardle shared the next meeting date of Tuesday, February 11th, 2025, @ 2 PM - City

There being no further business to discuss.

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                    March 11, 2025 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2 PM 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, 
Kevin Nelson, Cory Aadland, Dave Sietsema, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Tim Smith, and 
Jim Johnston. 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Jason Christensen, Bryan Dixon, and Dave 
Helleloid 
 
 Others present: Aaron Hieb and Stephanie Ellwein 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.  
 
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.  
 
 The following application(s) were presented and considered: 
 
A. Knights of Columbus Special Olympics State Basketball Tournament Banquet 
The Knights of Columbus submitted the Knights of Columbus Special Olympics State 
Basketball Tournament Banquet Grant Application for consideration, which is requesting 
$1,500. 

     • No one was in attendance from the Knights of Columbus to present the grant 
       application. 

 
 
B. A Night with Dan Gable 
JD Heinrich, American Outlaws Wrestling, presented A Night with Dan Gable Grant 
Application, which is requesting $7,000. 

     • American Outlaws Wrestling was formed in October 2022. Currently, American 
       Outlaws Wrestling consists of around 30 kids. There is no entry fee to join American 
       Outlaws Wrestling. Fundraising for the club consists of raffles and hosting two youth 
       wrestling tournaments (Youth Dual Tournament in July on the baseball diamond in 
       Dimock, SD and the Monster Brawl in November at the DWU/Avera Sports Complex in 
       Mitchell, SD). A Night with Dan Gable will take place on Saturday, April 26th, in 
       Dimock, SD at TNT Inflatables, with doors opening at 5 PM and the event will get over 
       around 10 PM. 350 seats are available; individual seats and/or tables can be 
       purchased. 

 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Jim Johnston to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
 presented, and seconded by Kevin Nelson. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of March 5th, 2025.  
 
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2025 are $55,500.  
 
Current Available Fund Balance of $94,500.  
 
Collections in December (for November records) are 24,482.00 with one establishment still 
past due.  
 
Collections in January (for December records) are $17852.00 with all collections submitted. 
 
Collections in February (for January records) are $17,637.50 with all collections submitted. 
 
The YTD collections for 2025 are $35,489.50, which equates to 17,745 total room nights sold.  
 
YTD comparisons for room nights sold were: up 4.6% (811 room nights sold) from 2024, up 
8.1% (1,430 room nights sold) from 2023, up 8.5% (1,500 room nights sold) from 2022, up 
24.3% from 2021, down 2.6% from 2020, and up 18.4% from 2019.  
 
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the financial report as presented, and 
 seconded by Cory Aadland. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms w/Financials with the SEA Committee: 
 
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials 
Mitchell Pickleball Indoor Tournament (January 4th-5th, 2025) 

     • The event exceeded (5) expectations. The first annual tournament drew a full field of 
       80 players in eight different divisions. Total participants of 80. The estimated number of 
       total hotel/motel room nights sold was 30 (Comfort Inn, Hampton Inn, Holiday Inn, 
       Quality Inn). The awarded funds ($2,500) were used for prizes and medals and the 
       purchase of equipment. Profits ($3,088.85) will be used to expand the tournament next 
       year and fund additional needs for the new outdoor pickleball courts at Hitchcock Park. 

 
SDMEA Middle School All-State Jazz Band (January 31st-February 1st, 2025) 
     • The event met (3) expectations. Thank you so much to SEA for sponsoring the event! 
       A few restaurants were slower in service, causing some of the members to return late 
       to the event. An estimated total spectator attendance of 204. Total participants of 38. 
       The estimated number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 45 (Hampton Inn). The 
       awarded funds ($1,000) were used to pay the guest directors. Profits ($667.67) will be 
       used to help pay for the SDMEA State Music Educator Conference. 

 
DWU/Culver's Girls & Boys High School Basketball Classic (February 14th-15th, 2025) 

     • The event was above (4) expectations. The event went well. Total participants of 36 
       teams. The estimated number of total hotel/motel room nights sold is unsure (Hampton 
       Inn, Holiday Inn, My Place). The awarded funds ($3,000) were used for rent and 
       referees' fees. Profits ($7,265.97) will be used for TeamMaker scholarships for MBB 
       and WBB.

A. Update and Review of Playeasy 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the HOME page of the Playeasy platform.

Authority: 319; Total active RFPs within the Marketplace: 266.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

Promote youth involvement in Wrestling as well as other
activities. We offer free practices to kids from anywhere, our door
is open to everyone free of charge. We will be bringing the
Wrestling community to the Dimock Area for the Dan Gable
event. People will be passing through Mitchell, as well as staying
overnight in Mitchell because of the event.

Our event will be featuring Dan Gable. He is a 1972 Olympic
Gold Medalist. He received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in
2020. He has had numerous College Titles with the Iowa
Hawkeyes 15 to be exact. He is one of the most decorated and
iconic wrestlers of all time. Gable will meet and greet people sign
autographs and take pictures. Then we will have a supper and
after supper we have 24 Outstanding wrestlers from around
South Dakota that will be recognized. The event will be held at

To promote Wrestling in South Dakota, Recognize Great Athletes
in this State. And to build an event we can continue each year.

2-11-25 SEA Meeting Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
February 11, 2025
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2 PM
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson,
Kevin Nelson, Jason Christensen, Dave Sietsema, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave
Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Cory Aadland and Bryan Dixon
Others present: Johanna Allen, Stephanie Ellwein, and Aaron Hieb
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.
The following application(s) were presented and considered:
A. Buckin' Wild Ranch Cabin Fever Auction
Nick Coulter, Buckin' Wild Ranch, presented the Cabin Fever Auction Grant Application, which
is requesting $2,000.
• The Cabin Fever Auction is going on its 7th annual, which takes place at the Davison
County Fairgrounds on February 21st-22nd. The grant request would help cover the
costs of hotel rooms for workers, food, and costs of the venue. Last year the event had
over 500 bidder numbers. Attendees come from WY, MT, SD, ND, and IA.
B. Rob Marchand/Harve Johnston Basketball Tourney
Jason Christensen presented the Rob Marchand/Harve Johnston Basketball Tourney Grant
Application, which is requesting $750.
• The Rob Marchand/Harve Johnston Basketball Tourney is Saturday, March 8th,
utilizing multiple facilities throughout Mitchell. The grant request provides food for the
volunteers and workers. Currently, there are 32 teams signed up so far. Entry fee for
teams is $125 per team with 3 games minimum. Some teams are coming from
Watertown, Aberdeen, Pierre, and Mobridge.

--- PAGE 1 OF 7 ---


C. 4th Annual Combat Veterans Motorcycle Association Comedy Night
Justin Hamer, Kyle, and Rick, Combat Veterans Motorcycle Association, presented the CVMA
Comedy Night Grant Application, which is requesting $1,500.
• The 4th Annual CVMA Comedy Night is being held on Saturday, March 22nd at the
Highland Conference Center. This is the biggest fundraising event of the year for
CVMA. Last year they teamed up locally, with Helping with Horsepower. Last year the
profit was $5,900, which was split between CVMA and Helping with Horsepower. There
were 138 tickets sold for last year's event. This year will consist of Dueling with Pianos
and a live auction.
D. DWU Spring Golf Invite
Jeff Meyerink, DWU Golf, presented the DWU Spring Golf Invite Grant Application, which is
requesting $5,000.
• The DWU Spring Golf Invite is April 7th-8th at Lakeview Golf Course. Last year there
were 82 players, mainly from North Dakota. As of December 2nd, 2024, there are 110
players registered for the event. This year the event format is practice round on
Sunday, April 6th, 36-hole competition on Monday, April 7th, and final 18 holes on
Tuesday, April 8th. The grant request would help cover costs such as cart rentals for
the 36 hole competition day, range balls, and complimentary meals for
players/coaches.
E. Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament
Stacy Murtha presented the Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament Grant Application, which
is requesting $4,000.
• The Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament is April 11th-13th at the Mitchell Activities
Center, utilizing both ice rinks. This is the 14th year for the event. SD, ND, MN, and WI
teams with over 300 hockey players plus families. Two years ago Sioux Falls created a
similar tournament, as well as, one year ago, Watertown did so as well. There is
competition to keep teams coming to the Mitchell tournament over going to the other
two cities. There is a max capacity of 22 teams for this tournament. This event does
support and sponsor 8U hockey here in Mitchell as well. The two biggest expenses for
this tournament are ice time and referee costs.
F. Powderhorn Ranch Regulators Outlaw Gauntlet Shoot (Jackpot Shoots, Blast for
Cash, & Veteran's Shoot)
Troy Bollock, Powderhorn Ranch Regulators, presented the Outlaw Gauntlet Shoot Grant
Application, which is requesting $4,500.

--- PAGE 2 OF 7 ---


• The Powderhorn Ranch Regulators Outlaw Gauntlet Shoot is June 12th-15th out at the
Mitchell Gun Club. This is the 22nd year for the cowboy fast draw. Due to changes in
the association, the date has changed to June and the title of the event is no longer SD
State & Territorial High Plains, but Outlaw Gauntlet Shoot. The grant request of $4,500
goes back into the shoot as payout prizes, none of it is kept by the PHRR.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by LaRee Rumbolz to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented, and seconded by Jim Johnston. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of February 4th, 2025.
Designated revenue for FY 2025 is $150,000.
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2025 are $28,250. This
amount does include the $12,000 Special Olympics State Basketball award check.
Current Available Fund Balance of $121,750.
Collections in December (for November records) are 24,482.00 with one establishment still
past due.
Collections in January (for December records) are $14,704.00 with one establishment past
due.
The YTD collections for 2025 is $14,704.00, which equates to 7,352 total room nights sold.
YTD comparison for room nights sold were: down 31.4% (2,307 room nights sold) from 2024,
down 11.1% (817 room nights sold) from 2023, down 22.9% (1,687 room nights sold) from
2022, up 7.2% from 2021, down 46.3% from 2020, and down 11.1% from 2019.
The one establishment past due for January collections has provided an average over the past
three years of 1,918 room nights sold. This would bring our YTD room nights sold to above
9,200 room nights sold, which is a more respectable number.
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to approve the financial report as presented, and
seconded by Jason Christensen. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms w/Financials with the SEA Committee:
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials
Palace City Kiwanis Half Marathon/10K/5K (October 6th, 2024)

--- PAGE 3 OF 7 ---


• The event met (3) expectations. A little disappointed in this year's turnout, but they
have hired a media professional for 2025. An estimated total spectator attendance of
200. Total participants of 166. The estimated number of total hotel/motel room nights
sold was 33 (Hampton Inn, Kelly Inn, My Place). The awarded funds ($1,500) were
used to offset the costs of the run - medals, shirts, swag bags, porta potties, and timing
and registration company. $1,000 was a donation in support of the event and $500 was

SD Fire Instructors Conference (January 4th-5th, 2025)

11th, 2026.

The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

Memorial Weekend in Mitchell marks 24 years of cherished
tradition for our wonderful city. This event attracts participants
from across the state to engage in activities such as the BBQ Rib
contest, Kid Pedal Pull, Car Show & Shine, Poker Run, Bean
Bags, Poker Walk, Family Fun and the SD Mud Races. Each
year, the excitement builds as families and friends gather to
celebrate the spirit of our community. The BBQ Rib contest is a
favorite, with local chefs and enthusiasts firing up their grills to
compete for the title of the best ribs in the region. The tantalizing
aroma of smoky, savory ribs fills the air, drawing visitors to the
heart of Main Street.
Meanwhile, the Kid Pedal Pull offers a delightful spectacle as
children test their strength and determination, pedaling their way
to victory amidst cheers from the crowd. It's a joyful reminder of
the simple pleasures and the supportive community spirit that
defines Mitchell.
Car enthusiasts revel in the Car Show & Shine, where gleaming
vintage and modern vehicles line the streets, each one a
testament to the passion and dedication of its owner. The
admiration for these beautifully maintained cars is palpable,
sparking conversations and connections among attendees.
For those seeking an adrenaline rush, the SD Mud Races
provide a thrilling experience, with competitors navigating their
way through muddy tracks, showcasing skill and daring. The roar
of engines and the thrill of the race add an exhilarating energy to
the weekend.
There something for anyone of any age at this event!

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

documents.fileName: Palace Ice Festival Evaluation Form
documents.text:
From: 	noreply@civicplus.com
To: 	Aaron Hieb
Subject: 	Online Form Submittal: Sports & Events Authority Evaluation Form
Date: 	Thursday, March 20, 2025 9:57:39 PM
Sports & Events Authority Evaluation Form
Sports & Events Authority Evaluation
Form
Event Information
Name of Event: 	Palace City Ice Festival
Date(s) of Event: 	January 17-19, 2025
Evaluation Information
How well did this event
meet your
expectations:
4 - Above Expectations
Additional Feedback -
Please share the
positive takeaways, as
well as, ways the SEA
can assist in the growth
of the event:
The skating competition went very well, as the weather was very
nice with very mild temperatures, which after last year was very
welcome. Everyone had an awesome time with the competition
running very smoothly for the US Figure Skating judges,
coaches, skaters, and spectators in attendance.
The skating competitors always learn a lot from the judges
positive feedback and skating critic to help them become better
skaters.
In addition all of city employee's we worked with to host this
event did a great job making sure things went well.
As always, one of the highlights every year, is that our out of
state judges look forward to seeing the new murals on the Corn
Palace as they are truly amazed that the artwork.
One other really positive feedback we received this year from our
judges, was that their evening supper meals at the local
restaurants were not only good but spectacular!!
The assistance of the SEA Grant really helps offset competition
expenses so as to allow for the club to continue to have a
positive competition outcome to better help our club skaters grow
in their skating skills.
One other thing the club did this year, was to redesign our
competition awards medals to better reflect Mitchells main
attraction, the Corn Palace, for another positive way to have

--- PAGE 1 OF 3 ---


people to remember Mitchell. We incorporated our clubs
registered skating logo with a Corn Palace design, and it turned
out great, even having several requests from people both
Mitchell and from out of town to purchase one.
I will email a picture of a first place medal Aaron for him to show
you, and also drop off a thank you card from the club.
Total spectator
attendance:
Approximately 330 spectators
Total number of
participants (number
per team, if applicable):

documents.fileName: May 20th, 2025, SEA Advisory Committee Meeting Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                     May 20, 2025 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:01 PM  
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin 
Nelson, Jason Christensen, Dave Sietsema, Bryan Dixon, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, 
Dave Helleloid, and Tim Smith 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Jill Larson, Cory Aadland, and Jim Johnston 
 
 Others present: Aaron Hieb, Stephanie Ellwein, Andrew Schneider, and Johanna Allen 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.  
 
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.  
 
 The following applications were presented and considered: 
 
A. Blarney's Amateur Baseball Classic 
Jason Christensen spoke on behalf of and presented the Blarney's Amateur Baseball 
Classic Grant Application for consideration, which is requesting $2,500. 

     • Jason Christensen shared that the event is the same weekend as the Harve's/Wilson 
       Memorial Youth Baseball Tournament at the Cadwell Sports Complex. There will be 12 
       amateur teams = 6 games on Saturday, June 14th at Cadwell Park Stadium. The event 
       will be run like and have an environment similar to the State Amateur Baseball 
       Tournament. There is uncertainty about the number of hotel room nights the event will 
       generate along with the financials. Profits from the event will be used towards the DWU 
       TeamMaker Scholarships. The grant request will be used to pay for umps, press box 
       workers, field rental, lights, baseball, and t-shirts. 

 
 
B. Palace City Cup 2025 
Scott Mullenmeister spoke on behalf of the Mitchell Soccer Association and presented the 
Palace City Cup 2025 Grant Application for consideration, which is requesting $5,000. 
     • Scott Mullenmeister shared that the Palace City Cup will take place Saturday, June 
       14th through Sunday, June 15th at the Pepsi Cola Soccer Complex. The event will host 
       teams U9-U18, which is different from the fall tournament they hosted in 2024. 
       Currently, there are 25 teams registered with the expectation of between 40 and 50 
       teams. This is one of only two tournaments hosted this same weekend throughout 
       South Dakota. Rapid City is the only other city to host a tournament. The grant request 
       will be used to cover the biggest expense, which is the referees. 

 
 
C. Palace City Mountain Bike Classic 
Kourtney Denne, via conference phone, spoke on behalf of MAC Area Events, INC. and 
presented the Palace City Mountain Bike Classic Grant Application for consideration, which is 
requesting $1,500. 

     • Kourtney Denne shared that this is the 4th annual event, which will take place on 
       Saturday, June 21st around Lake Mitchell, but the route will be done in reverse, 
       compared to previous years. Last year (2024), the event had 81 registered riders. This 
       year they are incorporating a variety of multiple youth races to increase participation. 
       The grant request will be used to pay for the timing system, which is the biggest 
       expense each year. 

 
 
D. Arts in the Park 
Mayor Hanson spoke on behalf of and presented the Arts in the Park Grant Application for 
consideration, which is requesting $1,500. 

     • Mayor Hanson shared that the event in 2024 had an estimated overall event 
       attendance of 10,000 plus. He expects even more attendance this year, with over 150 
       vendors and plenty of family-friendly activities. The grant request will be used to help 
       with the city and park fees, insurance, and general costs to hold the event. 

 
 
E. South Dakota Women's State Slowpitch Softball Tournament 
*Tabled from the April meeting, no presentation required. 
 
April presentation notes: 
 
Emily Hohn, Mitchell Women's Slowpitch Softball, presented the South Dakota Women's State 
Slowpitch Softball Tournament Grant Application, which is requesting $6,500. 

     • Emily Hohn shared that the state softball tournament will take place July 26th-27th, 
       2025, at Cadwell Sports Complex. The biggest expense and grant request would go 
       towards the umpire fees along with $2,500 going to the State Association. The local 
       association is looking into fundraisers as well. There are four divisions that will be 
       hosted in Mitchell. 

 
 
F. Special Olympics State Basketball Tournament 
Mitchell has been selected as the foreseeable host of the Special Olympics State Basketball 
Tournament, and is requesting an additional $4,000 ($2,000 for 2026 & $2,000 for 2027) to 
 cover the additional expenses to host state basketball. 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Sietsema to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
presented, and seconded by Jason Christensen. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion 
 passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of May 15th, 2025.  
 
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2025 are $63,250.  
 
Current Available Fund Balance of $86,750.  
 
Collections in March (for February records) are updated to $16,173.50 with all collected. 
 
Collections in April (for March records) are $19,182.00 with all collected. 
 
The YTD collections for 2025 are $70,845.00, which equates to 35,423 total room nights sold.  
 
YTD comparisons of room nights sold were: up 7.0% (2,467 room nights sold) from 2024, up 
4.3% (1,513 room nights sold) from 2023, up 0.6% (210 room nights sold) from 2022, up 
20.2% from 2021, up 7.7% from 2020, and up 12.4% from 2019.  
 
Motion: Motion was made by Bryan Dixon to approve the financial report as presented, and 
 seconded by Emily Liedtke. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms w/Financials with the SEA Committee: 
 
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials 
Dakota Oyate Challenge Volleyball (October 11th-12th, 2024) 

     • The event was above (4) expectations. We had a great first annual volleyball 
       tournament for the DOC. Cross Country will be added the same weekend in 2025. 
       Total spectator attendance was 200. Total participants were 300. The estimated 
       number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was about 160+ (AmericInn, Comfort Inn, 
       Days Inn, Hampton Inn, Holiday Inn, My Place, and Quality Inn). The awarded funds 
       ($4,200) were used to pay officials, workers, and for the awards. Balance due - The 
       World's Only Corn Palace ($1,595.95). 

 
Girl's & Boy's Hanson Classic(s) (January 17th & January 24th, 2025) 

     • The events met (3) expectations. Total participants of 32 teams. The estimated number 
       of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 40 - 50 (AmericInn and Comfort Inn). 
       Awarded funds ($3,000 - $1,500 for each classic). Profits of $1,638. 

 
Dakota Oyate Challenge (January 30th-31st, February 1st, 2025) 

     • The event met (3) expectations. Schools and fans appreciate the availability of hotel 
       rooms and eating establishments. Total spectator attendance of 1,038, which is a 19% 
       increase from last year. Total participants of 16 basketball teams (8 boys and 8 girls), 
       27 hand games, and 5 archery teams. The estimated number of total hotel/motel room 
       nights sold was 900, which was about 300 per night, for a 8-13% increase from last 
       year (Comfort Inn, Days Inn, Hampton Inn, Holiday Inn, Kelly Inn, My Place, Quality 
       Inn, and Super 8 Motel). The awarded funds ($5,000) were used for awards and the 
       additional hotel rooms for officials. Profits, total due - Dakota Oyate Challenge 
       ($1,944.35) which will go towards next year's DOC. 

 
Knights of Columbus Special Olympics State Basketball Tournament Banquet (March 29th, 
2025) 

     • The event was above (4) expectations. The event went smoothly with plenty of 
       volunteers. Total spectator and participant attendance was 700+. The estimated 
       number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 552 (AmericInn, Comfort Inn, Days 
       Inn, Hampton Inn, Holiday Inn, Kelly Inn, Motel 6, My Place, Quality Inn, Mitchell Inn, 
       Super 8, and Thunderbird Lodge). The awarded funds ($1,500) were used to purchase 
       food, beverages, and supplies for the banquet. Not-for-profit event. 

 
Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament (April 11th-13th, 2025) 

     • The event was above (4) expectations. It was another very successful event this year. 
       We had great weather and the tailgating was taken to a higher level with donated 
       burgers and brats. Teams were able to golf on Saturday as well. Some took to the 
       bowling lanes. Total spectator attendance was between 600 and 800. Total participants 
       of 308 = 22 teams. The total room nights sold is estimated to be between 165 and 200 
       (Comfort Inn and Hampton Inn). The awarded funds ($4,000) were used to help cover 
       the City ice time expenses. Profits ($14,115.02) will be used to sponsor all 8U youth 
       players in hockey and also host on-ice skills clinics. Our adult group also works with 
       the VJ and Varsity players all year long to keep the awareness and excitement alive. 
       As our funds grow, we plan to help with building improvements as well. 

 
 
6. Other Items 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed and provided an update to the committee on the progress of Playeasy. 
 
A. Update and Review of Playeasy 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the HOME page of the Playeasy platform.  
 
Event Organizers within the platform: 736; Destinations including the Mitchell Sports & Events 
Authority: 322; Total active RFPs within the Marketplace: 211.

of those have been passed on because the RFPs require more hotel room nights than

the date of the event on the requested RFP overlaps with events already taking place in 
 Mitchell, SD.

The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.

will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the

the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
April 8, 2025
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:00 PM
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson,
Kevin Nelson, Jason Christensen, Dave Sietsema, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave
Helleloid, and Tim Smith

2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.
The following applications were presented and considered:
[IGNORE_INDENT]
A. Amateur Boxing Night presented by 15th Round Boxing
Mayor Jordan Hanson spoke on behalf of 15th Round Boxing and presented the Amateur
Boxing Night presented by 15th Round Boxing Grant Application for consideration, which is
requesting $1,500.
• Mayor Hanson shared that there are 27 scheduled bouts for the event on Saturday,
April 19th, 2025, with doors opening at 4 PM and the first bout being at 5 PM in The
World's Only Corn Palace. Currently, there are 21 tables sold; around 200 tickets for
the event. The grant request would be used to pay for the hotel rooms for the boxers.
[IGNORE_INDENT]
B. Mitchell Main Street & Beyond Memorial Weekend in Mitchell
Elizabeth Luczak, Mitchell Main Street & Beyond, presented the Memorial Weekend in Mitchell
Grant Application for consideration, which is requesting $2,000.

--- PAGE 1 OF 9 ---


• Elizabeth Luczak shared that the 24th Annual MMS&B Memorial Weekend in Mitchell
is Saturday, May 24th, 2025, starting at Noon on South Main Street. This event draws
approximately 5,000 attendees. The grant request of $1,000 would go towards the cost
of the ribs and the other $1,000 would go towards the marketing efforts and being able
to reach parts of northwest Iowa, southwest Minnesota, and the northeastern corner of
Nebraska to attract people to stay overnight. The goal is to have 5% of the total
attendance stay overnight in Mitchell.
[IGNORE_INDENT]
C. Mitchell Area Community (MAC) Triathlon
Terasa Gillen and Emily Hohn, Mitchell Area Community Triathlon, presented the MAC
Triathlon Grant Application, which is requesting $2,500.
• Terasa Gillen and Emily Hohn shared that the "10th" Annual MAC Triathlon will take
place on Saturday, June 7th, 2025. The biggest expense for the event and grant
request would go towards the timing system. There have been approximately 60–70
runners come from South Dakota and other states. The majority of the runners stay at
campgrounds rather than hotels. The funds that are raised through the MAC Area
Events will go towards fitness equipment around Cadwell Sports Complex.
[IGNORE_INDENT]
D. South Dakota Women's State Slowpitch Softball Tournament
Emily Hohn, Mitchell Women's Slowpitch Softball, presented the South Dakota Women's State
Slowpitch Softball Tournament Grant Application, which is requesting $6,500.
• Emily Hohn shared that the state softball tournament will take place July 26th-27th,
2025, at Cadwell Sports Complex. The biggest expense and grant request would go
towards the umpire fees along with $2,500 going to the State Association. The local
association is looking into fundraisers as well. There are four divisions that will be
hosted in Mitchell.
[IGNORE_INDENT]
E. The 301 Rodz and Ridez Car Show
Jerry Wright, The 301 Rodz, presented The 301 Rodz & Ridez Car Show Grant Application,
which is requesting $2,000.
• Jerry Wright shared that The 301 Rodz & Ridez Car Show (formally Outkasts Car
Show) will take place September 19th-21st, 2025, in collaboration with Oktoberfest.
The biggest expenses and grant request will go towards the trophies, advertising,
which includes invitations to all participants from years past, and thank you cards to
everyone who attended. Last year, the car show had just over 150 cars with around
100 hotel room nights. Also, working with local main street bars to provide

--- PAGE 2 OF 9 ---


entertainment and keep people in town and downtown.
[IGNORE_INDENT]

presented, and seconded by Jason Christensen. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion
passed.

documents.fileName: June 10th, 2025, Sports & Events Authority Committee Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                     June 10, 2025 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Tim Smith @ 2:00 PM 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin Nelson, Bryan Dixon, 
LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, Cory Aadland, 
Jason Christensen, and Dave Sietsema 
 
 Others present: Aaron Hieb and Stephanie Ellwein 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.  
 
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.  
 
 The following applications were presented and considered: 
 
A. South Dakota ATA State Trap Shoot Tournament 
Jerry Opbroek spoke on behalf of and presented the South Dakota ATA State Trap Shoot 
Tournament Grant Application for consideration, which is requesting $2,200. 

     • Jerry Opbroek shared that the South Dakota ATA State Trap Shoot Tournament will be 
       at the Mitchell Gun Club on July 9th-13th, 2025. Mitchell is the host site every third 
       year. It rotates between Mitchell, Sioux Falls, Aberdeen, and now Rapid City with a 
       new facility in the works. Wednesday, July 9th, is Mitchell Gun Club Day, which is what 
       the grant request of $2,200 would go towards. This request would help provide the 
       awards on the Mitchell Gun Club Day of the tournament. If the grant request is 
       approved, the Mitchell Sports & Events Authority would receive substantial recognition 
       during the event. Total participant attendance is expected to be around 250 shooters, 
       along with parents and family members. 

 
 
B. South Dakota Golf Association Adult/Junior and Junior Championships 
Eric Hieb spoke on behalf of and presented the South Dakota Golf Association Adult/Junior 
and Junior Championships Grant Application for consideration, which is requesting $1,500. 
     • Eric Hieb shared that Lakeview Golf Course will host the SDGA Adult/Junior and Junior 
       Championships with practice round(s) on July 19th, and competition July 20th-23rd, 
       2025. Last year, the Adult/Junior had 252 participants (126 teams). 2025 sign-ups so 
       far are 138 Adult/Junior (69 teams) and 118 Juniors. The grant request of $1,500 
       would be used towards hospitality, extra staffing, and work hours to prepare the 
       course. 

 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Kevin Nelson to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
 presented, and seconded by Bryan Dixon. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
4. Financial Report

Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
May 20, 2025
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:01 PM
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin
Nelson, Jason Christensen, Dave Sietsema, Bryan Dixon, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke,
Dave Helleloid, and Tim Smith
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Jill Larson, Cory Aadland, and Jim Johnston
Others present: Aaron Hieb, Stephanie Ellwein, Andrew Schneider, and Johanna Allen
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.
The following applications were presented and considered:
A. Blarney's Amateur Baseball Classic
Jason Christensen spoke on behalf of and presented the Blarney's Amateur Baseball
Classic Grant Application for consideration, which is requesting $2,500.
• Jason Christensen shared that the event is the same weekend as the Harve's/Wilson
Memorial Youth Baseball Tournament at the Cadwell Sports Complex. There will be 12
amateur teams = 6 games on Saturday, June 14th at Cadwell Park Stadium. The event
will be run like and have an environment similar to the State Amateur Baseball
Tournament. There is uncertainty about the number of hotel room nights the event will
generate along with the financials. Profits from the event will be used towards the DWU
TeamMaker Scholarships. The grant request will be used to pay for umps, press box
workers, field rental, lights, baseball, and t-shirts.
B. Palace City Cup 2025
Scott Mullenmeister spoke on behalf of the Mitchell Soccer Association and presented the
Palace City Cup 2025 Grant Application for consideration, which is requesting $5,000.

--- PAGE 1 OF 7 ---


• Scott Mullenmeister shared that the Palace City Cup will take place Saturday, June
14th through Sunday, June 15th at the Pepsi Cola Soccer Complex. The event will host
teams U9-U18, which is different from the fall tournament they hosted in 2024.
Currently, there are 25 teams registered with the expectation of between 40 and 50
teams. This is one of only two tournaments hosted this same weekend throughout
South Dakota. Rapid City is the only other city to host a tournament. The grant request
will be used to cover the biggest expense, which is the referees.
C. Palace City Mountain Bike Classic
Kourtney Denne, via conference phone, spoke on behalf of MAC Area Events, INC. and
presented the Palace City Mountain Bike Classic Grant Application for consideration, which is
requesting $1,500.
• Kourtney Denne shared that this is the 4th annual event, which will take place on
Saturday, June 21st around Lake Mitchell, but the route will be done in reverse,
compared to previous years. Last year (2024), the event had 81 registered riders. This
year they are incorporating a variety of multiple youth races to increase participation.
The grant request will be used to pay for the timing system, which is the biggest
expense each year.
D. Arts in the Park
Mayor Hanson spoke on behalf of and presented the Arts in the Park Grant Application for
consideration, which is requesting $1,500.
• Mayor Hanson shared that the event in 2024 had an estimated overall event
attendance of 10,000 plus. He expects even more attendance this year, with over 150
vendors and plenty of family-friendly activities. The grant request will be used to help
with the city and park fees, insurance, and general costs to hold the event.
E. South Dakota Women's State Slowpitch Softball Tournament
*Tabled from the April meeting, no presentation required.
April presentation notes:
Emily Hohn, Mitchell Women's Slowpitch Softball, presented the South Dakota Women's State
Slowpitch Softball Tournament Grant Application, which is requesting $6,500.
• Emily Hohn shared that the state softball tournament will take place July 26th-27th,
2025, at Cadwell Sports Complex. The biggest expense and grant request would go
towards the umpire fees along with $2,500 going to the State Association. The local
association is looking into fundraisers as well. There are four divisions that will be

--- PAGE 2 OF 7 ---


hosted in Mitchell.
F. Special Olympics State Basketball Tournament
Mitchell has been selected as the foreseeable host of the Special Olympics State Basketball
Tournament, and is requesting an additional $4,000 ($2,000 for 2026 & $2,000 for 2027) to
cover the additional expenses to host state basketball.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Sietsema to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented, and seconded by Jason Christensen. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion
passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of May 15th, 2025.
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2025 are $63,250.
Current Available Fund Balance of $86,750.
Collections in March (for February records) are updated to $16,173.50 with all collected.
Collections in April (for March records) are $19,182.00 with all collected.
The YTD collections for 2025 are $70,845.00, which equates to 35,423 total room nights sold.
YTD comparisons of room nights sold were: up 7.0% (2,467 room nights sold) from 2024, up
4.3% (1,513 room nights sold) from 2023, up 0.6% (210 room nights sold) from 2022, up
20.2% from 2021, up 7.7% from 2020, and up 12.4% from 2019.
Motion: Motion was made by Bryan Dixon to approve the financial report as presented, and
seconded by Emily Liedtke. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Forms w/Financials with the SEA Committee:
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials
Dakota Oyate Challenge Volleyball (October 11th-12th, 2024)
• The event was above (4) expectations. We had a great first annual volleyball
tournament for the DOC. Cross Country will be added the same weekend in 2025.
Total spectator attendance was 200. Total participants were 300. The estimated
number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was about 160+ (AmericInn, Comfort Inn,
Days Inn, Hampton Inn, Holiday Inn, My Place, and Quality Inn). The awarded funds
($4,200) were used to pay officials, workers, and for the awards. Balance due - The

--- PAGE 3 OF 7 ---


World's Only Corn Palace ($1,595.95).
Girl's & Boy's Hanson Classic(s) (January 17th & January 24th, 2025)
• The events met (3) expectations. Total participants of 32 teams. The estimated number
of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 40 - 50 (AmericInn and Comfort Inn).
Awarded funds ($3,000 - $1,500 for each classic). Profits of $1,638.
Dakota Oyate Challenge (January 30th-31st, February 1st, 2025)
• The event met (3) expectations. Schools and fans appreciate the availability of hotel
rooms and eating establishments. Total spectator attendance of 1,038, which is a 19%
increase from last year. Total participants of 16 basketball teams (8 boys and 8 girls),
27 hand games, and 5 archery teams. The estimated number of total hotel/motel room
nights sold was 900, which was about 300 per night, for a 8-13% increase from last
year (Comfort Inn, Days Inn, Hampton Inn, Holiday Inn, Kelly Inn, My Place, Quality
Inn, and Super 8 Motel). The awarded funds ($5,000) were used for awards and the
additional hotel rooms for officials. Profits, total due - Dakota Oyate Challenge
($1,944.35) which will go towards next year's DOC.
Knights of Columbus Special Olympics State Basketball Tournament Banquet (March 29th,
2025)
• The event was above (4) expectations. The event went smoothly with plenty of
volunteers. Total spectator and participant attendance was 700+. The estimated
number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 552 (AmericInn, Comfort Inn, Days
Inn, Hampton Inn, Holiday Inn, Kelly Inn, Motel 6, My Place, Quality Inn, Mitchell Inn,
Super 8, and Thunderbird Lodge). The awarded funds ($1,500) were used to purchase
food, beverages, and supplies for the banquet. Not-for-profit event.
Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament (April 11th-13th, 2025)
• The event was above (4) expectations. It was another very successful event this year.
We had great weather and the tailgating was taken to a higher level with donated
burgers and brats. Teams were able to golf on Saturday as well. Some took to the
bowling lanes. Total spectator attendance was between 600 and 800. Total participants
of 308 = 22 teams. The total room nights sold is estimated to be between 165 and 200
(Comfort Inn and Hampton Inn). The awarded funds ($4,000) were used to help cover
the City ice time expenses. Profits ($14,115.02) will be used to sponsor all 8U youth
players in hockey and also host on-ice skills clinics. Our adult group also works with
the VJ and Varsity players all year long to keep the awareness and excitement alive.
As our funds grow, we plan to help with building improvements as well.
