documents.fileName: July 8th, 2025, Sports & Events Authority Committee Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                      July 8, 2025 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:00 PM  
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Kevin Nelson, Jason 
Christensen, Dave Sietsema, Bryan Dixon, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, 
Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Mayor Hanson, Jill Larson, and Cory Aadland 
 
 Others present: Aaron Hieb, Johanna Allen, and Stephanie Ellwein 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.  
 
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.  
 
 The following applications were presented and considered: 
 
A. SoDak 16 Basketball 
The SoDak 16 Basketball Grant Application is requesting $1,700. 

     • Cory Aadland was unable to attend the meeting. 

 
 
B. Mitchell Baseball Association Tournament(s) - Early Bird, Harve/Bryan Memorial, & 
State A Youth 
Nathan Sparks spoke on behalf of and presented the Mitchell Baseball Association 
Tournament(s) Grant Application, which is requesting $6,000. 

     • Nathan Sparks shared that the funding request of $6,000 is primarily for the State 
       Youth Baseball Tournament which is taking place July 18th-20th, 2025. There will be 
       60 teams from throughout all of South Dakota participating. Friday, July 18th, starts at 
       8 AM and Saturday, July 19th starts at 8 AM with pool play both days. Mitchell will be 
       hosting the 9U, 11U, & 12U. The request helps offset the costs of hosting these 
       tournaments.  
 
C. USA Men's Slowpitch Softball "D" State Tournament 
Joe Wenzel spoke on behalf of and presented the USA Men's Slowpitch Softball "D" State 
Tournament Grant Application, which is requesting $2,000. 

     • Joe Wenzel shared that this is the third men's state tournament Mitchell has hosted in 
       the last seven years. There will be 10–20 teams participating in this double-elimination 
       state tournament on August 9th-10th, with 95% of teams coming from out of town. Only 
       one local (Mitchell) team is participating. The grant request of $2,000 will help pay for 
       the umpires, hotels, and field costs. There is no gate fee, no shirt or swag sales, and all 
       revenue goes to the USA South Dakota Softball Association. 

 
 
D. Palace City Kiwanis Half Marathon, 10K, & 5K 
Crystal Freund spoke on behalf of and presented the Palace City Kiwanis Half Marathon, 10K, 
& 5K Grant Application, which is requesting $1,500. 

     • Crystal Freund shared that this is the 8th annual event and they "Run for the Kids." 
       This event starts with a kids' run on Saturday morning, which is in its second year of 
       the kids' run. Currently, they are 50% higher in participation at this time compared to 
       last year. 41% of participants come from over 50+ miles always and 21% come from 
       over 100+ miles away. The goal is to have a runner from all 50 states. The grant 
       request would assist with marketing the event and Mitchell, SD, and to help offset the 
       costs. They estimate the event brings in about 50 room nights for the duration of the 
       event. 

 
 
E. Palace City 8ball Open 
Jen Raymond and Corey Ditter spoke on behalf of and presented the Palace City 8ball Open 
Grant Application, which is requesting $5,000. 

     • Jen and Corey shared that the event will be held at the Highland Conference Center on 
       November 14th-16th, 2025. The event was originally hosted two years ago at two local 
       establishments on Main Street with no expenses, and that year's event had over 
       $16,000 in player payouts. The grant request would help cover the venue cost 
       (Highland Conference Center) and pool table rental costs from D&E. There is no 
       income for the Palace City Pool Promotions. Any additional income will be reinvested 
       into the player prize fund. Looking to have over 60 players from outside of Mitchell with 
       a goal of 88 players coming from IA, MN, NE, ND, and throughout SD. 

 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Bryan Dixon to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
 presented, and seconded by Jim Johnston. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.  
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb and Stephanie Ellwein reviewed the financial report as of July 3rd, 2025.  
 
Sports & Events Authority Revenue increased to $194,640 for FY 2025 as the BID #4 Board 
approved supplementing the remaining 2024 SEA balance to the 2025 SEA balance. 
 
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2025 are $79,950. 
 
Current Available Fund Balance of $114,690.00.  
 
Collections in May (for April records) are $20,504.00 with (1) one establishment outstanding. 
Collections in June (for May records) are $22,522.00 with (3) three establishments 
outstanding.  
 
The YTD collections for 2025 are $113,871.00, which equates to 56,936 total room nights 
sold.  
 
YTD comparisons of room nights sold were: down 5.3% (3,003 room nights sold) from 2024, 
down 1.1% (616 room nights sold) from 2023, down 4.4% (2,478 room nights sold) from 2022, 
up 6.3% from 2021, up 26.2% from 2020, and up 6.6% from 2019.  
 
Motion: Motion was made by Jason Christensen to approve the financial report as presented, 
 and seconded by Tim Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials with the SEA Committee: 
 
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s) 
Combat Veteran's Motorcycle Association Comedy Night (March 22nd, 2025) 

     • The event was Above (4) Expectations. Total spectator attendance was about 150. 
       Total participants were 15. Spectators and participants came from Sioux Falls, Huron, 
       Rapid City, Mitchell, Ethan, Alexandria, Chamberlain, and Kimball. The estimated 
       number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 15. Unsure of next year's location and 
       date(s). The funds awarded ($1,500) were used to pay for venue and advertising. Total 
       profit of $4,065.08, which was used in support of Helping with Horsepower and other 
       local veterans in need. 

 
15th Round Boxing Amateur Boxing Night (April 19th, 2025) 

     • The event Met (3) Expectations. SEA helped tremendously! Great attendance. Total 
       spectator attendance was 567 total (462 audience, 103 staff, officials, and boxers). 
       Total participants were 103 staff, officials, and boxers. Spectators and participants 
       came from Mitchell, Sioux Falls, Chicago, Denver, Iowa, Aberdeen, Brookings, Mt. 
       Vernon, Yankton and many others! The estimated number of total hotel/motel room 
       nights sold was 40-60. Unsure of next year's location and date(s). The funds awarded        ($1,500) were used to pay for hotel rooms. Total profit will be used for future events. 

 
Blarney's Amateur Baseball Classic (June 14th, 2025) 

     • The event was Above (4) Expectations. Total spectator attendance was 800. Total 
       participants were 130. The estimated number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 
       unsure. Unsure of next year's location and date(s). The funds awarded ($2,500) were 
       used to pay expenses. Total profit of $2,420.63, which was used towards TeamMaker 
       Scholarships. 

 
 
6. Other Items 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed and provided an update to the committee on the progress of Playeasy. 
 
A. Update and Review of Playeasy 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the HOME page of the Playeasy platform. Event Organizers within the 
platform: 755; Destinations including the Mitchell Sports & Events Authority: 329; Total active 
RFPs within the Marketplace: 157. 
 
LEADS. Currently, there are 183 leads that match the Mitchell Sports & Events Authority. 181 
of those have been passed on because the RFPs require more hotel room nights than 
Mitchell, SD can provide; The RFP requires facility space that Mitchell, SD does not have, or 
the date of the event on the requested RFP overlaps with events already taking place in 
Mitchell, SD.  
 
No hotel bookings from within the Playeasy platform. 
 
Aaron will meet with Shaun Davis (7v7 Football) on Thursday of this week to discuss and see 
if it makes sense to work on a local event/camp rather than reaching out to and connecting 
with a national organization. 
 
Aaron will also re-connect with Scott Mullenmeister (Mitchell Soccer Association) this winter to 
 re-evaluate a 5v5 Soccer tournament in 2026.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

1. Call to Order

2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.
The following applications were presented and considered:
A. South Dakota ATA State Trap Shoot Tournament
Jerry Opbroek spoke on behalf of and presented the South Dakota ATA State Trap Shoot
Tournament Grant Application for consideration, which is requesting $2,200.
• Jerry Opbroek shared that the South Dakota ATA State Trap Shoot Tournament will be
at the Mitchell Gun Club on July 9th-13th, 2025. Mitchell is the host site every third
year. It rotates between Mitchell, Sioux Falls, Aberdeen, and now Rapid City with a
new facility in the works. Wednesday, July 9th, is Mitchell Gun Club Day, which is what
the grant request of $2,200 would go towards. This request would help provide the
awards on the Mitchell Gun Club Day of the tournament. If the grant request is
approved, the Mitchell Sports & Events Authority would receive substantial recognition
during the event. Total participant attendance is expected to be around 250 shooters,
along with parents and family members.
B. South Dakota Golf Association Adult/Junior and Junior Championships
Eric Hieb spoke on behalf of and presented the South Dakota Golf Association Adult/Junior
and Junior Championships Grant Application for consideration, which is requesting $1,500.

--- PAGE 1 OF 5 ---


• Eric Hieb shared that Lakeview Golf Course will host the SDGA Adult/Junior and Junior
Championships with practice round(s) on July 19th, and competition July 20th-23rd,
2025. Last year, the Adult/Junior had 252 participants (126 teams). 2025 sign-ups so
far are 138 Adult/Junior (69 teams) and 118 Juniors. The grant request of $1,500
would be used towards hospitality, extra staffing, and work hours to prepare the
course.

documents.fileName: August 12th, 2025, Sports & Events Authority Committee Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                    August 12, 2025 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:00 PM 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin 
Nelson, Cory Aadland, Jason Christensen, Dave Sietsema, Bryan Dixon, Emily Liedtke, Dave 
Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Jill Larson and LaRee Rumbolz 
 
 Others present: Stephanie Ellwein, Aaron Hieb, and Johanna Allen 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.  
 
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.  
 
 The following applications were presented and considered: 
 
A. Tour de Corn 
Katina spoke on behalf of and presented the Tour de Corn Grant Application, which is 
requesting $3,000. 

     • Katina shared that there are 275 registered with 50% of those coming from out of town. 
       Those that stay overnight will utilize the local hotels and local campgrounds. The grant 
       request of $3,000 goes towards the costs of the meal and swag for the riders. Profits 
       from the event help promote bike safety throughout the Mitchell community. This is a 3-
       day event with a meal and glow run on Friday night, the Tour de Corn on Saturday, and 
       a family event on Sunday. There are participants from 13 different states. 

 
 
B. Powerplay Hockey Clinic 
Nick Lemke spoke on behalf and presented the Powerplay Hockey Clinic Grant Application, 
which is requesting $2,000. 

     • Nick Lemke shared that Powerplay Hockey Clinic is an event that has developed over 
       the last few years. Attendance has increased over the years from 20 to 46 last year. 
       The grant request of $2,000 goes towards their biggest expense, which is ice time. The 
       event is roughly three days, with the clinic going from 4 PM-9 PM on Friday, 8 AM-8 
       PM on Saturday, and 9 AM-3 PM on Sunday. Instructors for the clinic come from South 
       Dakota and surrounding states, along with some senior hockey players. Nick estimates 
       that about a total of 20 room nights will be generated from this event. This event is 
       sponsored by the Lucky Devils Adult Hockey. 

 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
 presented, and seconded by Bryan Dixon. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of August 4th, 2025. 
 
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2025 are $86,700.  
 
Current Available Fund Balance of $107,940.00.  
 
Collections in May (for April records) are $20,574.00 with all collected. Collections in June (for 
May records) are $29,236.00 with all collected. Collections in July (for June records) are 
$37,482.00 with all collected.  
 
The YTD collections for 2025 are $158,137.00, which equates to 79,069 total room nights 
sold.  
 
YTD comparisons of room nights sold were: up 2.8% (2,249 room nights sold) from 2024, up 
5.0% (3,932 room nights sold) from 2023, up 1.5% (1,152 room nights sold) from 2022, up 
7.9% from 2021, up 31.6% from 2020, and up 9.0% from 2019. 
 
The financial numbers do reflect the grant funds ($3,000) that were awarded to the Mitchell 
Baseball Association from the July meeting that the Mitchell Baseball Association did not 
accept.  
 
Motion: Motion was made by Jason Christensen to approve the financial report as presented, 
 and seconded by Dave Helleloid. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials with the SEA Committee: 
 
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s) 
DWU Spring Golf Invite (April 7th-8th, 2025) 

     • The event was Below (2) Expectations. The weather wasn't the greatest, which caused 
       a frost delay on the first morning of the tournament, resulting in only 18 holes 
       compared to 36 being played. The total spectator attendance was between 75-100. 
       The total participants were 87 golfers and 12 coaches. Spectators and participants 
       came from SD, ND, IA, NE, MN, WY, KS, and CO. The estimated number of total 
       hotel/motel room nights was 70-90. Next year's location and date(s) is Lakeview Golf 
       Course on April 6th-7th, 2026. The funds awarded ($4,000) were used to pay for 
       expenses for the event. Total profit of $4,967.50, which will be used to enhance our 
       student-athletes' college experience. It helps get us into more exclusive events, gives 
       us the opportunity to do a couple of team meals throughout the year at local 
       restaurants, and order merchandise from local businesses. 

 
Your Town Tour - Neal McCoy (April 25th, 2025) 

     • The event Met (3) Expectations. The Corn Palace exceeded our expectations in 
       several key areas. The location was easily accessible for fans, the city staff was 
       extremely helpful and accommodating, and the facilities were clean, safe, and well-
       maintained. Crowd flow was smooth, and the local support—from security to 
       volunteers—made for an enjoyable experience not only for our team but for Neal 
       McCoy and his crew as well. The energy from the Mitchell crowd was electric, and it 
       truly felt like the perfect stop on the YOUR TOWN TOUR. The total spectator 
       attendance was 800. The estimated number of total hotel/motel room nights was 275. 
       Next year's location and date is The World's Only Corn Palace, on April 11th, 2026. 
       The funds awarded ($7,500) were used towards marketing the event in the local and 
       regional area. No profit from the event (-$3,595). 

 
A Night with Dan Gable (April 26th, 2025) 

     • The event was Above (4) Expectations. The total spectator attendance was 225. 
       Attendees came from all over South Dakota: Rapid City, Madison, Sioux Falls, 
       Faulkton, Martin, Parker, Canton, Tea, & Aberdeen, and Texas. The estimated number 
       of total hotel/motel room nights was 30. Unsure of next year's location and date(s). The 
       funds awarded ($750) were used towards advertising. Total profit of $6,250.00, which 
       will go back to the club to help continue promoting youth wrestling in South Dakota. 

 
 
6. Other Items 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed and provided an update to the committee on the progress of Playeasy. 
 
A. Update and Review of Playeasy 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the HOME page of the Playeasy platform.  
 
Event Organizers within the platform: 766; Destinations including the Mitchell Sports & Events 
Authority: 330; Total active RFPs within the Marketplace: 152.  
 
LEADS. Currently, there are 187 leads that match the Mitchell Sports & Events Authority. 186 
of those have been passed on for the following reasons: the RFPs require more hotel room 
nights than Mitchell, SD can provide; the RFP requires facility space that Mitchell, SD does not 
have, or the facility does not meet the seating requirements requested on the RFP.  
 
No hotel bookings from within the Playeasy platform.  
 
Aaron will also re-connect with Scott Mullenmeister (Mitchell Soccer Association) this winter to 
re-evaluate a 5v5 soccer tournament in 2026. 
 
Aaron met with Shaun Davis, 7v7 Football, about opportunities to assist and grow camps and 
 tournaments in Mitchell, SD. 
 
B. Upcoming Events 

     • Tour de Corn (August 15th-17th) 
            o Kiwanis Park, Corn Palace, and Lake Mitchell 
     • MHS Boat Parade (August 15th) 
            o Lake Mitchell 
     • Young Professionals Frisbee Golf Outing (August 16th) 
            o Kiwanis Park 
     • Dakotafest (August 19th-21st) 
            o 2300 Spruce St. 
     • Corn Palace Festival (August 20th-24th) 
            o The World’s Only Corn Palace & Main Street 
     • Young Professionals Social Hour (August 21st) 
            o Blarney’s Back Room 
     • Tailgate Takedown (Month of September) 
            o Mitchell, South Dakota (MMS&B) 
     • South Dakota State Pedal Pull (September 1st) 
            o The World’s Only Corn Palace 
     • 1st Fridays on Main (September 5th) 
            o Mitchell Main Street 
     • Palace City Farmer’s Market (Each Saturday through September) 
            o Corn Palace Plaza 
     • Palace City Brewing Co. 
     • James Valley Community Center 
     • Highland Conference Center 
     • MHS Performing Arts Center 

 
Complete list of events – MITCHELL CHAMBER EVENTS CALENDAR & Mitchell SD Events 
Facebook 
 
 *BOLD – Awarded Sports & Events Authority Grant funding. 
 
7. Executive Session in accordance with SDCL 9-34-19: Discussion of confidential trade 
secrets, commercial, or financial information. 
 
Motion: Bryan Dixon made a motion to go into Executive Session, and was seconded by Tim 
 Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
8. Approval of Funding Applications 
Tour de Corn 
Date: August 15th-17th, 2025; Contact: Kourtney Denne; Grant Request: $3,000 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Bryan Dixon to award $2,500, and seconded by Dave 
       Helleloid. 
            o All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
Powerplay Hockey Clinic 
Date: October 3rd-5th, 2025; Contact: Nick Lemke; Grant Request: $2,000 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Jason Christensen to award $2,000, and seconded by 
       Tim Smith. 
            o All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
 
9. Next Meeting Date 
Kevin McCardle shared the next meeting date of Tuesday, September 9th, 2025, @ 2 PM - 
 City Hall, Council Chambers. 
 
10. Adjournment 
 Meeting adjourned by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:39 PM

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
July 8, 2025
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:00 PM
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Kevin Nelson, Jason
Christensen, Dave Sietsema, Bryan Dixon, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid,
Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Mayor Hanson, Jill Larson, and Cory Aadland
Others present: Aaron Hieb, Johanna Allen, and Stephanie Ellwein
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.
The following applications were presented and considered:
A. SoDak 16 Basketball
The SoDak 16 Basketball Grant Application is requesting $1,700.
• Cory Aadland was unable to attend the meeting.
B. Mitchell Baseball Association Tournament(s) - Early Bird, Harve/Bryan Memorial, &
State A Youth
Nathan Sparks spoke on behalf of and presented the Mitchell Baseball Association
Tournament(s) Grant Application, which is requesting $6,000.
• Nathan Sparks shared that the funding request of $6,000 is primarily for the State
Youth Baseball Tournament which is taking place July 18th-20th, 2025. There will be
60 teams from throughout all of South Dakota participating. Friday, July 18th, starts at
8 AM and Saturday, July 19th starts at 8 AM with pool play both days. Mitchell will be
hosting the 9U, 11U, & 12U. The request helps offset the costs of hosting these
tournaments.

--- PAGE 1 OF 7 ---


C. USA Men's Slowpitch Softball "D" State Tournament
Joe Wenzel spoke on behalf of and presented the USA Men's Slowpitch Softball "D" State
Tournament Grant Application, which is requesting $2,000.
• Joe Wenzel shared that this is the third men's state tournament Mitchell has hosted in
the last seven years. There will be 10–20 teams participating in this double-elimination
state tournament on August 9th-10th, with 95% of teams coming from out of town. Only
one local (Mitchell) team is participating. The grant request of $2,000 will help pay for
the umpires, hotels, and field costs. There is no gate fee, no shirt or swag sales, and all
revenue goes to the USA South Dakota Softball Association.
D. Palace City Kiwanis Half Marathon, 10K, & 5K
Crystal Freund spoke on behalf of and presented the Palace City Kiwanis Half Marathon, 10K,
& 5K Grant Application, which is requesting $1,500.
• Crystal Freund shared that this is the 8th annual event and they "Run for the Kids."
This event starts with a kids' run on Saturday morning, which is in its second year of
the kids' run. Currently, they are 50% higher in participation at this time compared to
last year. 41% of participants come from over 50+ miles always and 21% come from
over 100+ miles away. The goal is to have a runner from all 50 states. The grant
request would assist with marketing the event and Mitchell, SD, and to help offset the
costs. They estimate the event brings in about 50 room nights for the duration of the
event.
E. Palace City 8ball Open
Jen Raymond and Corey Ditter spoke on behalf of and presented the Palace City 8ball Open
Grant Application, which is requesting $5,000.
• Jen and Corey shared that the event will be held at the Highland Conference Center on
November 14th-16th, 2025. The event was originally hosted two years ago at two local
establishments on Main Street with no expenses, and that year's event had over
$16,000 in player payouts. The grant request would help cover the venue cost
(Highland Conference Center) and pool table rental costs from D&E. There is no
income for the Palace City Pool Promotions. Any additional income will be reinvested
into the player prize fund. Looking to have over 60 players from outside of Mitchell with
a goal of 88 players coming from IA, MN, NE, ND, and throughout SD.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Bryan Dixon to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented, and seconded by Jim Johnston. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.

Aaron Hieb and Stephanie Ellwein reviewed the financial report as of July 3rd, 2025.
Sports & Events Authority Revenue increased to $194,640 for FY 2025 as the BID #4 Board
approved supplementing the remaining 2024 SEA balance to the 2025 SEA balance.

outstanding.
The YTD collections for 2025 are $113,871.00, which equates to 56,936 total room nights
sold.
YTD comparisons of room nights sold were: down 5.3% (3,003 room nights sold) from 2024,
down 1.1% (616 room nights sold) from 2023, down 4.4% (2,478 room nights sold) from 2022,
up 6.3% from 2021, up 26.2% from 2020, and up 6.6% from 2019.

and seconded by Tim Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials with the SEA Committee:
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s)
Combat Veteran's Motorcycle Association Comedy Night (March 22nd, 2025)
• The event was Above (4) Expectations. Total spectator attendance was about 150.
Total participants were 15. Spectators and participants came from Sioux Falls, Huron,
Rapid City, Mitchell, Ethan, Alexandria, Chamberlain, and Kimball. The estimated
number of total hotel/motel room nights sold was 15. Unsure of next year's location and
date(s). The funds awarded ($1,500) were used to pay for venue and advertising. Total
profit of $4,065.08, which was used in support of Helping with Horsepower and other
local veterans in need.
15th Round Boxing Amateur Boxing Night (April 19th, 2025)
• The event Met (3) Expectations. SEA helped tremendously! Great attendance. Total
spectator attendance was 567 total (462 audience, 103 staff, officials, and boxers).
Total participants were 103 staff, officials, and boxers. Spectators and participants
came from Mitchell, Sioux Falls, Chicago, Denver, Iowa, Aberdeen, Brookings, Mt.
Vernon, Yankton and many others! The estimated number of total hotel/motel room
nights sold was 40-60. Unsure of next year's location and date(s). The funds awarded

Aaron Hieb reviewed and provided an update to the committee on the progress of Playeasy.
A. Update and Review of Playeasy
Aaron Hieb reviewed the HOME page of the Playeasy platform. Event Organizers within the
platform: 755; Destinations including the Mitchell Sports & Events Authority: 329; Total active
RFPs within the Marketplace: 157.
LEADS. Currently, there are 183 leads that match the Mitchell Sports & Events Authority. 181
of those have been passed on because the RFPs require more hotel room nights than
Mitchell, SD can provide; The RFP requires facility space that Mitchell, SD does not have, or
the date of the event on the requested RFP overlaps with events already taking place in
Mitchell, SD.
No hotel bookings from within the Playeasy platform.
Aaron will meet with Shaun Davis (7v7 Football) on Thursday of this week to discuss and see

with a national organization.
Aaron will also re-connect with Scott Mullenmeister (Mitchell Soccer Association) this winter to

The Corn Palace exceeded our expectations in several key
areas. The location was easily accessible for fans, the city staff
was extremely helpful and accommodating, and the facilities
were clean, safe, and well-maintained. Crowd flow was smooth,
and the local support—from security to volunteers—made for an
enjoyable experience not only for our team but for Neal McCoy
and his crew as well. The energy from the Mitchell crowd was
electric, and it truly felt like the perfect stop on the YOUR TOWN
TOUR.
What can the SEA do to help the concert grow in the future?
To build on this success, a few improvements could help take the
event to the next level. First, expanding promotional support
through local channels—radio, newspapers, and digital
advertising—could help boost regional attendance. Second,
enhancing the layout of the concert itself in which we would sell
VIP Tables for people to have a higher end experience.
Mitchell is a great partner, and we’re excited about the potential
for even bigger shows in the years ahead.

documents.fileName: September 11th, 2025, Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                  September 11, 2025 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM  
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Kevin Nelson, Jason 
Christensen, Dave Sietsema, Bryan Dixon, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, and Tim Smith 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Mayor Hanson, Jill Larson, Cory Aadland, 
LaRee Rumbolz, and Jim Johnston 
 
 Others present: Aaron Hieb, Stephanie Ellwein, and Johanna Allen 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.  
 
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.  
 
 The following applications were presented and considered: 
 
A. Cornicupia 2025 
Scott Mullenmeister spoke on behalf of and presented the Cornicupia 2025 Grant Application, 
which is requesting $5,000. 

     • Scott shared that Cornicupia 2025 will be Saturday and Sunday, September 13th-14th 
       at the Pepsi Cola Soccer Complex. Last year, the event hosted 41 teams and received 
       a $5,000 SEA grant. This year, the Mitchell Soccer Association is requesting $5,000 to 
       cover expenses, with the major expense being referee costs. This year, they have 52 
       teams registered (Sioux Falls-Dakota Alliance and Brookings bring the most teams; 
       Brandon, Pierre, Watertown, Aberdeen, Rapid City, Yankton, Tea, and Mitchell) from 
       U8—U14 age divisions. Each team is guaranteed a minimum of 3 games with 2 games 
       played on Saturday, and 1 game or more on Sunday. Profits made from the event go 
       back to the Mitchell Soccer Association to provide new equipment for the kids and 
       cover additional costs such as facility rental. 

 
 
B. Raise Em Rank Series Finals 
Dillon Swanson via conference phone spoke on behalf of and presented the Raise Em' Rank 
Series Finals Grant Application, which is requesting $5,000. 

     • Dillon shared that this is the 4th year that the series finals will be held in Mitchell, SD at 
       The World's Only Corn Palace. This year's event will be October 3rd-4th at The World's 
       Only Corn Palace. The budget for this event is around $80,000. The grant request of 
       $5,000 would go towards rental of the facility and rental of other items needed for the 
       event to happen. The number of events has almost doubled compared to 2024, where 
       in 2024 they produced 7–10 events, and this year, 2025, they have produced almost 
       30 events. 

 
 
C. Dakota Oyate Challenge Volleyball 
Silas Blaine via conference phone spoke on behalf of and presented the Dakota Oyate 
Challenge Volleyball Grant Application, which is requesting $11,780. 

     • Silas shared that the Dakota Oyate Challenge Volleyball is in its 2nd year, which takes 
       place October 10th-11th at The World's Only Corn Palace. This event is branching off 
       from the Dakota Oyate Challenge Basketball Tournament. Last year, they had 16 
       teams participate over the two days. SEA grant awarded $4,200 last year (2024), 
       which mostly went towards hotel room costs for the officials. This year they have 15 
       teams competing. 

 
 
D. American Outlaws Wrestling 2nd Annual Monster Brawl 
JD Heinrich spoke on behalf of and presented the American Outlaws Wrestling 2nd Annual 
Monster Brawl Grant Application, which is requesting that "Any Amount is Appreciated". 

     • JD shared that the 2nd Annual Monster Brawl which is taking place October 31st, 
       November 1st and 2nd at the DWU/Avera Sports & Wellness Complex. A portion of 
       this year's entry fees will go towards a fundraiser for the John Donovan family. Weigh-
       ins will be Friday evening with individuals on Saturday and duals on Sunday. Randy 
       Lewis will be part of the event handing out awards. Last year they had 204 wrestlers. 
       They are hoping for up to 500 wrestlers for this year's event. The American Outlaws 
       Wrestling is requesting any amount is appreciated towards the event. 

 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Bryan Dixon to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
 presented, and seconded by Dave Sietsema. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of September 3rd, 2025.  
 
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2025 are $91,200.  
 
Current Available Fund Balance of $103,440.00.  
 
Collections in August (for July records) are $34,026.00 with 2 establishments past due. 
Calculating an average of these two establishments over the last four years in collections of 
$3,500, hopefully, after the two establishments have submitted collections, the total collections 
for July records will be at or above $37,000. 
 
The YTD collections for 2025 are $192,163.00, which equates to 96,082 total room nights 
sold.  
 
YTD comparisons of room nights sold were: up 0.9% (842 room nights sold) from 2024, up 
3.2% (3,056 room nights sold) from 2023, down 1.2% (1,122 room nights sold) from 2022, up 
2.7% from 2021, up 27.8% from 2020, and up 3.1% from 2019.  
 
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the financial report as presented, and 
 seconded by Jason Christensen. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials, Survey(s), and event flyer 
 with Thank You note with the SEA Committee: 
 
A. SEA Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s) 
Special Olympics State Basketball Tournament (March 29th-30th, 2025) 

     • The event was Above (4) Expectations. The community has been very supportive and 
       willing to volunteer. DWU and their student-athletes were amazing in their willingness 
       to always help. The total spectator attendance was 1,500. The total participants were 
       900. Spectators and participants came from all over SD. The estimated number of total 
       hotel room nights was 500. Next year's date(s) are March 27th-29th, 2026. The funds 
       awarded ($12,000) were used to offset expenses for the event. No profit. 

 
Memorial Weekend in Mitchell (May 24th, 2025) 

     • The event Exceeded (5) Expectations. Listed positive takeaways from each aspect of 
       the event. 4,902 ribs were eaten! The total spectator attendance was 5,000+. The total 
       participants were 10 rib teams with about 3-15 people per team. Rib teams were listed 
       along with their location. The estimated number of total hotel room nights was 
       uncertain. Next year's date is May 23rd, 2026. The funds awarded ($1,500) were used 
       towards advertising and BBQ team incentives. Net profit of $4,632.19. Rural Office of 
       Community Services: $4,500 - Helping Mitchell community members in need | 401 
       Create By LifeQuest: $375 - Help support their mission with people support at 401 
       Create on Main Street | Helping with Horsepower $400 - Help support their mission of 
       building a community of individuals born or diagnosed with limitations, where they 
       create opportunities for purpose, wellbeing and growth | MMSB: $4,600 - to help with 
       our mission of advancement, development and use of the main street area, by 
       supporting business and retail development, delivering downtown events, and working 
       with stakeholders on improvements to infrastructure and buildings. 
 
Palace City Cup 2025 (June 14th-15th, 2025) 

     • The event was Below (2) Expectations. Did not have the registrations that they were 
       hoping for... listed 5 notable reasons. The total, estimated spectator attendance was 
       850. The total participants were 29 teams. Spectators and participants came from 
       Rapid City, Brandon Valley, Watertown, Tea, Sioux Falls, Pierre, Aberdeen, Spearfish, 
       and Bismarck, ND. The estimated number of total hotel room nights was 300. Next 
       year's possible date(s) are April 18th-19th, May 16th-17th, and June 13th-14th, 2026. 
       The funds awarded ($5,000) were used to pay for tournament expenses, most of which 
       were referee costs. Total profit of $9,421.49, which goes back into supporting our 
       programs through paying coaches and purchasing equipment. 

 
Palace City Mountain Bike Classic (June 21st, 2025) 

     • The event Exceeded (5) Expectations. Great event! Biggest year yet with 65 registered 
       riders! The total spectator attendance was 45. The total participants were 65 registered 
       riders. Spectators and participants came from Sioux Falls, Mitchell, Miller, MO, 
       Brookings, Letcher, Harrisburg, Woonsocket, Huron, Yankton, Custer, and Alexandria. 
       The estimated number of total hotel room nights was 5. Individuals like to stay at 
       campgrounds. The funds awarded ($1,500) were used towards rider swag and timing 
       systems. Total profit of 5,220.82, which was a donation back to Palace City Pedalers 
       for a skills area for youth. 

 
Tour de Corn (August 15th-17th, 2025) 

     • The event Exceeded (5) Expectations. The total spectator attendance was 400. The 
       total participants were 320, and listed where they came from. The estimated number of 
       total hotel room nights was 50+, including camp sites. Next year's date(s) are August 
       14th-16th, 2026. The funds awarded ($2,500) were used towards the riders' meal and 
       swag bags. Total profit of 13,739.79, which will be used towards Improving Safe 
       Cycling in the Mitchell community, along with further expansion of the trail system and 
       development of cycling in youth.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

The many festivals, conventions, and sporting

will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
August 12, 2025
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle @ 2:00 PM
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin
Nelson, Cory Aadland, Jason Christensen, Dave Sietsema, Bryan Dixon, Emily Liedtke, Dave
Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Jill Larson and LaRee Rumbolz
Others present: Stephanie Ellwein, Aaron Hieb, and Johanna Allen
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.
The following applications were presented and considered:
A. Tour de Corn
Katina spoke on behalf of and presented the Tour de Corn Grant Application, which is
requesting $3,000.
• Katina shared that there are 275 registered with 50% of those coming from out of town.
Those that stay overnight will utilize the local hotels and local campgrounds. The grant
request of $3,000 goes towards the costs of the meal and swag for the riders. Profits
from the event help promote bike safety throughout the Mitchell community. This is a 3-
day event with a meal and glow run on Friday night, the Tour de Corn on Saturday, and
a family event on Sunday. There are participants from 13 different states.
B. Powerplay Hockey Clinic
Nick Lemke spoke on behalf and presented the Powerplay Hockey Clinic Grant Application,
which is requesting $2,000.
• Nick Lemke shared that Powerplay Hockey Clinic is an event that has developed over
the last few years. Attendance has increased over the years from 20 to 46 last year.

--- PAGE 1 OF 5 ---


The grant request of $2,000 goes towards their biggest expense, which is ice time. The
event is roughly three days, with the clinic going from 4 PM-9 PM on Friday, 8 AM-8
PM on Saturday, and 9 AM-3 PM on Sunday. Instructors for the clinic come from South
Dakota and surrounding states, along with some senior hockey players. Nick estimates
that about a total of 20 room nights will be generated from this event. This event is
sponsored by the Lucky Devils Adult Hockey.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented, and seconded by Bryan Dixon. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of August 4th, 2025.
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2025 are $86,700.
Current Available Fund Balance of $107,940.00.
Collections in May (for April records) are $20,574.00 with all collected. Collections in June (for
May records) are $29,236.00 with all collected. Collections in July (for June records) are
$37,482.00 with all collected.
The YTD collections for 2025 are $158,137.00, which equates to 79,069 total room nights
sold.
YTD comparisons of room nights sold were: up 2.8% (2,249 room nights sold) from 2024, up
5.0% (3,932 room nights sold) from 2023, up 1.5% (1,152 room nights sold) from 2022, up
7.9% from 2021, up 31.6% from 2020, and up 9.0% from 2019.
The financial numbers do reflect the grant funds ($3,000) that were awarded to the Mitchell
Baseball Association from the July meeting that the Mitchell Baseball Association did not
accept.
Motion: Motion was made by Jason Christensen to approve the financial report as presented,
and seconded by Dave Helleloid. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials with the SEA Committee:
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s)
DWU Spring Golf Invite (April 7th-8th, 2025)
• The event was Below (2) Expectations. The weather wasn't the greatest, which caused
a frost delay on the first morning of the tournament, resulting in only 18 holes
compared to 36 being played. The total spectator attendance was between 75-100.
The total participants were 87 golfers and 12 coaches. Spectators and participants

--- PAGE 2 OF 5 ---


came from SD, ND, IA, NE, MN, WY, KS, and CO. The estimated number of total
hotel/motel room nights was 70-90. Next year's location and date(s) is Lakeview Golf
Course on April 6th-7th, 2026. The funds awarded ($4,000) were used to pay for
expenses for the event. Total profit of $4,967.50, which will be used to enhance our
student-athletes' college experience. It helps get us into more exclusive events, gives
us the opportunity to do a couple of team meals throughout the year at local
restaurants, and order merchandise from local businesses.
Your Town Tour - Neal McCoy (April 25th, 2025)
• The event Met (3) Expectations. The Corn Palace exceeded our expectations in
several key areas. The location was easily accessible for fans, the city staff was
extremely helpful and accommodating, and the facilities were clean, safe, and well-
maintained. Crowd flow was smooth, and the local support—from security to
volunteers—made for an enjoyable experience not only for our team but for Neal
McCoy and his crew as well. The energy from the Mitchell crowd was electric, and it
truly felt like the perfect stop on the YOUR TOWN TOUR. The total spectator
attendance was 800. The estimated number of total hotel/motel room nights was 275.
Next year's location and date is The World's Only Corn Palace, on April 11th, 2026.
The funds awarded ($7,500) were used towards marketing the event in the local and
regional area. No profit from the event (-$3,595).

• The event was Above (4) Expectations. The total spectator attendance was 225.
Attendees came from all over South Dakota: Rapid City, Madison, Sioux Falls,
Faulkton, Martin, Parker, Canton, Tea, & Aberdeen, and Texas. The estimated number
of total hotel/motel room nights was 30. Unsure of next year's location and date(s). The
funds awarded ($750) were used towards advertising. Total profit of $6,250.00, which
will go back to the club to help continue promoting youth wrestling in South Dakota.

of the event:
Car Show – A stunning lineup of classic and custom vehicles
drew crowds and sparked great conversations among
enthusiasts of all ages.
Poker Run – Riders enjoyed a scenic route and friendly
competition, all while supporting a great cause.
Cornhole Tournament – Teams battled it out in a fun and lively
atmosphere, with plenty of cheers and laughter throughout the
day.
Kid Fun Zone – Families loved the interactive games, inflatables,
and activities that kept the little ones smiling all weekend long.
4,902 Ribs Eaten! – Yes, you read that right! Our rib teams were
busy serving up mouthwatering BBQ that had everyone coming
back next year!
The event brought together neighbors, visitors, and local
businesses, creating a vibrant celebration of community spirit
and summer fun.

We did not have the registrations that we were hoping for due to
a number of reasons.
1. Our tournament was the 3rd weekend in a row of tournaments
(Brookings, Watertown, Mithcell).
2. We are at the tail end of the season and some teams may
have been done with tournaments for the year by our weekend
3. We are getting into the beginning of summer travel and teams
may have a more difficult time putting together a full rostered
team to attend
4. We are a first-year tournament and many of the other
tournaments that are held around the state have been around for
years
5. 2 notable clubs that were not in attendance were DASC (Sioux
Falls) and Brookings. These clubs traditionally bring a lot of

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                   October 14, 2025 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, 
Kevin Nelson, Jason Christensen, Dave Sietsema, Bryan Dixon, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily 
Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston  
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Cory Aadland 
 
 Others present: Aaron Hieb and Stephanie Ellwein 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.  
 
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.  
 
 The following applications were presented and considered: 
 
A. Pheasants Forever Banquet 
Kevin Bruscher spoke on behalf of and presented the Pheasants Forever Banquet Grant 
Application, which is requesting $2,500. 

     • Kevin shared some updates and progress that the Pheasant Country, Chapter 872 is 
       making with local game production areas within a 35-mile radius of Mitchell, SD. They 
       were also involved with the state trap shoot and hosted a youth pheasant hunt last 
       weekend. The money that is raised by Chapter 872 stays and is used locally, within a 
       35-mile radius of Mitchell, to improve habitat and invest in youth hunting activities and 
       experiences throughout the Mitchell community. The Pheasants Forever Banquet is 
       Friday, October 17th at The World's Only Corn Palace. Tickets available were 
       increased from 700 to 750. Estimated attendance is about 55% come from out of state. 

 
 
B. Dakota Riptide: Tide Winter Invite Swim Meet & Sprint Invite Swim Meet 
Rob Schelske spoke on behalf of and presented the Dakota Riptide: Tide Winter Invite Swim 
Meet & Sprint Invite Swim Meet Grant Application, which is requesting $5,000. 
     • Rob shared that the Dakota Riptide is hosting (2) winter meets, December 12th–14th, 
       2025, which usually brings 200+ swimmers and January 17th-18th, 2026, which will 
       bring 150+ swimmers. Dakota Riptide in Mitchell has around 80 members. Swimmers 
       come from Watertown, Sioux Falls, Brookings, Pierre, and Aberdeen. 

 
 
C. Hoop City Classic 2025 
Brad Bartscher spoke on behalf of and presented the Hoop City Classic 2025 Grant 
Application, which is requesting $20,000. 

     • Brad shared that the Hoop City Classic is a 5-day event with the youth basketball 
       tournament taking place December 27th-28th, 2025, which should bring 60–70 teams, 
       and the high school games taking place December 29th-31st, 2025. The youth 
       basketball tournament will take place in the facilities at Dakota Wesleyan University 
       and there will be 19 high school games and 12 JV games taking place at The World's 
       Only Corn Palace arena and armory over the 3 days with teams coming from all over 
       SD and out-of-state teams coming from GA and FL.  

 
 
D. Midwest Miracles Basketball Classic 
Brad Bartscher spoke on behalf of and presented the Midwest Miracles Basketball 
Classic Grant Application, which is requesting $5,000. 

     • Brad shared that the Midwest Miracles Classic is in its second year. The first year took 
       place in Hurley and was created by Kobee Sherman as a way to raise funds to help 
       cancer families pay for lodging, food, transportation, and other expenses during their 
       doctor visits and hospital stays. This will be an annual one-day event with girls' and 
       boys' games along with JV games taking place this year on January 3rd, 2026 at The 
       World's Only Corn Palace. Every other year the DWU Women's basketball team will 
       participate in the event by playing St. Mary's.  

 
 
E. 2nd Annual Mitchell Pickleball Indoor Tournament 
Kevin Doorn spoke on behalf of and presented the 2nd Annual Mitchell Pickleball Indoor 
Tournament Grant Application, which is requesting $2,500. 

     • Kevin shared that the 2nd Annual Mitchell Pickleball Indoor Tournament will take place 
       January 2nd-4th, 2026 at the DWU/Avera Sports & Wellness Complex. This year the 
       event added a third day to the tournament in hopes of bringing more people to Mitchell. 
       They are estimating 80–140 players will participate in the 3-day tournament. The grant 
       request of $2,500 will be utilized in the prize fund to incentivize players to come to the 
       tournament. 

 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Prior to the Approval of Minutes, JD Heinrich, American Outlaws Wrestling presented the 
Mitchell Sports & Events Authority with the Sponsor of the Year Award. JD presented the 
committee with a plaque and individual 'Thank You' cards and 'Thank you for Supporting' 
poker chips to each member.  
 
Motion: Motion was made by Bryan Dixon to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
presented, and seconded by Jason Christensen. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion 
 passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of October 2nd, 2025.  
 
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2025 are $107,400.00. 
 
Current Available Fund Balance of $87,240.00.  
 
Collections in August (for July records) are $38,390.00 with 1 establishment past due. 
Collections in September (for August records) are $36,884.00 with 1 establishment past due. 
 
The YTD collections for 2025 are $233,411.00, which equates to 116,706 total room nights 
sold.  
 
YTD comparisons of room nights sold were: up 1.8% (2,148 room nights sold) from 2024, up 
4.6% (5,322 room nights sold) from 2023, up 0.5% (612 room nights sold) from 2022, up 2.8% 
from 2021, up 26.3% from 2020, and up 2.4% from 2019.  
 
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the financial report as presented, and 
 seconded by Jim Johnston. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials and Thank You note with 
 the SEA Committee: 
 
A. SEA Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s) 
MAC Triathlon (June 7th, 2025) 

     • The event was Above (4) expectations. Help from the Rec Center with lifeguards and 
       pool assistance was super. The total spectator attendance was 100. The total 
       participants were 61; 14 teams, 8 series, and 39 regular. The estimated number of total

Powderhorn Ranch Regulators Outlaw Gauntlet Shoots (June 12th-15th, 2025) 
     • The event was Above (4) expectations. Contestants were very happy with the shoot 
       and the variety. The total spectator attendance was 150. The total participants were 70,

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

SEA Grant Application states that 70% of participants and attendance are from over 50 miles away.
Last year they had 80 participants.
In January 2026, the event is expanding to a three-day event.
The first day of the event is Friday, January 2nd, 2026, which will be singles play. Then Saturday, January 3rd through Sunday, January 4th will be doubles play.
Online registrations will begin the middle of October.

The profits and proceeds from the event will go to further improving the NEW outdoor pickleball courts at Hitchcock Park by providing benches and wind screens.

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
September 11, 2025
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Kevin Nelson, Jason
Christensen, Dave Sietsema, Bryan Dixon, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, and Tim Smith
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Mayor Hanson, Jill Larson, Cory Aadland,
LaRee Rumbolz, and Jim Johnston
Others present: Aaron Hieb, Stephanie Ellwein, and Johanna Allen
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.
The following applications were presented and considered:
A. Cornicupia 2025
Scott Mullenmeister spoke on behalf of and presented the Cornicupia 2025 Grant Application,
which is requesting $5,000.
• Scott shared that Cornicupia 2025 will be Saturday and Sunday, September 13th-14th
at the Pepsi Cola Soccer Complex. Last year, the event hosted 41 teams and received
a $5,000 SEA grant. This year, the Mitchell Soccer Association is requesting $5,000 to
cover expenses, with the major expense being referee costs. This year, they have 52
teams registered (Sioux Falls-Dakota Alliance and Brookings bring the most teams;
Brandon, Pierre, Watertown, Aberdeen, Rapid City, Yankton, Tea, and Mitchell) from
U8—U14 age divisions. Each team is guaranteed a minimum of 3 games with 2 games
played on Saturday, and 1 game or more on Sunday. Profits made from the event go
back to the Mitchell Soccer Association to provide new equipment for the kids and
cover additional costs such as facility rental.
B. Raise Em Rank Series Finals
Dillon Swanson via conference phone spoke on behalf of and presented the Raise Em' Rank

--- PAGE 1 OF 7 ---


Series Finals Grant Application, which is requesting $5,000.
• Dillon shared that this is the 4th year that the series finals will be held in Mitchell, SD at
The World's Only Corn Palace. This year's event will be October 3rd-4th at The World's
Only Corn Palace. The budget for this event is around $80,000. The grant request of
$5,000 would go towards rental of the facility and rental of other items needed for the
event to happen. The number of events has almost doubled compared to 2024, where
in 2024 they produced 7–10 events, and this year, 2025, they have produced almost
30 events.
C. Dakota Oyate Challenge Volleyball
Silas Blaine via conference phone spoke on behalf of and presented the Dakota Oyate
Challenge Volleyball Grant Application, which is requesting $11,780.
• Silas shared that the Dakota Oyate Challenge Volleyball is in its 2nd year, which takes
place October 10th-11th at The World's Only Corn Palace. This event is branching off
from the Dakota Oyate Challenge Basketball Tournament. Last year, they had 16
teams participate over the two days. SEA grant awarded $4,200 last year (2024),
which mostly went towards hotel room costs for the officials. This year they have 15
teams competing.
D. American Outlaws Wrestling 2nd Annual Monster Brawl
JD Heinrich spoke on behalf of and presented the American Outlaws Wrestling 2nd Annual
Monster Brawl Grant Application, which is requesting that "Any Amount is Appreciated".
• JD shared that the 2nd Annual Monster Brawl which is taking place October 31st,
November 1st and 2nd at the DWU/Avera Sports & Wellness Complex. A portion of
this year's entry fees will go towards a fundraiser for the John Donovan family. Weigh-
ins will be Friday evening with individuals on Saturday and duals on Sunday. Randy
Lewis will be part of the event handing out awards. Last year they had 204 wrestlers.
They are hoping for up to 500 wrestlers for this year's event. The American Outlaws
Wrestling is requesting any amount is appreciated towards the event.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Bryan Dixon to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented, and seconded by Dave Sietsema. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of September 3rd, 2025.
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2025 are $91,200.

--- PAGE 2 OF 7 ---


Current Available Fund Balance of $103,440.00.
Collections in August (for July records) are $34,026.00 with 2 establishments past due.
Calculating an average of these two establishments over the last four years in collections of
$3,500, hopefully, after the two establishments have submitted collections, the total collections
for July records will be at or above $37,000.
The YTD collections for 2025 are $192,163.00, which equates to 96,082 total room nights
sold.
YTD comparisons of room nights sold were: up 0.9% (842 room nights sold) from 2024, up
3.2% (3,056 room nights sold) from 2023, down 1.2% (1,122 room nights sold) from 2022, up
2.7% from 2021, up 27.8% from 2020, and up 3.1% from 2019.
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the financial report as presented, and
seconded by Jason Christensen. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials, Survey(s), and event flyer
with Thank You note with the SEA Committee:
A. SEA Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s)
Special Olympics State Basketball Tournament (March 29th-30th, 2025)
• The event was Above (4) Expectations. The community has been very supportive and
willing to volunteer. DWU and their student-athletes were amazing in their willingness
to always help. The total spectator attendance was 1,500. The total participants were
900. Spectators and participants came from all over SD. The estimated number of total
hotel room nights was 500. Next year's date(s) are March 27th-29th, 2026. The funds
awarded ($12,000) were used to offset expenses for the event. No profit.
Memorial Weekend in Mitchell (May 24th, 2025)
• The event Exceeded (5) Expectations. Listed positive takeaways from each aspect of
the event. 4,902 ribs were eaten! The total spectator attendance was 5,000+. The total
participants were 10 rib teams with about 3-15 people per team. Rib teams were listed
along with their location. The estimated number of total hotel room nights was
uncertain. Next year's date is May 23rd, 2026. The funds awarded ($1,500) were used
towards advertising and BBQ team incentives. Net profit of $4,632.19. Rural Office of
Community Services: $4,500 - Helping Mitchell community members in need | 401
Create By LifeQuest: $375 - Help support their mission with people support at 401
Create on Main Street | Helping with Horsepower $400 - Help support their mission of
building a community of individuals born or diagnosed with limitations, where they
create opportunities for purpose, wellbeing and growth | MMSB: $4,600 - to help with
our mission of advancement, development and use of the main street area, by
supporting business and retail development, delivering downtown events, and working
with stakeholders on improvements to infrastructure and buildings.

--- PAGE 3 OF 7 ---


Palace City Cup 2025 (June 14th-15th, 2025)
• The event was Below (2) Expectations. Did not have the registrations that they were
hoping for... listed 5 notable reasons. The total, estimated spectator attendance was
850. The total participants were 29 teams. Spectators and participants came from
Rapid City, Brandon Valley, Watertown, Tea, Sioux Falls, Pierre, Aberdeen, Spearfish,
and Bismarck, ND. The estimated number of total hotel room nights was 300. Next
year's possible date(s) are April 18th-19th, May 16th-17th, and June 13th-14th, 2026.
The funds awarded ($5,000) were used to pay for tournament expenses, most of which
were referee costs. Total profit of $9,421.49, which goes back into supporting our
programs through paying coaches and purchasing equipment.
Palace City Mountain Bike Classic (June 21st, 2025)
• The event Exceeded (5) Expectations. Great event! Biggest year yet with 65 registered
riders! The total spectator attendance was 45. The total participants were 65 registered
riders. Spectators and participants came from Sioux Falls, Mitchell, Miller, MO,
Brookings, Letcher, Harrisburg, Woonsocket, Huron, Yankton, Custer, and Alexandria.
The estimated number of total hotel room nights was 5. Individuals like to stay at
campgrounds. The funds awarded ($1,500) were used towards rider swag and timing
systems. Total profit of 5,220.82, which was a donation back to Palace City Pedalers
for a skills area for youth.
Tour de Corn (August 15th-17th, 2025)
• The event Exceeded (5) Expectations. The total spectator attendance was 400. The
total participants were 320, and listed where they came from. The estimated number of
total hotel room nights was 50+, including camp sites. Next year's date(s) are August
14th-16th, 2026. The funds awarded ($2,500) were used towards the riders' meal and
swag bags. Total profit of 13,739.79, which will be used towards Improving Safe
Cycling in the Mitchell community, along with further expansion of the trail system and
development of cycling in youth.

Porter Distributing presents: Miller Lite Palace City 8-Ball Open (November 14th-16th, 2025)
