November 18th, 2025, Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                  November 18, 2025 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM  
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, Kevin Nelson, 
Dave Sietsema, Bryan Dixon, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Mayor Hanson, Cory Aadland, Jason 
Christensen, and Dave Helleloid 
 
 Others present: Aaron Hieb and Stephanie Ellwein 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.  
 
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.  
 
 The following applications were presented and considered: 
 
A. NAIA National Women's Volleyball Tournament Opening Round 
 
*Action will be taken if The World's Only Corn Palace and Mitchell, SD are awarded a host 
site bid, which will be announced on Monday, November 17th, 2025. 
 
The World's Only Corn Palace and Mitchell, SD were not awarded the bid to host the NAIA 
 National Women's Volleyball Tournament Opening Round, so no action was taken. 
 
B. South Dakota Fire Instructors Conference 
Justin Adams spoke on behalf of and presented the South Dakota Fire Instructors 
Conference Grant Application, which is requesting $4,800. 

     • Justin shared that this is the second consecutive year that Mitchell, SD is hosting the 
       South Dakota Fire Instructors Conference. The conference takes place on January 10-
       11, 2026 at the Highland Conference Center. The grant request of $4,800 will go 
       towards bringing in a high-profile guest speaker instructor for the conference. There 
       are 300 total fire instructors throughout South Dakota. They are expecting up to 150        instructors to attend this conference. 

 
 
C. North Dakota Country Fest-Your Town Tour 
Dan Beukelman spoke on behalf of and presented the North Dakota Country Fest-Your Town 
Tour Grant Application, which is requesting $5,000. 

     • Dan shared that the Your Town Tour will take place April 11, 2026 at The World's Only 
       Corn Palace. This will be the second consecutive year that Mitchell, SD has hosted a 
       North Dakota Country Fest-Your Town Tour concert. This year's lineup will be The 
       Frontmen featuring Rogue Royal with over 3 hours of country music. Also, Dan shared 
       that the Your Town Tour will not feature stops in Nebraska, Sioux Falls, Sturgis, or 
       Aberdeen like there was in 2025. As a result, estimated attendance should be over 
       1,000 along with providing around 100 hotel room nights as well. The grant request of 
       $5,000 will go towards local and regional marketing/advertising. 

 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Bryan Dixon to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
 presented, and seconded by Jim Johnston. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of November 12th, 2025.  
 
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2025 are $134,900.00.  
 
Current Available Fund Balance of $59,740.00.  
 
Collections in August (for July records) are $38,450.00 with all collected.  
 
Collections in September (for August records) are $36,934.00 with all collected.  
 
Collections in October (for September records) are $32,008.00 with 1 establishment past due.  
 
The YTD collections for 2025 are $265,529.00, which equates to 132,765 total room nights 
sold.  
 
YTD comparisons of room nights sold were: up 0.5% (697 room nights sold) from 2024, up 
3.3% (4,414 room nights sold) from 2023, down 0.2% (209 room nights sold) from 2022, up 
2.2% from 2021, up 24.1% from 2020, and up 1.7% from 2019. 
 
Also, a question from the committee was asked if the (1) outstanding collection for October will 
bring us closer to last year's monthly collection amount. As a result, Aaron shared some of the 
events that took place or vice versa, did not take place during the past three months that may 
have contributed to the monthly collection amounts.  

     • Collections in August for the month of July             o State Trap Shoot 
            o SDGA Adult/Junior & Junior Championships 
            o Women's State Slowpitch Softball 
            o Palace City Pre-Sturgis Party (July 31st) normally falls on an August date. 
     • Collections in September for the month of August 
            o No State Amateur Baseball Tournament 
            o No Palace City Pre-Sturgis Party since it fell on July 31st. 
     • Collections in October for the month of September  
            o Cowboy Fast Draw was hosted in June. 

 
Also, Emily Liedtke shared that another factor for the subtle decline in collections the past 
couple of months compared to previous years could be that there are less hotel(s) reporting 
and contributing to the monthly collections since the restructuring of the BID #4 boundaries. 
 
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the financial report as presented, and 
 seconded by Bryan Dixon. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials and Thank You note with 
 the SEA Committee: 
 
A. SEA Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s) 
South Dakota State ATA Trapshoot Tournament (July 9th-13th, 2025) 

     • The event Met (3) expectations. Attendance was down slightly, but the weather was 
       excellent, and the shoot went well. The total spectator attendance was 1,500. The total 
       participants were 210; SD, IA, MN, CO, TX, ND. The estimated number of total hotel 
       room nights was 800+. Next year's date: Mitchell is awarded the State ATA Traphsoot 
       every 3rd year. The funds awarded ($2,200) were used towards the Mitchell SEA-
       sponsored shoot on Wednesday. Net profit of $19,723.43, which will be used to 
       upgrade several of the traphouses, to complete necessary repairs on trap machines, 
       and construct at least one new spectator shelter. 

 
South Dakota Golf Association Adult-Junior and Junior Championships (July 20th-23rd, 2025) 

     • The event Exceeded (5) expectations. Largest SDGA event on record for the 
       Adult/Junior Championship with 304 participants. Volunteers are a key to any 
       successful state event and assistance with that was great. The total spectator 
       attendance was 110. The total participants were 776 for the 4 days of competition. The 
       estimated number of total hotel room nights was 325. Next year's date is in Rapid City, 
       SD. The funds awarded ($1,500) were used to provide complimentary goods/services 
       to the participants and volunteers. Eric provided an event expense report for which the 
       amount awarded ($1,500) was used towards. 

 
South Dakota Women's State Slowpitch Softball Tournament (July 26th-27th, 2025) 

     • The event Met (3) expectations. The total spectator attendance was 300. The total        participants were 285 = 29 teams; Sioux Falls, Rapid City, Brookings, Pierre, 
       Aberdeen, Watertown. The estimated number of total hotel room nights was that the 
       event provided 2 nights of hotel room nights. Next year's date is in Aberdeen and 
       Brookings. The funds awarded ($2,500) went to the state association. There is no profit 
       for the local association. Kathy provided an expense report for the tournament. 

 
 
B. Thank You card 
 
 Palace City Kiwanis Half Marathon, 10k, & 5k (October 5th, 2025) 
 
6. Other Items 
 
 
A. Update and Review of Playeasy 
Mitchell Sports & Events Authority 

     • Aaron shared that he has not secured any events yet from the Playeasy platform, but 
       there are (3) leads that are being actively pursued. 
     • Aaron also shared an update regarding 5 V 5 Soccer. 
            o Aaron met with Scott Mullenmeister last Thursday afternoon and had a good 
              conversation about the progress and successes of the Mitchell Soccer 
              Association along with the establishment of (2) tournaments (Palace City Cup 
              and Cornicupia) that they have hosted the last two years. At this point, the 
              Mitchell Soccer Association Board will pass on the 5v5 Soccer opportunity, so 
              they can continue to put their time, energy, and focus on growing and hosting 
              successful tournaments (Palace City Cup & Cornicupia) that they rejuvenated in 
              2024. 
     • Aaron is in the early stages of utilizing the Playeasy Community Collaboration feature, 
       which sends an email inviting the store owner/manager to create an account to have 
       ADMIN access to their local business profile micro-site. Once they have ADMIN 
       access, they will be able to manage only their local business profile and create SEA 
       event-specific promotions or general promotion campaigns that are available to those 
       events that are awarded SEA funding. Once these promotions are created, Aaron will 
       distribute "Ear of Corn" coupons to SEA-funded organizations that they will share with 
       those participating local businesses to receive their promotion. 

 
 
B. Upcoming Events 

     • Soup & Sandwich Showdown (Month of November) 
            o Mitchell, SD 
     • DWU Women’s & Men’s Basketball vs. Morningside (November 19th) 
            o The World’s Only Corn Palace 
     • Holiday Arts Christmas Craft Show (November 21st-22nd) 
            o Davison County Fairgrounds      • Mitchell Food Pantry Turkey Giveaway (November 22nd) 
            o Parking lot between Graham Tire and TMA 
     • DWU Women’s & Men’s Basketball vs. Midland (November 22nd) 
            o The World’s Only Corn Palace 
     • CASA’s Got Talent (November 22nd) 
            o Highland Conference Center 
     • Happy Thanksgiving! (November 27th) 
     • Small Business Saturday (November 29th) 
            o Mitchell, SD 
     • Christmas at the Palace (December 2nd) 
            o The World’s Only Corn Palace 
     • Parade of Lights (December 2nd) 
            o Mitchell Main Street 
     • Not a Silent Night (December 5th) 
            o Highland Conference Center 
     • Christmas Shopping for Kids (December 6th) 
            o Mitchell, SD 
     • A Laura Ingalls Wilder Christmas (December 5th-7th) 
            o Mitchell Area Community Theatre 
     • Palace City Brewing Co. 
     • James Valley Community Center 
     • Highland Conference Center 
     • MHS Performing Arts Center 

 
Complete list of events – MITCHELL CHAMBER EVENTS CALENDAR & Mitchell SD Events 
Facebook 
 
 *BOLD – Awarded Sports & Events Authority Grant funding. 
 
7. Share and Discuss Additional Grading Criteria and Funding Opportunities within the 
Funding Matrix with the Recommendation to be Effective January 13th, 2026 
 
Aaron shared and reviewed the agenda item request with the committee regarding the 
 upgrade of the SEA Funding Matrix. 
 
8. Executive Session in accordance with SDCL 9-34-19: Discussion of confidential trade 
secrets, commercial, or financial information. 
 
Motion: Bryan Dixon made a motion to go into Executive Session, and was seconded by Tim 
 Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
9. Approval of Funding Applications 
NAIA National Women's Volleyball Tournament Opening Round 
Date: November 20th-23rd, 2025; Contact: Jason Christensen; Grant Request: $6,000 

     • Mitchell, SD and The World's Only Corn Palace was not awarded the bid to host the        NAIA National Women's Volleyball Tournament Opening Round, so no action was 
       taken. 

 
South Dakota Fire Instructors Conference 
Date: January 10th-11th, 2026; Contact: Justin Adams; Grant Request: $4,800 

     • Motion: Motion was made by LaRee Rumbolz to award $4,800, and seconded by 
       Kevin Nelson. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
North Dakota Country Fest-Your Town Tour 
Date: April 11th, 2026; Contact: Luke Shafer; Grant Request: $5,000 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to award $5,000, and seconded by Bryan 
       Dixon. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
 
10. Next Meeting Date 
Kevin McCardle shared the next meeting date of Tuesday, December 9th, 2025, at 2 PM — 
 City Hall, Council Chambers. 
 
11. Adjournment 
 Meeting adjourned by: Kevin McCardle at 2:47 PM

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conventions, and sporting
events hosted in the Mitchell area are an important
aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist
event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Special Projects: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism in the City of Mitchell or to fund area events that
will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/meetings, sporting events, and other events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event/tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of the Mitchell area.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee. Applicants must provide all of
the information requested and be in compliance with all criteria.
Incomplete applications will not be considered.

10-14-25 SEA Meeting Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
October 14, 2025
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson,
Kevin Nelson, Jason Christensen, Dave Sietsema, Bryan Dixon, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily
Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Cory Aadland
Others present: Aaron Hieb and Stephanie Ellwein
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.
The following applications were presented and considered:
A. Pheasants Forever Banquet
Kevin Bruscher spoke on behalf of and presented the Pheasants Forever Banquet Grant
Application, which is requesting $2,500.
• Kevin shared some updates and progress that the Pheasant Country, Chapter 872 is
making with local game production areas within a 35-mile radius of Mitchell, SD. They
were also involved with the state trap shoot and hosted a youth pheasant hunt last
weekend. The money that is raised by Chapter 872 stays and is used locally, within a
35-mile radius of Mitchell, to improve habitat and invest in youth hunting activities and
experiences throughout the Mitchell community. The Pheasants Forever Banquet is
Friday, October 17th at The World's Only Corn Palace. Tickets available were
increased from 700 to 750. Estimated attendance is about 55% come from out of state.
B. Dakota Riptide: Tide Winter Invite Swim Meet & Sprint Invite Swim Meet
Rob Schelske spoke on behalf of and presented the Dakota Riptide: Tide Winter Invite Swim
Meet & Sprint Invite Swim Meet Grant Application, which is requesting $5,000.

--- PAGE 1 OF 6 ---


• Rob shared that the Dakota Riptide is hosting (2) winter meets, December 12th–14th,
2025, which usually brings 200+ swimmers and January 17th-18th, 2026, which will
bring 150+ swimmers. Dakota Riptide in Mitchell has around 80 members. Swimmers
come from Watertown, Sioux Falls, Brookings, Pierre, and Aberdeen.
C. Hoop City Classic 2025
Brad Bartscher spoke on behalf of and presented the Hoop City Classic 2025 Grant
Application, which is requesting $20,000.
• Brad shared that the Hoop City Classic is a 5-day event with the youth basketball
tournament taking place December 27th-28th, 2025, which should bring 60–70 teams,
and the high school games taking place December 29th-31st, 2025. The youth
basketball tournament will take place in the facilities at Dakota Wesleyan University
and there will be 19 high school games and 12 JV games taking place at The World's
Only Corn Palace arena and armory over the 3 days with teams coming from all over
SD and out-of-state teams coming from GA and FL.
D. Midwest Miracles Basketball Classic
Brad Bartscher spoke on behalf of and presented the Midwest Miracles Basketball
Classic Grant Application, which is requesting $5,000.
• Brad shared that the Midwest Miracles Classic is in its second year. The first year took
place in Hurley and was created by Kobee Sherman as a way to raise funds to help
cancer families pay for lodging, food, transportation, and other expenses during their
doctor visits and hospital stays. This will be an annual one-day event with girls' and
boys' games along with JV games taking place this year on January 3rd, 2026 at The
World's Only Corn Palace. Every other year the DWU Women's basketball team will
participate in the event by playing St. Mary's.
E. 2nd Annual Mitchell Pickleball Indoor Tournament
Kevin Doorn spoke on behalf of and presented the 2nd Annual Mitchell Pickleball Indoor
Tournament Grant Application, which is requesting $2,500.
• Kevin shared that the 2nd Annual Mitchell Pickleball Indoor Tournament will take place
January 2nd-4th, 2026 at the DWU/Avera Sports & Wellness Complex. This year the
event added a third day to the tournament in hopes of bringing more people to Mitchell.
They are estimating 80–140 players will participate in the 3-day tournament. The grant
request of $2,500 will be utilized in the prize fund to incentivize players to come to the
tournament.

--- PAGE 2 OF 6 ---


3. Approval of Minutes
Prior to the Approval of Minutes, JD Heinrich, American Outlaws Wrestling presented the
Mitchell Sports & Events Authority with the Sponsor of the Year Award. JD presented the
committee with a plaque and individual 'Thank You' cards and 'Thank you for Supporting'
poker chips to each member.
Motion: Motion was made by Bryan Dixon to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented, and seconded by Jason Christensen. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion
passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of October 2nd, 2025.
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2025 are $107,400.00.
Current Available Fund Balance of $87,240.00.
Collections in August (for July records) are $38,390.00 with 1 establishment past due.
Collections in September (for August records) are $36,884.00 with 1 establishment past due.
The YTD collections for 2025 are $233,411.00, which equates to 116,706 total room nights
sold.
YTD comparisons of room nights sold were: up 1.8% (2,148 room nights sold) from 2024, up
4.6% (5,322 room nights sold) from 2023, up 0.5% (612 room nights sold) from 2022, up 2.8%
from 2021, up 26.3% from 2020, and up 2.4% from 2019.
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the financial report as presented, and
seconded by Jim Johnston. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials and Thank You note with
the SEA Committee:
A. SEA Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s)
MAC Triathlon (June 7th, 2025)
• The event was Above (4) expectations. Help from the Rec Center with lifeguards and
pool assistance was super. The total spectator attendance was 100. The total
participants were 61; 14 teams, 8 series, and 39 regular. The estimated number of total
hotel room nights was 3–4, with some staying with family/friends, and others at
campgrounds. Next year's date is June 6th, 2026. The funds awarded ($1,500) were
used towards the timing system. Net profit of $6,255.32, which will be used towards the
outdoor fitness park around Cadwell.
Powderhorn Ranch Regulators Outlaw Gauntlet Shoots (June 12th-15th, 2025)

--- PAGE 3 OF 6 ---


• The event was Above (4) expectations. Contestants were very happy with the shoot
and the variety. The total spectator attendance was 150. The total participants were 70,
coming from Nevada, California, Texas, Idaho, Nebraska, Iowa, Wisconsin, Minnesota,
Missouri, Washington, Kansas, and cities within South Dakota. The estimated number
of total hotel room nights was 102 with 27 camping nights. Next year's date is June
10th-14th, 2026. The funds awarded ($3,000) were used as cash payouts for the
Mitchell SEA-sponsored shoot. Net profit of $2,324.00 which is used to maintain their
normal operating expenses.

documents.fileName: December 9, 2025, Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                   December 9, 2025 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Tim Smith at 2:00 PM 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Jill Larson, Kevin Nelson, Jason Christensen, 
Dave Sietsema, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Cory Aadland, 
and Bryan Dixon 
 
 Others present: Aaron Hieb, Johanna Allen, and Stephanie Ellwein 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants. 
 
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding. 
 
 The following applications were presented and considered: 
 
A. Palace Ice Festival 
Brian Bultje spoke on behalf of and presented the Palace Ice Festival Grant Application, which 
is requesting $750. 

     • Brian shared that the 10th Annual Palace Ice Festival will be held January 16-18, 2026, 
       at the Mitchell Activities Center. There will be skaters from Sioux Falls, Rapid City, 
       Mitchell, and the surrounding area. Judges will be flown in from California, Washington 
       State, Arizona, and will travel from parts of South Dakota as well. The grant request will 
       be utilized to offset their list of expenses. Their biggest expense is the judges. 

 
 
B. Hanson Classic's (Girls & Boys) 
Tyler Payer spoke on behalf of and presented the Hanson Classic's (Girls & Boys) Grant 
Application, which is requesting $5,000. 

     • Tyler shared that the Hanson Classic's will be held January 17 (Girls) and January 24 
       (Boys), 2026 at The World's Only Corn Palace. He also shared and passed around 
       some documents with program artwork and a list of schools participating in this year's        classic's. The grant request will be utilized to help cover the costs of the hospitality 
       room, which provides 2 meals for the coaches, officials, and tournament workers. Their 
       biggest expense is the officials, which also includes paying them mileage. 

 
 
C. (SDMEA) South Dakota Middle School All-State Jazz Band 
Joel Van Peursem spoke on behalf of and presented the (SDMEA) South Dakota Middle 
School All-State Jazz Band Grant Application, which is requesting $1,500. 

     • Joel shared that this is the 9th consecutive year that Mitchell has hosted this event. 
       The South Dakota Middle School All-State Jazz Band will be held January 30-31, 2026, 
       at the Mitchell Performing Arts Center. He estimates that there will be between 38–40 
       students along with directors and parents, accounting for between 250-350 total 
       attendance for the performance(s) on Saturday, January 31, 2026. Also, he estimates 
       that this event will generate between 90-100 hotel room nights. They have room blocks 
       at the Hampton Inn, Comfort Inn, and My Place Hotel. The grant request will be utilized 
       towards the cost of the clinicians, which (2) clinicians are brought in with estimated 
       costs of $750 each. 

 
 
D. Mitchell Show Choir Classic 
Jim Miskimins and Jen Bradley spoke on behalf of and presented the Mitchell Show Choir 
Classic Grant Application, which is requesting $3,500. 

     • They shared that a new date for the Mitchell Show Choir Classic has been established 
       and will be held February 20-21, 2026, at the Mitchell Performing Arts Center. 
       Currently, there are teams coming from Sioux Falls Jefferson, Sioux Falls Roosevelt, 
       Harrisburg, and Omaha. Their goal is to build this event back up to where they are 
       hosting between 8–10 teams from around the Midwest. This event brings between 
       600–800 kids along with 2,000 spectators for total attendance. They estimate that this 
       event will generate between 50–100 room nights. The grant request will be utilized and 
       put towards their almost $100,000 in annual expenses to produce the show and costs 
       of production. 

 
 
E. Palace City Baseball Association 
Jordan Widstrom and Adam Kaus spoke on behalf of and presented the Palace City Baseball 
Association Grant Application, which is requesting $15,000. 

     • They shared the Palace City Baseball Association, which will include teams: 13U, 14U, 
       16U, and 18U (Legion). Currently, Palace City Baseball has 65 players that will 
       participate in baseball. They will look to host (36) home, double-header baseball 
       games at Drake Field and Cadwell Park Stadium. Currently, Palace City Baseball and 
       Mitchell Baseball Association(s) have come to an agreement that Mitchell Baseball will 
       continue to host the Early Bird and Harve Johnston/Bryan Wilson Memorial 
       Tournament(s), along with the SD State Amateur Tournament. Palace City Baseball        will have the rights to host the SD State Youth Tournament, which Mitchell does not 
       host in 2026, but will host in 2027 and 2028, and every two out of three years going 
       forward. The grant request will be utilized to offset their list of expenses, which is 
       estimated at around $90,000. They will have approximately $30,000 in revenue with 
       player fees. 

 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Kevin Nelson to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
 presented, and seconded by Dave Sietsema. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of December 4, 2025. 
 
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2025 are $139,900.00 with (1) 
awarded item — South Dakota Fire Instructors Conference ($4,800) where the check be 
written and cut following the December 15 City Council meeting.  
 
Current Available Fund Balance of $49,940.00. 
  
Collections in October (for September records) are $32,008.00 with 1 establishment past due. 
 
Collections in November (for October records) are $33,708.00 with 1 establishment past due. 
  
The YTD collections for 2025 are $299,237.00, which equates to 149,619 total room nights 
sold. 
  
YTD comparisons of room nights sold were: up 1.2% (1,853 room nights sold) from 2024, up 
3.8% (5,753 room nights sold) from 2023, down 0.7% (1,083 room nights sold) from 2022, up 
2.5% from 2021, up 22.3% from 2020, and up 1.7% from 2019. 
 
Motion: Motion was made by Jim Johnston to approve the financial report as presented, and 
 seconded by Dave Helleloid. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials with the SEA Committee: 
 
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s) 
Arts in the Park (July 26-27, 2025) 

     • The event Met (3) expectations. SEA always does a great job! Thanks for the help! The 
       total spectator attendance was 7,000+. The total participants were 133 vendors, 
       including food trucks; SD, ND, IA, MN, WY, NE. The estimated number of total hotel 
       room nights was 60. Next year's date: Hitchcock Park July 24-25, 2026. The funds 
       awarded ($1,500) were used towards the park closure and shelter rental fees. Net 
       profit of $378, which will be used towards next year's event.  
Cornicupia (September 13-14, 2025) 

     • The event Met (3) expectations. The Mitchell Soccer Association ran another 
       successful tournament with 52 teams, up from 41 teams in 2024. The total spectator 
       attendance was estimated at around 1,250. The total participants were 625 (52 teams); 
       Rapid City, Pierre, Aberdeen, Tea, Brookings, Watertown, Yankton, Sioux Falls, 
       Brandon, Mitchell. The estimated number of total hotel room nights was 350; 
       AmericInn, Comfort Inn, Days Inn, Hampton Inn, Holiday Inn, Kelly Inn, My Place, 
       Super 8. Next year's date: Pepsi Soccer Complex September 12–13, 2026. The funds 
       awarded ($5,000) were used to offset tournament expenses such as their biggest 
       expenses, referee costs. Net profit of $18,403.86, which will be used towards 
       equipment and coaches pay for their programs. 

 
 
6. Other Items 
 Aaron Hieb shared and reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee: 
 
A. Update and Review of Playeasy 

     • No events have been secured yet. 
     • (2) active leads having conversations and gathering information to possibly pursue. 
            o American Junior Golf Association (AJGA) Junior Championship 
            o LR Productions Gymnastic Competitions 2027/2028 RFP 
     • Continue to reach out to local businesses and gauge their interest in utilizing the 
       Playeasy Community Collaboration feature, which sends an email inviting the store 
       owner/manager to create an account to have ADMIN access to their local business 
       profile micro-site. Once they have ADMIN access, they will be able to manage only

       coupons to SEA-funded organizations that they will share with those participating local 
       businesses to receive their promotion. 
            o Aaron invited any businesses within Mitchell, SD that have an interest in

The many festivals, conventions, and sporting

aspect of the region’s tourism industry. The
Mitchell SEA grant program is designed to assist

advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:

Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.

will have a significant impact on a business located in the City of Mitchell, specifically
generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotel or other lodging options,
including campgrounds, in the Mitchell area.
Preference will be given to:

First-Time Event(s); (36) Home, double-header baseball games (13U-18U) with most games being played at Drake Field.
In most cases, fans would not stay in a hotel for a home, double-header.
Zero hotel room nights estimated during event(s).
Event(s) held during MAY, JUNE, & JULY.
Also, going forward, Mitchell will be granted the right to host half of the SD State Youth (9U-12U) baseball tournament in Mitchell two out of every three years, with Watertown and Brandon Valley being the other
sites in that annual rotation. In 2026, that event will be held in Watertown and Brandon Valley, but should be in Mitchell in 2027 and 2028.
Up to 250 hotel room nights during state youth in JULY X $10 per room night = $2,500
$2,500 X 10% (Event hosted on WEEKEND in JULY) = $250
NEW EVENT & NEW ORGANIZATION!
New organization with no prior assets.
$2,500 X 10% (NEW EVENT) = $250.
$2,500 + $250 + $250 = $3,000
SEA Grant Application states that 25-35% of average attendance should come from outside 50+ mile radius.
We are bringing in families from other SD Class A cities including Aberdeen, Watertown, Brookings, Brandon Valley, Tea, Pierre, Yankton, Renner, Sioux Falls, and possibly some from bordering states.
The grant request would be used to cover umpire, city field and concession use costs, and other expenses required to hold home games at Drake Field and Cadwell Park.
We will sell concessions and charge a small gate fee for fans to attend our home games. Any profits collected will be used towards the many other season expenses, especially concession goods and coaching wages.

City of Mitchell | Mitchell Sports & Events Authority
612 North Main Street | Mitchell, SD 57301

SEA FUNDING MATRIX Upgrade Recommendation
Meeting Date Requested: December 9th , 2025
Requested By: Aaron Hieb
Desired Action: Authorization & Approval
One common theme or takeaway from committee meetings, and in discussions with
organizations/events that were awarded funding throughout 2025.
• 	The amount of funding available in 2025 for the Sports & Events Authority Grant.
This prompted me to re-evaluate and consider some updates, and ultimately, revamp/upgrade the
funding matrix for (2) specific reasons.
1. 	Give organizations/events more opportunities to be awarded extra funding to potentially
increase marketing efforts, expand event resources, increase participation and attendance, and
etc. for their event(s).
2. 	Gives the SEA Advisory Committee and myself an opportunity for a deeper evaluation of the
grant application and event itself, and to consider and highlight the variety of ways the event
delivers an economic impact within Mitchell, SD.
a. 	It allows for more conversations and more questions regarding the event, not just the
leadoff and potentially the only question asked… “How many hotel room nights does
the event provide…”
Event Necessity/Month
• 	The priority month(s) have been updated to be relevant to the BID #4 Board and local hoteliers’
feedback from the survey, and to also mirror and reflect the total, monthly BID #4 collections
throughout the last two years.
Room Nights Sold X Common Denominator = Base Funding Amount(s)
• 	The organization selects a “number of hotel room nights” estimation on the grant application
OR we use the estimation amount provided on the previous year post-event Evaluation Form,
whichever number is greater.
• 	Multiply by $10/per room night sold
o 	This was the number ($10) agreed upon when Jeff Smith and I put this matrix together. It
can be increased to meet the economic times… with the committee’s recommendation.

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
January 13, 2026
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson,
Kevin Nelson, Cory Aadland, Jason Christensen, Dave Sietsema, Bryan Dixon, LaRee
Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: None
Others present: Aaron Hieb and Stephanie Ellwein
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.
The following applications were presented and considered:
A. Dakota Oyate Challenge
Silas Blaine, via conference phone, spoke on behalf of and presented the Dakota Oyate
Challenge Grant Application, which is requesting $10,500 plus (11) comp hotel rooms for 44
room nights for officials.
• Silas shared that the 37th Annual Boys' & 32nd Girls' Dakota Oyate Challenge will be
held February 5–7, 2026, at The World's Only Corn Palace. There will (8) boys teams
and (8) girls teams playing bracket play for three days. Each team utilizes 20–25 hotel
rooms for (3) nights. Along with the basketball tournament, the event offers Hand
Games, Archery, and NEW this year, Dakota Language Contest. The grant request will
be utilized to offset their list of expenses. Currently, each school pays a $2,000 entry
fee to participate, which is quite high, so they are looking to lower that expense for
each school.
B. DWU/Culver's Girls' & Boys' High School Basketball Classic
Jason Christensen spoke on behalf of and presented the DWU/Culver's Girls & Boys High
School Basketball Classic Grant Application, which is requesting $5,000.

--- PAGE 1 OF 7 ---


• Jason shared that the 17th Annual Boys' & 13th Annual Girls' DWU/Culver's Classic
will be held February 13–14, 2026, at The World's Only Corn Palace. There will be (9)
games each day for a total of 18 games for the classic. The grant request will be
utilized to offset their list of expenses and pay their table workers and officials more as
well. Any profits/proceeds from the classic goes back into the DWU Men's & Women's
Basketball programs to provide scholarships.
C. South Dakota Girls Varsity Hockey State Tournament
Tyler Graham and Kira Tronnes spoke on behalf of and presented the South Dakota Girls
Varsity Hockey State Tournament Grant Application, which is requesting $5,000.
• Tyler shared that Mitchell will be hosting the South Dakota Girls Varsity Hockey State
Tournament on March 5–7, 2026, at the Mitchell Activities Center. There will be (8)
teams, roughly 170 players, from South Dakota competing in the state tournament —
Brookings, Sioux Falls, Pierre, Watertown, Rapid City, Sioux Center, Mitchell, and
Aberdeen. Teams will be here for (3) nights with games starting at Noon on Thursday,
March 5. The grant request will be utilized to rent a replay screen to be set up in the
Mitchell Activities Center for the tournament. Any profits and proceeds will go back into
the Mitchell Skating & Hockey Association.
D. South Dakota Middle School All-State Band
Tessa Belgum, via conference phone, spoke on behalf of and presented the South Dakota
Middle School All-State Band Grant Application, which is requesting $1,000.
• Tessa shared that the SD Middle School All-State Band will be held March 6–7, 2026,
at the Mitchell Performing Arts Center. There will be 200 registered students from
around the state, which accounts for 71 schools being represented. The grant request
will be utilized towards the hospitality room for the band director's, along with items to
go in each student's swag bag. They make multiple local purchases at Walmart and
County Fair, and many families eat at local restaurants and visit local shops.

Troy Bollock spoke on behalf of and presented the PowderHorn Ranch Regulators Outlaw
Gauntlet Shoot Grant Application, which is requesting $5,000.
• Troy shared that the 23rd Annual PowderHorn Ranch Regulators shoot will be held
June 10-14, 2026, at the Mitchell Gun Club. This year they are estimating 85–95
shooters, with over 90% traveling from more than 100+ miles from Mitchell. The grant
request ($5,000), $3,000 will be used as cash prizes for the Blast for Cash-Mitchell
Sports & Events Authority sponsored shoot and $2,000 will go towards updating and
repairing equipment.

Convention Grant Application, which is requesting $3,200.

2026, at the Highland Conference Center. There will be veterans traveling from all over
South Dakota with approximately 94% of the attendance coming from 100+ miles from
Mitchell. This event usually generates 50–100 room nights along with over 275
attendees during the annual banquet on Saturday night. Mitchell SEA has supported
and awarded the event $3,130 in 2022 and 2023. The grant request will be utilized for
facility and hotel costs at the Highland Conference Center.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45

The many festivals, conferences, conventions,
concerts, and sporting events hosted in Mitchell,
SD are an important aspect of the region’s sports
tourism industry.
The Mitchell SEA grant program is available to assist organizations in hosting events that
will promote a positive image to potential visitors, generate overnight visits, extend visitor
stays, and create a desire to return to the area.
The grant program is designed to assist event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Concerts/Special Events: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism and visitor spending in Mitchell, SD, or to fund area
events that will have a significant economic impact on businesses located in Mitchell,
specifically, by generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotels or the
Lake Mitchell Campground.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/conferences, sporting events, concerts, and other special
events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event and tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of Mitchell, SD.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conferences, conventions,
concerts, and sporting events hosted in Mitchell,
SD are an important aspect of the region’s sports
tourism industry.
The Mitchell SEA grant program is available to assist organizations in hosting events that
will promote a positive image to potential visitors, generate overnight visits, extend visitor
stays, and create a desire to return to the area.
The grant program is designed to assist event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Concerts/Special Events: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism and visitor spending in Mitchell, SD, or to fund area
events that will have a significant economic impact on businesses located in Mitchell,
specifically, by generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotels or the
Lake Mitchell Campground.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/conferences, sporting events, concerts, and other special
events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event and tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of Mitchell, SD.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee.

The Mitchell Skating and Hockey Association is dedicated to
providing accessible, high-quality hockey programs for youth in
our community. Through structured athletic development and
competitive training, we promote sportsmanship, respect,
integrity, discipline, teamwork, and a strong work ethic. Our
programs are designed to support the holistic development of
student-athletes by fostering academic responsibility, personal
growth, and leadership skills. By offering a safe, inclusive, and
challenging environment, we strive to positively impact the lives
of young athletes and inspire a lifelong commitment to physical
activity and the sport of hockey.

Briefly describe the
purpose of your
organization; what your
organization provides
to the community; the
group of people you
are targeting to bring
Mitchell Hockey has not had the opportunity to host a Varsity
level hockey tournament for several years. This event represents
a rare opportunity to serve as a regional hub for youth athletics,
community pride, and positive economic activity. The tournament
will attract student-athletes, families, coaches, officials, and
spectators from across the state, resulting in increased use of
local hotels, restaurants, retail businesses, and community
facilities. Beyond the immediate economic impact, the event

--- PAGE 4 OF 7 ---


into the community with
this event? elevates the community’s profile as a destination capable of
hosting high-quality, statewide athletic events. We want to show
SDAHA that Mitchell is willing and able to utilize our facility and
that we have community support to bring varsity level hockey
tournaments, as well as other youth tournaments (which we also
do annually) to Mitchell and have them be successful.
The primary group targeted by this event is female student-
athletes at the varsity level, with a broader focus on youth and
families throughout the region. By highlighting girls’ athletics at a
state-championship level, the tournament promotes gender
equity in sports and reinforces the importance of providing
competitive, high-visibility opportunities for young women.
Secondary audiences include local students, youth hockey
participants, families, educators, and community members who
benefit from increased access to high-level athletic competition
and positive youth development experiences.
Describe your event.
Be sure to include who,
what, where, when,
and how activities will
take place.
Games begin Thursday 3/5 at 12:00 noon - there are four games
played on Thursday. Friday morning at 9am is the opening
ceremonies for the Tournament that we have planned to take
place at the Corn Palace. All teams are invited to this as well as
open to the community. At the opening ceremonies we have a
motivational speaker planned, state awards are handed out and
All-state teams are announced. Friday games start at 12:00 pm.
Saturday games are the trophy games and there are 3 games on
Saturday, starting at 1:00pm.
What % of attendance
will be visitor draw
outside of 100+ miles
of Mitchell, SD?
Approximately 80% will be outside the 100 miles of Mitchell.
What geographic areas
are you bringing event
participants from?
Indicate geographic
areas you are
marketing for visitor
attraction to your event.
There are 8 towns participating in the Girls Varsity tournament
this year: Brookings, Sioux Falls, Pierre, Watertown, Rapid City,
Aberdeen Sioux Center and Mitchell. I anticipate that only Sioux
Falls and possibly Brookings would have people drive back and
forth for the event, the rest of the towns would be staying
overnight. We market the event to all of these associations for
support of their local teams.
What are the specific
goals for this event?
We want to show SDAHA that Mitchell is willing and able to
utilize our facility and that we have community support to bring
varsity level hockey tournaments, as well as other youth
tournaments (which we also do annually) to Mitchell and have
them be successful. We want to showcase our two ice sheet
facility as a host site option for more state and district sponsored
development events.
We also want to provide our local association with a great event

--- PAGE 5 OF 7 ---


that is enjoyable for all and is a great recruitment tool for more
female and male athletes to join into the sport of hockey. We
want to give back to the businesses that provides support for us
to keep our association going each year by having a successful
event.
Explain how your grant
request would be used
to promote tourism in
Mitchell? Note the
resulting impact of your
event if the request for
funding were denied.
We are hosting the opening ceremonies at the Corn Palace, they
have graciously offered us a discounted fee, but we still have a
fee that we need to pay. We will use the grant funds to add into
our program that goes to each family the tourism information
from the Chamber. Each team only plays 1 game per day they
are here, so there is a lot of time that families will be able to
explore Mitchell. We will use grant money to make advertising for
around the rink, we can provide additional information to hotels
as well.
Mitchell Skating and Hockey is a non-profit entity, so without SEA
grant funding, the amount of available funds for additional things
like advertising and such is strictly limited as the small amount of
funds we have will have to ne used for facility fees, referee fees
and rental costs first.

documents.fileName: 12-9-25 SEA Meeting Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
December 9, 2025
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Tim Smith at 2:00 PM
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Jill Larson, Kevin Nelson, Jason Christensen,
Dave Sietsema, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, and Jim Johnston
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Cory Aadland,
and Bryan Dixon
Others present: Aaron Hieb, Johanna Allen, and Stephanie Ellwein
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.
The following applications were presented and considered:
A. Palace Ice Festival
Brian Bultje spoke on behalf of and presented the Palace Ice Festival Grant Application, which
is requesting $750.
• Brian shared that the 10th Annual Palace Ice Festival will be held January 16-18, 2026,
at the Mitchell Activities Center. There will be skaters from Sioux Falls, Rapid City,
Mitchell, and the surrounding area. Judges will be flown in from California, Washington
State, Arizona, and will travel from parts of South Dakota as well. The grant request will
be utilized to offset their list of expenses. Their biggest expense is the judges.
B. Hanson Classic's (Girls & Boys)
Tyler Payer spoke on behalf of and presented the Hanson Classic's (Girls & Boys) Grant
Application, which is requesting $5,000.
• Tyler shared that the Hanson Classic's will be held January 17 (Girls) and January 24
(Boys), 2026 at The World's Only Corn Palace. He also shared and passed around
some documents with program artwork and a list of schools participating in this year's

--- PAGE 1 OF 7 ---


classic's. The grant request will be utilized to help cover the costs of the hospitality
room, which provides 2 meals for the coaches, officials, and tournament workers. Their
biggest expense is the officials, which also includes paying them mileage.
C. (SDMEA) South Dakota Middle School All-State Jazz Band
Joel Van Peursem spoke on behalf of and presented the (SDMEA) South Dakota Middle
School All-State Jazz Band Grant Application, which is requesting $1,500.
• Joel shared that this is the 9th consecutive year that Mitchell has hosted this event.
The South Dakota Middle School All-State Jazz Band will be held January 30-31, 2026,
at the Mitchell Performing Arts Center. He estimates that there will be between 38–40
students along with directors and parents, accounting for between 250-350 total
attendance for the performance(s) on Saturday, January 31, 2026. Also, he estimates
that this event will generate between 90-100 hotel room nights. They have room blocks
at the Hampton Inn, Comfort Inn, and My Place Hotel. The grant request will be utilized
towards the cost of the clinicians, which (2) clinicians are brought in with estimated
costs of $750 each.
D. Mitchell Show Choir Classic
Jim Miskimins and Jen Bradley spoke on behalf of and presented the Mitchell Show Choir
Classic Grant Application, which is requesting $3,500.
• They shared that a new date for the Mitchell Show Choir Classic has been established
and will be held February 20-21, 2026, at the Mitchell Performing Arts Center.
Currently, there are teams coming from Sioux Falls Jefferson, Sioux Falls Roosevelt,
Harrisburg, and Omaha. Their goal is to build this event back up to where they are
hosting between 8–10 teams from around the Midwest. This event brings between
600–800 kids along with 2,000 spectators for total attendance. They estimate that this
event will generate between 50–100 room nights. The grant request will be utilized and
put towards their almost $100,000 in annual expenses to produce the show and costs
of production.
E. Palace City Baseball Association
Jordan Widstrom and Adam Kaus spoke on behalf of and presented the Palace City Baseball
Association Grant Application, which is requesting $15,000.
• They shared the Palace City Baseball Association, which will include teams: 13U, 14U,
16U, and 18U (Legion). Currently, Palace City Baseball has 65 players that will
participate in baseball. They will look to host (36) home, double-header baseball
games at Drake Field and Cadwell Park Stadium. Currently, Palace City Baseball and
Mitchell Baseball Association(s) have come to an agreement that Mitchell Baseball will
continue to host the Early Bird and Harve Johnston/Bryan Wilson Memorial
Tournament(s), along with the SD State Amateur Tournament. Palace City Baseball

--- PAGE 2 OF 7 ---


will have the rights to host the SD State Youth Tournament, which Mitchell does not
host in 2026, but will host in 2027 and 2028, and every two out of three years going
forward. The grant request will be utilized to offset their list of expenses, which is
estimated at around $90,000. They will have approximately $30,000 in revenue with
player fees.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Kevin Nelson to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented, and seconded by Dave Sietsema. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of December 4, 2025.
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2025 are $139,900.00 with (1)
awarded item — South Dakota Fire Instructors Conference ($4,800) where the check be
written and cut following the December 15 City Council meeting.
Current Available Fund Balance of $49,940.00.
Collections in October (for September records) are $32,008.00 with 1 establishment past due.
Collections in November (for October records) are $33,708.00 with 1 establishment past due.
The YTD collections for 2025 are $299,237.00, which equates to 149,619 total room nights
sold.
YTD comparisons of room nights sold were: up 1.2% (1,853 room nights sold) from 2024, up
3.8% (5,753 room nights sold) from 2023, down 0.7% (1,083 room nights sold) from 2022, up
2.5% from 2021, up 22.3% from 2020, and up 1.7% from 2019.
Motion: Motion was made by Jim Johnston to approve the financial report as presented, and
seconded by Dave Helleloid. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form(s) w/Financials with the SEA Committee:
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s)
Arts in the Park (July 26-27, 2025)
• The event Met (3) expectations. SEA always does a great job! Thanks for the help! The
total spectator attendance was 7,000+. The total participants were 133 vendors,
including food trucks; SD, ND, IA, MN, WY, NE. The estimated number of total hotel
room nights was 60. Next year's date: Hitchcock Park July 24-25, 2026. The funds
awarded ($1,500) were used towards the park closure and shelter rental fees. Net
profit of $378, which will be used towards next year's event.

--- PAGE 3 OF 7 ---


Cornicupia (September 13-14, 2025)
• The event Met (3) expectations. The Mitchell Soccer Association ran another
successful tournament with 52 teams, up from 41 teams in 2024. The total spectator
attendance was estimated at around 1,250. The total participants were 625 (52 teams);
Rapid City, Pierre, Aberdeen, Tea, Brookings, Watertown, Yankton, Sioux Falls,
Brandon, Mitchell. The estimated number of total hotel room nights was 350;
AmericInn, Comfort Inn, Days Inn, Hampton Inn, Holiday Inn, Kelly Inn, My Place,
Super 8. Next year's date: Pepsi Soccer Complex September 12–13, 2026. The funds
awarded ($5,000) were used to offset tournament expenses such as their biggest
expenses, referee costs. Net profit of $18,403.86, which will be used towards
equipment and coaches pay for their programs.
6. Other Items
Aaron Hieb shared and reviewed the following items with the SEA Committee:
A. Update and Review of Playeasy
• No events have been secured yet.
• (2) active leads having conversations and gathering information to possibly pursue.
o American Junior Golf Association (AJGA) Junior Championship
o LR Productions Gymnastic Competitions 2027/2028 RFP
• Continue to reach out to local businesses and gauge their interest in utilizing the
Playeasy Community Collaboration feature, which sends an email inviting the store
owner/manager to create an account to have ADMIN access to their local business
profile micro-site. Once they have ADMIN access, they will be able to manage only
their local business profile and create SEA event-specific promotions or general
promotion campaigns that are available for those events that are awarded SEA
funding. Once these promotions are created, Aaron will distribute "Ear of Corn"
coupons to SEA-funded organizations that they will share with those participating local
businesses to receive their promotion.
o Aaron invited any businesses within Mitchell, SD that have an interest in
learning more and/or participating in this feature to reach out to Aaron Hieb
(605-990-7942; Aaron.Hieb@cityofmitchellsd.gov)
B. Upcoming Events

Motion: Kevin Nelson made a motion to approve the SEA Funding Matrix Upgrade effective
January 1, 2026, and was seconded by Dave Helleloid. All members voted 'Aye' and the
motion passed.

--- PAGE 5 OF 7 ---

secrets, commercial, or financial information.
Motion: Dave Sietsema made a motion to go into Executive Session, and was seconded by

February 11, 2026, Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
February 11, 2026
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Kevin Nelson, Cory Aadland,
Jason Christensen (via phone), Dave Sietsema, LaRee Rumbolz, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith,
Jim Johnston, and Scott Morgan
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Mayor Hanson, Jill Larson, and Emily Liedtke
Others present: Aaron Hieb and Stephanie Ellwein
2. Scott Morgan to the Sports & Events Authority Committee for a term to run from
February 2026-June 2028
Scott Morgan introduced as a newly appointed committee member.
3. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.
The following applications were presented and considered:
A. SDHSAA State Gymnastics Meet
Cory Aadland spoke on behalf of and presented the SDHSAA State Gymnastics Meet Grant
Application, which is requesting $7,500.
• Cory shared that the SDHSAA State Gymnastics Meet will take place on February 13-
14, 2026 at Mitchell High School. Cory provided the committee with a list of Class A
and Class AA schools that will be competing in the team competition on Friday,
February 13. He also reviewed the schedule of events for both days. The grant request
of $7,500 will mainly go towards paying the staff and hospitality room for the workers
and judges.
B. 16th Annual DWU Futsal Classic Indoor Tournament

--- PAGE 1 OF 7 ---


Nicolas Reinhard spoke on behalf of and presented the 16th Annual DWU Futsal Classic
Indoor Tournament Grant Application, which is requesting $2,700.
• Nicolas shared some contributing factors with the committee regarding the difficulty
recruiting teams for futsal in South Dakota compared to the middle 2010s. The DWU
Futsal Classic Indoor Tournament will take place on February 20-22, 2026, at the
DWU/Avera Sports & Wellness Complex as well as at the Christen Family Center on
DWU campus. Currently, the event has 60 teams registered. The grant request of
$2,700 will go towards referee expenses.
C. South Dakota Swimming 13 & Over State Championships
Jason Wede and Rob Schelske spoke on behalf of and presented the South Dakota
Swimming 13 & Over State Championships Grant Application, which is requesting $5,000.
• Jason and Rob shared that the event will be 4 days and take place from February 26–
28, March 1, 2026, at the Mitchell Recreation & Indoor Aquatic Center. This event will
bring approximately 250-300+ youth swimmers to Mitchell, SD. The Dakota Riptide will
sell a program and run concessions as means of revenue from the event. The grant
request of $5,000 will go towards expenses incurred from hosting the meet such as
pool rental and lifeguard wages.
D. MARCH CLASSIC Gymnastics Invitational
Removed from the agenda due to uncontrollable circumstances, the event will not take place
in 2026.
E. 5th Annual Comedy Night presented by CVMA 30-2
Justin Hamer spoke on behalf of and presented the 5th Annual Comedy Night presented by
CVMA 30-2 Grant Application, which is requesting $1,500.
• Justin shared that the 5th Annual Comedy Night presented by the Combat Veterans
Motorcycle Association Chapter 30-2 will take place on March 21, 2026, at the Masonic
Lodge. Last year's (2025) attendance was 150. He also shared the event flyer along
with the entertainment for this year. The grant request of $1,500 will go towards the hall
rental and advertisement for the event.
F. Knights of Columbus Special Olympics State Basketball Banquet
Dan Froning spoke on behalf of and presented the Knights of Columbus Special Olympics
State Basketball Banquet Grant Application, which is requesting $1,200.
• Dan shared that the Knights of Columbus Special Olympics State Basketball
Tournament Banquet will take place on March 28, 2026, in the John Paul II School
Auditorium and Multi-purpose room. This has been the fifth time since 2017 that the

--- PAGE 2 OF 7 ---


Knights of Columbus have hosted this banquet. They will serve a spaghetti dinner with
bread sticks, refreshments, and a Dilly Bar to approximately 750 athletes. There will
also be a dance to follow the dinner. The grant request of $1,200 will go towards costs
for food, condiments, and cleaning.
G. Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament
Stacy Murtha spoke on behalf of and presented the Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament
Grant Application, which is requesting $4,000.
• Stacy shared that the 15th Annual Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament will take
place April 10-12, 2026, in the Mitchell Activities Center, utilizing both sheets of ice.
The tournament will host up to 26 adult teams. Stacy shared where the teams and
players come from along with the other activities that they will participate in while in
Mitchell, SD. The grant request of $4,000 will go towards ice rental costs.
H. DWU Spring Golf Invitational
Jeff Meyerink spoke on behalf of and presented the DWU Spring Golf Invitational Grant
Application, which is requesting $4,000.
• Jeff shared a different format than the last couple of years for the invite. The DWU
Spring Golf Invitational will take place on April 12-13, 2026, with practice rounds taking
place on April 11. There will be a 36-hole format on Sunday and a final 18-holes on
Monday. Currently, there are approximately 80 golfers registered with a max field of 96.
The grant request of $4,000 will go towards a variety of items to provide the players
and coaches with a top-notch experience at Lakeview Golf Course.
I. Sioux Area 4-H Rodeo
Kelly Dunkelberger spoke on behalf of and presented the Sioux Area 4-H Rodeo Grant
Application, which is requesting $10,000.
• Kelly shared that the Sioux Area 4-H Rodeo is in its sixth year and is transitioning from
Sioux Falls to Mitchell (Horseman's Sports Arena) on June 27-28, 2026. The event will
bring approximately 200–250 (ages 8-18) along with 50 volunteers to Mitchell, SD. The
grant request of $10,000 will go towards stock for the event plus a variety of items to
keep the costs for the participants minimal.
J. South Dakota Chess Open
Jim Perry spoke on behalf of and presented the South Dakota Chess Open Grant Application,
which is requesting $4,175.

--- PAGE 3 OF 7 ---


• Jim shared that the South Dakota Chess Open will take place at the Masonic Lodge on
August 8-9, 2026. He is uncertain on the number of participants the event will draw, but
that state events around South Dakota usually draw between 50-60 players. The grant
request of $4,175 will go towards the costs of bringing Carissa Yip, (4-time U.S
Women's Chess Champion and International Chess Master) to the event.
4. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by LaRee Rumbolz to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented, and seconded by Tim Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of February 5, 2026.
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2026 are $39,200.
Current Available Fund Balance of $110,800.00.
Collections in December (for November records) are $26,494.00 with all collected. The total
collections for 2025 are $325,841.00, which accounts for 162,921 rooms nights.
Collections in January 2026 (for December 2025 records) are $16,591.00.
The YTD collections for 2026 are $16,591.00, which equates to 8,296 total room nights sold.
YTD comparisons of room nights sold were: down 7.6% (630 room nights sold) from 2025,
down 16.4% (1,363 room nights sold) from 2024, up 1.5% (127 room nights sold) from 2023,
down 9.0% from 2022, up 17.7% from 2021, and down 29.7% from 2020.
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Sietsema to approve the financial report as presented, and
seconded by Jim Johnston. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
6. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys

($2,500) were used towards prize money, and to purchase balls and supplies. Net
profit of $2,916.60, which will go towards promoting pickleball in Mitchell and to keep
supplies and equipment in good condition.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conferences, conventions,
concerts, and sporting events hosted in Mitchell,
SD are an important aspect of the region’s sports
tourism industry.
The Mitchell SEA grant program is available to assist organizations in hosting events that
will promote a positive image to potential visitors, generate overnight visits, extend visitor
stays, and create a desire to return to the area.
The grant program is designed to assist event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Concerts/Special Events: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism and visitor spending in Mitchell, SD, or to fund area
events that will have a significant economic impact on businesses located in Mitchell,
specifically, by generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotels or the
Lake Mitchell Campground.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/conferences, sporting events, concerts, and other special
events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event and tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of Mitchell, SD.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee.

The many festivals, conferences, conventions,
concerts, and sporting events hosted in Mitchell,
SD are an important aspect of the region’s sports
tourism industry.
The Mitchell SEA grant program is available to assist organizations in hosting events that
will promote a positive image to potential visitors, generate overnight visits, extend visitor
stays, and create a desire to return to the area.
The grant program is designed to assist event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Concerts/Special Events: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism and visitor spending in Mitchell, SD, or to fund area
events that will have a significant economic impact on businesses located in Mitchell,
specifically, by generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotels or the
Lake Mitchell Campground.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/conferences, sporting events, concerts, and other special
events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event and tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of Mitchell, SD.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee.

The state meet takes place on Thursday, February 26 - Sunday, March 1, 2026, at the Mitchell Recreation Center & Indoor Aquatic Center.
The purpose of the Dakota Riptide is to provide area kids with a place to learn the different swim strokes and complete competitively if they desire.

Purpose of

The purpose of the Sioux Area Rodeo Club is to host and
support a 4-H youth rodeo that provides South Dakota 4-H
members the opportunity to participate in the sport of rodeo. Our
rodeo is open to any South Dakota 4-H rodeo participant and
offers four youth divisions, allowing young competitors of all ages
and experience levels to take part. Rodeo is the official state
sport of South Dakota, and the State 4-H program strongly
believes in giving youth the opportunity to learn, grow, and
compete through rodeo. As one of only two states to offer 4-H
rodeo, South Dakota provides a unique and valuable starting
point for youth interested in the sport. The Sioux Area Rodeo
Club has hosted a 4-H youth rodeo at the W.H. Lyons
Fairgrounds in Sioux Falls for the past five years. Due to
circumstances beyond our control, we were required to find a
new location for our event. The HSI Arena in Mitchell has worked
closely with our club to provide an excellent facility that will allow
the rodeo to continue and serve youth from across the South
Dakota 4-H rodeo program.

The Sioux Area Rodeo Club is dedicated to providing a safe,
well-organized 4-H youth rodeo that supports positive youth
development through rodeo. This event specifically targets South
Dakota 4-H rodeo participants ages 8–18 and their families from
across the state, with many traveling from eastern South Dakota
to attend. Because the rodeo spans multiple days, our
participants, spectators, and families rely heavily on local hotels,
restaurants, gas stations, and entertainment options during their
stay. This creates a meaningful economic impact while also
bringing youth, families, and agricultural supporters into the

The Sioux Area 4-H Rodeo is a two-day youth rodeo event that
brings together South Dakota 4-H members ages 8–18 and their
families from across the state. Hosted by the Sioux Area Rodeo
Club, the rodeo will be held June 27–28, 2026, at the HSI Arena
in Mitchell, South Dakota. The event features a full schedule of
traditional 4-H rodeo competitions, including barrel racing, pole
bending, breakaway roping, goat tying, team roping, bull riding,
and more. Competition takes place throughout both days and is
conducted by experienced judges, volunteers, and arena staff to
ensure a smooth and well-organized rodeo. Spectators, including
parents, grandparents, and community members, are invited to
attend and enjoy full days of youth rodeo competition. The
purpose of the event is to provide a high-quality 4-H rodeo that
brings participants and visitors to Mitchell, showcases South
Dakota 4-H rodeo, and supports community engagement through
attendance and tourism.

participants from eastern South Dakota, while also welcoming
youth from across the entire state. On this particular weekend,
there are usually only three South Dakota 4-H rodeos available
for the SD 4-H rodeo members to choose from. We take pride in
hosting a high-quality, well-run rodeo that consistently attracts

reputation encourages youth and families to travel to our event,
making it a preferred choice among 4-H rodeo participants
statewide.
What are the specific
goals for this event?
The Sioux Area Rodeo Club’s goals are to develop strong, well-
rounded young agriculturalists who are passionate about rodeo,
horses, 4-H, and agriculture. Through participation in rodeo,
members learn responsibility, sportsmanship, respect, and good
behavior while building confidence and life skills that extend
beyond the arena. The club also strives to reward hard work and
dedication by offering high-quality prizes that participants can
earn through their efforts and commitment in competition. In
addition, the rodeo is designed to provide parents, grandparents,
and spectators with a fun and memorable experience as they
watch South Dakota 4-H youth compete and grow. Whether
participants place or not, our goal is for every youth to leave the
event feeling successful, encouraged, and proud of the progress
they have made in their rodeo events and activities.

The Sioux Area Rodeo Club’s youth rodeo is a strong driver of
tourism in the Mitchell area, bringing participants and their
families into the community from across South Dakota. Rodeo
participants travel from as far away as Aberdeen, along with
families from communities closer to Mitchell who may not
otherwise spend a full weekend in town. By attending this multi-
day event, visitors stay in local hotels, dine at area restaurants,
purchase fuel, and enjoy entertainment and attractions
throughout Mitchell. This influx of visitors helps promote the
community as a weekend destination while generating increased
exposure and economic activity for local businesses.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conferences, conventions,
concerts, and sporting events hosted in Mitchell,
SD are an important aspect of the region’s sports
tourism industry.
The Mitchell SEA grant program is available to assist organizations in hosting events that
will promote a positive image to potential visitors, generate overnight visits, extend visitor
stays, and create a desire to return to the area.
The grant program is designed to assist event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Concerts/Special Events: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism and visitor spending in Mitchell, SD, or to fund area
events that will have a significant economic impact on businesses located in Mitchell,
specifically, by generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotels or the
Lake Mitchell Campground.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/conferences, sporting events, concerts, and other special
events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event and tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of Mitchell, SD.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee.

education in South Dakota.

(South Dakota Open) is James F. Perry, operating through the

An introductory tournament held November 22, 2025 in Mitchell

possibly for a much longer period of time.
The addition of a prize fund, the rating of the planned event
