this event?
The James Valley Chess Club, the financial guarantor of the
event and an official U.S. Chess Federation affiliate, has
provided books and equipment (sets and boards) to almost all
libraries in the James River Valley between Mitchell and
Aberdeen and, in addition, has provided introductory books on
chess to schools in Mitchell and Huron with an offer of additional
books and equipment should the school establish a chess club.
The JVCC has also purchased equipment (sets, boards, and
clocks) in support of its tournaments.
Should this grant be approved, the JVCC will also be purchasing
an electronic chess board (eBoard) so that Carissa Yip's games
can be live streamed over the Internet. The board and pieces will
subsequently become the property of the South Dakota Chess
Association, the official USCF affiliate for the state of South
Dakota.
Total dollar value of such contributions (thus far) is around $900,
not including the eBoard.
Describe your event.
Be sure to include who,
what, where, when,
and how activities will
take place.
The South Dakota Open chess tournament, an official US Chess
Federation rated event, will be one of only a few major chess
tournaments in South Dakota, roughly equal to (or greater than)
in attendance than the South Dakota Chess Championship, the
S.D. Teams Championship, and exceeded only by the
Governor's Cup, with the majority of entrants coming from
outside the Mitchell area.
The event will be held at the Masonic Lodge in Mitchell. It will be
held on the weekend of August 8 and 9, 2026.
Participation in the tournament itself will be open to members of
the United States Chess Federation. There are no age or gender

--- PAGE 5 OF 8 ---


restrictions on tournament participation. Spectators will be
welcome but the playing area itself will be restricted to players,
officials, press (with limitations) and others with special passes.
The Masonic Hall has a balcony area capable of accommodating
spectators who wish to view the event and see Carissa Yip in
person.
What % of attendance
will be visitor draw
outside of 100+ miles
of Mitchell, SD?
Approximately 50%.
What geographic areas
are you bringing event
participants from?
Indicate geographic
areas you are
marketing for visitor
attraction to your event.
We will be marketing to chess players throughout South Dakota
and in surrounding states. Nearly all entrants will be coming from
more than 50 miles from Mitchell with many out-of-state entrants.
The presence of U.S. Women's Chess Champion Carissa Yip
should prove a significant draw.
What are the specific
goals for this event?
We want to significantly increase the number of U.S. Chess
Federation members to the point where it will prove feasible to
hold USCF rated events on a regular basis.
We want to project the image of South Dakota generally, and of
Mitchell in particular, as a significant chess center and as a
center of culture in the state.
In addition, we want to establish a Trust Fund so that this event
can be established on a continuing basis with money from the
interest earned on the principal being used each year to bring a
top ranked chessplayer, alternating between male and female, to
Mitchell. This should prove a significant factor in the promotion of
chess in the state and in support of women chessplayers
nationwide.
Attempts will also be made to find and develop a corporate
sponsor or endorsement package for Ms. Yip. This would, to the
best of my knowledge, be the first ever such out-of-industry
support for a chessplayer in this country.
Explain how your grant
request would be used
to promote tourism in
Mitchell? Note the
resulting impact of your
event if the request for
funding were denied.
Most participants in the tournament would be coming from out-of-
area and thus would qualify as tourists. Historically, it has been
true that chess tournaments in South Dakota, except for the large
population centers of Sioux Falls and Rapid City, have drawn a
very large percentage of participants from outside the immediate
area. This is because there is not, at present, the basis in
available players within the smaller towns in South Dakota to
support such tournaments without such outside draws. I would
expect that a tournament such as the South Dakota Open, held
in Mitchell, would draw around 80% of entries from outside the

--- PAGE 6 OF 8 ---


immediate area.
Note that when chess players attend an event, they would be in
Mitchell for the duration of the event rather than come for just a
short time and then leave. This means that they would be renting
hotel rooms, purchasing meals and gas, etc.
The event promotion and publicity would include a press release
sent to media outlets statewide. In addition, promotion would
include a colorful, eye-catching event flyer posted in numerous
community bulletin boards across the state. The flyer would
prominently feature the top draw player (Carissa Yip) and note
the funding support from the City of Mitchell SEA as well as
advertise local chess clubs and activities.
If we were not able to bring a top draw player such as Carissa
Yip, the event would most likely not be able to be held this year.
In such a case, it would probably take another full year of chess
promotion and tournament organizing to develop the base of
USCF members to justify holding such an event as the South
Dakota Open.

2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.
The following applications were presented and considered:
A. Dakota Oyate Challenge
Silas Blaine, via conference phone, spoke on behalf of and presented the Dakota Oyate
Challenge Grant Application, which is requesting $10,500 plus (11) comp hotel rooms for 44
room nights for officials.
• Silas shared that the 37th Annual Boys' & 32nd Girls' Dakota Oyate Challenge will be
held February 5–7, 2026, at The World's Only Corn Palace. There will (8) boys teams
and (8) girls teams playing bracket play for three days. Each team utilizes 20–25 hotel
rooms for (3) nights. Along with the basketball tournament, the event offers Hand
Games, Archery, and NEW this year, Dakota Language Contest. The grant request will
be utilized to offset their list of expenses. Currently, each school pays a $2,000 entry
fee to participate, which is quite high, so they are looking to lower that expense for
each school.
B. DWU/Culver's Girls' & Boys' High School Basketball Classic
Jason Christensen spoke on behalf of and presented the DWU/Culver's Girls & Boys High
School Basketball Classic Grant Application, which is requesting $5,000.

--- PAGE 1 OF 7 ---


• Jason shared that the 17th Annual Boys' & 13th Annual Girls' DWU/Culver's Classic

well. Any profits/proceeds from the classic goes back into the DWU Men's & Women's
Basketball programs to provide scholarships.
C. South Dakota Girls Varsity Hockey State Tournament
Tyler Graham and Kira Tronnes spoke on behalf of and presented the South Dakota Girls
Varsity Hockey State Tournament Grant Application, which is requesting $5,000.
• Tyler shared that Mitchell will be hosting the South Dakota Girls Varsity Hockey State
Tournament on March 5–7, 2026, at the Mitchell Activities Center. There will be (8)
teams, roughly 170 players, from South Dakota competing in the state tournament —
Brookings, Sioux Falls, Pierre, Watertown, Rapid City, Sioux Center, Mitchell, and
Aberdeen. Teams will be here for (3) nights with games starting at Noon on Thursday,
March 5. The grant request will be utilized to rent a replay screen to be set up in the
Mitchell Activities Center for the tournament. Any profits and proceeds will go back into
the Mitchell Skating & Hockey Association.
D. South Dakota Middle School All-State Band
Tessa Belgum, via conference phone, spoke on behalf of and presented the South Dakota
Middle School All-State Band Grant Application, which is requesting $1,000.
• Tessa shared that the SD Middle School All-State Band will be held March 6–7, 2026,
at the Mitchell Performing Arts Center. There will be 200 registered students from
around the state, which accounts for 71 schools being represented. The grant request
will be utilized towards the hospitality room for the band director's, along with items to
go in each student's swag bag. They make multiple local purchases at Walmart and
County Fair, and many families eat at local restaurants and visit local shops.
E. PowderHorn Ranch Regulators Outlaw Gauntlet Shoot
Troy Bollock spoke on behalf of and presented the PowderHorn Ranch Regulators Outlaw
Gauntlet Shoot Grant Application, which is requesting $5,000.
• Troy shared that the 23rd Annual PowderHorn Ranch Regulators shoot will be held
June 10-14, 2026, at the Mitchell Gun Club. This year they are estimating 85–95
shooters, with over 90% traveling from more than 100+ miles from Mitchell. The grant
request ($5,000), $3,000 will be used as cash prizes for the Blast for Cash-Mitchell
Sports & Events Authority sponsored shoot and $2,000 will go towards updating and
repairing equipment.

--- PAGE 2 OF 7 ---


F. South Dakota VFW & Auxiliary Annual Convention
Anna Arnold spoke on behalf of and presented the South Dakota VFW & Auxiliary Annual
Convention Grant Application, which is requesting $3,200.
• Anna shared that the 97th Annual SD VFW State Convention will be held June 11–14,
2026, at the Highland Conference Center. There will be veterans traveling from all over
South Dakota with approximately 94% of the attendance coming from 100+ miles from
Mitchell. This event usually generates 50–100 room nights along with over 275
attendees during the annual banquet on Saturday night. Mitchell SEA has supported
and awarded the event $3,130 in 2022 and 2023. The grant request will be utilized for
facility and hotel costs at the Highland Conference Center.

March 10, 2026, SEA Advisory Committee Meeting Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
March 10, 2026
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin
Nelson, Cory Aadland, Jason Christensen, Dave Sietsema, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke,
Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, Jim Johnston, and Scott Morgan
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Jill Larson
Others present: Aaron Hieb, Stephanie Ellwein, and Johanna Allen
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.
The following applications were presented and considered:
A. NAIA Women's Basketball National Championship First & Second Round
Jason Christensen spoke on behalf of and presented the NAIA Women's Basketball National
Championship First & Second Round Grant Application, which is requesting $10,000.
• Jason shared that the NAIA Women's Basketball National Championship First &
Second Round will take place Friday, March 13 with (2) games and Saturday, March
14 with (1) game at The World's Only Corn Palace. The following teams are
participating: Dakota Wesleyan University, University of St. Francis (Ill.), Eastern
Oregon University, and College of the Ozarks (Mo.), with all three teams arriving on
Wednesday. Jason shared and reviewed an estimated event budget, highlighting, to
host this event, the bid fee is $12,500, along with additional major expenses for referee
costs and hotel rooms for referees and staff. The grant request will go towards these
expenses listed on the event budget.
B. Palace City Baseball Association
Jordan Widstrom and Adam Kaus spoke on behalf of and presented the Palace City Baseball
Association Grant Application, which is requesting $15,000.

--- PAGE 1 OF 6 ---


• Tabled from the December 2025 meeting.
o Jordan and Adam shared that Palace City Baseball Association was accepted
for both American Legion Baseball affiliation and 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status.
Palace City Baseball will consist of 13U, 14U, Junior Legion, and Legion
baseball. They are still working to secure and establish a teener and legion
tournament for 2026. Mitchell Baseball Association and Palace City Baseball
worked an agreement to allow Palace City Baseball hosting rights for the Harve
Johnston/Bryan Wilson Memorial Baseball Tournament in June. Mitchell will not
be host of the Class 'A' State Youth Tournament until 2027 and 2028. Jordan
and Adam reviewed an updated financials breakdown with the committee. Their
biggest expense is the umpire's wages for their games and tournaments.
Currently, Palace City Baseball Association has secured $40,800 out of
$70,000 in sponsorship contributions.
C. The 301 Rodz & Ridez Car Show
Jerry Wright spoke on behalf of and presented The 301 Rodz & Ridez Car Show Grant
Application, which is requesting $1,500.
• Jerry shared that The 301 Rodz & Ridez Car Show is a 3-day event and will take place
on September 18-20, 2026. Friday, September 18 will be pre-registration along with a
cruise night. Saturday is the car show taking place on Main Street. Sunday is a
gathering at Hitchcock Park. Last year, the event had 160-200 cars. He estimates
between 60-70 hotel room nights. A unique feature is that any car that has been in the
event for the past 10 years receives a personal invitation along with a personal 'Thank
You' from The 301 Rodz. The grant request will go towards their biggest expenses of
advertising and awards.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Sietsema to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented, and seconded by Kevin Nelson. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of March 5, 2026.
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2026 are $61,100.
Current Available Fund Balance of $88,900.00.
Collections in February 2026 (for January 2026 records) are $14,670.00 with (1) establishment
past due.
The YTD collections for 2026 are $31,261.00, which equates to 15,631 total room nights sold.
YTD comparisons of room nights sold were: down 13.5% (2,114 room nights sold) from 2025,

--- PAGE 2 OF 6 ---


down 8.3% (1,303 room nights sold) from 2024, down 4.4% (684 room nights sold) from 2023,
down 3.9% from 2022, up 14.0% from 2021, and down 16.5% from 2020.
Motion: Motion was made by Jim Johnston to approve the financial report as presented, and
seconded by LaRee Rumbolz. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s) with the SEA Committee:
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s)
Palace City 8-Ball Open (November 14-16, 2025)
• The event Exceeded (5) expectations. SEA's support was pivotal to the success of the
event, and they are very grateful. The total spectator attendance was approximately
50. The total participants were 88; SD, ND, MN, IA, NE. The estimated number of total
hotel room nights was approximately 56. Next year's date: October 2–4, 2026. The
funds awarded ($4,000) were used to pay off operating expenses. Net profit of
$1,492.16, which will be carried over and go towards next year's event.
South Dakota Fire Instructors Conference (January 10-11, 2026)
• The event met (3) expectations. The total participants were 130; all across South
Dakota. The estimated number of total hotel room nights was 150. Next year's date:
Unsure. The funds awarded ($4,800) were used to cover the cost of the instructor
along with other associated costs. Net profit of $12,982.08.
SDMEA South Dakota Middle School All-State Jazz Band (January 30-31, 2026)
• The event was Above (4) expectations. SEA support was greatly appreciated. The total
spectator attendance was 190. The total participants were 38. The estimated number
of total hotel room nights was 50. Next year's date: January 29-30, 2027 in Mitchell,
SD. The funds awarded ($1,500) were used to pay for guest directors. Net profit of
$240.39, which will go to the SDMEA to continued putting on these events.
6. Other Items
Aaron Hieb shared the following information with the SEA Committee:
A. Update and Review of Playeasy
No events have been secured through the platform yet.
Active conversations with the following event organizations:
• American Junior Golf Association

--- PAGE 3 OF 6 ---


• Royal Events Cheer & Dance Championship
Aaron also shared and provided an update on the SEA Promotional Coupon that is being
distributed to SEA events. Currently, there are (14) local businesses that have taken the time
to register and SIGN UP so they have ADMIN access to their specific local business profile
micro-site.
• Area Community Theatre (ACT)
• Blarney's Sports Bar & Grill
• Bradley's Pub & Grille
• Cattleman's Club Steakhouse
• Culver's
• Main Street Mercantile
• Mitchell Chamber of Commerce
• Pizza Ranch
• Subway
• The Mitchell Indigenious Archaeological Site & Museum
• The Vault Clothing Co.
• The World's Only Corn Palace
• Triple Play Pawn
• Waterin Hole
Aaron shared the Activity Leaderboard from the past 30 days, which takes into consideration
EVENTS and DESTINATIONS Unique Users and Page Views
• Mitchell Sports & Events Authority was currently ranked 5th and spent a month or so at
#1
• The DWU/Culver's Girl & Boys High School Basketball Classic was also ranked within
the top 5.
Last of all, Aaron shared that the Mitchell Sports & Events Authority was selected as a
destination in Playeasy to assist in the rollout of the new feature, AI Compass. Compass is
powered entirely by context in our profile - the stronger, more intentional content - the more
accurate and strategic the responses will be to the user.
B. Upcoming SEA Events
• Comedy Night presented by CVMA 30-2 (March 21)
o The Masonic Hall
• Special Olympics South Dakota State Basketball Tournament (March 27-29)
o DWU/MHS
• Knights of Columbus Special Olympics State Basketball Banquet (March 28)
o John Paul II
• Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament (April 10-12)
o Mitchell Activities Center
• North Dakota Country Fest-Your Town Tour (April 11)

--- PAGE 4 OF 6 ---


o The World’s Only Corn Palace
• DWU Spring Golf Invitational (April 12-13)
o Lakeview Municipal Golf Course
Complete list of events – MITCHELL CHAMBER EVENTS CALENDAR & Mitchell SD Events
Facebook
7. Executive Session in accordance with SDCL 9-34-19: Discussion of confidential trade
secrets, commercial, or financial information.
Motion: Dave Helleloid made a motion to go into Executive Session, and was seconded by
Tim Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
8. Approval of Funding Applications
NAIA Women's Basketball National Championship First & Second Round
Date: March 13–14, 2026; Contact: Jason Christensen; Grant Request: $10,000
• Motion: Motion was made by Kevin McCardle to award $10,000, and seconded by Tim
Smith. (10) members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
• Abstain: Jason Christensen and Dave Sietsema abstained from voting.
Palace City Baseball Association
Date: May, June, & July 2026; Contact: Adam Kaus; Grant Request: $15,000
• Tabled from December 2025 meeting
• Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to award a total of $7,500 ($2,500 for
each tournament (3) that Palace City Baseball is planning to host in 2026) and
contingent on, if a tournament is not hosted, the respective awarded funding per
tournament, will be returned to the SEA, and seconded by Scott Morgan. All members
voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
The 301 Rodz & Ridez Car Show
Date: September 18-20, 2026; Contact: KayLynn Bren; Grant Request: $1,500
• Motion: Motion was made by Jason Christensen to award $1,500, and seconded by
Kevin Nelson. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
9. Next Meeting Date
Kevin McCardle shared the next meeting date of Tuesday, April 14, 2026, at 2 PM — City Hall,
Council Chambers.

--- PAGE 5 OF 6 ---


10. Adjournment
Brief discussion about Airbnb's and VRBO's being considered as part of the BID #4 District
and contributing to the $2.00 per room per night hotel occupancy tax collections in Mitchell,
SD.
Meeting adjourned by: Kevin McCardle at 3:19 PM

--- PAGE 6 OF 6 ---

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conferences, conventions,
concerts, and sporting events hosted in Mitchell,
SD are an important aspect of the region’s sports
tourism industry.
The Mitchell SEA grant program is available to assist organizations in hosting events that
will promote a positive image to potential visitors, generate overnight visits, extend visitor
stays, and create a desire to return to the area.
The grant program is designed to assist event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Concerts/Special Events: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism and visitor spending in Mitchell, SD, or to fund area
events that will have a significant economic impact on businesses located in Mitchell,
specifically, by generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotels or the
Lake Mitchell Campground.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/conferences, sporting events, concerts, and other special
events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event and tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of Mitchell, SD.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee.

Funding Matrix:
The 22nd annual event takes place on Friday, September 18 - Sunday, September 20, 2026, on Mitchell, SD Main Street.
The 301 Rodz is a group of classic car enthusiasts that share their love of vehicles and community.
For the first 20 years it was called the OutKast's Car Show and then last year it was changed to the 301 Rodz and Ridez Car Show. This event has proven to be very successful in years past and we
continue to grow in attendance every year. We will be teaming up with Mitchell's Main Street and Beyond again this year with the Oktoberfest event which draws in a great crowd and we are
going to keep up this tradition to draw in bigger and better crowds for years to come.
The SEA Grant Application states that approximately 40% of participants and spectators will come from 100+ miles of Mitchell, SD.
In 2025 (total participants and attendance): 4,000-5,000
Our event is hosted by the 301 Rodz Car Club and will be held on Mitchell's Main Street from 1st to 7th Ave. Our event will be held Friday, September 18th with pre-registration, location TBA, Saturday,
September 19th with registration, location TBA from 9-11, a parade down Main Street at 11:45 and car show on Mitchell's Main Street from 12-4, and on Sunday, September 20th will we hold coffee
and donuts at Hitchcock Park. During the car show on Saturday, we will sell 50/50 tickets and do a silent auction with all proceeds going to local organizations.
We mail out flyers to previous attendees that range from Minnesota, Wisconsin, Colorado, Nebraska, Wyoming and as far away as Canada.
Up to 100 hotel room nights (based on the Evaluation Form submitted for 2025 event) in SEPTEMBER X $10 per room night = $1,000
$1,000 X 10% (Event hosted in SEPTEMBER) = $100
$1,000 X 20% (COMBINATION) = $200
$1,000 X 10% (<50% come from 100+ miles) = $100
$1,000 + $100 + $200 + $100 = $1,400
The grant money will be used for the awards to be given out to the top participants choice winners.
Any profit we make goes into an account that will be used to fund next year's show.

Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
February 11, 2026
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Kevin Nelson, Cory Aadland,
Jason Christensen (via phone), Dave Sietsema, LaRee Rumbolz, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith,
Jim Johnston, and Scott Morgan
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Mayor Hanson, Jill Larson, and Emily Liedtke
Others present: Aaron Hieb and Stephanie Ellwein
2. Scott Morgan to the Sports & Events Authority Committee for a term to run from
February 2026-June 2028
Scott Morgan introduced as a newly appointed committee member.
3. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.
The following applications were presented and considered:
A. SDHSAA State Gymnastics Meet
Cory Aadland spoke on behalf of and presented the SDHSAA State Gymnastics Meet Grant
Application, which is requesting $7,500.
• Cory shared that the SDHSAA State Gymnastics Meet will take place on February 13-
14, 2026 at Mitchell High School. Cory provided the committee with a list of Class A
and Class AA schools that will be competing in the team competition on Friday,
February 13. He also reviewed the schedule of events for both days. The grant request
of $7,500 will mainly go towards paying the staff and hospitality room for the workers
and judges.
B. 16th Annual DWU Futsal Classic Indoor Tournament

--- PAGE 1 OF 7 ---


Nicolas Reinhard spoke on behalf of and presented the 16th Annual DWU Futsal Classic
Indoor Tournament Grant Application, which is requesting $2,700.
• Nicolas shared some contributing factors with the committee regarding the difficulty
recruiting teams for futsal in South Dakota compared to the middle 2010s. The DWU
Futsal Classic Indoor Tournament will take place on February 20-22, 2026, at the
DWU/Avera Sports & Wellness Complex as well as at the Christen Family Center on
DWU campus. Currently, the event has 60 teams registered. The grant request of
$2,700 will go towards referee expenses.
C. South Dakota Swimming 13 & Over State Championships
Jason Wede and Rob Schelske spoke on behalf of and presented the South Dakota
Swimming 13 & Over State Championships Grant Application, which is requesting $5,000.
• Jason and Rob shared that the event will be 4 days and take place from February 26–
28, March 1, 2026, at the Mitchell Recreation & Indoor Aquatic Center. This event will
bring approximately 250-300+ youth swimmers to Mitchell, SD. The Dakota Riptide will
sell a program and run concessions as means of revenue from the event. The grant
request of $5,000 will go towards expenses incurred from hosting the meet such as
pool rental and lifeguard wages.
D. MARCH CLASSIC Gymnastics Invitational
Removed from the agenda due to uncontrollable circumstances, the event will not take place
in 2026.
E. 5th Annual Comedy Night presented by CVMA 30-2
Justin Hamer spoke on behalf of and presented the 5th Annual Comedy Night presented by
CVMA 30-2 Grant Application, which is requesting $1,500.
• Justin shared that the 5th Annual Comedy Night presented by the Combat Veterans
Motorcycle Association Chapter 30-2 will take place on March 21, 2026, at the Masonic
Lodge. Last year's (2025) attendance was 150. He also shared the event flyer along
with the entertainment for this year. The grant request of $1,500 will go towards the hall
rental and advertisement for the event.
F. Knights of Columbus Special Olympics State Basketball Banquet
Dan Froning spoke on behalf of and presented the Knights of Columbus Special Olympics
State Basketball Banquet Grant Application, which is requesting $1,200.
• Dan shared that the Knights of Columbus Special Olympics State Basketball
Tournament Banquet will take place on March 28, 2026, in the John Paul II School
Auditorium and Multi-purpose room. This has been the fifth time since 2017 that the

--- PAGE 2 OF 7 ---


Knights of Columbus have hosted this banquet. They will serve a spaghetti dinner with
bread sticks, refreshments, and a Dilly Bar to approximately 750 athletes. There will
also be a dance to follow the dinner. The grant request of $1,200 will go towards costs
for food, condiments, and cleaning.
G. Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament
Stacy Murtha spoke on behalf of and presented the Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament
Grant Application, which is requesting $4,000.
• Stacy shared that the 15th Annual Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament will take
place April 10-12, 2026, in the Mitchell Activities Center, utilizing both sheets of ice.
The tournament will host up to 26 adult teams. Stacy shared where the teams and
players come from along with the other activities that they will participate in while in
Mitchell, SD. The grant request of $4,000 will go towards ice rental costs.
H. DWU Spring Golf Invitational
Jeff Meyerink spoke on behalf of and presented the DWU Spring Golf Invitational Grant
Application, which is requesting $4,000.
• Jeff shared a different format than the last couple of years for the invite. The DWU
Spring Golf Invitational will take place on April 12-13, 2026, with practice rounds taking
place on April 11. There will be a 36-hole format on Sunday and a final 18-holes on
Monday. Currently, there are approximately 80 golfers registered with a max field of 96.
The grant request of $4,000 will go towards a variety of items to provide the players
and coaches with a top-notch experience at Lakeview Golf Course.
I. Sioux Area 4-H Rodeo
Kelly Dunkelberger spoke on behalf of and presented the Sioux Area 4-H Rodeo Grant
Application, which is requesting $10,000.
• Kelly shared that the Sioux Area 4-H Rodeo is in its sixth year and is transitioning from
Sioux Falls to Mitchell (Horseman's Sports Arena) on June 27-28, 2026. The event will
bring approximately 200–250 (ages 8-18) along with 50 volunteers to Mitchell, SD. The
grant request of $10,000 will go towards stock for the event plus a variety of items to
keep the costs for the participants minimal.
J. South Dakota Chess Open
Jim Perry spoke on behalf of and presented the South Dakota Chess Open Grant Application,
which is requesting $4,175.

--- PAGE 3 OF 7 ---


• Jim shared that the South Dakota Chess Open will take place at the Masonic Lodge on
August 8-9, 2026. He is uncertain on the number of participants the event will draw, but
that state events around South Dakota usually draw between 50-60 players. The grant
request of $4,175 will go towards the costs of bringing Carissa Yip, (4-time U.S
Women's Chess Champion and International Chess Master) to the event.
4. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by LaRee Rumbolz to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented, and seconded by Tim Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of February 5, 2026.
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2026 are $39,200.
Current Available Fund Balance of $110,800.00.
Collections in December (for November records) are $26,494.00 with all collected. The total
collections for 2025 are $325,841.00, which accounts for 162,921 rooms nights.
Collections in January 2026 (for December 2025 records) are $16,591.00.
The YTD collections for 2026 are $16,591.00, which equates to 8,296 total room nights sold.
YTD comparisons of room nights sold were: down 7.6% (630 room nights sold) from 2025,
down 16.4% (1,363 room nights sold) from 2024, up 1.5% (127 room nights sold) from 2023,
down 9.0% from 2022, up 17.7% from 2021, and down 29.7% from 2020.
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Sietsema to approve the financial report as presented, and
seconded by Jim Johnston. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
6. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form w/Financials with the SEA Committee:
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s)
DWU/Mitchell Pickleball Indoor Tournament (January 2-4, 2026)
• The event Exceeded (5) expectations. The total spectator attendance was 150. The
total participants were 140; Spearfish, Watertown, Rapid City, Sioux Falls, Brookings,
Huron, 22 cities in 5 different states participated. The estimated number of total hotel
room nights was 75-80. Next year's date: January 1-3, 2027. The funds awarded
($2,500) were used towards prize money, and to purchase balls and supplies. Net
profit of $2,916.60, which will go towards promoting pickleball in Mitchell and to keep
supplies and equipment in good condition.

--- PAGE 4 OF 7 ---


7. Other Items
Aaron Hieb shared the following information with the SEA Committee:
A. Upcoming SEA Events
• DWU/Culver’s Girls’ & Boys’ High School Basketball Classic (February 13-14)
o The World’s Only Corn Palace
• Mitchell Show Choir Classic (February 20-21)
o Mitchell Performing Arts Center
• South Dakota Girls Varsity Hockey State Tournament (March 5-7)
o Mitchell Activities Center
• South Dakota Middle School All-State Band (March 6-7)
o Mitchell Performing Arts Center
Complete list of events – MITCHELL CHAMBER EVENTS CALENDAR & Mitchell SD Events
Facebook
*BOLD – Awarded Sports & Events Authority Grant funding.
8. Executive Session in accordance with SDCL 9-34-19: Discussion of confidential trade
secrets, commercial, or financial information.
Motion: Dave Helleloid made a motion to go into Executive Session, and was seconded by
Tim Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
9. Approval of Funding Applications
SDHSAA State Gymnastics Meet
Date: February 13-14, 2026; Contact: Cory Aadland; Grant Request: $7,500
• Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to award $5,000 along with providing a post-

• Abstain: Cory Aadland abstained from voting.

10. Next Meeting Date
Kevin McCardle shared the next meeting date of Tuesday, March 10, 2026, at 2 PM — City
Hall, Council Chambers.
11. Adjournment
Meeting adjourned by: Kevin McCardle at 3:48 PM

documents.fileName: April 14, 2026, SEA Advisory Committee Meeting Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
April 14, 2026
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, Kevin Nelson,
Cory Aadland, Jason Christensen, Dave Sietsema, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Tim Smith,
Jim Johnston, Scott Morgan
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Mayor Hanson and Dave Helleloid
Others present: Aaron Hieb, Stephanie Ellwein, Johanna Allen
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.
The following applications were presented and considered:
A. Early Bird Baseball Tournament
Jim Johnston spoke on behalf of and presented the Mitchell Baseball Association Early Bird
Baseball Tournament Grant Application, which is requesting $2,500.
• Jim shared that the tournament will be a one-day tournament on Saturday, May 2,
2026, at Cadwell Sports Complex. Currently, there are 27 teams registered, and he
shared where some of those teams are coming from. Last year (2025), the tournament
had 42 teams participate. The grant request of $2,500 will go towards umpire and field
usage fees. Any profits from the tournament will be put back into the Cadwell Sports
Complex for maintenance and upgrades.
B. Memorial Weekend in Mitchell
Elizabeth Luczak spoke on behalf of and presented the MMS&B Memorial Weekend in
Mitchell Grant Application, which is requesting $2,000.
• Elizabeth shared that Memorial Weekend in Mitchell will take place on Saturday, May
23 on Mitchell's Main Street. She shared a timetable and overview of the events taking

--- PAGE 1 OF 4 ---


place throughout the day. Also, she shared some of the marketing criteria and
exposure that the Mitchell SEA would receive if awarded funding for the event. The
grant request of $2,000 will go towards costs for out-of-state marketing, BBQ Ribs for
the contest, and the Kid Pedal Pull awards.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented, and seconded by Emily Liedtke. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of April 9, 2026.
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2026 are $80,100.
Current Available Fund Balance of $69,900.00.
Collections in February 2026 (for January 2026 records) are $14,670.00 with (1) establishment
past due.
Collections in March 2026 (for February 2026 records) are $16,786.00 with (1) establishment
past due.
The YTD collections for 2026 are $48,047.00, which equates to 24,024 total room nights sold.
YTD comparisons of room nights sold were: down 7.5% (1,808 room nights sold) from 2025,
down 0.2% (48 room nights sold) from 2024, up 2.1% (500 room nights sold) from 2023, down
2.6% from 2022, up 20.9% from 2021, and down 10.6% from 2020.
Motion: Motion was made by Kevin Nelson to approve the financial report as presented, and
seconded by Jill Larson. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s) with the SEA Committee:
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s)
Powerplay Hockey Clinic (October 3-5, 2025)
• The event met (3) expectations. The goal going forward is to get more participation
from kids outside the Mitchell area. The total participants were 53; Mitchell, Yankton,
Huron. The estimated number of total hotel room nights was approximately 10. The
funds awarded ($2,000) were used for advertising, posters, and players' gifts and
apparel. Net loss of ($84.36).
Palace Ice Festival (January 16-18, 2026)

--- PAGE 2 OF 4 ---


• The event was Above (4) expectations. This year's event was a success and SEA's
support helps to offset some of the event expenses. The total spectator attendance
was approximately 345. The total participants were 43 skaters, 13 coaches, 5 US
Figure Skating Judges and Representatives. The estimated number of total hotel room
nights was approximately 42-45. Next year's date: January 14-16, 2027. The funds
awarded ($750) were used to offset expenses. Net profit of $1,598.05, which allows the
club to continue to bring in experienced higher level coaches, whether in person or via
virtual lessons, as to allow for the continued growth of skating skills for the skaters.
Mitchell Show Choir Classic (February 20-21, 2026)
• The event was Above (4) expectations. The event went smoothly and was enjoyed by
all who attended. The total spectator attendance was approximately 1,000. The total
participants were 11 teams; Sioux Falls, Harrisburg, Vermillion, Sloan (IA), Omaha
(NE). The estimated number of total hotel room nights was 0. Next year's date:
February 20, 2027. The funds awarded ($3,500) were used for production of the event.
Net profit of $21,532.84, which will assist with production and travel costs.
SD Swimming 13 & Over State Championships (February 26-March 1, 2026)
• The event was Above (4) expectations. Slightly disappointed in the amount awarded
from the SEA. The total spectator attendance was approximately 400+. The estimated
number of total hotel room nights was approximately 405. The funds awarded ($2,500)
were used to pay off operating expenses. Net profit of $6,550.92, which will be used to
help fund the club.
SD Middle School All-State Band (March 6-7, 2026)
• The event was Above (4) expectations. The total spectator attendance was
approximately 1,000. The total participants were 200. The estimated number of total
hotel room nights was approximately 200+. Next year's date: March 5-6, 2027 in
Brookings, SD. The funds awarded ($2,000) were used towards directors hotels,
directors meals and gas, kids water and snacks, directors lounge, director's workshop
fees. Total expenses of $2,541.
Knights of Columbus Special Olympics State Basketball Banquet (March 28, 2026)
• The event met (3) expectations. Served over 500 athletes. The total spectator
attendance was approximately 500+. The estimated number of total hotel room nights
was approximately 601-650. Next year's date: March 27, 2027. The funds awarded
($1,200) were used to pay for meal expenses. No profit. Total expenses of $1,538.63.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conferences, conventions,
concerts, and sporting events hosted in Mitchell,
SD are an important aspect of the region’s sports
tourism industry.
The Mitchell SEA grant program is available to assist organizations in hosting events that
will promote a positive image to potential visitors, generate overnight visits, extend visitor
stays, and create a desire to return to the area.
The grant program is designed to assist event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Concerts/Special Events: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism and visitor spending in Mitchell, SD, or to fund area
events that will have a significant economic impact on businesses located in Mitchell,
specifically, by generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotels or the
Lake Mitchell Campground.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/conferences, sporting events, concerts, and other special
events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event and tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of Mitchell, SD.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee.

The many festivals, conferences, conventions,
concerts, and sporting events hosted in Mitchell,
SD are an important aspect of the region’s sports
tourism industry.
The Mitchell SEA grant program is available to assist organizations in hosting events that
will promote a positive image to potential visitors, generate overnight visits, extend visitor
stays, and create a desire to return to the area.
The grant program is designed to assist event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Concerts/Special Events: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism and visitor spending in Mitchell, SD, or to fund area
events that will have a significant economic impact on businesses located in Mitchell,
specifically, by generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotels or the
Lake Mitchell Campground.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/conferences, sporting events, concerts, and other special
events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event and tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of Mitchell, SD.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee.

Mitchell Main Street & Beyond is an economic development
program dedicated to supporting and revitalizing Mitchell’s
historic commercial district. Our downtown offers a distinctive
sense of place that reflecting national revitalization trends is
becoming an increasingly popular destination to do business,
shop, dine, live, and enjoy family-friendly activities.
We take great pride in fostering a clean, welcoming, and vibrant
downtown environment. By preserving Mitchell’s historic
character while encouraging new opportunities, we strive to
create a space where residents and visitors alike can shop, eat,
work, and play in a thriving community atmosphere.
Memorial Weekend in Mitchell - This event draws participants
from across the state to enjoy a full slate of activities including
the BBQ Rib Contest, Kid Pedal Pull, Car Show & Shine, Poker
Run, Bean Bags, Poker Walk, Family Fun Zone, and the
always-thrilling SD Mud Races. Each year, the energy and
anticipation grow as families and friends gather to celebrate the
spirit of our community.
The BBQ Rib Contest remains a signature highlight, with local
chefs and backyard grill masters firing up their smokers in a
friendly competition for the title of “Best Ribs in the Region.” The
unmistakable aroma of smoky, savory ribs fills Main Street,
drawing visitors into the heart of the festivities.
The Kid Pedal Pull brings smiles to spectators of all ages as

pedaling toward victory. It’s a charming reminder of the simple
joys and supportive community atmosphere that define Mitchell.
Auto enthusiasts look forward to the Car Show & Shine, where
pristine vintage, classic, and modern vehicles line Main Street.
Each car reflects the dedication of its owner and sparks
conversation, admiration, and connection among attendees.
For those seeking high-energy excitement, the SD Mud Races
deliver with roaring engines and mud-slinging action.
Competitors navigate challenging tracks with skill and grit,
creating an exhilarating experience for all who watch.
With such a wide variety of offerings, there is truly something for
everyone of every age at this event!

Mitchell Main Street & Beyond is committed to advancing
preservation-based economic development and improving our

Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
March 10, 2026
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin
Nelson, Cory Aadland, Jason Christensen, Dave Sietsema, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke,
Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, Jim Johnston, and Scott Morgan
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Jill Larson
Others present: Aaron Hieb, Stephanie Ellwein, and Johanna Allen
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.
The following applications were presented and considered:
A. NAIA Women's Basketball National Championship First & Second Round
Jason Christensen spoke on behalf of and presented the NAIA Women's Basketball National
Championship First & Second Round Grant Application, which is requesting $10,000.
• Jason shared that the NAIA Women's Basketball National Championship First &
Second Round will take place Friday, March 13 with (2) games and Saturday, March
14 with (1) game at The World's Only Corn Palace. The following teams are
participating: Dakota Wesleyan University, University of St. Francis (Ill.), Eastern
Oregon University, and College of the Ozarks (Mo.), with all three teams arriving on
Wednesday. Jason shared and reviewed an estimated event budget, highlighting, to
host this event, the bid fee is $12,500, along with additional major expenses for referee
costs and hotel rooms for referees and staff. The grant request will go towards these
expenses listed on the event budget.
B. Palace City Baseball Association
Jordan Widstrom and Adam Kaus spoke on behalf of and presented the Palace City Baseball
Association Grant Application, which is requesting $15,000.

--- PAGE 1 OF 6 ---


• Tabled from the December 2025 meeting.
o Jordan and Adam shared that Palace City Baseball Association was accepted
for both American Legion Baseball affiliation and 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status.
Palace City Baseball will consist of 13U, 14U, Junior Legion, and Legion
baseball. They are still working to secure and establish a teener and legion
tournament for 2026. Mitchell Baseball Association and Palace City Baseball
worked an agreement to allow Palace City Baseball hosting rights for the Harve
Johnston/Bryan Wilson Memorial Baseball Tournament in June. Mitchell will not
be host of the Class 'A' State Youth Tournament until 2027 and 2028. Jordan
and Adam reviewed an updated financials breakdown with the committee. Their
biggest expense is the umpire's wages for their games and tournaments.
Currently, Palace City Baseball Association has secured $40,800 out of
$70,000 in sponsorship contributions.
C. The 301 Rodz & Ridez Car Show
Jerry Wright spoke on behalf of and presented The 301 Rodz & Ridez Car Show Grant
Application, which is requesting $1,500.
• Jerry shared that The 301 Rodz & Ridez Car Show is a 3-day event and will take place
on September 18-20, 2026. Friday, September 18 will be pre-registration along with a
cruise night. Saturday is the car show taking place on Main Street. Sunday is a
gathering at Hitchcock Park. Last year, the event had 160-200 cars. He estimates
between 60-70 hotel room nights. A unique feature is that any car that has been in the
event for the past 10 years receives a personal invitation along with a personal 'Thank
You' from The 301 Rodz. The grant request will go towards their biggest expenses of
advertising and awards.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Sietsema to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented, and seconded by Kevin Nelson. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of March 5, 2026.
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2026 are $61,100.
Current Available Fund Balance of $88,900.00.

Evaluation Information
How well did this event
meet your
expectations:
4 - Above Expectations
Additional
Feedback/Positive
Takeaways/Ways the
SEA can assist in the
growth of the event:
The skating competition went very well, with skaters, coaches,
judges, and families having a great experience. The skating
competitors always learn a lot from the USFS judges as they give
them skating feedback to help grow their skating skills.
This year we were very privileged to have Jennifer Freedman, a
Masters Level Skater from Connecticut, along with her
coach/dance partner Oleg Voyko from New York, who
represented Ukraine in both the 2002 & 2006 Winter Olympics,
perform skating dance programs for everyone.
As in past years the city employees did a wonderful job ensuring
things ran very smoothly.
The assistance of the SEA Grant greatly helps to offset
competition expenses to allow the club to continue to host a
competition, grow skater skating skills, and to bring people to the
community of Mitchell.

documents.fileName: May 12, 2026, SEA Advisory Committee Meeting Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
May 12, 2026
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin Nelson,
LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, Jim Johnston, Scott Morgan
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Jill Larson, Cory Aadland, Jason Christensen,
Dave Sietsema
Others present: Aaron Hieb, Stephanie Ellwein
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.
The following applications were presented and considered:
A. Battle at the Corn Palace 2 presented by 15th Round Boxing
Mayor Hanson spoke on behalf of and presented the Battle at the Corn Palace 2 presented by
15th Round Boxing Grant Application, which is requesting $1,500.
• Mayor Hanson shared that the event will take place this Saturday, May 16, 2026, at The
World's Only Corn Palace. There are 17 bouts scheduled, starting at 5 PM. Currently,
there are approximately 100 tickets sold, and he shared that the majority of the ticket
sales last year took place the day before and day of the event. Last year, there were 462
tickets sold. The grant request of $1,500 will go towards hotel fees for the boxers,
workers, and staff. The only source of income for the event is ticket sales and any profits
from the event help fund future events and the boxers' fees for national events.
B. South Dakota Golf Association (SDGA) Mid-Am Championship

--- PAGE 1 OF 7 ---


Eric Hieb spoke on behalf of and presented the South Dakota Golf Association (SDGA) Mid-Am
Championship Grant Application, which is requesting $800.
• Eric shared that the tournament will be Saturday and Sunday, June 6–7, with a practice
round that the majority of golfers participate in on Friday, June 5, 2026, at Lakeview
Municipal Golf Course. Currently, there are 67 golfers registered and the deadline to
sign up is May 27. He estimates that approximately 75% of the golfers will stay overnight
on Friday and Saturday. The grant request of $800 will go towards hospitality for the
golfers and lunches for the volunteers. Any profits from the event will go towards the
daily operations of the golf course.
C. Mitchell Area Community (MAC) Triathlon
Emily Hohn and Terasa Gillen spoke on behalf of and presented the Mitchell Area Community
(MAC) Triathlon Grant Application, which is requesting $2,500.
• Emily and Terasa shared that the 10th Annual event will take place on Saturday, June 6,
2026, at Hitchcock Park. They expect 65–80 participants, with many of those registered
this year being local. Those that stay overnight do not stay in hotels, rather
campgrounds, so they do recommend the Lake Mitchell Campground, which does
voluntarily submit the $2 per campsite per night BID #4 collection. They are currently in
the process of a three-year contract to purchase their own timing system. The grant
request of $2,500 will go towards the purchase of the timing system along with permit
fees for their event. Any profits from the event go back into the community along with
supporting their MAC Area Event.
Kiwanis Youth Baseball Tourney
Linda McEntee spoke on behalf of and presented the Kiwanis Youth Baseball Tourney Grant
Application, which is requesting $1,000.
• Linda shared that the tournament will be a one-day tournament on Saturday, June 6,
2026, at Cadwell Sports Complex. The Kiwanis Club of Mitchell is partnering with Palace
City Baseball Association. Currently, there are 21 teams registered, and there will also
be a Pitch, Hit, and Run competition available for all players as well. The grant request
of $1,000 will go towards umpire fees and awards. Any profits from the tournament will
be split between the Kiwanis Club of Mitchell and Palace City Baseball Association.
D. Lowell Rang Memorial Girls Fastpitch Softball Tournament
Jim Misiaszek spoke on behalf of and presented the Lowell Rang Memorial Girls Fastpitch
Softball Tournament Grant Application, which is requesting $3,000.
• Jim shared that the 20th Annual tournament will be Friday, June 12 through Sunday,
June 14, 2026, at Cadwell Sports Complex. Currently, there are 50 teams registered,

--- PAGE 2 OF 7 ---


and he shared that each year they compete with Sioux Falls tournaments, as well as,
every fourth year, the SDHSAA State Softball Tournament will overlap the event. The
grant request of $3,000 will go towards umpire fees and hospitality, along with field
usage fees. Any profits from the tournament will be put back into the maintenance and
upgrades of their equipment.
E. Cornbelt Team Camps
Josh Davies, via conference phone, spoke on behalf of and presented the Cornbelt Team
Camps Grant Application, which is requesting $1,250.
• Josh shared that the camps will be held (Girls Varsity) June 10-11, (Boys Varsity) June
17-18, and (Girls/Boys JV) June 24-25, 2026. Currently, there are around 80 teams
registered. Josh surveyed each team and these camps will account for 60 total room
nights. He has not guaranteed the school(s) or coaches any sort of rebate funding yet,
but he would like to be able to receive some funding, so he can provide those schools
that stay overnight with some funding to cover hotel room costs. The grant request of
$1,250 will go back to those schools that stayed overnight to help cover hotel room
costs. Any profits from the camps will help to fund future camps.
F. Arts in the Park
Mayor Hanson spoke on behalf of and presented the Arts in the Park Grant Application, which
is requesting $2,500.
• Mayor Hanson shared that this is the third year of the revival of Arts in the Park and will
take place on Saturday, July 25 through Sunday, July 26, 2026, at Hitchcock Park.
Currently, there are approximately 140 vendors attending the event. They estimate that
approximately 50–60% of vendors stay overnight in hotels. The grant request of $2,500
will go towards offsetting expenses such as security, park use fees, and permit fees.
Any profits from the event will go towards funding future events.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Kevin Nelson to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented, and seconded by Jim Johnston. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of May 8, 2026.
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2026 are $84,100.

--- PAGE 3 OF 7 ---


Current Available Fund Balance of $65,900.00.
Collections in February 2026 (for January 2026 records) still have one (1) establishment past
due.
Collections in March 2026 (for February 2026 records) still have (1) establishment past due.
Collections in April 2026 (for March 2026 records) are $18,648.00 with (1) establishment past
due.
The (1) establishment past due is the same establishment for all three past due collections,
which would account for 90–120 total room nights.
The YTD collections for 2026 are $66,695.00, which equates to 33,348 total room nights sold.
YTD comparisons of room nights sold were: down 6.2% (2,075 room nights sold) from 2025, up
1.2% (392 room nights sold) from 2024, down 1.7% (562 room nights sold) from 2023,
down 5.6% from 2022, up 15.2% from 2021, and up 2.0% from 2020.
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the financial report as presented, and
seconded by Emily Liedtke. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s) with the SEA Committee:
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s)
Dakota Oyate Challenge Volleyball (October 10-11, 2025)
• The event Exceeded (5) expectations. It was a great tournament. The total participants
were 15 teams = 240 participants. The estimated number of total hotel room nights was
approximately 320. Next year's event is September 18–19, 2026 in The World's Only
Corn Palace. The funds awarded ($4,200) were used to pay officials, tournament
workers, and hotel rooms for officials and workers. Net loss of (619.26).
Pheasants Forever Banquet (October 17, 2025)
• The event Exceeded (5) expectations. The total participants were 750. From all across
the United States. The estimated number of total hotel room nights was approximately
200. Next year's event is Friday, October 16, 2026, in The World's Only Corn Palace.
The funds awarded ($2,000) were used to offset the costs of holding the banquet. Profits
from the event help benefit the youth hunters in our area. A Pheasants Country
Donations listing was shared with the committee.
American Outlaws Wrestling Monster Brawl (November 1–2, 2025)

--- PAGE 4 OF 7 ---


• The event was Above (4) expectations. This year there was an increase in entries along
with more people from out of state. The total spectator attendance was: 700. The total
participants were 260 for the individual tournament and 6 teams = 108 wrestlers for the
dual tournament on Sunday. The estimated number of total hotel room nights was
approximately 150–200. Next year's event date will be a belt series 4-tournament series
taking place July 18–19, 2026 and November 14–15, 2026 in Mitchell, SD. The funds
awarded ($2,000) were used for awards. Net profit of $18,600.88, which will be used to
put on future events and help fund the wrestling club.
Hoop City Classic (December 27–30, 2025)
• The event was Above (4) expectations. The total spectators for the youth tournament
was 1,572, with 36 teams that accounted for an estimated 30 room nights. The total
spectators for the classic were 3,800, with 31 teams = 465 participants. The estimated
number of total hotel room nights was approximately 180. Next year's event will be a
youth tournament: December 27–28, 2026 and December 28–31, 2026 in Mitchell, SD.
The funds awarded ($12,500) were used to promote the event and pay for expenses.
Net profit of 2,368.42, which is used to promote Hoop City events throughout the year.
Dakota Oyate Challenge Basketball (February 5–7, 2026)
• The event met (3) expectations. The total spectator attendance was 1,088. The total
participants were 16 teams = 240 players, along with 5 archery teams and 27 hand
games teams. The estimated number of total hotel room nights was approximately 800–
900 for (4) nights. Next year's event dates are January 28–30, 2027 at The World's Only
Corn Palace. The funds awarded ($7,000) were used to pay officials, the hospitality
room, announcers, book, and clock, and additional hotel rooms for officials. Net profit of
$2,452.50, which will be used to fund DOC Volleyball 2026 and DOC Basketball 2027.
6. Other Items
Aaron Hieb shared the following information with the SEA Committee:

Mitchell Sports & Events Authority

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conferences, conventions,
concerts, and sporting events hosted in Mitchell,
SD are an important aspect of the region’s sports
tourism industry.
The Mitchell SEA grant program is available to assist organizations in hosting events that
will promote a positive image to potential visitors, generate overnight visits, extend visitor
stays, and create a desire to return to the area.
The grant program is designed to assist event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Concerts/Special Events: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism and visitor spending in Mitchell, SD, or to fund area
events that will have a significant economic impact on businesses located in Mitchell,
specifically, by generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotels or the
Lake Mitchell Campground.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/conferences, sporting events, concerts, and other special
events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event and tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of Mitchell, SD.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee.

Funding Matrix:
The 10th Annual Mitchell Area Community (MAC) Triathlon takes place on Saturday, June 6, 2026 at Hitchcock Park.
The Mitchell Area Community (MAC) is dedicated to promoting health and wellness, hosting a must-attend event right here in Mitchell, SD, and giving back to local youth organizations.
Last year's attendance: 250 participants and spectators
The SEA Grant Application states that approximately 30-40% of attendees will come from 100+ miles of Mitchell, SD.
Event Description:
Sprint Triathlon
500 meter swim at Hitchcock pool
14 mile bike around Mitchell and rural areas
3.1 mile run around Mitchell
Our event includes individuals as well as team registrants. The event begins at the pool, then goes into the biking portion, and finally the run portion which concludes again at the park.
Up to 50 hotel room nights in JUNE X $10 per room night = $500
$500 X 10% (Event hosted in JUNE) = $50
$500 X 20% Combination (Youth & Adult) = $100
$500 X 10% (TEAM) = $50
$500 X 10% (<50% come from 100+ miles) = $50
$500 + $50 + $100 + $50 + $50 = $750
We have athletes that come from Rapid City, Yankton, Sioux City, Huron, Sioux Falls, North Dakota, Minnesota, Iowa, Nebraska.
The grant request will be used for the timing company and Special Event Permit (street closures).
As an annual event, we proudly contribute a portion of our proceeds to support community and youth activities in Mitchell. In past years, we've partnered with organizations such as Dakota
Riptide, Girls on the Run, Big Friend Little Friend, and local biking initiatives, among others. More recently, our primary focus has been supporting the Mitchell Area Community Events organization, which is working to bring outdoor fitness equipment to our community.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conferences, conventions,
concerts, and sporting events hosted in Mitchell,
SD are an important aspect of the region’s sports
tourism industry.
The Mitchell SEA grant program is available to assist organizations in hosting events that
will promote a positive image to potential visitors, generate overnight visits, extend visitor
stays, and create a desire to return to the area.
The grant program is designed to assist event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Concerts/Special Events: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism and visitor spending in Mitchell, SD, or to fund area
events that will have a significant economic impact on businesses located in Mitchell,
specifically, by generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotels or the
Lake Mitchell Campground.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/conferences, sporting events, concerts, and other special
events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event and tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of Mitchell, SD.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee.

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
April 14, 2026
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, Kevin Nelson,
Cory Aadland, Jason Christensen, Dave Sietsema, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Tim Smith,
Jim Johnston, Scott Morgan
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Mayor Hanson and Dave Helleloid
Others present: Aaron Hieb, Stephanie Ellwein, Johanna Allen
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.
The following applications were presented and considered:
A. Early Bird Baseball Tournament
Jim Johnston spoke on behalf of and presented the Mitchell Baseball Association Early Bird
Baseball Tournament Grant Application, which is requesting $2,500.
• Jim shared that the tournament will be a one-day tournament on Saturday, May 2,
2026, at Cadwell Sports Complex. Currently, there are 27 teams registered, and he
shared where some of those teams are coming from. Last year (2025), the tournament
had 42 teams participate. The grant request of $2,500 will go towards umpire and field
usage fees. Any profits from the tournament will be put back into the Cadwell Sports
Complex for maintenance and upgrades.
B. Memorial Weekend in Mitchell
Elizabeth Luczak spoke on behalf of and presented the MMS&B Memorial Weekend in
Mitchell Grant Application, which is requesting $2,000.
• Elizabeth shared that Memorial Weekend in Mitchell will take place on Saturday, May
23 on Mitchell's Main Street. She shared a timetable and overview of the events taking

--- PAGE 1 OF 4 ---


place throughout the day. Also, she shared some of the marketing criteria and
exposure that the Mitchell SEA would receive if awarded funding for the event. The
grant request of $2,000 will go towards costs for out-of-state marketing, BBQ Ribs for
the contest, and the Kid Pedal Pull awards.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented, and seconded by Emily Liedtke. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
4. Financial Report

past due.

down 0.2% (48 room nights sold) from 2024, up 2.1% (500 room nights sold) from 2023, down
2.6% from 2022, up 20.9% from 2021, and down 10.6% from 2020.

seconded by Jill Larson. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys

A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s)
Powerplay Hockey Clinic (October 3-5, 2025)
• The event met (3) expectations. The goal going forward is to get more participation
from kids outside the Mitchell area. The total participants were 53; Mitchell, Yankton,
Huron. The estimated number of total hotel room nights was approximately 10. The
funds awarded ($2,000) were used for advertising, posters, and players' gifts and
apparel. Net loss of ($84.36).
Palace Ice Festival (January 16-18, 2026)

--- PAGE 2 OF 4 ---


• The event was Above (4) expectations. This year's event was a success and SEA's
support helps to offset some of the event expenses. The total spectator attendance
was approximately 345. The total participants were 43 skaters, 13 coaches, 5 US
Figure Skating Judges and Representatives. The estimated number of total hotel room
nights was approximately 42-45. Next year's date: January 14-16, 2027. The funds
awarded ($750) were used to offset expenses. Net profit of $1,598.05, which allows the
club to continue to bring in experienced higher level coaches, whether in person or via
virtual lessons, as to allow for the continued growth of skating skills for the skaters.
Mitchell Show Choir Classic (February 20-21, 2026)
• The event was Above (4) expectations. The event went smoothly and was enjoyed by
all who attended. The total spectator attendance was approximately 1,000. The total
participants were 11 teams; Sioux Falls, Harrisburg, Vermillion, Sloan (IA), Omaha
(NE). The estimated number of total hotel room nights was 0. Next year's date:
February 20, 2027. The funds awarded ($3,500) were used for production of the event.
Net profit of $21,532.84, which will assist with production and travel costs.
SD Swimming 13 & Over State Championships (February 26-March 1, 2026)
• The event was Above (4) expectations. Slightly disappointed in the amount awarded
from the SEA. The total spectator attendance was approximately 400+. The estimated
number of total hotel room nights was approximately 405. The funds awarded ($2,500)
were used to pay off operating expenses. Net profit of $6,550.92, which will be used to
help fund the club.
SD Middle School All-State Band (March 6-7, 2026)
• The event was Above (4) expectations. The total spectator attendance was
approximately 1,000. The total participants were 200. The estimated number of total
hotel room nights was approximately 200+. Next year's date: March 5-6, 2027 in
Brookings, SD. The funds awarded ($2,000) were used towards directors hotels,
directors meals and gas, kids water and snacks, directors lounge, director's workshop
fees. Total expenses of $2,541.
Knights of Columbus Special Olympics State Basketball Banquet (March 28, 2026)
• The event met (3) expectations. Served over 500 athletes. The total spectator
attendance was approximately 500+. The estimated number of total hotel room nights
was approximately 601-650. Next year's date: March 27, 2027. The funds awarded
($1,200) were used to pay for meal expenses. No profit. Total expenses of $1,538.63.

documents.fileName: June 9, 2026, SEA Advisory Committee Meeting Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                     June 9, 2026 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin 
Nelson, Jason Christensen, Dave Sietsema, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Tim Smith, Jim 
Johnston, Scott Morgan 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Jill Larson, Cory Aadland Dave Helleloid 
 
 Others present: Aaron Hieb, Johanna Allen, Stephanie Ellwein, Gretchen 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.  
 
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.  
 
 The following applications were presented and considered: 
 
A. Palace City Soccer Cup 2026 
Adam Trimble spoke on behalf of and presented the Palace City Soccer Cup 2026 Grant 
Application, which is requesting $5,000. 

     • Adam shared that the event will take place on Saturday, June 13–Sunday, June 14, 
       2026, at the Pepsi Cola Soccer Complex. This tournament is U9-U14 with a total of 19 
       teams, (12) of those are from outside of Mitchell. This number of teams is down 
       compared to 2025, and they are looking at changing the date in 2027, so it doesn't 
       overlap with a tournament in Rapid City. The grant request of $5,000 will go towards 
       offsetting expenses related to hosting the event.  

 
 
B. Palace City Mountain Bike Classic 
Cody Denne spoke on behalf of and presented the Palace City Mountain Bike Classic Grant 
Application, which is requesting $1,200. 

     • Cody shared that the event will take place on Saturday, June 20, 2026, at the Lake 
       Mitchell Trails starting at Sandy Beach Access. So far, they have 41 racers signed up,        with more sign-ups will take place a few days before and the day of the event. The 
       grant request of $1,200 will go towards paying for the timing system. 

 
 
C. DWU Girls' Basketball Team Camps 
Jason Christensen spoke on behalf of and presented the DWU Girls' Basketball Team Camps 
Grant Application, which is requesting $1,100. 

     • Jason shared that the one-day team camps will take place on June 29 and July 27 at 
       DWU/ Avera Sports and Wellness Complex. Currently, there are 44 teams signed up 
       for the June session. The July session will pick up with registrations as it gets closer. 
       The grant request of $1,100 will be used to offset the costs of running the camps. 

 
 
D. American Outlaws Wrestling Open & Showdown Belt Series 
JD Heinrich via conference phone spoke on behalf of and presented the American Outlaws 
Wrestling Open & Showdown Belt Series Grant Application, which is requesting $10,000. 

     • JD shared that this is the first year of a new wrestling tournament series that is broken 
       down into four different competitions, with the first 2 (Open & Showdown) taking place 
       on Saturday, July 18–Sunday, July 19, 2026, at the DWU/Avera Sports & Wellness 
       Complex. The age divisions are: 6U, 8U, 10U, 12U, 14U, High School (9-12th grade), 
       Seniors, Masters, Grand Masters, and Elite. Currently, there are approximately 60–70 
       participants signed up, with expectations of approximately 300–400 when all is said 
       and done. The grant request of $10,000 will go towards rent and concessions food and 
       supplies costs. Concession items will all be bought locally. 

 
 
E. SD State Amateur Baseball Tournament 
Jim Johnston spoke on behalf of and presented the SD State Amateur Baseball Tournament 
Grant Application, which is requesting $5,000. 

     • Jim shared that the tournament will take place August 5-16, 2026, at the Cadwell Park 
       Stadium and Drake Field. There are a total of 36 teams to start the tournament, which 
       brings in approximately 10,000–12,000 total spectators for the tournament. He 
       estimates around 350 rooms nights for the entirety of the event. The grant request of 
       $5,000 will go towards the hospitality, field rental and maintenance costs, PA 
       announcer, and ticket takers. He estimates around 100 volunteers from the Mitchell 
       Baseball Association and Exchange Club of Mitchell assist in the success of the 
       tournament. 

 
 
F. Dakota Oyate Challenge Volleyball 
Silas Blaine, via conference phone, spoke on behalf of and presented the Dakota Oyate Challenge Volleyball Grant Application, which is requesting $17,147.26 / $6,300. 

     • Silas shared that the Dakota Oyate Challenge Volleyball made a date change this year, 
       so the event didn't overlap with the Pow Wow that takes place in Rapid City over the 
       October date the past two years. The new date for the tournament is September 18–
       19, 2026, at The World's Only Corn Palace. Silas confirmed the grant request amount 
       is $6,300, which, based on the submitted event budget, would assist in keeping the 
       event out of the red or a negative income. The grant request of $6,300 would go 
       towards the Corn Palace rental costs, hotel rooms for officials, awards, and the 
       hospitality room. The event is also looking at expanding in the upcoming years, by 
       adding cross-country and hand games. 

 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
presented, and seconded by Jason Christensen. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion 
 passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of June 3, 2026. 
 
The supplemental carryover from the 2025 remaining balance of $39,190 has been added to 
the SEA Revenue. 
 
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2026 are $93,650.00. 
 
There is (1) committed item where the award check has not been written — MAC Triathlon 
($1,500). 
 
Current Available Fund Balance of $94,040.00.  
 
Collections in February 2026 (for January 2026 records) still have one (1) establishment past 
due.  
 
Collections in March 2026 (for February 2026 records) still have (1) establishment past due.  
 
Collections in April 2026 (for March 2026 records) still have (1) establishment past due.  
 
Collections in May 2026 for (April 2026 records) are $21,286.00 with (1) establishment past 
due. 
 
The (1) establishment past due is the same establishment for all past due collections.  
 
The YTD collections for 2026 are $87,981.00.00, which equates to 43,991 total room nights 
sold.  
 
YTD comparisons of room nights sold were: down 3.9% (1,719 room nights sold) from 2025, 
down 2.3% (1,031 room nights sold) from 2024, up 0.6% (269 room nights sold) from 2023, down 2.7% from 2022, up 12.6% from 2021, and up 18.2% from 2020.

The many festivals, conferences, conventions,
concerts, and sporting events hosted in Mitchell,
SD are an important aspect of the region’s sports
tourism industry.
The Mitchell SEA grant program is available to assist organizations in hosting events that
will promote a positive image to potential visitors, generate overnight visits, extend visitor
stays, and create a desire to return to the area.
The grant program is designed to assist event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Concerts/Special Events: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism and visitor spending in Mitchell, SD, or to fund area
events that will have a significant economic impact on businesses located in Mitchell,
specifically, by generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotels or the
Lake Mitchell Campground.
Preference will be given to:

events.
