The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the

stays, and create a desire to return to the area.
The grant program is designed to assist event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.

The grant exists to encourage tourism and visitor spending in Mitchell, SD, or to fund area
events that will have a significant economic impact on businesses located in Mitchell,
specifically, by generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotels or the
Lake Mitchell Campground.

events.

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
May 12, 2026
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin Nelson,
LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, Jim Johnston, Scott Morgan
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Jill Larson, Cory Aadland, Jason Christensen,
Dave Sietsema
Others present: Aaron Hieb, Stephanie Ellwein
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.
The following applications were presented and considered:
A. Battle at the Corn Palace 2 presented by 15th Round Boxing
Mayor Hanson spoke on behalf of and presented the Battle at the Corn Palace 2 presented by
15th Round Boxing Grant Application, which is requesting $1,500.
• Mayor Hanson shared that the event will take place this Saturday, May 16, 2026, at The
World's Only Corn Palace. There are 17 bouts scheduled, starting at 5 PM. Currently,
there are approximately 100 tickets sold, and he shared that the majority of the ticket
sales last year took place the day before and day of the event. Last year, there were 462
tickets sold. The grant request of $1,500 will go towards hotel fees for the boxers,
workers, and staff. The only source of income for the event is ticket sales and any profits
from the event help fund future events and the boxers' fees for national events.
B. South Dakota Golf Association (SDGA) Mid-Am Championship

--- PAGE 1 OF 7 ---


Eric Hieb spoke on behalf of and presented the South Dakota Golf Association (SDGA) Mid-Am
Championship Grant Application, which is requesting $800.
• Eric shared that the tournament will be Saturday and Sunday, June 6–7, with a practice
round that the majority of golfers participate in on Friday, June 5, 2026, at Lakeview
Municipal Golf Course. Currently, there are 67 golfers registered and the deadline to
sign up is May 27. He estimates that approximately 75% of the golfers will stay overnight
on Friday and Saturday. The grant request of $800 will go towards hospitality for the
golfers and lunches for the volunteers. Any profits from the event will go towards the
daily operations of the golf course.
C. Mitchell Area Community (MAC) Triathlon
Emily Hohn and Terasa Gillen spoke on behalf of and presented the Mitchell Area Community
(MAC) Triathlon Grant Application, which is requesting $2,500.
• Emily and Terasa shared that the 10th Annual event will take place on Saturday, June 6,
2026, at Hitchcock Park. They expect 65–80 participants, with many of those registered
this year being local. Those that stay overnight do not stay in hotels, rather
campgrounds, so they do recommend the Lake Mitchell Campground, which does
voluntarily submit the $2 per campsite per night BID #4 collection. They are currently in
the process of a three-year contract to purchase their own timing system. The grant
request of $2,500 will go towards the purchase of the timing system along with permit
fees for their event. Any profits from the event go back into the community along with
supporting their MAC Area Event.
Kiwanis Youth Baseball Tourney
Linda McEntee spoke on behalf of and presented the Kiwanis Youth Baseball Tourney Grant
Application, which is requesting $1,000.
• Linda shared that the tournament will be a one-day tournament on Saturday, June 6,
2026, at Cadwell Sports Complex. The Kiwanis Club of Mitchell is partnering with Palace
City Baseball Association. Currently, there are 21 teams registered, and there will also
be a Pitch, Hit, and Run competition available for all players as well. The grant request
of $1,000 will go towards umpire fees and awards. Any profits from the tournament will
be split between the Kiwanis Club of Mitchell and Palace City Baseball Association.
D. Lowell Rang Memorial Girls Fastpitch Softball Tournament
Jim Misiaszek spoke on behalf of and presented the Lowell Rang Memorial Girls Fastpitch
Softball Tournament Grant Application, which is requesting $3,000.
• Jim shared that the 20th Annual tournament will be Friday, June 12 through Sunday,
June 14, 2026, at Cadwell Sports Complex. Currently, there are 50 teams registered,

--- PAGE 2 OF 7 ---


and he shared that each year they compete with Sioux Falls tournaments, as well as,
every fourth year, the SDHSAA State Softball Tournament will overlap the event. The
grant request of $3,000 will go towards umpire fees and hospitality, along with field
usage fees. Any profits from the tournament will be put back into the maintenance and
upgrades of their equipment.
E. Cornbelt Team Camps
Josh Davies, via conference phone, spoke on behalf of and presented the Cornbelt Team
Camps Grant Application, which is requesting $1,250.
• Josh shared that the camps will be held (Girls Varsity) June 10-11, (Boys Varsity) June
17-18, and (Girls/Boys JV) June 24-25, 2026. Currently, there are around 80 teams
registered. Josh surveyed each team and these camps will account for 60 total room
nights. He has not guaranteed the school(s) or coaches any sort of rebate funding yet,
but he would like to be able to receive some funding, so he can provide those schools
that stay overnight with some funding to cover hotel room costs. The grant request of
$1,250 will go back to those schools that stayed overnight to help cover hotel room
costs. Any profits from the camps will help to fund future camps.
F. Arts in the Park
Mayor Hanson spoke on behalf of and presented the Arts in the Park Grant Application, which
is requesting $2,500.
• Mayor Hanson shared that this is the third year of the revival of Arts in the Park and will
take place on Saturday, July 25 through Sunday, July 26, 2026, at Hitchcock Park.
Currently, there are approximately 140 vendors attending the event. They estimate that
approximately 50–60% of vendors stay overnight in hotels. The grant request of $2,500
will go towards offsetting expenses such as security, park use fees, and permit fees.
Any profits from the event will go towards funding future events.

presented, and seconded by Jim Johnston. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.

documents.fileName: July 14, 2026, SEA Advisory Committee Meeting Minutes
documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                     July 14, 2026 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM  
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Kevin Nelson, Jason 
Christensen, Dave Sietsema, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, Jim Johnston  
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Mayor Hanson, Jill Larson, Cory Aadland, Tim 
Smith, Scott Morgan  
 
 Others present: Aaron Hieb, Stephanie Ellwein 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.  
 
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.  
 
 The following applications were presented and considered: 
 
A. Tour de Corn 
Emily Hohn spoke on behalf of and presented the Tour de Corn Grant Application, which is 
requesting $2,500. 

     • Emily shared that the events would take place on August 14–16, 2026, at The World's 
       Only Corn Palace Plaza. This event brings around 320 participants from Mitchell and 
       the surrounding states such as IA, NE, MN. The grant request of $2,500 will go 
       towards the meal and swag for the riders. Profits from the event will help to continue 
       supporting events/projects in the Mitchell community such as the Lake Mitchell Bike 
       Trail, bicycles at Christmas for students who use them for transportation, Cranksgiving, 
       etc. 

 
 
B. Palace City 8 Ball Open 
Jen Raymond and Corey Ditter spoke on behalf of and presented the Palace City 8 Ball Open 
Grant Application, which is requesting $5,000. 

     • Jen and Corey shared that the event would take place on October 2–4, 2026, at        Highland Conference Center. The event changed its dates from November to the first 
       weekend in October because of hunting season and the availability of hotel rooms. So 
       far, they have approximately 50 players signed up between the two divisions. The 
       Highland Conference Center can fit 20 pool tables in their venue. A portion of the entry 
       fees are considered "green fees", which are used towards their expenses. The grant 
       request of $5,000 will go towards paying for venue and pool table rental along with 
       increasing the prize pool awarded to the winners. Profits from the event will be added 
       towards this year's prize fund that is awarded to the winners. 

 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Sietsema to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
presented, and seconded by Jason Christensen. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion 
 passed. 
 
4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of July 1, 2026.  
 
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2026 are $113,950.00.  
 
Current Available Budgeted Balance of $75,240.00.  
 
Collections in February 2026 (for January 2026 records) still have one (1) establishment past 
due.  
 
Collections in March 2026 (for February 2026 records) still have (1) establishment past due.  
 
Collections in April 2026 (for March 2026 records) still have (1) establishment past due.  
 
Collections in May 2026 for (April 2026 records) still have (1) establishment past due.  
 
Collections in June 2026 for (May 2026 records) are $26,796.00 with (2) establishments past 
due.  
 
The (1) establishment past due is the same establishment for all past due collections in 2026, 
along with (1) additional establishment for the most recent collections. 
 
An average from past year's shows that the establishment(s) past due will account for 
approximately 650 - 700 room nights, once collected. 
 
The YTD collections for 2026 are $114,777.00, which equates to 57,389 total room nights 
sold. 
 
YTD comparisons of room nights sold were: down 5.1% from 2025, down 4.4% from 2024, 
down 0.3% from 2023, down 3.5% from 2022, up 7.1% from 2021, and up 26.8% from 2020.  
 
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to approve the financial report as presented, and 
 seconded by Jim Johnston. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.  
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
 Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s) with the SEA Committee: 
 
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s) 
DWU/Culver's Girls' & Boys' High School Basketball Classic (February 13-14, 2026) 

     • The events Exceeded (5) expectations. The total spectators were about 3,000 plus 
       those viewers using Live Stream. The total participants were 36 teams. The estimated 
       number of total hotel room nights was approximately 75. The funds awarded $5,000 
       were used to pay expenses for the event. Net Profit of $7,917.15, which was used as a 
       fundraiser for DWU Men's & Women's Basketball. Aaron shared that this event cracked 
       the Top 5 on the Activity Leader board for Playeasy, out of over 1,500 events on the 
       platform. Jason Christensen and Dave Sietsema also shared that this year's event was 
       a success. 

 
South Dakota VFW & Auxiliary Annua Convention (June 10-14, 2026) 

     • The event was Above (4) expectations. SEA was very helpful and we appreciate their 
       support. The total spectator attendance was: 185. The estimated number of total hotel 
       room nights was approximately 325. Next year's event will be hosted in Brandon, SD 
       on June 10-13, 2027. The funds awarded ($3,200) were used to pay for the rental of 
       the Highland Conference Center. Net loss of ($1,919.38). 

 
Cornbelt Team Camps 2026 (Varisty Girls June 10-11; Varsity Boys June 17-18, JV June 24-
25, 2026) 

     • The events were Above (4) expectations. The second day of the boys' camp had to 
       relocate to Ethan, SD because of the increase in rent of the Rec Center. Next year, the 
       event will ask for consideration to award additional funding to cover the cost of the Rec 
       Center, so the events can all be hosted in Mitchell, SD. Good attendance was seen by 
       both Aaron Hieb and Jason Christensen when they were at the camps. The total 
       participants were 82 teams. The estimated number of total hotel room nights was 
       approximately 72. Next year's dates are June 9-10, 16–17, 23–24, 2027, in Mitchell, 
       SD. The funds awarded $1,250 were distributed to each team who stayed overnight to 
       assist in reimbursement for their hotel room(s). Any profit from the events will carry 
       over into next year's camps. 

 
 
6. Other Items 
 Aaron Hieb shared the following information with the SEA Committee: 
 
A. Update and Review of Playeasy 
 
In the July 7, 2026, BID #4 Board meeting, the board did not motion and authorize funding to 
renew the yearly subscription to Playeasy for 2027. The Mitchell Sports & Events Authority  Playeasy subscription will end on December 31, 2026. 
 
B. Upcoming SEA Events

Complete list of events – MITCHELL CHAMBER EVENTS CALENDAR & Mitchell SD Events 
 Facebook 
 
7. Executive Session in accordance with SDCL 9-34-19: Discussion of confidential trade 
secrets, commercial, or financial information. 
 
Motion: Kevin Nelson made a motion to go into Executive Session at 2:22 PM, and was 
 seconded by Dave Helleloid. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.

9. Next Meeting Date 
Kevin McCardle shared the next meeting date of Tuesday, August 11, 2026, at 2 PM — City 
 Hall, Council Chambers. 
 10. Adjournment 
 Meeting adjourned by: Kevin McCardle at 2:38 PM

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conferences, conventions,
concerts, and sporting events hosted in Mitchell,
SD are an important aspect of the region’s sports
tourism industry.
The Mitchell SEA grant program is available to assist organizations in hosting events that
will promote a positive image to potential visitors, generate overnight visits, extend visitor
stays, and create a desire to return to the area.
The grant program is designed to assist event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Concerts/Special Events: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism and visitor spending in Mitchell, SD, or to fund area
events that will have a significant economic impact on businesses located in Mitchell,
specifically, by generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotels or the
Lake Mitchell Campground.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/conferences, sporting events, concerts, and other special
events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event and tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of Mitchell, SD.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee.

the Cranksgiving event and repairs of bicycles for those who are unable to afford their own.

Funding Matrix:
The Palace City 8 Ball Open takes place on Friday, October 2-Sunday, October 4, 2026, at the Highland Conference Center in Mitchell, SD.
The purpose of the Palace City Pool Promotions / Palace City 8 Ball Open is to host pool tournaments in Mitchell to keep growing the game and bringing competition in from across SD and surrounding states.
Last year's attendance: Total spectators: 50; Total participants: 88 from SD, ND, MN, IA, NE.
The SEA Grant Application states that approximately 70% of attendees will come from 100+ miles of Mitchell, SD.
Targeting players from MN, IA, NE, ND, SD, WY
Event Description:
We will host 2 main tournaments; an Open (any level) division limited to 64 players and a Sports (lower level) division limited to 24 players. The Open division brings in some of the best players from all over SD and our surrounding states. The Sports division gives the opportunity for lower ability players to compete in a
smaller field of their peers while still remaining competitive.
Up to 100 hotel room nights in early OCTOBER X $10 per room night = $1,000
$1,000 X 10% (Event hosted in early OCTOBER) = $100
$1,000 X 20% COMBINATION (Youth/Adult) = $200
$1,000 X 25% (>50% come from 100+ miles) = $250
$1,000 + $100 + $200 + $250 = $1,550
The grant requested will be used to cover our expenses; venue rental, pool table rental, promotional materials and event supplies.
All money received from the grant and sponsors that is left over from the tournament expenses will be added to the prize fund that the players will be playing for. If there happens to be small amount of funds left after paying expenses and players, any remaining funds will be rolled over into the next year's event.

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
June 9, 2026
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Mayor Hanson, Kevin McCardle, Kevin
Nelson, Jason Christensen, Dave Sietsema, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Tim Smith, Jim
Johnston, Scott Morgan
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Jill Larson, Cory Aadland Dave Helleloid
Others present: Aaron Hieb, Johanna Allen, Stephanie Ellwein, Gretchen
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.
The following applications were presented and considered:
A. Palace City Soccer Cup 2026
Adam Trimble spoke on behalf of and presented the Palace City Soccer Cup 2026 Grant
Application, which is requesting $5,000.
• Adam shared that the event will take place on Saturday, June 13–Sunday, June 14,
2026, at the Pepsi Cola Soccer Complex. This tournament is U9-U14 with a total of 19
teams, (12) of those are from outside of Mitchell. This number of teams is down
compared to 2025, and they are looking at changing the date in 2027, so it doesn't
overlap with a tournament in Rapid City. The grant request of $5,000 will go towards
offsetting expenses related to hosting the event.
B. Palace City Mountain Bike Classic
Cody Denne spoke on behalf of and presented the Palace City Mountain Bike Classic Grant
Application, which is requesting $1,200.
• Cody shared that the event will take place on Saturday, June 20, 2026, at the Lake
Mitchell Trails starting at Sandy Beach Access. So far, they have 41 racers signed up,

--- PAGE 1 OF 6 ---


with more sign-ups will take place a few days before and the day of the event. The
grant request of $1,200 will go towards paying for the timing system.
C. DWU Girls' Basketball Team Camps
Jason Christensen spoke on behalf of and presented the DWU Girls' Basketball Team Camps
Grant Application, which is requesting $1,100.
• Jason shared that the one-day team camps will take place on June 29 and July 27 at
DWU/ Avera Sports and Wellness Complex. Currently, there are 44 teams signed up
for the June session. The July session will pick up with registrations as it gets closer.
The grant request of $1,100 will be used to offset the costs of running the camps.
D. American Outlaws Wrestling Open & Showdown Belt Series
JD Heinrich via conference phone spoke on behalf of and presented the American Outlaws
Wrestling Open & Showdown Belt Series Grant Application, which is requesting $10,000.
• JD shared that this is the first year of a new wrestling tournament series that is broken
down into four different competitions, with the first 2 (Open & Showdown) taking place
on Saturday, July 18–Sunday, July 19, 2026, at the DWU/Avera Sports & Wellness
Complex. The age divisions are: 6U, 8U, 10U, 12U, 14U, High School (9-12th grade),
Seniors, Masters, Grand Masters, and Elite. Currently, there are approximately 60–70
participants signed up, with expectations of approximately 300–400 when all is said
and done. The grant request of $10,000 will go towards rent and concessions food and
supplies costs. Concession items will all be bought locally.
E. SD State Amateur Baseball Tournament
Jim Johnston spoke on behalf of and presented the SD State Amateur Baseball Tournament
Grant Application, which is requesting $5,000.
• Jim shared that the tournament will take place August 5-16, 2026, at the Cadwell Park
Stadium and Drake Field. There are a total of 36 teams to start the tournament, which
brings in approximately 10,000–12,000 total spectators for the tournament. He
estimates around 350 rooms nights for the entirety of the event. The grant request of
$5,000 will go towards the hospitality, field rental and maintenance costs, PA
announcer, and ticket takers. He estimates around 100 volunteers from the Mitchell
Baseball Association and Exchange Club of Mitchell assist in the success of the
tournament.
F. Dakota Oyate Challenge Volleyball
Silas Blaine, via conference phone, spoke on behalf of and presented the Dakota Oyate

--- PAGE 2 OF 6 ---


Challenge Volleyball Grant Application, which is requesting $17,147.26 / $6,300.
• Silas shared that the Dakota Oyate Challenge Volleyball made a date change this year,
so the event didn't overlap with the Pow Wow that takes place in Rapid City over the
October date the past two years. The new date for the tournament is September 18–
19, 2026, at The World's Only Corn Palace. Silas confirmed the grant request amount
is $6,300, which, based on the submitted event budget, would assist in keeping the
event out of the red or a negative income. The grant request of $6,300 would go
towards the Corn Palace rental costs, hotel rooms for officials, awards, and the
hospitality room. The event is also looking at expanding in the upcoming years, by
adding cross-country and hand games.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented, and seconded by Jason Christensen. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion
passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of June 3, 2026.
The supplemental carryover from the 2025 remaining balance of $39,190 has been added to
the SEA Revenue.
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2026 are $93,650.00.

($1,500).

due.

5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s) with the SEA Committee:

• The event was Above (4) expectations. Thank you for the continued support! The total

facility rental, food, hotels, equipment, transportation, and other operating costs. Profits
of $19,419.31.

--- PAGE 4 OF 6 ---


towards hotels. Net loss ($5,252).

documents.fileName: 2016 Mitchell Parks and Recreation Donor Guidelines
documents.text:
Page 1 of 3
2016 Mitchell Parks & Recreation Donor Guidelines
Memorial Donations
Minimum $2,500 donation
Plaque or sign near item
Donation must cover the full cost of Statues, Fountains, Plazas, Gardens etc.
Tree Donations
Minimum $100 donation
No plaque permitted
Trees may be donated to commemorate an event, individual or group. This could include a
wedding, birth of a child or an anniversary. Businesses could donate a tree to celebrate a
milestone or honor an employee for exceptional service.
Bench Donation
Minimum Donation $2,500
Plaque in front of bench
The bench donation of $2,500 includes the bench, plaque, installation and maintenance for the
life of the bench. The plaque inscription may be up to 70 characters. Inscription language must
be approved by the Parks and Recreation Director.
General Donations
No Minimum Amount Required
General donations given to the parks and recreation department will be acknowledged by a
letter of appreciation. All donations will meet the current needs of the department as
determined by the Director. Please notify the Director for specific project donations. Requests
can be made for current projects by contacting the Parks and Recreation office at 605-995-
8450.

--- PAGE 1 OF 3 ---


Page 2 of 3
Park Project Naming Opportunities
Minimum Donation $10,000
Donation must pay for the majority of the project for naming input, sign or plaque. The
duration of the naming rights shall be determined by the Parks Board at the time of donation.
New Facility Naming Opportunities
Minimum Donation $30,000
Donation must pay for the majority of the construction costs of the new facility for naming
input, plaque or sign. The duration of the naming rights shall be determined by the Parks Board
at time of donation.
Existing Facility Naming Opportunities
Minimum Donation $30,000
Upgrades to an existing facility that meet the minimum donation requirement will be
commemorated with a plaque or sign. Naming input will be considered if the facility has not
been named as a result of a previous donation and the upgrades are made to the entire facility.
The donation must pay for the majority of the upgrade costs. The duration of the naming rights
shall be determined by the Parks Board at the time of donation.
Signs
Associations
Associations with a majority stake in the facility may sell advertising for fundraising efforts. All
signs within the same area should be the same size. There will be a maximum of three different
size signs allowed within the same facility. Sign sizes and locations must be approved by the
Parks and Recreation Director prior to installation. Sign aesthetics will be taken into
consideration. Sign revenue must help fund facility upgrades or lease agreements with the City.
Association signs should not overpower or replace City signs, or make City facility names
unrecognizable.

--- PAGE 2 OF 3 ---


Page 3 of 3
Partnership/Donor Signs
Directional and informative signs can be considered as a place for partnership or donor
recognition. The recognition of donors should not overpower the sign information. Below is an
example of a donor sign:
Sponsorship Program
Adopt an Access Sponsor programs are available. For more information, please inquire with the
Parks and Recreation office at 605-995-8450.
*All donations will be recognized by letters of appreciation.
*The Parks and Recreation Board and City Council has the discretion of honoring donors based
on the above multi-tiered system with regards to funding, impact to the project, or other special
considerations.
*If the facility or donation reaches the end of its useful life, or if the duration of the naming
rights has expired, recognition signage will be returned to the donor.

MEMORANDUM
REPORT #1
DATE OF REPORT: 06/24/2026
SUBJECT: Soil-Cement Recommendations for 5th Avenue
Introduction
This correspondence presents our observations and recommendations for the project regarding the use of soil -cement.
Our work was performed in accordance with your authorization.
Project Information
It is our understanding that the design section for 5th Avenue includes 4 inches of asphalt and 12 inches of aggregate
base course overlying a geotextile fabric. It is our understanding that a section consisting of 4 inches of asphalt and 6
inches of aggregate base course overlying 12 inches of cement -treated subgrade soils has been proposed as an
alternative.
Soil-Cement Recommendations
We visited the site, on June 19, 2026, to observe the subgrade and to determine the suitability of the utilizing
soil-cement/cement-treated-subgrade for the project. We observed light brown to brown lean clay soils, brown sandy lean
clay soils, dark brown fat clay soils, and very dark brown lean clay soils within the upper portions of the subgrade.
With that said, it is our opinion that if the cement-treated subgrade soils are adequately hardened, then the proposed
section with 4 inches of asphalt and 6 inches of aggregate base course overlying 12 inches of cement -treated subgrade
soils should provide a similar or longer pavement life than the design section. Based on previous experience with similar
soil types, it is our opinion that a cement application rate of 5% (by dry weight) will be suitable in the areas with the light
brown to brown lean clay soils and brown sandy lean clay soils; however, in areas with mostly dark brown fat clay soils or
very dark brown lean clay soils, we recommend increasing the cement application rate to 6%. Also, areas with high
moisture contents (more than 3.5% over the optimum moisture content before the cement has been applied) will likely
need additional cement. If desired, we can provide testing (at a later date) to verify that the recommended cement
application rates adequately harden the subgrade soils.
The cement should be placed uniformly over the subgrade surface at the specified percentage with a computerized
spreader truck. Then, a self-propelled pulvimixer/reclaimer should be used to reclaim the upper 12 to 13 inches of the

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee 
                        612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers  
                                    August 18, 2026 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM  
 
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Jill Larson, Dave Sietsema, 
LaRee Rumbolz, Dave Helleloid, Tim Smith, Jim Johnston, Scott Morgan 
 
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Mayor Hanson, Kevin Nelson, Cory Aadland, 
Jason Christensen, Emily Liedtke 
 
 Others present: Aaron Hieb 
 
2. Presentation of Funding Applications 
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.  
 
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.  
 
 The following applications were presented and considered: 
 
A. Mitchell Area Bass Clef Festival 
Nicolas Caberos spoke on behalf of and presented the Mitchell Area Bass Clef Festival Grant 
Application, which is requesting $2,500. 

     • Nicolas shared that this would be the first annual event, which would take place on 
       Monday, September 14, 2026, at the Mitchell High School Performing Arts Center with 
       the final performance at 5:30 PM. When deciding to host an event like this, Nicolas 
       attended and referenced a similar event being hosted on the campus of the University 
       of Nebraska-Lincoln. The event is expecting around 250 6th-12th grade students from 
       across the state of South Dakota along with 30 directors from participating schools. 
       The grant request will go towards paying the clinicians. The event is not for profit 
       based, and any excess funds will go towards paying the clinicians for the following 
       years. 

 
 
B. Cornicupia 2026 
Scott Mullenmeister spoke on behalf of and presented the Cornicupia 2026 Grant Application, 
which is requesting $5,000.      • Scott shared that the 3rd annual two-day tournament will take place on September 26–
       27, 2026, at the Pepsi-Cola Soccer Complex. The tournament will host 9U-14U teams 
       from across the state of South Dakota. The first year of the tournament had 41 teams, 
       the second year had 52 teams, and currently, they have 14 non-Mitchell teams signed 
       up with a promising outlook for this year's tournament. The grant request will go 
       towards their biggest expense, which are referee fees. Profits from the tournament will 
       go towards the Mitchell Soccer Association — coaches pay, field use costs throughout 
       the year, and new equipment. 

 
 
C. Palace City Kiwanis Half Marathon 10K 5K & Kids Fun Run 
Julie Hart Schutte spoke on behalf of and presented the Palace City Kiwanis Half Marathon 
10K 5K & Kids Fun Run Grant Application, which is requesting $1,000. 

     • Julie shared that the 9th annual event would start with the Kids Fun Run on Saturday, 
       October 3 and conclude with the Half Marathon, 10K, & 5K starting at 7:30 AM on 
       Sunday, October 4, 2026, in front of The World's Only Corn Palace. They currently 
       have 127 participants signed up, which is up from 2025 (77). There are 12 states 
       represented so far. Last year, they received feedback that 17 room nights were 
       accounted for, and so far, for 2026, that number is at 12 room nights with more 
       responses yet to come. The grant request will go towards the different sponsorship 
       levels, which account for event promotion, runner awards / T-shirts, and other race 
       expenses, including the timing system. Profits from the event directly benefit children's 
       initiatives throughout the Mitchell community. 

 
 
D. South Dakota Parks and Recreation Annual Conference 
Kevin Nelson joined via conference phone and spoke on behalf of and presented the South 
Dakota Parks and Recreation Annual Conference Grant Application, which is requesting 
$5,000. 

     • Kevin shared that every 10 years the annual state rotation of the conference lands in 
       Mitchell, SD. This year the conference will be October 6–8, 2026, at the Highland 
       Conference Center. The average attendance for the last two years (Sioux Falls / 
       Spearfish) was around 121 participants. The annual conference is the only revenue-
       producing event / fundraiser that the state association hosts, so the grant request will 
       go towards expenses of hosting the conference in Mitchell, SD. Profits from the 
       conference go to the state association. 

 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Sietsema to approve the previous meeting minutes as 
 presented, and seconded by Jim Johnston. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 4. Financial Report 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of August 18, 2026.  
 
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2026 are $118,450.00.  
 
Current Available Budgeted Balance of $70,740.00.  
 
Collections in February 2026 (for January 2026 records) are $14,710.00 with all collected.  
 
Collections in March 2026 (for February 2026 records) are $16,826.00 with all collected.  
 
Collections in April 2026 (for March 2026 records) are $18,688.00 with all collected.  
 
Collections in May 2026 for (April 2026 records) are $21,326.00 with all collected.  
 
Collections in June 2026 for (May 2026 records) are $26,840.00 with (1) establishments past 
due.  
 
Collections in July 2026 for (June 2026 records) are $33,940.00 with (1) establishment past 
due. 
 
An average from past year's shows that the establishment past due will account for 
approximately 1,300–1,500 room nights, once collected.  
 
The YTD collections for 2026 are $148,921.00, which equates to 74,461 total room nights 
sold.  
 
YTD comparisons of room nights sold were: down 6.2% (4,608 room nights) from 2025, down 
3.2% (2,359 room nights) from 2024, down 0.9% (676 room nights) from 2023, down 4.6% 
from 2022, up 2.2% from 2021, and up 27.3% from 2020.  
 
The committee had some additional discussion about reasons for the shortfall in room nights 
so far in 2026. 
 
Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to approve the financial report as presented, and 
 seconded by Scott Morgan. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys 
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s) and Thank You card with 
 the SEA Committee: 
 
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s) 
Lucky Devils Adult Hockey Tournament (April 10-12, 2026) 

     • The event Met (3) expectations. The event cannot grow without another sheet of ice. 
       The total spectators were between 600–800. The total participants were 22 teams, 
       which accounts for approximately 308 players. Teams came from: Fargo, Minneapolis, 
       Wisconsin, Sioux Falls, Sioux City, Aberdeen, Minnesota, Pierre, Watertown, Huron, 
       and Mitchell. The estimated number of total hotel room nights was approximately 165–       200. Next year's event will be April 9–11, 2027. The funds awarded $4,000 were used 
       to pay for expenses such as the ice rental fees. The Net Profit of $11,049.95 goes 
       towards the sponsorship of all 8U hockey players in Mitchell as well as a couple of 
       development clinics throughout the year. 

 
DWU Spring Golf Invitational (April 12–13, 2026) 

     • The event was Below (2) expectations. They fell short of the number of golfers 
       expected. The total spectators were between 100–150. The total participants were 72 
       golfers and 12 coaches. Teams came from: Yankton, Missouri, North Dakota, Kansas, 
       and Mitchell. The estimated number of total hotel room nights was approximately 70–
       90. Next year's event will be April 11–12, 2027. The funds awarded $3,000 were used 
       to pay for the coach's meals, complimentary water on the course, green fees and 
       coaches gift. The Net Profit of $5,026.69 will go towards the Men's & Women's golf 
       programs to assist in expenses to compete at premier golf course in the US. 

 
 
B. Thank you card 
 MAC Triathlon / Palace City Mountain Bike Classic (MAC Area Events, INC.)

7. Executive Session in accordance with SDCL 9-34-19: Discussion of confidential trade 
secrets, commercial, or financial information. 
 
Motion: Dave Sietsema made a motion to go into Executive Session at 2:28 PM, and was 
 seconded by Dave Helleloid. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 
 
8. Approval of Funding Applications 
Mitchell Area Bass Clef Festival 
Date: September 14, 2026; Contact: Nicolas Caberos; Grant Request: $2,500 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to award $1,000, and seconded by Tim 
       Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
Cornicupia 2026 
Date: September 26–27, 2026; Contact: Scott Mullenmeister; Grant Request: $5,000 
 

     • Motion: Motion was made by LaRee Rumbolz to award $5,000, and seconded by 
       Scott Morgan. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 Palace City Kiwanis Half Marathon 10K 5K & Kids Fun Run 
Date: October 3-4, 2026; Contact: Paula Deckert; Grant Request: $1,000 
 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to award $750 with $250 going towards 
       the Shirt Sponsor Level, and seconded by Tim Smith. All members voted 'Aye' and the 
       motion passed. 

 
South Dakota Parks and Recreation Annual Conference 
Date: October 6–8, 2026; Contact: Kevin Nelson; Grant Request: $5,000 
 

     • Motion: Motion was made by Tim Smith to award $2,500, and seconded by LaRee 
       Rumbolz. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed. 

 
 
9. Next Meeting Date 
Kevin McCardle shared the next meeting date of Tuesday, September 8, 2026, at 2 PM — City 
 Hall, Council Chambers. 
 
10. Adjournment 
 Meeting adjourned by: Kevin McCardle at 2:46 PM

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conferences, conventions,
concerts, and sporting events hosted in Mitchell,
SD are an important aspect of the region’s sports
tourism industry.
The Mitchell SEA grant program is available to assist organizations in hosting events that
will promote a positive image to potential visitors, generate overnight visits, extend visitor
stays, and create a desire to return to the area.
The grant program is designed to assist event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Concerts/Special Events: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism and visitor spending in Mitchell, SD, or to fund area
events that will have a significant economic impact on businesses located in Mitchell,
specifically, by generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotels or the
Lake Mitchell Campground.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/conferences, sporting events, concerts, and other special
events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event and tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of Mitchell, SD.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee.

The Palace City Kiwanis Half Marathon 10K 5K & Kids Fun Run starts and endin front of The World's Only Corn Palace on Saturday, October 3-Sunday, October 4, 2026 in Mitchell, SD.
The purpose of the Kiwanis Club of Mitchell is to support children, including the Kiwanis Woodlot Park and the Patton Young Story Walk, local children's initiatives and events.
Last year's attendance: approximately 500 total between 200 runners, volunteers, and spectators.
The SEA Grant Application states that approximately 30% of attendees will come from 100+ miles of Mitchell, SD.
Event Description:
The event starts and ends at the Corn Palace with the Half Marathon runners running around Lake Mitchell. Runners range in age from teenagers to senior citizens. All ages have ran and competed in the event. From the kids in Mitchell and participant's children for the Fun Run and all ages for the
Half Marathon, 10K, and 5K. Since adding the 5K to the race there is a wider range of runners who participate.
Up to 50 hotel room nights in EARLY OCTOBER X $10 per room night = $500
$500 X 10% (Event hosted in EARLY OCTOBER) = $50
$500 X 20% COMBINATION (Youth/Adult) = $100
$500 X 10% TEAM = $50
$500 X 10% (<50% come from 100+ miles) = $50
$500 + $50 + $100 + $50 + $50 = $750
The grant requested will be used to cover event promotion, runner awards and t-shirts, and other race expenses.
Proceeds from the run directly benefit children's initiatives, including but not all inclusive, scholarships, Kiwanis Woodlot Park, Patton Young Story Walk, Mitchell Little Libraries, CASA, Big Friend Little Friend, First Responder blanket project.

Sports & Events Authority Grant Application
***Application must be received no less than 45
days prior to the first day of the event.***
The many festivals, conferences, conventions,
concerts, and sporting events hosted in Mitchell,
SD are an important aspect of the region’s sports
tourism industry.
The Mitchell SEA grant program is available to assist organizations in hosting events that
will promote a positive image to potential visitors, generate overnight visits, extend visitor
stays, and create a desire to return to the area.
The grant program is designed to assist event planners by providing funds for marketing,
advertising, printing, and postage in the following categories:
Meetings: conventions, conferences, seminars, retreats, etc.
Sporting Events: tournaments, competitions, etc.
Festivals/Concerts/Special Events: Other events that generate overnight stays.
The grant exists to encourage tourism and visitor spending in Mitchell, SD, or to fund area
events that will have a significant economic impact on businesses located in Mitchell,
specifically, by generating overnight stays and/or extending visitor stays at hotels or the
Lake Mitchell Campground.
Preference will be given to:
1. New festivals, conventions/conferences, sporting events, concerts, and other special
events.
2. Existing events showing an expanded focus for event and tourism growth. All events
must project a positive image of Mitchell, SD.
The grant program is appropriated and administered to qualifying organizations by the
Mitchell SEA on review by the SEA Advisory Committee.

On October 2, 1965, The South Dakota Parks and Recreation
Association was founded. The SDPRA mission is “to promote the
growth, status, and unity of all phases of parks, recreation, and
leisure in the state of South Dakota."
"We’re a community. Our members work in every discipline in
parks and recreation across the state." Our common goals are:
“To improve public places and recreation in South Dakota.”

The association holds annual meetings (conferences) to share
best practices, exchange information, and award outstanding
performance in the industry. Members are nominated for
recognition in the categories of “Professional Service”, are given
citations for “Individual and Organizational Contributions”, and

--- PAGE 4 OF 6 ---


are recognized for “Community Excellence”. Related vendors are
invited to sponsor and/or rent space to promote their applicable

What are the specific
goals for this event?
The association holds annual meetings (conferences) to share
best practices, exchange information, and award outstanding
performance in the industry. Host communities generally provide
tours to local sites to highlight accomplishments in facility
improvements and to demonstrate new equipment, be it that of a
vendor or that recently acquired by the host community. At the
conferences, members are nominated for recognition in the
categories of “Professional Service”, are given citations for
“Individual and Organizational Contributions”, and are recognized
for “Community Excellence”. Related vendors are invited to
sponsor and/or rent space to promote their applicable product
lines.
Explain how your grant
request would be used
to promote tourism in
Mitchell? Note the

SDPRA members network amongst themselves, as well as with
residents of their respective communities. We discuss
improvements and successes within our respective communities,
making certain to take notes on such for possible incorporation
into our own communities. In addition, some conferences include
bus tours to see major improvements within parks, facilities, golf
courses, streetscapes, and new businesses. Because roughly
25-30 percent of participants are State of South Dakota Game,
Fish, and Parks employees, it might also overview improvements
at nearby state parks and other state-run facilities. I will be
discussing improvements (new playgrounds) made at several
parks, the improvements at Cadwell Field, the new (in 2025)
pickleball courts, new and existing trails, streetscape
improvements along Main Street, the upcoming Lake Mitchell
draw down and related work, the to-be new storm shelter/comfort
station at Lake Mitchell Campground, and the possibility of the
new indoor sports facility. Our event is being held at the Highland
Conference Center, which continues to speak for itself.

Were the request to be denied, we'll hope for an otherwise
'healthy' bottom line to the conference to sustain SDPRA's needs
for the coming year, and we will still speak highly of all that SEA
does for the community and to promote Mitchell to visitors.

Funding Matrix:
The South Dakota Parks and Recreation Annual Conference takes place in Mitchell, SD at the Highland Conference Center on Tuesday, October 6-Thursday, October 8, 2026.
Mitchell last hosted this annual rotation conference 10 years ago, in 2016.
The SDPRA is a professional association of people who manage or work in various municipal and regional parks and a variety of other recreational facilities around the state. It’s members include both public and private
employees, from the state, cities, and others from the non-profit organization, and people owning or managing private park and recreational facilities.
SEA Grant Application states that between 60-70% of attendance comes from outside 100+ miles of Mitchell, SD.
The average attendance the last couple of years, in Sioux Falls and Spearfish has been 121 participants.
The association holds annual meetings (conferences) to share best practices, exchange information, and award outstanding performance in the industry. Members are nominated for recognition in the categories of “Professional
Service”, are given citations for “Individual and Organizational Contributions”, and are recognized for “Community Excellence”. Related vendors are invited to sponsor and/or rent space to promote their applicable product lines.
The conference keynote speaker, Becky Geyer, is originally from De Smet, South Dakota. She now serves as a professor at Texas A&M.
Up to 200 hotel room nights in EARLY OCTOBER X $10 per room night = $2,000
$2,000 X 10% (Event hosted in EARLY OCTOBER) = $200
$2,000 X 10% (Event hosted during WEEKDAY ROOM NIGHTS) = $200
$2,000 X 15% (ADULT) = $300
$2,000 X 25% (>50% come from 100+ miles) = $500
$2,000 + $200 + $200 + $300 + $500 = $3,200
Each year, the financial goal of the conference is to generate ~$20,000 in revenue. This is the only revenue producing event of our organization to allow us to operate for the upcoming year.
Profits and proceeds from the annual conference are used to operate the organization/association.

documents.text:
Sports & Events Authority Advisory Committee
612 N. Main, City Hall - Council Chambers
July 14, 2026
1. Call to Order
Meeting called to order by: Kevin McCardle at 2:00 PM
SEA Advisory Committee members present: Kevin McCardle, Kevin Nelson, Jason
Christensen, Dave Sietsema, LaRee Rumbolz, Emily Liedtke, Dave Helleloid, Jim Johnston
SEA Advisory Committee members absent: Mayor Hanson, Jill Larson, Cory Aadland, Tim
Smith, Scott Morgan
Others present: Aaron Hieb, Stephanie Ellwein
2. Presentation of Funding Applications
SEA Grant Application presentations by applicants.
The SEA Advisory Committee reviewed applications for grant funding.
The following applications were presented and considered:
A. Tour de Corn
Emily Hohn spoke on behalf of and presented the Tour de Corn Grant Application, which is
requesting $2,500.
• Emily shared that the events would take place on August 14–16, 2026, at The World's
Only Corn Palace Plaza. This event brings around 320 participants from Mitchell and
the surrounding states such as IA, NE, MN. The grant request of $2,500 will go
towards the meal and swag for the riders. Profits from the event will help to continue
supporting events/projects in the Mitchell community such as the Lake Mitchell Bike
Trail, bicycles at Christmas for students who use them for transportation, Cranksgiving,
etc.
B. Palace City 8 Ball Open
Jen Raymond and Corey Ditter spoke on behalf of and presented the Palace City 8 Ball Open
Grant Application, which is requesting $5,000.
• Jen and Corey shared that the event would take place on October 2–4, 2026, at

--- PAGE 1 OF 5 ---


Highland Conference Center. The event changed its dates from November to the first
weekend in October because of hunting season and the availability of hotel rooms. So
far, they have approximately 50 players signed up between the two divisions. The
Highland Conference Center can fit 20 pool tables in their venue. A portion of the entry
fees are considered "green fees", which are used towards their expenses. The grant
request of $5,000 will go towards paying for venue and pool table rental along with
increasing the prize pool awarded to the winners. Profits from the event will be added
towards this year's prize fund that is awarded to the winners.
3. Approval of Minutes
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Sietsema to approve the previous meeting minutes as
presented, and seconded by Jason Christensen. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion
passed.
4. Financial Report
Aaron Hieb reviewed the financial report as of July 1, 2026.
Current expenses and award checks that have been written for 2026 are $113,950.00.
Current Available Budgeted Balance of $75,240.00.
Collections in February 2026 (for January 2026 records) still have one (1) establishment past
due.
Collections in March 2026 (for February 2026 records) still have (1) establishment past due.
Collections in April 2026 (for March 2026 records) still have (1) establishment past due.
Collections in May 2026 for (April 2026 records) still have (1) establishment past due.
Collections in June 2026 for (May 2026 records) are $26,796.00 with (2) establishments past
due.
The (1) establishment past due is the same establishment for all past due collections in 2026,
along with (1) additional establishment for the most recent collections.
An average from past year's shows that the establishment(s) past due will account for
approximately 650 - 700 room nights, once collected.
The YTD collections for 2026 are $114,777.00, which equates to 57,389 total room nights
sold.
YTD comparisons of room nights sold were: down 5.1% from 2025, down 4.4% from 2024,
down 0.3% from 2023, down 3.5% from 2022, up 7.1% from 2021, and up 26.8% from 2020.
Motion: Motion was made by Dave Helleloid to approve the financial report as presented, and
seconded by Jim Johnston. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.

--- PAGE 2 OF 5 ---


5. Evaluation Forms/Financials/Surveys
Aaron Hieb reviewed the following Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s) with the SEA Committee:
A. Evaluation Form(s) w/Financial(s)
DWU/Culver's Girls' & Boys' High School Basketball Classic (February 13-14, 2026)
• The events Exceeded (5) expectations. The total spectators were about 3,000 plus
those viewers using Live Stream. The total participants were 36 teams. The estimated
number of total hotel room nights was approximately 75. The funds awarded $5,000
were used to pay expenses for the event. Net Profit of $7,917.15, which was used as a
fundraiser for DWU Men's & Women's Basketball. Aaron shared that this event cracked
the Top 5 on the Activity Leader board for Playeasy, out of over 1,500 events on the
platform. Jason Christensen and Dave Sietsema also shared that this year's event was
a success.
South Dakota VFW & Auxiliary Annua Convention (June 10-14, 2026)
• The event was Above (4) expectations. SEA was very helpful and we appreciate their
support. The total spectator attendance was: 185. The estimated number of total hotel
room nights was approximately 325. Next year's event will be hosted in Brandon, SD
on June 10-13, 2027. The funds awarded ($3,200) were used to pay for the rental of
the Highland Conference Center. Net loss of ($1,919.38).
Cornbelt Team Camps 2026 (Varisty Girls June 10-11; Varsity Boys June 17-18, JV June 24-
25, 2026)
• The events were Above (4) expectations. The second day of the boys' camp had to
relocate to Ethan, SD because of the increase in rent of the Rec Center. Next year, the
event will ask for consideration to award additional funding to cover the cost of the Rec
Center, so the events can all be hosted in Mitchell, SD. Good attendance was seen by
both Aaron Hieb and Jason Christensen when they were at the camps. The total
participants were 82 teams. The estimated number of total hotel room nights was
approximately 72. Next year's dates are June 9-10, 16–17, 23–24, 2027, in Mitchell,
SD. The funds awarded $1,250 were distributed to each team who stayed overnight to
assist in reimbursement for their hotel room(s). Any profit from the events will carry
over into next year's camps.
6. Other Items
Aaron Hieb shared the following information with the SEA Committee:
A. Update and Review of Playeasy
In the July 7, 2026, BID #4 Board meeting, the board did not motion and authorize funding to
renew the yearly subscription to Playeasy for 2027. The Mitchell Sports & Events Authority

--- PAGE 3 OF 5 ---


Playeasy subscription will end on December 31, 2026.

o Cadwell Park Stadium

secrets, commercial, or financial information.
Motion: Kevin Nelson made a motion to go into Executive Session at 2:22 PM, and was
seconded by Dave Helleloid. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
8. Approval of Funding Applications
Tour de Corn
Date: August 14-16, 2026; Contact: Kourtney Denne; Grant Request: $2,500
• Motion: Motion was made by Jason Christensen to award $2,500, and seconded by
Jim Johnston. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
Palace City 8 Ball Open
Date: October 2-4, 2026; Contact: Jennifer Raymond; Grant Request: $5,000
• Motion: Motion was made by Kevin Nelson to award $4,000, and seconded by Dave
Helleloid. All members voted 'Aye' and the motion passed.
9. Next Meeting Date
Kevin McCardle shared the next meeting date of Tuesday, August 11, 2026, at 2 PM — City
Hall, Council Chambers.

10. Adjournment
Meeting adjourned by: Kevin McCardle at 2:38 PM
